Cardinals Fans Sound Off After Week 7 Loss to Broncos
full_text:
GLENDALE — The losses continue to pile for the Arizona Cardinals, who fell to the Denver Broncos in 30-16 fashion in Week 7.
The loss dropped Arizona to 2-5 on the year and further down the NFC standings. While there was some hope of a potential upset brewing, Denver was in control for most of action at State Farm Stadium.
We asked , you delivered. Here's Cardinals' fans reactions to their loss against Denver:
"I thought i knew what the struggle bus was.... AZ has shown there is a worse bus to be on," Bryan A said.
Depression... we might beat Dallass next week but same damn thing all over again. offense can't do anything...O-line is struggling, Burnt Brisket doing Burnt brisket things, bidwill doesn't care since the Broncos fans cut him a check. Back to reality smfh
Cardinals owner Michael Bidwill was again a massive talking point for fans following another loss.
Bruce added, "This team is so devoid of talent & direction, it doesn’t matter who the coach or QB are. The problem will always be Bidwill. Not worth getting upset over. He doesn’t care as long as he’s getting $. Visiting fans pay $ too when they fill 90% of seats. He gets paid either way."
Ten. In a row. In the desert. Twenty-five teams in NFL history lost ten straight at home. Only one did it while charging fans for parking, beer, and a stadium Wi-Fi subscription. #BidwillOut
"Trade everyone. Brisket released. Beck starting. Owner won’t care all he sees is money," added KIZ.
#BidwillOut pic.twitter.com/VVR6vq8FKW
The Cardinals, on a brighter note, did induct Larry Fitzgerald into their Ring of Honor today. It was an impressive halftime ceremony that finally brought Arizona's coveted hero home.
"I wish Larry could’ve been presented a game ball! He deserves so much better the product we witnessed on the field today! Sorry Larry, you deserve better!" Chris said.
Bidwill was present for Fitzgerald's speech on the field and was met with boos throughout the stadium whenever the Hall of Fame wideout mentioned and thanked him. Bidwill did not speak at halftime.

Dustin added, "Not easy being a Cardinals fan. The fans in the stadium thing though - Yikes!"

title: Cardinals’ Jacoby Brissett Decision Is Only Delaying the Inevitable
full_text:
GLENDALE — The Arizona Cardinals insist on delaying the inevitable.
The team dropped to 2-5 after Sunday's loss to the Denver Broncos, one where the Cardinals' offense again failed to come alive. Their red zone woes continued from last week, which led to their second straight outing with less than 20 points scored while marking their third instance in the first seven weeks of play.
The Cardinals fell 30-16 against a talented Denver defense, which ranked as one of the tougher units entering today and very much stamped their reputation, hitting Jacoby Brissett 13 times and limited the Cardinals' offense to just 5-of-17 on third-down conversions with only one touchdown in five red zone trips.
Arizona's offense under the first-year play-calling of Mike LaFleur will again be led by Brissett in Week 8 against the Dallas Cowboys , LaFleur confirmed post-game.
When pressed about what Brissett brings to the table, LaFleur offered:
"I'm not even going to talk about any of the individuals. It's us collectively. We just gotta finish better," he said.
"... We had opportunities to make some plays that we didn't, and when we get to the point where we're going to flip this thing, we got to make those plays. This is a collective deal in terms of coaching and playing, but we can make that easier on ourselves."
Brissett has started every game for the Cardinals since striking a re-worked contract in the early stages of training camp, ending an offseason-long holdout that guaranteed more money on the final of a two-year deal.
There are several problems plaguing the Cardinals at this point in time, ones that will eventually be dug into later this week. Brissett, in totality, is not the biggest issue Arizona's offense faces at this point in time.
However, he's clearly not a solution to the team's 2-5 start to the season, and that in itself is an issue that LaFleur and the rest of the coaching staff is going to have to acknowledge sooner rather than later.
While Brissett's profile resides in a veteran passer who can hang in the pocket and take care of the ball, his ceiling and quick trigger when throwing the ball largely caps what the Cardinals can do. LaFleur's offense was expected to be innovative, though Arizona's attack has been largely stagnant through their first seven weeks.
The Cardinals could get away with the "we believe he gives us the best chance to win games now" mantra early in the season, where hope is still alive and teams aren't sinking to the bottom of the standings.
Arizona's now 2-5 with little optimism of a quick turnaround on either side of the ball. The Cardinals need to change something, that's not negotiable. And to Brissett's defense, his offensive line has been below par while his pass-catchers, to various extents, haven't lived up to their billing.
Yet a quarterback is supposed to be the engine that makes an offense go, and the Cardinals have stalled out more times than not.
While it's admirable for LaFleur to prioritize winning here and now, a move to the likes of Gardner Minshew or even Carson Beck wouldn't signal a team that's throwing in the towel — it would be Arizona acknowledging Brissett's simply capped in the potential he can carry this offense to.
It feels like only a matter of when — not if — the Cardinals make a change. However, the longer Arizona delays the inevitable benching of Brissett for other opportunities, the bigger of a hole they're going to dig themselves.

title: Instant Reactions: Bo Nix Exposes Cardinals' Biggest Problems
full_text:
For a week, optimism filled Arizona Cardinals land.
After the Cardinals beat the division-rival Los Angeles Rams ahead of their Week 7 matchup with Denver, there was hope they could beat a Broncos team that, despite its strong record, had some weaknesses.
However, that wasn't the case. The Broncos downed the Cardinals 30 to 16 at State Farm Stadium, pushing Arizona to 2-5 on the season.
Four big takeaways from their Week 7 loss:
Defensive coordinator Nick Rallis' unit was the main headline in the win over the Rams, as the defense played extremely well. Their defense again started strong for the Cardinals this week, with the defensive line pressuring Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix early in action, which included a sack by defensive end Darius Robinson.
At the end of the first quarter, the Cardinals held the Broncos to only two field goals and no touchdowns; however, that changed for the rest of the game.
Things went downhill for the Cardinals' defense when they made a struggling Bo Nix look like legendary scrambling San Francisco 49ers quarterback Steve Young. Nix scrambled for a 62-yard Denver touchdown, going untouched to the end zone.
The big plays continued when Nix hit Broncos running back R.J. Harvey for a 52-yard touchdown on a screen pass. The Broncos blocked this screen well, but Arizona's defense saw Harvey weave in and out of traffic on his touchdown reception, which was dissapointing especially after they tackled so well against the Rams last week.
Simply put, this Cardinals defense was dissapointing. While they did have some good moments, it was erased by some horrendous defensive play.
As awesome as tight end Trey McBride and wideout Michael Wilson are, the Cardinals still need another viable pass catcher. The Cardinals' pass game struggled heavily in this matchup despite quarterback Jacoby Brissett actually threading some nice deep passes that the Cardinals' pass-catchers couldn't haul in.
A big issue is that the Cardinals lack a speed threat on the outside. McBride and Wilson specialize more in strength and possession rather than being downfield burners, and such was even the case when Marvin Harrison Jr. was present.
The NFL's best offenses have great speed threats, such as Khalil Shakir on the Buffalo Bills and Luther Burden III on the Chicago Bears. Adding a player with that skillset could greatly help head coach Mike LaFleur's offense.
While Nix didn't have an amazing game, he played the kind of game Cardinals fans have wanted from their own signal caller. Nix moved the ball downfield without turning it over. On the day, Nix threw one touchdown pass, no interceptions, and finished with an 88.6 passer rating.
Going into the season, Arizona was expected to get these types of games from Brissett. However, that has not been the case. Brissett has turned the ball over more than expected and hasn't made the best reads.
Cardinals fans aren't expecting Brissett to play at the level of an MVP like Josh Allen of the Buffalo Bills or Lamar Jackson of the Baltimore Ravens. The main issue is the simple stuff Brissett has struggled with.
I still don't think the Cardinals' infrastructure is great for any quarterback, but after this game, going with Gardner Minshew or Carson Beck is the right choice.
After a week where the Cardinals didn't score a touchdown and settled for six field goals in the red zone, their Week 7 red zone offense wasn't much better against Denver, going one for five on the day. The Cardinals' lone touchdown came when Brissett found McBride for a touchdown on a seven-yard pass.
Arizona's lack of red-zone execution over the past two weeks is very concerning. The Cardinals' more possession-heavy personnel should make for a better red-zone offense. However, that has not been the case.
Out of all the issues the Cardinals have, this is the one that will cost them the most games. Settling for field goals consistently can not win you a game every week. Hopefully, head coach Mike LaFleur can turn the red-zone offense around. If not, it's going to be a very long back half of the season.

title: 9 Winners And Losers From Cardinals Loss to Broncos
full_text:
ARIZONA — It was close, until it wasn't.
The Arizona Cardinals emerge from their Week 7 clash with a 30-16 loss to the Denver Broncos, dropping their record to 2-5 on the season.
Don't let the final score fool you — the Cardinals were outplayed today, especially in the second half.
Winners and losers from Arizona's loss to the Broncos:
It's time to start those conversations again.
After an impressive win last week in Los Angeles, the Cardinals' defense is back to their typical standard of play after allowing 30 points to a struggling Denver offense. Bo Nix looked more than a competent quarterback, which is saying something.
Rallis' crew has now allowed 30 or more points in five of Arizona's seven games this season.
How much longer does he last?
Robinson needed to have a strong third season to get himself back on track, as the former first-round pick very much filled the "bust label" and couldn't shed it through the first two years of his career.
However, Robinson's silently had a strong 2026 season, which continued today with a sack on Bo Nix, his second on the year.
He ended the day with four tackles, tied for third-most on Arizona.
With multiple safeties sidelined, it was Garrett Williams who primarily operated as Budda Baker's partner in crime on the backend. Even with the Cardinals thin at cornerback, Arizona opted to take their best available corner and place him at safety over Dadrion Taylor-Demerson.
That didn't last long, as Williams missed a tackle on an explosive Broncos pass while being responsible for a deep coverage bust down the field on another. He was replaced by Taylor-Demerson and played sparingly the rest of the way.
With Jeremiyah Love again out of action, the Cardinals leaned on Bam Knight once again to shoulder the load for Arizona's backfield.
Acknowledging the dropped touchdown pass in the first half, Knight did have an overall solid day — they just didn't run the ball all that often. Knight finished with seven rushes for 48 yards, a 6.9 YPC average.
He also added three receptions for 15 yards.
Look, there's penalties every game. It's hard to play a smooth game from start to finish, and it's especially dependent on the crew of officials. And while the Cardinals have shown to have a penalty problem in the past, this is a general take for both Arizona and Denver. Both teams ranked in the bottom half of the NFL in terms of total penalties for the 2026 season entering today.
The amount of flags thrown at State Farm Stadium was ridiculous. 20 total penalties for over 170 yards is eye-opening.
Happy National Tight Ends Day, Trey!
McBride, after scoring just once in his last four games, found the end zone for Arizona and ended their red zone woes after connecting with Jacoby Brissett on a seven-yard touchdown to get the Cardinals' offense going.
McBride's had a string of quieter games compared to his usual standard, though he bounced back with a nice ten reception, 111 yard and one score outing.
Brissett, after leading the Cardinals on a game-winning drive against the Rams last week, has come back down to earth. Hard.
Brissett completed 27 of 48 passes for 272 yards and one touchdown with no interceptions.
He was extremely limited in his operations of the offense, again, especially in the red zone.
On a brighter note for the Cardinals, Larry Fitzgerald was inducted into the team's Ring of Honor at halftime, where the Hall of Fame receiver spoke and saw his famous No. 11 immortalized forever in Arizona history.
It was a special day for a special player and fans who never got to see their hero officially say goodbye after he retired in 2020. Even with a loss, it was still an incredible day for Cardinals fans and Fitzgerald.
Brissett had a whopping 13 quarterback hits today to pair with two sacks. Entering today, he had one of the NFL's fastest average times to throw, and the Broncos got after him early and often.
Arizona's offensive line featured a rookie seventh-round pick at left tackle and their effective fourth-string right guard, which was pitted against a Broncos front seven who had 60 pressures through six games entering today.
Brissett, while clearly having ownership of issues in Arizona's offense, simply was under duress the entire day. His offensive line never stood a chance.

title: Cardinals Linked to Josh Sweat Trade With Cowboys
full_text:
ARIZONA — Weeks after Marvin Harrison Jr. was traded to the Houston Texans, the Arizona Cardinals might not be done moving off their biggest names.
Outside linebacker Josh Sweat, initially dealing with injury to begin the 2026 season, has found his footing in recent weeks by amassing two sacks in the last three games. After a 12-sack season in 2025, Sweat is getting closer and closer to reaching his prior form.
That's perhaps at the right time for the Cardinals, who could be open to trading Sweat if the price is right. Sweat reportedly requested a trade earlier this offseason with numerous teams calling for his availability at different points of the summer.
NFL insider Jeremy Fowler says that could very well happen near the Nov. 10 trade deadline, and there's one team specifically he circled as a landing spot.
In his weekly buzz file, Fowler ended his writing with this nugget on Sweat:
"Josh Sweat: The Arizona Cardinals already have shown they are willing to trade a player for the right price. In August, general manager Monti Ossenfort said the Cardinals were not interested in trading Sweat. But now the Cardinals are 2-4, and unless they turn it around, they could be willing to listen to meaningful offers," he wrote.
"One team that could explore the possibility of a Sweat trade is the Cowboys, who are trying to salvage their season Monday night in Philadelphia."
Dallas, after trading Micah Parsons last season, is still in search for another top edge rusher to help a Cowboys defense that desperately needs it. With a team that should conceivably be winning now, owner and desirer of splash moves in Cowboys owner Jerry Jones isn't afraid to pull the trigger on a move that could help solve some issues.
The Cowboys are also familiar with Sweat, spending years game-planning for him when he was a member of the Philadelphia Eagles before Sweat joined Arizona last season. After the Cardinals fired head coach Jonathan Gannon in January — who played a big role in helping land Sweat — things began to crumble.
Sweat didn't participate in any bit of OTAs, minicamp, training camp or preseason but has been active for every Cardinals regular season game. Through six games, Sweat has tallied 14 tackles and two sacks.
Arizona has been consistent in their public messaging of not trading Sweat, who also is looking for a new contract. He's in the second of a four-year, $76 million deal that features no guaranteed money in the final two seasons (2027 and 2028).
Rumors around the desert are the Cardinals will part from Sweat for a second-round pick, which was a similar compensation they got for Harrison. However, Sweat is 29 and has obvious injury concerns with his knee.
While Sweat could very well be traded next offseason, his value around the deadline will never be higher — especially if he continues improving on a weekly basis like his form suggests.
And for what it's worth, the Cowboys do host the Cardinals in Week 8.

title: Cardinals-Broncos Inactives: Budda Baker, Pat Surtain II Final Status Revealed
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals and Denver Broncos got drastically different injury news Sunday morning ahead of their Week 7 clash at State Farm Stadium.
The Cardinals officially have star safety Budda Baker active today after he entered the weekend questionable with illness and a groin injury. Baker missed two days of practice but secures an Arizona backend that's already missing Andrew Wingard.
The Broncos, meanwhile, officially do not have star cornerback Patrick Surtain II, as he's out with an ankle injury that will keep him sidelined for a third consecutive game.
Full inactives for both sides:
Melton is ruled out after being questionable while Darius Robinson is good to go.
The Cardinals elevated offensive lineman Kingsley Eguakun and defensive lineman Jared Harrison-Hunte on Saturday among a flurry of roster moves, which you can read more about here .
Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur on Robinson, who is having his best year to date:
“You guys obviously see it Sunday. I see it every day since I’ve been here. He’s a pleasure to work with too. He is made of all the right stuff in terms of what you want in a worker and a person. I don’t think he puts any unneeded stress or anything on himself. He just shows up to work and tries to get better. He’s an extremely coachable dude," he said.
"You can just tell by his teammates’ response in terms of how well he’s played of what he means to them. Because again, I think everyone’s just looking for intentions and his intentions are right. He just wants to do right. He just wants to play as hard as he can. I’m happy for the start he’s had and I still think he’s got a long way to go — in a good way.”
The Broncos activated running back Jonah Coleman and outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper to the 53-man roster this weekend. Denver also elevated safety Taylor Rapp and defensive back Sean Fresch Jr. from the practice squad ahead of their clash in the desert.
If you haven't heard, the Cardinals are inducting Larry Fitzgerald into their Ring of Honor this weekend. Broncos head coach Sean Payton had great things to say when asked about Fitzgerald earlier this week:
“He was amazing. Fortunately I was able to spend some time with him at the [Pro Football] Hall of Fame. There are so many things that he represented that are right. So consistent, competitive," he said of Fitzgerald.
"It was an amazing statistic, I never knew they kept track of it. He had more tackles—maybe that’s not a good stat—but he had more tackles than dropped passes. He was smart, tough, reliable. He knew then that he was going to be at this game and gave me a hard time about it. Tremendous player. Really, really good.”
Kickoff is at 1:05 PM MST in State Farm Stadium.

title: Cardinals vs Broncos: How to Watch, Listen, TV Map, Uniform Matchup
full_text:
Who : Denver Broncos at Arizona Cardinals What : NFL Regular Season, Week 7 When : Sunday, Oct. 25 at 1:05 PM MST Where : State Farm Stadium, Glendale, AZ
The Arizona Cardinals are set to induct Larry Fitzgerald at halftime of their Week 7 matchup against the Denver Broncos, though Sean Payton and co. have plans of playing spoiler to a special day in Glendale.
The Broncos, despite being 4-2, are very much hoping to get themselves back on track with a road win against the Cardinals.
Between Payton's long interview with Arizona before ditching them for Denver years ago, former Cardinals defensive coordinator Vance Joseph running one of the league's best units in Denver and defensive end Zach Allen emerging into one of the league's better players, Arizona faithful will see quite a few familiar faces today.

The Spanish call (Latino Mix 100.3 FM KQMR) features Jesus Quinonez (play-by-play) and Irving Villanueva (analyst).

Arizona Attire ⚪️ pic.twitter.com/KEFER0R8G1
Larry Fitzgerald on entering the Cardinals' Ring of Honor:
“I've told people this would probably be a lot more emotional for me because it's home. It's where I live. It's with the people that I grew up with. The Hall of Fame is league wide. It's a lot of people that are in Canton. There are Saints fans, there are Carolina Panthers fans. Everybody's there because it's a testament to what professional football is. It's not a Cardinals representation. I mean, there is Cardinal representation there, but it's not solely a Cardinals experience. This will be a solely Cardinals experience, which is authentic to my experience as a Cardinal only.
"That's why it will mean so much to be out there and to be there. I start thinking about other things. Mr. Bidwill (Former Owner William Bidwill); his number was retired. I was here when (Former Cardinals S) Pat Tillman's number was put up, (Former Cardinals DB) Adrian Wilson, (Former Cardinals QB) Carson Palmer, (Former Cardinals CB and Pro Football Hall of Famer) Roger Wehrli, (Former Cardinals CB and Pro Football Hall of Famer) Aeneas Williams, (Former Cardinals WR) Roy Green. I was in the building playing in a uniform when all of these people were going up.
"To now be able to experience it, it's surreal. So many great memories flood into my mind.”

title: Cardinals About to Get Hit With Broncos 'Old-School' Defense
full_text:
For Denver Broncos fans, their defense has been a blast from the past. For the Arizona Cardinals, it will be anything but a blast going against Vance Joseph's unit on Sunday.
Week 7 features a Cardinals-Broncos matchup at State Farm Stadium that figures to be a low-scoring affair, as they're only one of five games with an over/under line set under 44 points.
That's partly due to struggling offenses, but also due to a Denver defense that ranks as one of the best in the league.
And while they're not quite their famous "Orange Crush" defense or their dominant 2015 unit that won a Super Bowl, Denver's defense is doing things in an old-school fashion.
“They’re very smart. They’re very well coached. I have as much respect for ‘VJ’ (Broncos Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph) as anyone in this league. They do it their own way. I don’t want to say they’re not with the times — whatever that means but it’s got an old-school approach to it in terms of some of their coverage and that’s a credit to them," said Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur.
"You can tell ‘VJ’ and those guys believe in what they believe in and they’re unapologetic with it. They play really hard. I see 11 guys working in unison. It’s a challenge. Yes, it’s the last two weeks, but it’s really been all year, and it’s been for a few years now. We have our hands full with this group, for sure.”
The Broncos are allowing just 20.8 points per game and are tied for the league's second-most takeaways at ten.
"Oh yeah, no doubt. No, it's how they play their football from the front structures to the back end," Cardinals offensive coordinator Nathaniel Hackett said when asked if Denver's defense was truly old-school.
"Everything. It's funny the league has changed so much to a certain extent from how they play the back end, and it's evolved, and we've evolved on things. I mean, in the past couple years there were certain routes you could never even consider hitting, and now you can hit those. But now you face this team, and you can't hit those, so it's an adjustment. Every week has great challenges, and this defense is — I feel like I'm a broken record. I've said it every week — but the reality is we've gone against some really good defenses, and this is one of them."
The Broncos feature two former Cardinals (DC Vance Joseph, DL Zach Allen) among other pieces in a vastly talented Denver defense. In a league that primarily utilizes zone coverage, the Broncos are one of eight teams who use man coverage at a 22% or higher clip.
More interestingly, their usage rates of specific Cover 2 man looks are tied for the second-most in the league. If that coverage sounds familiar, it was the play that baited Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold into an interception late in Denver's win on Thursday Night Football in Week 6.
BRONCOS INTERCEPT SAM DARNOLD WITH 1:25 LEFT IN THE GAME SEAvsDEN on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/7vK2rjBe1k
Only 13 teams run Cover 1 at similar or higher rates than Joseph. When they do run zone, they primarily use Cover 3 — which is standard for NFL defenses.
The Broncos blitz at a top ten rate in the league and have a stacked box rate (8+ defenders) of 31.1%, which is fourth in the league.
"I don't care what scheme you run on defense, as long as you have conviction in it, which they do," LaFleur continued. "There's clarity with the players, which they do. You have good players that matches the scheme that they're trying to run, which they do. ... But as we know, this defense has been playing really well for a few years, and it's going to be a challenge not only because of the scheme, but because of the players that are actually running the scheme."
Modern NFL defenses mostly adopt a "bend but don't break" rule where they'll always opt to play conservatively. The Broncos' defense, rather than sitting back, brings the pressure to opposing offenses on a weekly basis thanks to a strong mix of personnel and scheme.
LaFleur's a new head coach — but we're about to see how he handles a defense from the past.

title: Cardinals' Pivotal Broncos Test Just Might Change Their Season
full_text:
When the Arizona Cardinals' 2026 schedule came out, inducting legendary wide receiver Larry Fitzgerald into the Ring of Honor seemed to be the only weight carrying their Week 7 matchup against the Denver Broncos.
With the Broncos one game away from the Super Bowl last season and the Cardinals winning only three games, many figured Denver would destroy Arizona. While that could still happen, the way that this NFL season has gone, this game suddenly carries a lot more weight for the Cardinals.
So far, the Cardinals' two wins this season have both been against the NFL's two Los Angeles teams — the Rams and Chargers. While both have their fair share of talented players, they've combined for only two wins this season, as the Rams are 2-4 and the Chargers are 0-6.
The Broncos head into Week 7 with an impressive 4-2 record. If the Cardinals were to down the Broncos, they would join the Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers as the only teams to beat Denver so far. The Chiefs and 49ers are both undefeated, so it would be an impressive club for the Cards to join.
The Cardinals' last two regular season games against the Broncos have been absolutely dreadful. In 2022, Denver won 24-15 in a game where Arizona's offense was terrible. Former Cardinals quarterback Trace McSorley and Colt McCoy threw three interceptions, scored no touchdowns, and managed only 167 passing yards.
Running back James Conner scored the Cardinals' lone touchdown of the day. However, the Cardinals' running game averaged a very measly 3.7 yards per carry. It was a very poor game; however, the Cardinals' 2018 performance against the Broncos is one of the worst in the past ten years of Cardinals football.
In this game, Denver won 45 to 10 in an absolute thrashing. Former Cardinals quarterback Josh Rosen threw three interceptions, including two pick-sixes. The Cardinals defense also played poorly.
Mike LaFleur and his crew clearly have a shot at redemption this Sunday.
Even though the Cardinals beat the Rams last week, it was due to the defense and special teams, not the offense. Brissett had a pretty poor game, throwing one interception and only 218 passing yards. Brissett's last two weeks against the Rams and Lions have been tough outings.
I rate Brissett higher than most, but two bad games in a row, and possibly a third against a tough Broncos defense, could signal it's time to go with rookie Carson Beck or veteran Gardner Minshew. Especially Minshew, who has shown some good flashes in his NFL career that dates back to 2019
While the Cardinals are in a rebuilding phase, they have a fair amount of offensive talent in tight end Trey McBride, wide receiver Michael Wilson, and running back Jeremiyah Love. However, with Brissett at quarterback, he hasn't made the most of those weapons.
Before he became the Broncos' head coach in ahead 2023, Sean Payton was in the Cardinals' facility for a day-long interview. From 2006 to 2021, Payton built an impressive resume as the New Orleans Saints' head coach, leading them to a Super Bowl win in 2009 and many great offensive seasons.
However, the Cardinals didn't land Payton, and many fans weren't too happy about it, since it seemed likely he could come to Arizona. Payton has done an incredible job with the Broncos so far, leading them to the playoffs twice in three seasons, including an AFC Championship Game appearance last year.
Instead of Payton, the Cardinals went with Jonathan Gannon, who lasted only three seasons before being fired. The Cardinals then hired Mike LaFleur this past offseason, who has had a solid start as the team's head coach. However, LaFleur has struggled with inconsistent play-calling so far.
A win over Payton would be a huge win for Arizona's front office. If Payton destroys the Cardinals, it would be just another reminder than the Cardinals missed out on something special.
Overall, a victory would be huge for Arizona. It would be two wins in a row and could be a great turning point for an organization that desperately needs it.

title: Falcons Defense Sends Clear Message After Beating Undefeated 49ers
full_text:
ATLANTA – The word “identity” swirled around the Atlanta Falcons ’ locker room on Sunday evening. Winless at home this season and, more often than not, outnumbered in their own stands, the Falcons' defense knew the assignment started with them.
“Identity is a good word,” head coach Kevin Stefanski said. “You can talk about it until you're blue in the face, and you can put it on a T-shirt, but we gotta go do it. We gotta go be who we say we are, and I thought today we did that.”
They were tasked with slowing down an undefeated San Francisco 49ers team that, despite a depleted wide receiver room, was loaded with stars. Christian McCaffrey, Brock Purdy, George Kittle, and an overpowering offensive line are more than enough for Kyle Shanahan's wizardry. His unit was third in scoring offense (29.5) and second in EPA/play (+0.16).
“That’s a great offense, great coaches, and a quarterback and team playing as well as anybody in this league,” Stefanski said about the 49ers. “So, you’re not going to shut them out. We understood it was going to be a 60-minute game.”
After the first three possessions, it looked like the Falcons would be just another team the 49ers checked off en route to a playoff run. They raced to a 14-3 lead and piled up 150 yards, with Christian McCaffrey nearly hitting 100 yards on his own.
San Francisco was in full control.
The Falcons’ defensive identity had wavered in recent weeks. Against the 49ers, it held.
“We didn't have the first half that we would like,” defensive lineman Gervon Dexter Sr. said. “To come out and make those adjustments and do some of those things and fix some of those things and come out, that takes a detailed team.”
Atlanta never fully shut down the 49ers, but they punished them for every mistake. San Francisco outgained Atlanta by 105 yards, but the Falcons forced four turnovers, including on both of their final two possessions, plus another turnover on downs. They sacked Purdy twice, defended seven passes, and finished with six tackles for loss.
The Falcons’ defense gave the 49ers everything they could handle.
“We want to get off the field early enough, so we're going to be able to make the big plays, the game-changing plays,” Maason Smith said. “We want to continue on that road throughout the rest of the season.”
And after running for 105 yards in the first half, San Francisco managed just 18 rushing yards in the second. A hampered McCaffrey played a role, but so did this Atlanta defense's mentality.
“They're a team that prides themselves on running the ball, and everything we do is centered around stopping the run,” linebacker Josh Woods said. “They got some leaky yards, whatever. They had some good runs. But it was definitely an identity game. It was a heavyweight fight.”
The Falcons had plenty of heroes, including safety Jessie Bates III and rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels , but this was a total team win for this defense. Woods believes this group earned some of that respect on Sunday.
Now, the challenge is doing that again.
“It’s an identity game every week,” cornerback A.J. Terrell Jr. said, “and just being able to go out and do what we practice all week, and just going out there trying to prove us right. Prove we are who we are. So, every week is an identity game.”

title: Falcons Rookie Goes From Scary Injury to Game-Sealing Hero in One Week
full_text:
ATLANTA – Seven days ago, Kendal Daniels was rushed to Grady Hospital following a scary injury at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. On Sunday, the rookie linebacker sealed the Atlanta Falcons ’ Week 7 win over the San Francisco 49ers with an interception and fumble recovery.
Daniels spent nearly 10 minutes on the turf as medical staff tended to him after he took a knee on the helmet. That personnel ultimately immobilized him and carted him off the field. In the hours following the game, media members saw him walking in the locker room, and there was a sense of relief.
What came next is still hard to believe.
He not only recovered, but did so in time to suit up and play against the previously undefeated 49ers. He filled in for Divine Deablo, wore the green dot, led the Falcons in tackles, and recorded two takeaways.
Head coach Kevin Stefanski called it remarkable, and the player called it the craziest week of his life.
“I've never not walked off the field after an injury,” Daniels said after the game. “Mentally, I had to be prepared and going back home and just making sure I was okay mentally more than anything, and not playing timid. I've never not gotten up from an injury. So, being stretched off the field ­– I won't let it happen again. It was a bad feeling, and I'm blessed to be able to play this week.”
Daniels avoided a major injury last week, but he couldn't move his neck in the days after the game. By Wednesday, he was practicing and feeling better each day.
“He’s a dog,” defensive lineman Gervon Dexter Sr. said. “Not a lot of players will go out there and play after something like that happened. He did, and he got all our respect in this building.”
Linebacker Josh Woods spoke with Daniels on Sunday after the “scary” injury, but never doubted that he would be down for long.
“He’s got whatever ‘it’ is,” Woods said. “Everything that he does is pretty dope. Then, for last week to go how it went, and then for him to have the game that he had today, it's a testament to his preparation. He's kind of got that ‘X-factor’, that ‘it’-thing about him.”
That ‘it factor’ showed in the waning minutes on Sunday.
Daniels’ interception snuffed out a 49ers possession that started at midfield and could have put San Francisco in front. The Falcons had just gone three-and-out, and it felt like momentum had flipped entirely in the away team's favor.
Instead, the rookie stepped in front of a Brock Purdy pass and returned it to the Falcons’ red zone. Nick Folk converted the field goal, making it a two-score game.
He recovered a fumble on the next drive, and that officially ended it.
“He put his head down and goes to work every day,” Maason Smith said. “He understands that nothing is given. Everything is earned. When you have size and speed like him, with a mind like his, and you combine both of those things together. Man, there's nothing but excellence waiting to happen.”

title: Winners and Losers from Falcons' 29-20 Win Over 49ers
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons upset the San Francisco 49ers 29-20 in Sunday's Week 7 matchup.
It's the biggest win of the season for a Falcons team coming off a loss to the Bears last week, and it’s now their first home win of the season.
Here are the winners and losers from Atlanta's victory at Mercedes-Benz Stadium.
Penix delivered an efficient performance against San Francisco, completing 25 of 34 passes for 213 yards and three touchdowns without throwing an interception. The Falcons quarterback consistently made the most of his opportunities, helping Atlanta score enough points to secure a nine-point victory.
Penix's three touchdown passes were the highlight of his afternoon. He connected with Drake London, Kyle Pitts, and Nick Muse for scores, spreading the ball around and keeping the 49ers' defense from focusing on one primary target.
Atlanta's passing attack was particularly effective in the red zone, where the Falcons capitalized on their opportunities. Penix also demonstrated improved decision-making by protecting the football and avoiding costly mistakes.
The Falcons managed just 25 yards of offense in the first quarter, making their eventual offensive production even more impressive. Penix helped Atlanta overcome that sluggish start and finish with a winning performance against one of the NFC's top teams.
Smith was one of Atlanta's biggest defensive difference makers, recording a sack, forcing a fumble, batting down a pass, finishing with two tackles for loss and adding a quarterback hit.
His performance demonstrated the impact he can make when he consistently disrupts opposing offenses. Smith affected San Francisco's passing game with his pressure while also making plays behind the line of scrimmage.
The forced fumble was an especially important moment in a game where Atlanta needed its defense to deliver timely stops.
Smith's performance was one of the most encouraging individual developments from Sunday's victory. Atlanta will need that type of production from its defensive line as it moves forward through the season.
Daniels had a memorable afternoon after entering the week with questions surrounding his availability following last week's injury concerns.
The rookie linebacker made his presence felt in Atlanta's 29-20 win, recording three tackles and one assist while contributing to a defense that made several crucial plays.
Daniels also recovered a late fumble to help the Falcons close out the victory. Jessie Bates III punched the ball out, and Daniels was in position to secure the recovery, giving Atlanta possession at a critical point in the fourth quarter.
BOOM! @KendalDaniels__ picks it off! FOX | NFL+ pic.twitter.com/7VBExpgNMh
After uncertainty about whether he would be able to play, Daniels' return was an encouraging development. Not only was he back on the field, but he also made an important contribution to a win over a talented opponent.
For a young defender, being available after an injury scare and making a decisive play in a game of this magnitude is a significant moment. Daniels deserves credit for getting back on the field and helping Atlanta finish the job.
Jessie Bates just always seems to be around the football. Bates came through with one of the game's biggest defensive plays, intercepting Brock Purdy in the red zone to prevent San Francisco from capitalizing on a scoring opportunity.
The veteran interception was a momentum-changing play, particularly because it denied the 49ers a chance to add points in a close contest. Bates displayed excellent awareness and positioning to make the takeaway when Atlanta needed a stop.
JB3 in his own league 🔥 FOX | NFL+ pic.twitter.com/1mdXYHdXKY
He also helped seal the victory late in the fourth quarter by punching the ball out and creating the fumble that Daniels recovered.
Bates showed why having an experienced playmaker in the secondary is so valuable. His interception helped prevent San Francisco from scoring, while his forced fumble helped Atlanta regain possession and protect its lead.
In a game where the Falcons needed their defense to make plays at critical moments, Bates delivered twice.
National Tight Ends Day turned into a productive occasion for Atlanta's tight end group, which contributed two touchdown receptions and an important career milestone.
Pitts led the way with five receptions for 22 yards and a touchdown. His scoring reception was one of Penix's three touchdown passes, and Pitts also reached 300 career receptions during the game.
Austin Hooper added two receptions for 21 yards, while Charlie Woerner caught one pass for nine yards. Nick Muse finished with two receptions for two yards and a touchdown, providing another scoring option for Atlanta.
Our MUSE on National Tight End's Day! FOX | NFL+ pic.twitter.com/UQNMR1Pvrb
Muse's touchdown was particularly valuable because it demonstrated the Falcons' ability to find production beyond their established offensive playmakers. Pitts also delivered in the red zone, helping Atlanta turn a passing opportunity into points.
The group provided Penix with reliable targets throughout the game, and having multiple tight ends contribute helped diversify the offense.
Pitts reaching 300 career receptions was a notable individual accomplishment, but the entire group deserves recognition for helping Atlanta secure the victory.
Atlanta's kickoff return unit provided an important boost in field position, with Zachariah Branch and Khalil Herbert combining for 126 return yards.
Branch delivered a 60-yard return, while Herbert added a 38-yard return to open the second half. Both plays gave the Falcons opportunities to start drives with favorable field position and helped generate momentum.
Explosive returns can have a significant impact in close games, especially when an offense is working to establish consistency. Atlanta's return unit helped ease some of that pressure by creating opportunities for Penix and the offense.
Herbert's return to begin the second half was particularly important because it gave Atlanta a strong start coming out of the locker room.
The Falcons received a boost from their special teams, and the return unit deserves recognition for helping the team control field position in a nine-point victory.
The Falcons’ offensive line took a lot of criticism after last week’s loss to the Bears. On Sunday, not only did they not give up a sack, but the 49ers weren’t credited with even a hit on Penix.
Atlanta's opening quarter was far from ideal, as the Falcons managed just 25 yards of total offense and punted on both of their first two drives.
Against a San Francisco team that entered the matchup undefeated, the slow start put unnecessary pressure on the defense and prevented Atlanta from establishing an early rhythm.
The Falcons struggled to sustain drives, leaving little room for error against a dangerous opponent. Although Penix eventually settled in and threw three touchdown passes, the opening quarter demonstrated how quickly the offense can stall when it cannot consistently move the chains.
Atlanta deserves credit for adjusting and finding ways to score, but a 25 yard opening quarter is not a formula the team should want to repeat. Against other playoff contenders, a similarly sluggish start could prove much more costly.
The Falcons got the result they wanted, but the early offensive struggles remain an area to address moving forward.
Atlanta's run defense had some difficult moments against San Francisco's ground attack, allowing 123 rushing yards on 23 carries. That amounted to approximately 5.3 yards per attempt, giving the 49ers opportunities to move the chains on the ground.
Kaelon Black led San Francisco with 63 rushing yards on 12 carries, including a 30-yard run and a touchdown. Christian McCaffrey added 39 yards on seven attempts and another rushing touchdown.

title: 7 Bite-Sized Takeaways as Atlanta Falcons Hand 49ers First Loss 29-20
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons continued their roller coaster season with a XX-XX upset win over the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday. After arguably their worst performance of the season last week against the Chicago Bears, the Falcons got one of their best against the 49ers.
Last week, rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels suffered a scare when he experienced neck pain after a hit. He was stretchered off, but walked back into the locker room after the game.
He used his 6'5 frame to get a crucial interception to snatch back momentum from the 49ers in the fourth quarter.  Then he recovered a George Kittle fumble with a minute left in the game for the final dagger.
From worrying about his future to making arguably the biggest play of his football career, what a difference a week makes.
BOOM! @KendalDaniels__ picks it off! FOX | NFL+ pic.twitter.com/7VBExpgNMh
The Falcons got off to another slow start against the 49ers, falling behind 14-3 before reeling off 16 straight points to take the lead. The defense stepped up with McCaffrey missing some time with a leg injury, and they got a pair of key turnovers.
Penix heated up, pushing the ball to eight different targets in the first half.
How did the Chicago Bears limit Bijan Robinson? They kept the ball for 40 minutes. The Falcons learned from that last week. While the Falcons were scoring 23 unanswered points, they ran 36 plays to 6 at one point.
Box score scouts and fantasy football owners aren't going to be impressed with Falcons' wide receiver Jahan Dotson's numbers. He had just one catch for six yards. But he also induced two key penalties on third down to extend a Falcons drive at the end of the third quarter. The big one was a 20-yard pass interference that put the Falcons in field goal range.
Turnovers: 49ers 4, Falcons 0
Penix looked a little antsy to start. Then he settled in and started dealing. He threw three touchdowns last week against the Bears, but some of that could be attributed to garbage time. No such case on Sunday against the 49ers.
He had three touchdown passes again this week, including a nice touch pass to tight end Nick Muse. Maybe one of the biggest growth points for Penix is the ability to flush a bad play. He missed a wide-open Drake London on a deep shot, but instead of letting it affect him, he followed it with one of his best passes of the day, a 21-yard seam to London.
Cookin' with the SAUCE 🔥 @DrakeLondon_ FOX | NFL+ pic.twitter.com/ljV4yxVwac
The Falcons kept Penix protected, and Penix rewarded them. The 49ers didn't have a sack or even a QB hit credited to them.
The Falcons ran a direct snap for tight end Charlie Woerner. They threw a play-action touchdown pass to Nick Muse. Austin Hooper had a catch for 10 yards in the first half. They were slower getting Kyle Pitts Sr. involved, with just two targets for six yards, both receptions coming in the last three minutes.
Someone got in Tommy Rees' ear at halftime, because Pitts had three catches, including a touchdown on the Falcons' opening drive of the second half. Four tight ends were active, and all four had catches.
HAPPY NATIONAL TIGHT ENDS DAY KP! FOX | NFL+ pic.twitter.com/CwdtcwKPHk
James Pearce Jr.'s eight-game suspension ends after next week's game in Tampa. The Falcons miss his speed. The defensive front for the Falcons is excellent at getting penetration and collapsing the pocket, but they're not fast enough to catch mobile quarterbacks who escape the initial pressure.
49ers quarterback Brock Purdy isn't nearly as comfortable in a two-minute offense if Pearce is pinning his ears back and coming off the edge.
Atlanta has this terrible habit of following a terrific performance with a stinker. They go on the road next week to face a suddenly resurgent Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The Bucs got Baker Mayfield back and blew the doors off the Panthers in Charlotte.
At 3-4, the Falcons are in a good spot, but they have to start showing some consistency.

title: Kyle Pitts Sr Has a Chance to Make National Tight Ends Day Special for Falcons
full_text:
Sunday's National Tight Ends Day gives Atlanta Falcons tight end Kyle Pitts Sr. another opportunity to make an impact, and offensive coordinator Tommy Rees believes the talented pass catcher can play a major role in the team's success.
Pitts has delivered several memorable performances on National Tight Ends Day throughout his career, including a two-touchdown outing against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2024.
With Atlanta looking to maximize its offensive potential, offensive coordinator Tommy Rees thinks he knows how to unlock more production.
“I think he’s at his best when he has the ball in his hand in open space,” Rees said. “Kyle’s shown that throughout his entire career. He certainly has shown that over the last few weeks.”
Rees also discussed creating opportunities for the tight end to use his athleticism after the catch.
“Again, it’s our job to put him in position to have those plays,” Rees said.
Pitts has a history of producing on National Tight Ends Day, providing an encouraging storyline heading into Sunday's game.
Across five National Tight Ends Day games from 2021 through 2025, Pitts has recorded 26 receptions for 369 yards and two touchdowns, averaging 5.2 catches and 73.8 receiving yards per game.
His most productive performance came in 2021 against the Miami Dolphins, when he caught seven passes for 163 yards. In 2024, Pitts delivered another standout performance against the Buccaneers, catching four passes for 91 yards and two touchdowns.
Pitts also caught nine passes for 59 yards against Miami in 2025, setting a career high for receptions across his five appearances. His other performances included three catches for nine yards against the Cincinnati Bengals in 2022 and three receptions for 47 yards against Tampa Bay in 2023.
Although his production has varied, Pitts has demonstrated the ability to deliver impactful performances on occasion. His challenge now is helping Atlanta establish a more consistent passing attack.
Rees acknowledged the frustration surrounding Atlanta's recent performance but expressed appreciation for Pitts' work and patience as the team looks to get him more involved.
“There wasn’t a lot of happiness on Sunday, to be completely honest,” Rees said. “I’m happy for Kyle because of the work he’s put in, the patience he’s had, to get him going.”
Rees' comments reflect the importance of establishing Pitts as a consistent contributor rather than relying on occasional flashes of production.
Rees made the expectation clear when discussing what the Falcons need to accomplish offensively.
“For us to reach our full potential, he’s got to be a big part of that,” Rees said.
For Rees and the Falcons, the priority is ensuring Pitts remains a consistent part of the offense, beginning Sunday against the 49ers... on National Tight Ends Day.

title: 3 Crucial Keys for Falcons to Beat 6-0 49ers in Week 7
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons face a major test Sunday when they welcome the undefeated San Francisco 49ers to Mercedes-Benz Stadium. At 2-4, Atlanta needs a statement victory against a 6-0 San Francisco team that has established itself as one of the NFL’s most complete squads.
The 49ers enter the matchup averaging 29.5 points and 366.7 total yards per game, while allowing just 18.3 points and 300 yards per contest. The Falcons have the offensive talent to challenge San Francisco, but they will need to execute in three critical areas to pull off the upset.
Atlanta’s best opportunity to control the game begins with Bijan Robinson. The Falcons rank fourth in the NFL with 149.5 rushing yards per game and average an impressive 5.1 yards per carry. Robinson has been a major part of that success, recording 641 rushing yards on 111 carries through six games, averaging 5.8 yards per attempt.
However, San Francisco presents a difficult challenge. The 49ers allow just 90.2 rushing yards per game, ranking eighth in the NFL.
Atlanta must find ways to get Robinson into space, utilize outside runs and involve him as a receiver. Sustaining the ground attack would help keep Brock Purdy and the San Francisco offense on the sideline while creating more manageable situations for quarterback Michael Penix Jr.
The Falcons’ defense must find a way to slow down an offense averaging 29.5 points per game. San Francisco averages 238.5 passing yards per contest, and they are the league's best in EPA, according to Sumer Sports .
Atlanta’s biggest weakness has been defending the pass. The Falcons surrender 252 passing yards per game, ranking 28th in the NFL. That makes Sunday’s matchup particularly concerning against a 49ers offense capable of exploiting coverage breakdowns. Atlanta may have caught a break with the 49ers missing their top two receivers , Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel, but Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle still present a big challenge underneath.
Getting pressure on Purdy without consistently committing extra defenders will be crucial. Atlanta needs its defensive line to win individual matchups, force hurried throws, and prevent Purdy from comfortably working through his progressions. The secondary must also limit yards after the catch and avoid giving up explosive plays.
Atlanta cannot afford to give an undefeated opponent extra possessions. Turnovers have been a concern for the Falcons, who average two giveaways per game, making ball security a significant factor heading into Week 7.  At -7, the Falcons are 31st in the NFL in turnover differential.
San Francisco’s defense allows only 18.3 points per game and limits opponents to 300 total yards per contest. The Falcons will need to turn productive drives into touchdowns rather than settling for field goals or coming away empty-handed.
Penix must make smart decisions, protect the ball, and take advantage of opportunities when San Francisco’s defense leaves openings. Atlanta also needs to improve its execution on third downs to sustain drives and keep its defense rested.
The Falcons have the rushing production to challenge San Francisco, but beating the 49ers will require more than moving the ball between the 20-yard lines. If Atlanta controls the clock, pressures Purdy and wins the turnover battle, it will give itself a legitimate chance to deliver a much-needed home victory.

San Francisco’s offensive weapons could prove too much for Atlanta’s defense, leading to another disappointing home result for the Falcons.
Prediction : 49ers 28, Falcons 17
At first glance, the betting line makes this matchup appear favorable for Atlanta. A 6-0 San Francisco team might be expected to be a bigger favorite, but the 49ers’ extensive injury concerns could be keeping the matchup closer than anticipated.
The Falcons have enough talent to beat any team when they put everything together. The problem is finding that consistency against quality opponents. Atlanta must figure out how to handle opposing pressure, or the 49ers could overwhelm Penix with aggressive blitz packages.
San Francisco is vulnerable because of its injuries, giving Atlanta a puncher’s chance. However, until the Falcons prove they can consistently perform against strong competition, picking them to pull off an upset remains difficult.
Prediction :  49ers 31, Falcons 23
After Bears fans took over Mercedes-Benz Stadium last week, I expect another takeover from 49ers fans on Sunday. Atlanta should deliver a much better performance, but I still have concerns about whether the offense can do enough to secure a victory.
San Francisco’s injuries will have an impact, but Brock Purdy and Christian McCaffrey will ultimately be too much for Atlanta’s defense. Meanwhile, the 49ers’ pass rush could make life difficult for Penix, particularly if the Falcons struggle to protect their young quarterback.
I expect Atlanta to keep the game competitive and give its home crowd something to cheer about. However, until the Falcons demonstrate they can finish against a quality opponent, I cannot pick them to get over the hump.
San Francisco escapes with a narrow victory, leaving Atlanta with another frustrating home loss.
Prediction : 49ers 28, Falcons 24
The 49ers are currently the best team in football in my opinion which makes this a tough matchup for the Falcons.
This would be a lopsided matchup if the 49ers were healthy, but that’s not the case. The 49ers have been led by arguably the best passing attack in the league, but they’ll be without Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel . Stopping Georgie Kittle and McCaffrey will still be a tall order, however.
The Falcons offense matches up well against the 49ers defense on paper, especially given that Nick Bosa will be out. The key will be can the Falcons o-line deal with all of the twists and stunts that the 49ers will throw at them, and can they keep Fred Warner from taking over the game.
I have the 49ers winning, but I think the Falcons will keep it close.
Prediction: 49ers 27, Falcons 20
These are the kind of games the Falcons win. But after the last two weeks, it’s hard to pick them. This Atlanta team is still a work in progress, more than we assumed during the two-game winning streak, and the 49ers are a well-oiled machine. The skid continues.
Prediction: 49ers 37, Falcons 23

title: Why Bijan Robinson Is ‘Fired Up’ for Falcons’ Showdown With Undefeated 49ers
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons have a golden opportunity this Sunday.
They can end their two-game losing streak while earning a statement win over one of the NFL’s final three unbeaten teams, the San Francisco 49ers.
“That’s why you love this game,” said Falcons running back Bijan Robinson .
“They’re a very good team, and there’s the underdog story and everything. We’re really just focused on ourselves and what we need to do. But these are the games that you love to play for.”
The other two undefeated NFL teams are the Kansas City Chiefs and the Minnesota Vikings, squads that the Falcons will meet in the four games after facing the 49ers.
The Falcons entered the 2026 season with one of the hardest schedules across the league, and the coming weeks are unrelenting.
After a 0-2 start while in quarterback purgatory, the Falcons (2-4) strung together two consecutive wins, but then lost two straight. Atlanta’s last outing was a failed comeback loss to the Chicago Bears, 31-23, last Sunday, Oct. 18.
As for the 49ers (6-0), they defeated the Washington Commanders 23-17 on Oct. 19’s Monday Night Football on Oct. 19 to remain perfect on the season.
San Fran boasts the ninth-best total offense out of the NFL’s 32 teams, with quarterback Brock Purdy leading the way with his pocket presence and opportunistic running . Behind Purdy is one of the league’s top running backs, Christian McCaffrey, the 2025 NFL Comeback Player of the Year.
Their offense is second in total EPA and No. 1 in passing EPA, according to Sumer Sports. However, they're missing several key weapons .
Defensively, the 49ers are fifth in the NFL total defense. Former Falcons head coach Raheem Morris is the defense coordinator. Robinson said he and Morris spoke “a couple of weeks ago.”
Additionally, the Niners have star linebacker Fred Warner, whom Robinson deems “the best in the game.”
“It’s all the little things that are going to require us to win this game,” Robinson said. “This is a great opponent coming in. Just that alone, I’m fired up. I can’t wait. I’m juiced up, I know the other guys are too. It comes with the competitiveness that we have to bring. We have to come in here and make sure we’re on top of what we’re supposed to do to win this game.”
Falcons-49ers kickoff at 1 p.m. on Sunday at Atlanta’s Mercedes-Benz Stadium. FOX will televise the NFL Week 7 matchup.
The teams met a season ago, when San Francisco hosted and won the Sunday Night Football meeting 20-10 last October.

title: Falcons Make A.J. Terrell Decision, Plus Several Roster Moves
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons announced several roster moves Saturday ahead of their Week 7 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, including activating cornerback A.J. Terrell Jr. from injured reserve, signing defensive end Drake Jackson, and placing offensive tackle Michael Jerrell on injured reserve for a bicep injury.
Terrell has missed the last four weeks with a groin injury suffered in Week 2. The veteran cornerback practiced throughout the week after opening his 21-day return window Wednesday. With his activation to the active roster, Terrell will not carry an injury designation and is expected to play Sunday.
Atlanta also added Jackson to the active roster, adding depth to its defensive line ahead of a matchup against a San Francisco offense ranked No. 3 in scoring and No. 9 in total offense. Jackson gives the Falcons another option along the defensive front as they look to pressure the quarterback and slow down the 49ers' passing attack.
The Falcons placed Jerrell on injured reserve with a biceps injury, adding to an offensive line already dealing with personnel concerns. Atlanta also ruled out wide receiver Beaux Collins, who is recovering from a hip injury, and offensive tackle Cameron Williams, who has an ankle injury.
Meanwhile, Atlanta used standard practice squad elevations on running back Khalil Herbert and linebacker Brian Asamoah.
Herbert's elevation adds running back depth as the Falcons manage injuries after losing Brian Robinson Jr. to a hamstring ailment that will keep him out Sunday. Asamoah's elevation gives Atlanta another linebacker option as the team prepares for San Francisco without Divine Deablo.
Defensive back Avieon Terrell is also dealing with a back injury and an illness. His status remains questionable for Sunday's game, leaving the Falcons waiting for further clarity on his availability.
The roster adjustments come as Atlanta looks to improve on both sides of the ball against a difficult opponent. The Falcons rank 28th in the NFL in passing yards allowed, surrendering 252 yards per game, making the older Terrell's return particularly valuable for the secondary.
While Terrell's activation is the headline move, Atlanta will also rely on its newly available depth pieces to help navigate injuries and prepare for a critical Week 7 matchup. The Falcons will look to make the most of their roster changes when they host the 49ers on Sunday.

title: Raheem Morris Has a Message for Falcons Before Return to Atlanta
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are set for a Week 7 homecoming with former head coach Raheem Morris coming to Mercedes-Benz Stadium for the first time since the two parted ways in January.
Morris, who is now the defensive coordinator for the San Francisco 49ers, spent the last two seasons with the Falcons. While he ultimately missed the playoffs in both years, he laid the groundwork for this 2026 team’s makeup. His first year at the helm was marked by signing Kirk Cousins to a lucrative free-agent deal, then drafting Michael Penix Jr. with the eighth overall pick just a few months later.
That strategy didn't go as planned, and it marked an inauspicious start to two roller-coaster seasons in Atlanta before he was fired in January alongside general manager Terry Fontenot.
Some floated the idea that Morris could hold on for one more season after he rallied the Falcons to four straight (albeit meaningless) wins to end the year. Instead, he finished 16-18 overall, and Arthur Blank took the organization in a new direction.
The NFL is a business, and the 49ers will be looking to go about their business this Sunday, but could there be a little added motivation for San Francisco? Not likely, says 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan when he was asked this week about the defense’s desire to “win this game” for their defensive coordinator.
“I don’t think they can be more motivated,” Shanahan said. “I think our guys are as motivated as they can get each week. I don’t think they get too caught up in that stuff, but I know they care about Raheem a lot and definitely would want to do that for him, but I don’t think we’re looking at too much of a personal game like that.”
All-Pro linebacker Fred Warner echoed Shanahan's perspective, emphasizing that the 49ers approach every game with the same level of urgency.
“I feel like we treat every week as if it is the biggest week of our lives,” Warner said. “To play with even more emotion than what we play with already would be – I’m not even sure about what that would look like at this point, right? But every week has its own challenges. I’m sure Raheem wants this one in a big way because he was the former head coach there. We want it in the biggest way, as the 49ers, because this is the next one.”
The former Falcons head coach wasn't directly asked about his feelings on returning to Atlanta for the first time since being fired, but he said it is “helpful” to understand the makeup of the players in that locker room.
But in typical Morris fashion, he did pour out a lot of love for his former players.
“Love the kid, you know, love everything about him: the personality, who he was, the thrower,” Morris said about Penix. “He's back healthy, and he's everything that you thought and hoped for. As far as being a play-action passer, he can push the ball down the field and can make all the throws, and go through the whole process. He’s just one of those guys that I have a lot of appreciation for and love for.”
As for running back Bijan Robinson, whom he called “the best player in football” last season, the praise remained.
“I talked about Bijan last year – I talked about him being the best player in the NFL, and he certainly is, arguably, the best player in the National Football League,” Morris said. “He's special. He's one of those guys. He's as special a talent that we see in this league and can do everything.”
It appears to be business as usual for Morris and the 49ers. The former head coach may be on the opposite sideline Sunday, but his appreciation for the players he coached in Atlanta hasn't changed. Whether that familiarity gives San Francisco an edge remains to be seen.
Shanahan and Warner made it clear that the 49ers plan to approach this matchup the same way they do every other week. On Sunday, Morris will find out if that appreciation translates to a defensive game plan that can stop his former team.

title: Ravens Rookie Coach Jesse Minter Is Getting Exposed: Hiring Outside Help Could Save The Season
full_text:
Jesse Minter, the aspiring head coach, is undermining Jesse Minter, the proven defensive coordinator. Or perhaps, Jesse Minter, the esteemed defensive play caller, isn’t nearly skilled enough to overcome Jesse Minter, the guy who is still pretending to be an NFL head coach.
However you want to frame it, Minter is getting exposed in the second half of games in embarrassing fashion and general manager Eric DeCosta is getting unmasked for being fraudulent with another suspect roster and for hiring a staff full of novices who are collectively failing at a historic rate. Minter and his band of start-ups are blowing 10-point leads in a flurry that fired head coach John Harbaugh couldn’t ever touch their lack of cunning and expertise is eviscerating this team in the clutch. To call them overmatched right now would be complimentary.
Minter needs to do something about it, and do it now.
Maybe the Ravens players weren’t quitting as they allowed 35 unanswered points after leading, 13-0, at the half over the Bengals, but they damn sure weren’t trying their best either. They are making Minter look like a naïve joke; their lack of tackling and mental focus in the second half is not NFL caliber. It appears as if they are walking all over this staff, making them look silly for all the boastful talk about this roster all offseason long . It’s an ugly look.
“Not really good enough, starting with me,” was the joist of what we got from the rook coach, who was getting abused by garbage QBs so of course he got utterly punked as Joe Burrow for four touchdown passes and a perfect rating in the second half against his impotent pass rush and utterly predictable schemes. Mind you, Minter is handcuffed by another roster devoid of sufficient playmakers in their prime - a $19M corner who wouldn’t start for a real contender, a $20M linebacker whose been maybe $6M guy the last three years, and a $30M edge rusher who has yet to show up in the second half of a football game and whose former team, the Bengals, do not miss him one bit.
The season might be slipping away as Minter hinted ahead of a trip to Buffalo: “Right now, I think it's just a big point in the season for us to determine what type of team we want to be.” Unless this organization takes major corrective action to try to prop Minter up in a way that should have been emphasized when the staff was originally put together (a former head coach or two on this staff; Miami is the only staff without it), expect more of the same results.
They had best take one of the measures we suggest below, immediately. First, let’s first quantify the extent of Minter’s defensive failures.
Coaches are judged in no small degree based on how they adjust at halftime and how they change tendencies and tactics from week to week. Minter seems entirely lost in the second half as a coordinator despite having incredibly favorable game conditions on that side of the ball, and the pressure is breaking him; passing on chip-shot field goal to go up 16-14 with the game sliding away, instead having Snoop Huntley (with Lamar Jackson out three weeks with what Minter kept calling a “day-to-day injury ") try a fourth-down pass was telling.
Minter probably knew his garbage second-half defense was cooked anyway, but how about doing something about it instead of playing ridiculous amounts of dime coverage with inept defensive backs with zero ball skills? Sitting back in nickel/dime over 80% of the time, again, being scared to blitz (30%), again, isn’t working. Selling out to keep a shell on everything and giving up the fifth-most big plays in the second half doesn’t look very smart.
The Ravens have a +65 first-half scoring margin and a -70 in the second half – that appears to be a first in NFL history through seven games of a seasons. Coupled with the fact the Ravens have now DeCosta-ed 17 times since 2019 – blown a double-digit lead to lose  – and three times already this season including back-to-back weeks against division foes, Minter needs to show he is cut out for this soon if he doesn’t want this to be a lost season with the upcoming schedule.
They have allowed 114 points in the second half, most in the NFL, and the next-worst scoring differential is -51. Here are their second-half rankings:
Yards Per Play: 6.0 (29th) Passing Yards : 147 (29th) Yds/Att.: 8.0 (30th)
INT/Att .: 0.00% (T-last) First Downs : 12.3 (30th) 3rd Down: 44% (24th)
QB Rating: 117.0 (28th) Comp % : 81.3% (28th( TD-INT : 8-0 (32nd)
He is failing at both parts of his job, he is in a difficult position with a Machiavellian GM pulling his strings, but the idea he could put together a staff this short on proven NFL chops with his dad, Rick, as the sage shoulder for him to lean on was a joke.
There are many reasons why Minter’s best buddy Mike Macdonald hired Leslie Frazier for his staff, and it was a blight not to lean into this (longtime NFL head coach and coordinator Todd Haley explained on “The Daily Flock Show” ). And there’s a reason we have seen a slew of coordinator moves already this season, like the Cowboys bringing in Mike Pettine (remember him) or Texans coach DeMeco Ryans taking over defensive play calling or Sean Payton (mentor to Ravens OC Declan Doyle) doing the same in Denver.
More such moves are coming around the NFL, we can all remember when the Ravens brought back Chuck Pagano or Dean Pees or Jerry Rosburg to the fold to assist in some capacity. It worked better at some times than others, but this staff needs real help, right now.
Marvin Lewis might not want anything to do with being in an NFL building trying to bail out some kid who probably got hired too soon who should have been all over him in February to join his staff. He has seen it all and done it all and has oodles of AFC North head coaching and coordinating experience and saw this Ravens defensive lineage at its birth.
He knows Ozzie Newsome incredibly well and this front office is losing all touch with that era (check out Solomon Wilcots, who knows Newsome well, breaking it down here ). Lewis can take things off Minter’s plate and help him immeasurably. This is an ongoing defensive crisis and needs to be dealt with as such.
Wink Martindale has his faults, and he hasn’t been a head coach, but I got news for you, he knows firsthand what a fraud DeCosta is building defensive rosters and he would be a vital check on the front office. Minter better realize the same thing Martindale and Zach Orr and others around here did – all the money in the secondary and all the over-drafted corners with no ability to impact the ball in flight won’t win for you.
Few can dial up the blitz like Martindale, he has Harbaugh and Michigan ties like Minter and the Cowboys should have hired him and not Pettine. Having him help create man-coverage pressure looks that run counter to Minter’s pansy schemes is necessary; his zones were picked apart by bad QBs, and the real gauntlet has just begun.
