title: Ravens Allow 35 Unanswered Points To Bengals: Key Takeaways For A Team On The Brink
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens have been the NFL’s most pathetic chokers throughout Lamar Jackson’s tenure with the team, dating back to 2018.
Even by their lowly standards, giving up 35 unanswered points to the Bengals in the second half is a new low for general manager Eric DeCosta (ties worst in franchise history), the one constant in all those heartless losses that now span seven coordinators and two head coaches after Sunday’s epic meltdown.
DeCosta’s rosters have done it with regularity and reckless abandon many, many times with the two-time MVP on the field, and without him, it feels almost inevitable. Rookie head coach Jesse Minter – yet to prove he is remotely ready to run a sideline and call a defense at the same time – blew a double-digit lead for the fourth time in seven games, and lost doing so two weeks in a row; Minter is a master at this, doing it twice at home already this season and three times in 2026.
Minter’s feeble scheme and weak-minded players blew a 13-0 lead Sunday as Joe Burrow destroyed them like lesser QBs like Tyler Shough and Cam Ward have in the past. The Ravens now have lost 17 games with a double-digit lead since 2019, Minter has proven to be far more adroit and adept at it than anyone else, the fraud GM who builds these awful defenses year after year got platitudes from the owner when coach John Harbaugh was fired, and this 35-13 loss at M&T Bank Stadium is as ugly as any of them, even if it was Snoop Huntley at QB.
Imagine getting DeCosta-ed now at 17 times-and-running in this short a period of time and thinking swapping out a veteran staff for a bunch of rookies coaches who are younger and cheaper and way more malleable was going to fix Baltimore’s clear, systemic problems of which DeCosta and team president Sashi Brown are prevailing culprits. Oh well. Steve Bisciotti has been yammering about selling the team for years. Maybe they will finally get a real GM in charge then. Maybe DeCosta can hide the standings from his boss (John Harbaugh and Todd Monken look like they can coach after all).
The Ravens (4-3, last in AFC North) have won three times in their last 10 home games, they are remarkably devoid of anything approximating a true playmaker on defense, Minter’s scheme has been an utter failure in the second half and they face Josh Allen in Buffalo off a bye next week. Jackson returning might not be enough.
“Starting with me, just a bad effort by the defense in the second half,” Minter said.
The Ravens dominated the first half but didn’t have enough to show for it, stalling twice deep in Bengals’ territory and settling for field goals. They built a 13-0 lead into the half but settled for three after an 18-play, 78-yard march that took 11 minutes off the clock and stalled at the 16. And then went 13 plays and 82 yards on their next drive, taking six minutes off the clock and reaching the 6 before settling for three. Six offensive penalties in the first half – including four false starts and a delay of game – led to some of that stalling out.
It’s truly pathetic what must go on in the Ravens locker room during halftime with a big lead. They ceded momentum in the second half like they can’t wait to hand a game away. It’s staggering, really, but it’s their brand. Sunday they wasted no time swinging the tenor of the game after owning the Bengals in the first half and holding the ball for nearly 23 minutes.
How’s this sequence – Burrow carves them up in the underneath passing game for a TD drive to make it 13-7, Ravens offensive line gets swallowed up again on the next drive with a three-and-out that ends on a sack and then a huge return on the ensuing punt that forces the long-snapper to make a tackle.
And that was followed up by Baltimore’s secondary getting absolutely carved up – and no semblance of a pass rush – on Cincy’s second drive of the second half, this capping it with a TD pass to Tee Higgins to make it 14-13. Burrow was 9/10 for 100 yards and two TD passes on the first two drives of the second half.
Baltimore’s tackling was once against atrocious in the second half, even Kyle Hamilton fell prey to it several times including on a TD run (Marlon Humphrey, a $19M corner, made an even bigger a mockery of “tackling”’ the net drive), and this team will have to win shootouts when Jackson returns because the defense is just as fraudulent in 2026 as it was in 2025 and 2024.
Burrow was 16/18 with four TD passes and a perfect 158.3 rating in the second half. Joe Flacco got to play the final four minutes in this debacle.
"it was the tale of two halves," defensive lineman Calais Campbell said of what could be their motto.
"We have complete control over that mentality," Minter said, admitting he isn;t sure how to correct their mentality.
Minter has been fairly atrocious in the second half of games and seems to be suffering trying to run the team and call the defense at the same time. He also has become a big part of Baltimore’s choking tendencies and it’s in his head now, too, and he made a failed decision to open the fourth quarter that blew up in his face.
Minter opted to eschew a chip shot field goal to re-take the lead after having a full timeout at the end of the quarter to think about it. If he really thinks his defense is any good – and its one of the worst in the NFL in the second half – he grabs the lead.
Instead, they had the back-up attempt a pass on fourth and two and it fell woefully incomplete and never had a chance of working. And Burrow went right back to picking apart this secondary with short passes, and when he did have to step away from pressure he found Tee Higgins for 40 yards.
He entered this game with a bottom five second half defense in points per drive and points allowed and pressure rating and sacks, and hit new lows Sunday. He has made no adjustments and has no answers and his players with the Chargers were better than DeCosta’s bloated mess of a roster; his defenses there were never this bad.
Overpaying in a desperate trade for Cam Jurgens, while in concussion protocol no less, wasn’t likely to fix much overnight . And it didn’t. Baltimore could not operate the under-center rushing game, Derrick Henry remains an ineffective running back on the inside – like all season – but also now on the outside as linebackers sell out to take away outside zone and whack Henry behind the line of scrimmage before he gets going.
Henry ended up with 17 carries for 46 yards and an unthinkable 2.6 yards/carry average..  He once again was a non-factor on short-yardage plays and the return of Jackson may open up the run game some for sure, but Henry has been a blow-average back, at age 32 he needs major help from the line, and rookie guard-center-guard Vega Ioane was ruled out in the first half with a knee injury.
“I’m certainly concerned about that,” Minter said of the run game. “We've got to search for those better answers in how people are playing us.”
Look one guy can’t muster a pass rush all on his own, but when you give an oft-injured, older pass rusher who isn’t good against the run $30M a year to just rush the passer , dude needs to make some big plays. But DeCosta – a failure at quite a bit but especially pass rush and offensive line construction – doesn’t find those guys and Hendrickson’s revenge game was a dud.
Hendrickson is well removed from the hand procedure he underwent and he did get close to Burrow a time or two early in the game but Baltimore’s second-half defense has been a joke because the overrated corners and safeties never touch the football and their defensive front never gets home. Hendrickson was lauded as a ”closer” but hasn’t sniffed a QB in the fourth quarter in his Ravens career (Bengals have the NFL’s best fourth-quarter pressure rate without him) and Burrow cough laugh in this defensive line’s face the entire second half.
They couldn’t make him flinch. Hendrickson has two sacks all season and just two pressures in this game and the Ravens had an inept 22% pressure rate, which will get…

title: Four Ravens X-Factors For Clash vs. Bengals
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens will continue the 2026 regular season back at home against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 7 , and the difference in the game could come down to how an individual player performs when it matters most or over the course of the game by capitalizing on their opportunities when presented with them.
With a win, the Ravens improve to 5-2 and could move back into the top spot in the AFC North division standings. A loss could drop them to last place after the Pittsburgh Steelers' overseas win, especially since the Cleveland Browns play a one-win team on Sunday.
Here are four players who could wind up tilting the scales in favor of the Ravens and first-year head coach Jesse Minter.
Even before fourth-year pro Tavius Robinson went down with a season-ending pectoral injury , the second-round rookie was already following in his footsteps by playing regularly on defense in a rotational edge-setting role on early downs in his first season. Now that the Ravens' sack leader through six games is out for the year, Young will likely be asked to assume an even larger role as a pass rusher moving forward, starting in this game.
The two-time Pro Bowl center will finally be making his debut for the Ravens after being acquired via trade a couple of weeks ago from the Philadelphia Eagles. His insertion into the starting lineup couldn't have come at a better time, as the Ravens will be facing a revamped Bengals interior defensive line that features a pair of multi-time Pro Bowlers in Jonathan Allen and Dexter Lawrence, whom he faced twice a year in the NFC East when he played against the New York Giants.
Jurgens' presence will allow standout first-round rookie Vega Ioane to return to his natural spot at right guard, where he began the season before a litany of injuries at center caused him to spend the last three games playing out of position.
With veteran safety Jaylinn Hawkins out for a couple of weeks due to a knee injury, the second-year pro and special teams ace will likely not only get to see his first defensive snaps of the season but could emerge as a difference-maker in DIME packages. The Ravens could play him in the box near the line of scrimmage as a blitzer and heat-seeking missile in underneath coverage while allowing three-time All Pro Kyle Hamilton to play further back in a somewhat more traditional safety role to help the unit better cover the middle of the field.
Despite having last week off while on bye, the Bengals still lead the league in most receiving yards allowed to the tight end position this season with 451 yards through six weeks. While the Ravens have a pair of exciting young rookies at the position who have shown impressive flashes when called upon to play bigger roles this year, the three-time Pro Bowler remains a fixture in Baltimore's passing attack, leading all tight ends in offensive snaps played, targets, receptions and receiving yards. Andrews has had some of his best career games in this rivalry against the Bengals, where he has terrorized their off-ball linebackers and defensive backs alike.

title: Five Pivotal Ravens Matchups to Watch vs. Bengals
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens' Week 7 bout against the Cincinnati Bengals could ultimately be decided by battles between specific position groups or individual players outperforming their counterparts on the other side of the ball.
It'll be the team's first game back at M&T Bank Stadium after a two-week road stint and second straight clash with an AFC North rival. With two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson out for a third straight game with an ankle sprain , they're entering this matchup as slight home underdogs.
If the Ravens prevail, they will improve to 5-2 and could be in a two-way tie for first in the AFC North standings, depending on how the Cleveland Browns fare on the road against the one-win Tennessee Titans this week. Here are the five matchups that can either make or break this game:
To avoid getting into a shootout with his backup quarterback, Tyler Huntley, under center, Baltimore and head coach Jesse Minter will need their tandem of Nate Wiggins and Marlon Humphrey to continue their strong start to the season. They're going to be facing arguably the most lethal wideout duo in the league and one that has given their defense fits and put up prolific numbers over the past half-decade. While Chase has been the more dangerous of the two in their previous matchups and is a threat to take it to the house any time he touches the ball, Higgins has been the more productive of the two, leading the team in receiving with 134 more yards than the next closest pass catcher.
It'll be interesting to see if the Ravens have Wiggins follow Chase to whatever side he lines up on, since that's best-on-best. From a physicality standpoint, Humphrey would be a good matchup against Higgins, although both excel at attacking the ball at the catch point.
Both teams turned one of their most glaring weaknesses from last season into a strength this year by importing new blood and multi-time Pro Bowlers. For the Bengals, it was trading for star nose tackle Dexter Lawrence and signing Jonathan Allen as a salary cap casualty, while the Ravens reunited with left guard John Simpson in free agency, selected stud rookie Vega Ioane in the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft and traded for Cam Jurgens a couple of weeks ago . Lawrence and Jurgens have history and are used to clashing twice a year as former members of opposing NFC East teams and will continue to do so in the AFC North. Since most games are won and lost in the trenches, this matchup could truly wind up tipping the scales in favor of the team whose unit imposes its will and consistently executes at a high level.
This game will mark the first time that four-time Pro Bowler Trey Hendrickson will be playing against his former team since his five-year stint in Cincinnati came to an acrimonious end. After half a decade of not getting to hit or even get too close to Joe Burrow in practice, he'll be free to terrorize his former teammate as often as he's on the field. In order to do so, he'll have to get past and around a fellow four-time Pro Bowler and former Raven, Orlando Brown Jr. On the opposite side, Ravens second-year edge defender Mike Green will have his hands full in obvious passing situations going up against Bengals third-year right tackle Amarius Mims, whose 96.1% pass-block win rate in one-on-ones is the highest mark among offensive tackles with a minimum of 150 snaps this season, according to Pro Football Focus .
The Bengals have struggled mightily to limit the impact of opposing tight ends due to their young second-year off-ball linebackers still not being adept at having a natural feel in coverage. Through five games, Cincinnati has allowed 451 receiving yards to tight ends this season. The Ravens have a three-time Pro Bowler in Mark Andrews and two rookies at the position in Matt Hibner and Josh Cuevas, who has flashed this and will likely get ample opportunities to exploit that trend, especially off of play-action if they can get the run game going with Henry.
With fellow starting safety Jaylinn Hawkins out for this game due to a knee injury, the Ravens could have their three-time All Pro playing further back this week. This would allow Minter to deploy other aggressive downhill defenders closer to the line of scrimmage, such as fourth-year breakout inside linebacker Trenton Simpson and second-year safety Keondre Jackson. Having Hamilton assume more coverage responsibilities could help the Ravens defend the middle of the field better in the zones behind the linebackers where Deshaun Watson feasted on last week. Burrow won't hesitate to follow suit and try to exploit as well, given how high a level of processor he is at reading and carving up defenses.

title: 3 Critical Adjustments The Ravens Offense Must Make For QB Snoop Huntley
full_text:
The Ravens offense has been carrying the defense for the most part through the first six games of the Jesse Minter era. That’s got to change.
This will be a third-straight week with Snoop Huntley at quarterback instead of Lamar Jackson, who is dealing what he called an incredible painful high-ankle sprain that prevented him from really trying to run for two weeks but which the team insists on calling “day-to-day.” That’s problematic on many levels and the Bengals are the best team they have faced without the two-time MVP this season.
If this becomes a scenario where Huntley has to try to keep pace with a big day from Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow, then it’s fair to expect the Ravens will be sitting at 4-3 come Sunday night with successive setbacks in the AFC North. This is going to require highly complimentary football. It mandates a significant contribution from Baltimore’s run game – and beyond just Derrick Henry, trust me – to keep Burrow off the field, shorten this game and give the ball-control and high-percentage approach required by Huntley’s limitations in the downfield passing game to make this a ballgame.
If this is another record day for Bengals receiver Ja’Marr chase – and he has done things to Baltimore’s defense that no pass catcher has ever done to any defense – it’s hard to see, say, Huntley doing the same sort of things with Zay Flowers throwing nothing but short and underneath passes. So, what can we expect from Huntley, realistically?
Well, here’s what Doyle is going to have to help him concoct if the offense is going to sustain more than what we’ve seen in the first two games – almost nothing against the Falcons until the final two drives and almost nothing in their final nine drives after a great start against the Browns.
Catching like eight balls for 60 yards or six for 66 isn’t going to work. Not against this opponent, Even if the Ravens had an excellent game on defense we’re still talking about holding the Bengals to 24-27 points; the Ravens aren’t getting there without Flowers getting loose.
It doesn’t have to be on a long ball, but it needs to do explosive yards after the catch and Doyle is going to have to get even more creative with Flowers than he’s been (and former head coach and player caller Todd Haley, who isn’t easily impressed, was gushing about Doyle’s use of Flowers to me on “The Daily Flock” ). Probably going to have to deploy him in the backfield more. Might need to see more targets at or behind the line of scrimmage.
The Bengals do not have a very good run defense against outside runs, but the Browns were terrible against them and depleted by injury and they shut Henry down. Doyle needs to sell the threat or hint of Huntley running more than he has to this point. It needs to be a staple or quasi-staple.
It’s likely going to take more Justice Hill in the pistol with Huntley. Probably needs to be more RPO looks than anything close to how the game plans have functioned the past two weeks. Have a hard time seeing the Ravens win this game without Huntley running for 3-5 first downs himself and several of them for more than just a handful of yards.
This is yet another new offensive line for the Ravens. Stop me if you’ve heard that one before.
Five guys up front who have never played together before. A center who was probably going to get benched as a guard for the Eagles, just coming off a concussion in a new offense he’s still learning (Cam Jurgens), lining up against one of the dominant defensive tackles in the NFL with arguably the deepest group of DTs with him .
Huntley is going to get pressured, for sure, and the Bengals are generating a 50% pressure rate in the fourth quarter this season, and in his career, well, he’s been quite bad under pressure: 49% completions, just 5.0 yards per attempt and a 66.3 passer rating.
There need to be answers in the screen game and answers with hots and answers with a pass protection plan, that, again, might require more of Hill, their best pass protecting back at a time their best blocking tight end is already lost for the season. This QB needs to have as much of an incubator as possible, and some quick answers to what are likely to be probing questions from the Bengals defensive front.
There is YAC waiting to happen with rookie tight end Matthew Hibner. It needs to be an emphasis Sunday.

title: Four Storylines For Ravens' Divisional Matchup vs. Bengals
full_text:
After two weeks away, the Baltimore Ravens will be back at home in Week 7 for their second straight game against an AFC North opponent when they take on the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday afternoon at M&T Bank Stadium.
Coming off an ugly loss to the Cleveland Browns in Week 6 on the road, in which they blew another double-digit lead, the Ravens are currently tied for the best record in the division at 4-2, but are no longer in first place.
There are several intriguing storylines surrounding this divisional matchup between these two rival teams. Here are the top four.
After only managing 40 points and four touchdowns in the 10 quarters since the two-time league MVP-winning quarterback went down with what he revealed to be a high ankle sprain, the Ravens are going to have to find a way to prevail without him for the third week in a row. Jackson returned to practice this week but was a limited participant on all three days and went from being listed as questionable on the final injury report Friday to being downgraded to out on Saturday .
QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) has been downgraded to “out” for tomorrow’s game vs. Cincinnati.
Both Jackson and Pro Bowl backup Tyler Huntley, who went 1-1 starting in his absence, spoke to the media on Friday, and neither tipped their hand on who'd be under center for this game. Now that the cat is out of the bag, the Ravens will need Huntley and the offense as a whole to rebound from a woeful final three quarters that led to them blowing a double-digit lead to the Cleveland Browns in Week 6 .
"Just like every week, I just prepare to play, and once we get to Sunday, we're going to see," Huntley said.
If it weren't for the uncertainty surrounding the Ravens' starting quarterback situation, this storyline would be headlining this list heading into this game. The four-time Pro Bowler downplayed the significance of going up against his former team, whom he spent the last five years with and enjoyed the most successful stretch of his career with during his media availability earlier this week.
However, the acrimonious end to his tenure in Cincinnati is well-documented and while he denies that there's any bad blood between him and the franchise that refused to compensate him for elite production, his Ravens teammates believe he's going to feast off that extra motivation. With current sack leader Tavius Robinson out for the rest of the season with a pectoral injury, he'll be counted on even more to carry the pass rush .
"I am excited to see him against his former team," inside linebacker Trenton Simpson said. "The things he [does] in practice, the way he rushes the passer and just how he gets off the ball, I believe that this game for him is about to be like one of those ones, like [a] multiple-sack game. I'm calling it, [and] I'm excited to see the celebration he does."
After trotting out makeshift blocking units over the last three weeks, featuring their second- and third-string right guards and moving their stud first-round rookie guard, Vega Ioane, to center, the Ravens are set to have a league-high fifth different configuration on Sunday. With two-time Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens, whom they acquired in a trade with the Philadelphia Eagles, the Ravens could have their best configuration yet by a wide margin.
The Ravens' new-look interior offensive line will have quite the tough first test in this game, going up against a revamped Bengals interior defensive line that features a pair of multi-time Pro Bowl imports in Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen, who each have three sacks through their team's first five games, which ties edge rusher Boye Mafe for the team lead.
While the Cincinnati defense has been susceptible to runs to the outside, which lean toward the strength of the Ravens' outside zone-centric rushing attack, the trio of Jurgens, Ioane and veteran left guard John Simpson will still have to hold up in pass protection and when offensive coordinator Declan Doyle dials inside run concepts like trap and power.
Prior to last week, when they held the Cleveland Browns' leading wideout, Denzel Boston, to one catch for 15 yards on five targets, the Ravens' secondary had struggled to keep the top receivers of opposing teams under control, as the defense as a whole has been rounding into shape. They'll be facing arguably their toughest challenge of the season, and at least since they face the Dallas Cowboys in Week 3, when they go up against the Bengals' lethal duo of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins on Sunday.
Chase, in particular, has been a nagging thorn in the Ravens' side ever since he entered the league. The five-time Pro Bowler has had his most prolific outings against Baltimore, with averages of just under 10 receptions and 125 receiving yards per game and has scored five touchdowns in his last five games in this rivalry series. Higgins leads the Bengals this season with 423 receiving yards and is tied with Chase for the team lead in receptions with 27. The Ravens' outside cornerback duo of Nate Wiggins and four-time Pro Bowl veteran Marlon Humphrey will have their hands full anytime Joe Burrow drops back to pass.

title: Ravens Make Final Decision On Lamar Jackson's Status For Sunday
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens opted not to drag out Lamar Jackson’s medical situation through the weekend.
After head coach Jesse Mitner said on Friday the team was willing to take any decision with Jackson down to the wire if need be, and Jackson signaled how “very, very painful” the high ankle sprain was, the two-time MVP’s status ended up clarified well before kickoff. Baltimore ruled him out Saturday afternoon, making the messaging about this being a day-to-day injury for three weeks seem even more baffling.
Where twice before they ruled out Jackson on Friday, this time the team and player took it until Saturday. It was the same result, despite very different practice weeks,Jackson spoke about the severity of the injury and its limitations on him as anything but a daily complication, while Ravens head coach Jesse Minter has stuck with that messaging, which probably hasn't served the player, the team or its fans well.
Jackson was always quite likely to miss at least two games with the injury as we originally reported and in fact he will miss at least three including Sunday's key divisional game with the Bengals. While Minter has been calling Jackson “day-to-day” for three weeks the reality couldn’t be further from the truth as even after three limited practice sessions Jackson was not cleared for Week 7 after suffering the injury at the end of the first half in Week 4.
At this point it’s fair to expect that Jackson will have to practice fully a time or two in order for he and the Ravens to be comfortable with his return. Minter reiterated through the week that any final decision would include all parties being aligned that it was the right time for Jackson to return. Jackson is also the rarest of truly elite quarterback who has no future guarantees on his contract beyond this season and he has as much leverage as any NFL player ever has for 2027 with an $85M cap hit, a no-trade clause and a no-franchise tag clause. Which makes any injury with him the focus of increased attention.
“Again, between Lamar, our staff and us, it's going to be a decision based on him, how he feels and how effective [we] feel like it could be,” Minter said Friday after practice.
On Friday Jackson explained what it would take to be able to help the team enough to play:
“I don't feel like I have to be 100%,” Jackson said. “If I can just be out there and tolerate the pain in my ankle, that's it. If I can just go out there and feel the pain a little bit, I can play. But I'm restricted and I can't do what I do, I'm not helping. If I can just go out there and just be a statue and be hit, that's not helping my team at all.”
Jackson also said on Friday: "I started feeling better, like I said, Sunday. Monday (entering Week 7). We came out and tried to run a little bit. I did better than I did the week prior, because I couldn't run at all the week prior. It was just crazy. It was hurting bad.."
Veteran Snoop Huntley gets the start instead. Huntley is a significantly limited passer, the entire scope of the passing game falters with him out and rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle better do a significantly better job of leaning into the screen game and multiplicity in the run game with Jackson out. He also better design more runs for Huntley, who can still move, and dabble with more RPOs.
The Bengals have a lethal interior pass rush led by offseason acquisition Dexter Lawrence – they are the best fourth-quarter pass rush in the NFL by a mile – and the Ravens are starting new center Cam Jurgens, who was struggling mightily for the Eagles at guard , and will field their fifth offensive line in seven weeks.
Doyle also better find ways to get role players into bigger roles with the potential for yards after the catch (especially two of these potential contributors ). Jackson has an 11-2 record against the Bengals (7-2 against Joe Burrow) and has run for 837 yards against them, the most any QB has amassed against any team in the history of the NFL.
Baltimore’s offense was a mess for three quarters against Atlanta with Huntley at the helm and for the final nine drives against the Browns, which produced no points.

title: Ravens Stock Report: 3 Role Players Who Can Provide A Boost Vs Bengals
full_text:
There will be no shortage of starpower on the field at M&T Bank Stadium Sunday.
Whether two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson, still iffy with an ankle injury, plays or no t.
Joe Burrow and Ja’Marr Chase have enjoyed historic games at Baltimore’s expense and Ravens $30M pass rusher Trey Hendrickson faces his former team for the first time, one he left with plenty of acrimony but a revenge spot he’s mostly tried to downplay. The AFC North battle is rich with subplots and drama, but could be decided by some lesser discussed players do things they don’t always do.
In particular, there are three role players who could be in position to make a pivotal play or two to shift this game in Baltimore’s favor. Given their issues holding leads and winning games at home, and considering how messy the secondary has been and what might still be to come at the trade deadline, and with the Bengals coming off a bye, the Ravens are going to need more than just their highest-paid players to step up and these three could be standouts if given the opportunity:
Rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle was pretty hard on  for the offense for their debacle in Week 6, back-up QB or not, and for good reason. He didn’t experiment nearly enough with multiplicity  in the run game and didn’t get enough people involved and didn’t attack the perimeter enough with others than Derrick Henry.
“I would say that what we put on tape wasn't up to our standard,” Doyle said.
The Bengals will not allow inside runs with tackle Dexter Lawrence anchoring and no one is really trying it. When Cincy allows nine yards a pop off left end and six off right end, while not go there? And pistol looks with Hill should work better the some of the stuff with Henry. Not sure how much under center runs should be a point of emphasis but designed screens for Hill and some pony package looks with Henry better be.
Thankfully, his hand injury only put him out one week. Without him, Baltimore’s tight end issues – top blocker Durham Smythe is out for the season and veteran Mark Andrews (one catch for four yards) is washed despite his top-10 compensation at his position. So getting Hibner back and off the injury report entirely is a big deal.
He has caught all five of his targets and made little plays into big gains. He can win on a double move in the slot or win after the catch and 9.0 yards of YAC per reception (Andrews is at 2.0 over the last two years) should have Declan Doyle seeking ways to activate him more and subjugate Andrews. Fellow rookie right end Josh Cuevas is doing more each week too. Hibner catching a ball out of the backfield feels inevitable and bet he is in motion quite a bit in this game.
Losing edge defender Tavius Robinson for the year is a big deal . A really big deal. He excels setting the edge, plays with real power and was coming along as a pass rusher and had a toolkit to naturally play opposite Hendrickson. The Ravens know that Hendrickson and Green both feel at their best rushing against the left tackle and it’s time for Jesse Minter to get creative about how to get him and Hendrickson on the field together.
I’ve liked what I’ve seen from Green when he twists inside and attacks the A Gap some. They could use a NASCAR package where Green starts in the wide position, almost a Wide 9, and loops inside with the pass rush like Hendrickson does.
Not that the Bengals will run much, or run well, but that’s not either of these guy’s fortes, Still, finding a way to keep Hendrickson healthy and effective for all four quarters is a must, and he has waned through games with his hand issue a concern.
He’s supposed to be the “closer” but has no sack and just four pressures in the fourth-quarter all season – Baltimore is among the dregs in pressure and sacks in that quarter – yet the Bengals are tops in the NFL in those metrics this season without him in the fourth. Having Green and Hendrickson try to impact the quarterback together needs to be a thing.
“Trey definitely feels more comfortable on the right,” defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver said, “and … Mike seems pretty indifferent to it. So, both of those guys I think can eat regardless of where they're aligned.”

title: Top Four Reasons The Bengals Could Beat The Ravens Sunday
full_text:
The Ravens used to be one of the best home teams in the NFL.
Sunday will be a difficult test for rookie head coach Jesse Minter, who is once again juggling unusual personnel situations and tricky injury situations including starting quarterback Lamar Jackson, who is questionable with an ankle injury and made progress this week but perhaps not enough to play. The Bengals are fresh off a bye and in considerably better health. Jackson has owned them with an 11-2 record while averaging 29 points per game, but the Bengals offense has also had some legendary days at Baltimore’s expense and Minter’s defense was quite shaky in critical areas through the first third of the season.
These are the top four reasons the Bengals could win Sunday and push the Ravens down in the AFC North standings:
Even if Jackson plays, he has barely practiced for three weeks since suffering the injury, he has never worked much at all with new center Cam Jurgens at all (more on that in a minute) and his legs have been a huge part of his success against Cincy. Jackson has 837 rushing yards against them; most of any QB against any NFL team, but how much of that will be in the cards even if Jackson does suit up?
Rookie play caller Declan Doyle, coming off his worst performance as an offensive coordinator, has been hesitant to lean into designed runs and RPOs and Jackson’s legs have not been as much of a weapon since 2024, honestly. The Bengals also fortified their defensive line in a major way, they are holding opposing passers to the same rating Baltimore’s vaunted secondary is (87.0) and it certainly looks like this will be a situation where Jackson will have to feel out his ankle though the game.
That’s enough to sway the margins with two teams this well matched.
“I don't feel like I have to be 100%,” Jackson said on Friday about being able to play. “If I can just be out there and tolerate the pain in my ankle, that's it. If I can just go out there and feel the pain a little bit, I can play. But (if) I'm restricted and I can't do what I do, I'm not helping. If I can just go out there and just be a statue and be hit, that's not helping my team at all.”
The Bengals have arguably the deepest and most impactful rotation of defensive tackles in the NFL right now and it goes way beyond just offseason-acquisition Dexter Lawrence . They are leading the NFL in sacks and pressures from that position and Jurgens has only had really two full workdays on the job in practice and that was somewhat split between two QBS.
Jurgens has not played center with any consistency in quite some time, moving to guard with the Eagles, he was playing poorly for Philadelphia and may have been on the cusp of being benched before the trade, he barely knows the offense and his teammates and he just came out of concussion protocol. If that seems like a lot, that’s because it is.
This will be the Ravens fifth offensive line combination in seven weeks and there is little interior cohesion and it’s been a problem all season. Not sure Jurgens fixes it right away against Sexy Dexy and this bunch and Lawrence knows him well from his time with the Giants battling Jurgens in the NFC East.
The Ravens are a joke in the fourth quarter, and they continue to set records for choking away double-digits leads and have blown three already this season and lost two of those games. With 16 losses in games where they lead by 10 or more since 2019, and having just done it again last week in Cleveland, this might be the Bengals catching them in a vulnerable moment.
None of the Ravens’ corners has been any good in the second half of games and top receivers have gutted them to the point it might need to be addressed before the trade deadline and its left hybrid safety Kyle Hamilton exacerbated by it all. Minter has tried to explain it away at times (I know a corner I would be trying to trade away ) but their late-game mental breakdowns are real and this team lacks the clutch gene and Joe Burrow has it and it might come down to the final possession. (Oh, and Bengals receiver Ja’Marr Chase has done things to the Ravens no WR has done to any other team in league history).
Former Bengal Trey Hendrickson may need to take this game over in a revenge spot; Baltimore is bottom seven in the NFL in fourth-quarter pressure rate and sack rate, while the Bengals are number one and it’s not even close with a 50% pressure rate and sublime 18.5% sack rate in the final quarter.
Baltimore’s choking is most acute at home. The Ravens recently had a five-game losing streak at home and they snapped it Week 4 against the Titans, but again failed to score in the second half of that game after Jackson went down and allowed Tennessee to hang around.
Kicker Tyer Loop hasn’t been great anywhere but has really struggled at home since the preseason and now he has competition back in the building. The Ravens seem incapable of putting forth a pure, focused four-quarter game at home and that might be what it takes to beat a talented Bengals squad.
Burrow is just 2-4 at Baltimore, so the Ravens do have that going for them, but he won at M&T Bank Stadium last year and two of those losses came when mastermind Mike Macdonald was running the Baltimore defense.

title: Ravens Final Week 7 Injury Report Reveals Major Change for Lamar Jackson
full_text:
After taking the practice field for the first time since suffering what he revealed was a high ankle sprain during his Friday media availability, Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson was one of five players given a designation on the team's final injury report .
Fortunately for them, he joined defensive tackle Broderick Washington in being listed as questionable to play against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday in a massively important Week 7 AFC North showdown.
Game status vs. Bengals pic.twitter.com/bJIL9hngwi
"Right now, I'm headed in the right direction," Jackson said. "If it feels better tomorrow, we'll know tomorrow. So I can't call it. I just have a grace period until Sunday."
While seeing the two-time league MVP on the practice field all week was a welcome sight, it was still on a limited basis. However, head coach Jesse Minter shared that Jackson "was able to get a pretty good amount of work in" Friday's practice session.
"Between Lamar and our staff and us [coaches], it's going to be a decision based on him and how he feels and how effective and things like that it can be," Minter said. "He's had a good couple days, but we'll see how it goes over the next 48 hours.
Minter had already ruled out veteran safety Jaylinn Hawkins with a knee injury that will keep him sidelined for multiple games, and he also ruled out fourth-year outside linebacker Tavius Robinson with what he revealed was a season-ending pectoral injury. This leaves the Ravens without one of their three starting safeties and their sack leader through the first six weeks with 3.5 .
The only other player given a final designation was third-year cornerback T.J. Tampa, who is listed as doubtful to play with a knee injury, as remains on injured reserve but returned to practice for the first time this week in a limited capacity.
The team's media podium might as well have been a ballroom floor with all the dancing around the question of whether Jackson or primary backup Tyler Huntley would be starting against the Bengals this week.
Usually, only the head coach and starting quarterback step to the podium to address the media on the Friday before upcoming games, which had been Huntley the previous two weeks and Jackson the four weeks before.
This time around, the Ravens had both quarterbacks speak after practice, and neither confirmed or denied who would and wouldn't start on Sunday, although Huntley expressed that he'd be ready to make his third straight start and 19th of his career if called upon.
"I just got to be ready to play Sunday if that's the case," Huntley said. Once we get to Sunday, we'll see."
The Ravens have posted 116 points, 14 touchdowns, 967 passing yards and 1,464 total yards in the 14 quarters with Jackson under center, and barely managed a third of those figures in the 10 quarters without him with 40 points, four touchdowns, 429 passing yards and 742 total yards.
While having the best dual-threat quarterback of all time back in the lineup would be a major boost not only for overall morale but also for the production and efficiency of the offense, Jackson doesn't want to be selfish by rushing back on the field if he can't be his usual dynamic and elusive self.
"I'm just trying to move how I move," Jackson said. "If I can't do that, I can't help my team. I can't put my team in a situation like that. I feel like I'm doing a disservice then."
The Bengals coaches were likely going to prepare to face either quarterback anyway. By having Jackson listed as questionable, which essentially equates to probable, and having him speak to the media in surprising depth about the nature and severity of his injury, they're giving their rivals a worst-case scenario for them to seriously consider coming to fruition on Saturday. Jackson as an 11-3 career record against the Bengals as a starter and was playing at an MVP level prior to suffering his injury.
"I don't feel like I have to be 100%.," Jackson said. "If I can just go out there and feel the pain a little bit, I can play. But I'm restricted. Like, I can't do what I do. I'm not helping nobody. If I can just go out there and just be a statue and get hit, [there's] no positives in that. That's not helping my team at all. I feel like I'm being selfish because it's about me at that point, you know, getting out there and be hurt. That's dumb."

title: Colts Trade Rumors Should Have Bills Targeting Two Players
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills made it clear this offseason that they expect to win a Super Bowl. They fired head coach Sean McDermott , who had them in the playoffs seven consecutive years, but never made it to the big game.
Joe Brady was promoted as his replacement, and the goal was clear. Despite being a rookie, he was expected to put this team over the top . While he's done well with the offense, the Buffalo defense is still trying to find its footing.
Through six games, they're 31st in defensive yardage and 28th in points . Much of their shortcomings have been put on the shoulders of the secondary, but they could still improve by beefing up the interior of their defensive line, where Ed Oliver has struggled to stay healthy leaving them with little production outside of Deone Walker .
With that being the case, general manager Brandon Beane should be paying attention to a report from ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport , which says the Indianapolis Colts could be interested in trading both DeForest Buckner and Grover Stewart before the NFL trade deadline on November 10.
Indianapolis owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon recently fired general manager Chris Ballard, and according to Schefter and Rapoport, she and new chief of personnel Ed Dodds will monitor the team's performance over the next few games. If the 2-5 Colts continue to struggle, they might be willing to unload veteran players on expiring contracts.
Of the two defensive tackles named, Buckner is the more intriguing name. The 6-foot-7, 295-pounder can play all over the defensive line and has been a disruptive pass rusher with four sacks during his first seven games. His run defense hasn't been ideal this season, earning a 45.3 from PFF, but his 75.3 pass rush grade would be a welcome addition to a team that needs to figure out how to slow down the pass. Adding a player such as Buckner, who can destroy the pocket, would do exactly that.
Stewart wouldn't be a bad addition either. He's better against the run, earning a 60.7 from PFF this season . Listed at 6-foot-4 and 314 pounds, Stewart would be more help in the run game, and while the Bills are 13th in the league in run defense, it never hurts to improve, especially as the colder months get here and teams rely on the run more.
Neither player would be a long-term answer for the Bills. Not only are they both over 30 (Buckner is 32 and Stewart is 33), but they are both scheduled for free agency in the offseason.
That's one thing the Bills would need to consider when it comes to how much capital they're willing to give up for a rental player. Buffalo would also need to figure out the cap situation since they have just $4.5 million in space . Buckner has a cap hit of $26.6 million this season while Stewart is at $14.258 million. The Bills could lessen the cap hit on that if Indianapolis agreed to pay a certain amount of what he's due for the rest of 2026.
Of course, that only happens if Buffalo offers enough to entice Indianapolis to play ball. It would take some maneuvering, but a team eyeing a championship should be ready to jump through a few hoops.

title: Ranking Buffalo Bills' Four Toughest Remaining Games After Bye Week
full_text:
Prior to the New England Patriots’ loss to the Chicago Bears on Amazon Prime’s Thursday Night Football to begin Week 7—an outcome Bills Mafia should’ve been rooting fo r entering the intraconference matchup—the combined record of the Buffalo Bills’ first six opponents was 14-21.
A stretch that was once feared to be a gauntlet prior to the start of the season proved to be more of a mirage, as first-year head coach Joe Brady’s squad finished the months of September and October with a 5-1 mark .
And, although there are plenty of areas to clean up for Buffalo following its current bye week , the Bills are sitting pretty atop the AFC East and second in the AFC right now behind the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs.
Buffalo’s upcoming opponents heading into Week 7 had a combined record of 34-29, though, so things appear like they’re only about to get even harder for the “Brady Bunch” in Western New York through the final 11 games of the season.
Will their somewhat lucky ways continue ? Or will the tide take a turn for the worse in November and December?
Here are the four toughest remaining games on the Bills’ schedule.
A primetime game on Thanksgiving night in Western New York is going to be electric!
Although fans will certainly be ready to cheer on their beloved Bills following a day of tailgating, turkey, and some select beverages before this matchup, the game on the field will be anything but easy.
The Kansas City Chiefs are the only undefeated team remaining in the AFC at the current moment ahead of Sunday Night Football , and they’ll undoubtedly be looking for revenge against Buffalo after quarterback Josh Allen and Co. have served up five straight losses to Kansas City in the regular season dating back to October 10, 2021.
The Bills might have the Chiefs’ number in the autumn months, but that could change this time around. It doesn’t help that each team will be on short rest, either.
Thursday night games are always wonky, so it should be quite the holiday spectacle in Orchard Park.
The last time quarterback Josh Allen played at Lambeau Field was during his rookie season in 2018 . . . and it wasn’t pretty.
The former 2024 NFL MVP was a shell of himself back then, and it showed on the field as the one-time University of Wyoming gunslinger completed just 16-of-33 passes for 151 yards through the air, two interceptions, and one fumble in a 22-0 loss.
Allen was also sacked seven times.
Needless to say, he’ll be looking for redemption on the road later this December. However, just as was mentioned above with the Chiefs’ matchup, it’ll be much easier said than done.
Despite starting their 2026 campaign with a 1-2 mark, the Packers have since reeled off three straight wins and are second in the NFC North standings going into Week 7.
Of course things could go always sideways for head coach Matt LaFleur, quarterback Jordan Love, and the remainder of Green Bay’s roster the rest of the way, but right now they look like they’ll be a tough out when the Bills come to town prior to Christmas, especially in a historic environment like Lambeau Field.
Love is capable of shredding Buffalo’s susceptible secondary with his live arm, and who knows how things will turn out on the offensive side of the ball for Allen and his teammates under the bright lights while facing the Packers’ defense in addition to a hostile crowd.
For that reason, this game appears to be one of the tougher ones remaining on the Bills’ upcoming slate.
Not much needs to be written here.
A game between the Bills and the Patriots in December in Foxborough? Yeah, it’s going to be a battle: no doubt.
And, given the fact that Buffalo appears to have a bit of a “Drake Maye problem” on its hands no matter who the defensive coordinator is, it makes this matchup all the more enticing . . . and difficult for the current divisional leader.
However, hopefully the Bills will have built up a little bit of a cushion in the standings before their next tussle with the Patriots.
If not, then there could be a potential issue brewing in the AFC East later on in December.
Ben Johnson’s offense vs. Joe Brady’s offense . . . in primetime . . . in a possibly snowy December setting in Orchard Park?
This meeting of the offensive minds has all the makings of a possible classic at the new Highmark Stadium just days before Christmas. It’s almost as if the bearded man in the big red suit is bringing NFL fans an early gift or something.
With that said, however, the matchup will be anything but a lovely winter evening stroll through Orchard Park for the Bills.
And, depending on their record at that point in the season, it could be disastrous if Buffalo were to suffer a loss at the hands of Chicago at home.
This will be one of the toughest games left for Brady’s team.

title: Five Bills' Players Powering NFL's Hottest Special Teams Unit
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills are scoring points at a higher frequency than any other NFL club, and they're also enjoying a noticeable advantage over their opponents on special teams.
The Bills have been particularly sharp on specials during their back-to-back road victories, earning praise from head coach Joe Brady in the wake of the October 18 win over the Las Vegas Raiders.
"Loving the way, the confidence that our special teams is playing with and the standard that they kind of showed and have to keep going," said Brady.
Buffalo has climbed up to second overall in DVOA special teams metrics, and coordinator Jeff Rodgers is Bills On SI Assistant Coach of the Year at the bye week.
As for the players who are making it happen, here are five individuals who are spearheading the Bills' special teams success.
Andreessen has not seen a defensive rep yet this season, but he's on the field for 77 percent of special teams snaps. The Bills recognized his importance by signing the local product to a two-year contract extension last month.
Affectionately known as Buffalo Joe, Andreessen leads the team with nine special teams tackles, and he's a key reason why the kick and punt coverage has been so effective.
"I thought our kickoff [coverage] team was elite yesterday, and I think we had like 12 different guys in on tackles," said Brady. "I mean, I showed the whole team. I just showed every kickoff over and over and over. It's just guys making plays."
After missing the entire 2025 campaign due to a core muscle injury, Bass has returned in grand fashion. He has made 13 consecutive field goal attempts to start the season.
After nailing the walk-off 45-yard winner on Monday Night Football against the Los Angeles Rams, Bass hit four field goals in the 33-30 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders. It was his third 3+ field goal performance on the road this season, going 3-for-3 against the Rams and the Houston Texans.
The seventh-round rookie punter has been an upgrade over Mitch Wishnowsky after beating out the veteran for a roster spot in training camp.
Doman is netting 46.0 yards per punt, which would lead the NFL if he met the minimum attempts required (2.5/game). Six of his 12 punts have pinned the opponent inside its own 20-yard line. He has no touchbacks and has forced fair catches in multiple key spots.
The rookie punted twice last time out against the Raiders, netting 47.5 yards per boot and allowing no return yards. In the opener against the Texans, he punted twice to the tune of 54.5 net yards per kick.
"I hate when Tommy punts, but he had some elite hang time yesterday. He was able to pin the one inside the 10," said Brady one day after the Week 6 win.
The Bills post-cutdown day pickup has been the perfect addition for the return game. Dortch has been steady and consistent as the primary punt returner and occasional kickoff returner.
Dortch totaled 84 return yards last time out in Las Vegas, including an impressive 22-yard punt return. For the season, he's averaging 10.1 yards per punt return.
"Dortch, I'm surprised he didn't fair catch one, but he was an arm away from maybe cribbing one," said Brady.
Above all, Dortch appears to consistently exercise good judgement when fielding kicks. He's also protected the ball well.
Davis appeared to start slow, but he's suddenly back on top of the NFL in kick return average (31.0). The 2025 All-Pro selection has opened back-to-back road games by ripping off big kick returns.
"All-Pro Ray Davis, outstanding two games in a row," said Brady.
He took the opening kickoff 70 yards on Monday Night Football in Week 5. Last time out, he ran it back 40 yards against the Raiders. Both returns set up field goals.

title: Will Lamar Jackson Return vs. Bills in Week 8? Buffalo on Crash Course to Face Ravens QB
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills were hoping to avoid Baltimore Ravens signal-caller Lamar Jackson in Week 8, when the two teams meet at Highmark stadium.
However, when the Bills return from their bye next week, it appears Jackson might be ready to go and return from his ankle injury.
NFL Network's Ian Rapoport is reporting that Jackson is "expected" to make his return to the field in Week 8.
"(Jackson) is likely to return next week against the Bills. Expected to return, actually," Rapoport said. "He was really close to going this week, but because they got the Bills and then a short week after this, (the Ravens said) you know what, let's just be cautious."
Jackson, who has now missed three games in a row, was able to finally return to practice this past week before drawing a questionable tag and being ruled out on Saturday.
Jackson made it quite clear during the week that he still wasn't at 100% .
"I'm restricted. Like I can't really do what I do. So I'm not helping nobody if I can just go out there and be a statue and get hit," he said. "No positive. Like that's not helping my team at all. That's just me. I feel like I'm being selfish because it's about me at that point for me to get out there and be hurt. That's dumb."
It goes without saying that Buffalo's matchup against the Ravens just got harder.
Not only is Jackson an elite runner, but he's also obviously a much better passer than his backup, Tyler Huntley, who is a quality QB2, at best.
The Bills are giving up 15.5 rushing yards per game against signal-callers this season, but they also haven't faced someone like Jackson, who the team is quite familiar with.
What's even more concerning for the Bills is they sport the second-worst pass defense in the NFL, which is why facing Huntley would have been a huge reprieve. Now, Buffalo's struggling secondary will have a tougher test.
On the flip side, the Bills expect to enter the matchup relatively healthy across the board .
Over five regular season games against the Bills, Jackson has completed 67.3% of his passes, but he's only averaging 135.6 passing yards per contest against Buffalo and has eight touchdowns to three picks through the air.
Jackson has, however, been a nightmare for the Bills on the ground with 55.2 rushing yards per game and two scores throughout those contests.
In his last game against the Bills in Week 1 of last season, Jackson was 14-of-19 for 209 yards and two scores to no picks and added 70 yards and a touchdown on six carries.

title: Are Bills Playing Today? When Is NFL MVP Favorite Josh Allen's Next Game?

For those Bills' fans who plan to watch football on a stress-free Sunday with their team on its bye, here are the rooting interests for October 25 .

title: Bills' Best Asset Not Enough NFL Experts Are Talking About Responsible for 5-1 Start
full_text:
It's a sometimes forgotten aspect of the game that was emphasized by Buffalo Bills ' Hall-of-Fame head coach Marv Levy.
For as good as the Bills' offense has been through the first six games of the 2026 season, the special teams have been nearly flawless. Buffalo currently ranks second overall in the DVOA metric measuring special teams production and efficiency.
In fact, Buffalo has been so brilliant in that one-third of the game that special teams coordinator Jeff Rodgers earned Bills' Assistant Coach of the Year honors in On SI's bye week superlatives .
Making the production even more impressive, it's not only one or two areas where the Bills' specialists are thriving during the team's 5-1 season start. Buffalo has enjoyed efficient across the board from kicking, punting, returning, covering kicks and winning the field position battle in key spots.
"Loving the way, the confidence that our special teams is playing with and the standard that they kind of showed and have to keep going," said head coach Joe Brady in the aftermath of the Week 6 road win over the Las Vegas Raiders.
Of note, Ray Davis leads the NFL in kickoff return average (31.0) and Tyler Bass has made all 13 field goal tries .
Realistically, the Bills' special teams can claim credit for turning the tide in three of the five victories. Their special teams play was clearly superior on the road in Weeks 5 and 6.
The Bills went on the road and pulled out a season-opening victory with plenty of help from the kicking game. In his first game in more than one year, Tyler Bass hit all three field goals in his return. Meanwhile, seventh-round rookie punter Tommy Doman netted  54.5 yards per punt on two boots.
Ray Davis opened the primetime affair by returning the Rams' kickoff 70 yards, setting up an early Bills' field goal. Then, in overtime, Greg Rousseau blocked a 48-yard game-winning field goal attempt by the Rams to give the Bills new life on Monday Night Football. On the ensuing possession, Bass ended the marathon by nailing a 45-yard field goal coming out of the two-minute warning.
Bass made all four of his field goal attempts in the road win over the Raiders. His first three-pointer, which capped Buffalo's opening possession, was set up by a 40-yard kickoff return by Davis. Doman punted twice during the victory, forcing two fair catches by Las Vegas.

title: Who Should Bills' Fans Root For During Week 7 Bye?
full_text:
Following back-to-back narrow victories on the road over the past two weeks out West against the Los Angeles Rams and Las Vegas Raiders, the Buffalo Bills have recently had a few days of rest during a seemingly much-needed bye week .
However, although the players and coaches in Western New York might be taking things a little easier this week , that doesn’t mean there isn’t still some business to attend to before next week’s preparations begin for an enticing AFC matchup against the Baltimore Ravens in Orchard Park at the new Highmark Stadium on November 1 at 1 p.m. ET.
Bills ON SI recently highlighted some critical changes that must be made despite the team’s 5-1 record, including some possible trades that could be processed by Bills’ general manager Brandon Beane before the NFL’s trade deadline of November 10 at 4:00 p.m. ET.
And, with that said, there’s some work for Bills Mafia to do this weekend, as well, as the fanbase will be tasked with the ever important job of scoreboard watching around the league on Sunday afternoon and evening.
As of now, the Bills hold a slight lead over the New England Patriots in the AFC East after quarterback Drake Maye and Co.’s disappointing primetime loss to the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on Amazon Prime’s Thursday Night Football just the other day, and there’s a chance that other teams nipping at Buffalo’s heels could—hopefully—suffer a similar fate this weekend.
With that in mind, here are seven crucial games for Bills’ fans to keep tabs on during this upcoming slate of NFL games in Week 7.
Despite starting the 2026 campaign with a 2-2 record to begin the fall, Pittsburgh has since reeled off two consecutive victories to even things up with the Cleveland Browns and Baltimore Ravens in the AFC North Standings.
The Steelers are seemingly finding their stride right now behind longtime NFL quarterback Aaron Rodgers and running back Jaylen Warren, so it’d be a nice gesture by the Saints if they could somehow slow Pittsburgh’s roll at the current moment.
An international loss by the Steelers is what Bills’ fans should be rooting for on Sunday morning this weekend.
Ultimately, neither Miami nor New York seem to be too much of a threat to the Bills in the AFC standings or the divisional standings this fall , but that still doesn’t matter.
Given that the Jets have two wins on the season and the Dolphins have zero to their name yet, it’d be a good idea for Bills’ fans to root for Miami and first-year head coach Jeff Hafley to get off the schneid to end October.
It’ll be a tough task on the road at MetLife Stadium, though, especially after the Jets just held tough with the Patriots in Week 6 during a 26-19 loss at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts.
The upcoming meeting between the Bengals and the Ravens is intriguing for a multitude of reasons, but for Bills’ fans it’ll be interesting for at least two specific points of discussion.
First, is quarterback Lamar Jackson playing against Cincinnati? If he isn’t, which could certainly be the case given that he’s missed the last two weeks with an ankle injury, then it’ll be longtime backup quarterback Tyler Huntley running the show once again.
And, if that does end up being the situation for Baltimore, then it’ll also mean that Jackson has another week of rest and preparation to get ready for a crucial AFC matchup against the Bills at Highmark Stadium next week.
The second reason it’s important?
Well, both the Bengals and Ravens possess a winning record at the moment, so it’ll be important to have the game end in a loss for one of Buffalo’s AFC counterparts instead of ending in a tie like the Washington Commanders and New York Giants did over in the NFC in bizarre fashion just two weeks ago.
For momentum purposes, it might be a good idea to have Baltimore top Cincinnati in the game on Sunday so that Jackson and Co. aren’t looking for even more revenge next week at Highmark Stadium following two straight losses to the Bills over the past few seasons.
In the end, this game probably won’t wind up being much of a contest given how surprisingly well the Cleveland Browns have started off the season, but it’ll still be important for fans to root for the Tennessee Titans in an upset at Nissan Stadium on Sunday afternoon.
Cleveland currently sits atop the AFC North through six weeks of the season under first-year head coach Todd Monken, and it’s been one of the biggest shockers of the 2026 season thus far.
The sooner that some teams can start knocking the Browns down a peg in the AFC standings, then the better it’ll be for Buffalo’s playoff chances later on this season . . . particularly when it pertains to possibly getting the No. 1 seed in the conference.
That was always the goal under former Bills’ head coach Sean McDermott over the past nine years, but unfortunately it never happened .
At this point of the season, things are looking a little bleak for the Denver Broncos despite their 4-2 record.
Quarterback Bo Nix has been receiving criticism for practically being a shell of himself on the field through the first six weeks of the season, and it’s a bit hard to fathom that this is the same squad that dismissed the Bills and quarterback Josh Allen from the AFC divisional round playoffs this past January.
The Cardinals are coming off a big win against the reeling Rams this past week, so it’ll be interesting to see how they stack up against Denver on Sunday.
It’d be a big boost for Buffalo if Arizona was somehow able to come away with an intraconference victory at State Farm Stadium.
Bills’ fans should be rooting for the continued downfall of head coach Sean Payton’s Broncos the rest of the season, especially considering the two teams will meet up later this season on Christmas night for a big matchup that will be broadcast on Netflix .
Although Buffalo managed to defeat both of these teams in back-to-back weeks following a dismal divisional loss to the Patriots at home, it’s still an important game to watch for Bills’ fans.
Well, the hope is that Los Angeles will be able to right the ship after two straight losses and knock the reeling Raiders down another peg heading into November.
Las Vegas looked like a sneaky AFC contender to start September, but now they’re sitting at 3-3. So, if Los Angeles can serve the AFC West squad another loss for a fourth straight week, then it’ll only mean positive things for Buffalo moving forward.
The less possible playoff competition the Bills have to worry about later on this season, the better.
This is the big one, Bills’ fans.
Sitting at a perfect 5-0 following a bye of their own a couple weeks ago in Week 5, the Chiefs are the only remaining undefeated squad in the AFC at this point in time.
Buffalo is right behind Kansas City in the standings, though, so it’ll be crucial for the Seahawks to give quarterback Patrick Mahomes, head coach Andy Reid, and the rest of the Chiefs’ team their first loss of the 2026 campaign.
For years, the Bills have been desperately trying to obtain the No. 1 seed in the playoffs ahead of the Kansas City Chiefs, and it’s yet to happen during former 2024 MVP quarterback Josh Allen’s first eight years in the league.
If it’s going to happen in Year 9, then the Chiefs are going to have to start piling up some losses sooner than later.
This game certainly seems like the first possible one.
Bills Mafia must put all of their cheering efforts into joining Seattle’s 12th-man on NBC ’s Sunday Night Football to end this weekend.
A loss by the Chiefs on Sunday evening would only make Buffalo’s meeting with Kansas City at Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park on Thanksgiving night all the more exciting.
Let’s hope it happens, folks.

title: One NFL Trade Deadline Move Bills Must Make
full_text:
With the NFL trade deadline approaching, Buffalo Bills general manager Brandon Beane should be working the phones in an attempt to shore up his team's defense. The Bills currently have two major needs, with cornerback and safety being problematic through their first six games.
Buffalo brought back Tre'Davious White , who started 16 games in 2025. White is currently on the practice squad, but the Bills will be working to get him up to speed as soon as possible.
While his addition will help, the Bills are still without a game-changing safety and C.J. Gardner-Johnson reminded them that he shouldn't be relied upon after getting ejected in Week 6, and eventually suspended for Week 8 , for spitting at Brock Bowers.
The good news for Beane is that there are several names rumored to be available , with the biggest name being Budda Baker of the Arizona Cardinals. As good as Baker is, he shouldn't be the top priority. Instead, Beane should be calling the Tennessee Titans about Amani Hooker.
Baker is a true playmaker at the position, but he's better in the box rather than as a deep cover safety. In Buffalo, it's far more urgent for them to address their coverage woes.
The Bills enter their bye week ranked 31st in defensive passing yards, and much of that has fallen on the performance of the safeties. Six games into the season, their highest-rated safety in coverage has been Gardner-Johnson, who has a 62.7 grade from PFF . Fellow starter Cole Bishop has a coverage grade of 47.5, while Damar Hamlin is sitting at 56.1.
Baker's coverage grade is lower than all three of those safeties, with a 47.1 entering Week 7 . It'sd a completely different story with Hooker, however, who has a 71.7 coverage grade , which is the 16th-highest at the position.
What makes Hooker even more intriguing, though, is that he's been even better against the run. The veteran currently has an 88.5 against the run, which helped him earn an 81.1 overall, which is currently the eighth-highest score at safety.
Tennessee is just 1-5 and they're expected to be sellers at the deadline. The Bills are on the other end of the spectrum, sitting at 5-1 and are one of the favorites to contend for a Super Bowl. To help increase their odds of finally winning a title, they need to shore up their primary weakness and Hooker is the perfect addition to do exactly that.

title: Bills Face Major Test After Bye With One of NFL’s Toughest Schedules
full_text:

Meanwhile, franchise quarterback Josh Allen is expecting the team to play its "best football" coming out of the Week 7 bye. That's vital because Buffalo will face a huge test right off the bat.

title: Bills Brought Tre'Davious White Back, So What's Next Move to Boost Subpar Defense?
full_text:
It's no secret that the Buffalo Bills ' defense needs to improve at multiple positions.
The Bills, who are allowing 28.5 points per game, ranks next to last amongst their NFL peers in pass defense (285.8).
After keeping only three true outside cornerbacks on its 53-man roster, Buffalo finally reinforced its depth there by bringing  veteran Tre'Davious White back into the building this past week.
While there's an argument to be made that the Bills must seek more cornerback help on the trade market prior to the November 10 deadline, the reality is they likely won't be able to add anyone more capable than White at this point.
Buffalo has only $4.5 million in salary cap space available (per Spotrac), and there are needs for upgrades at safety and inside linebacker, too. In all likelihood, however, any changes at those two positions will come from within.
In the wake of a suspension and poor performance, one has to think Chauncey Gardner-Johnson is in danger of losing his starting status . The Bills simply need more from their safeties in former NFL safety Jim Leonhard's defense.
Unfortunately, former All-Pro Jordan Poyer isn't walking through that door this time. It also doesn't appear realistic for the Bills to add a true difference-maker like Budda Baker due to cap constraints.
While veteran Damar Hamlin can be serviceable in a starting role, Buffalo has two other options to explore.
One line of thinking says fifth-round rookie Jalon Kilgore, the fourth safety on the roster,  should get a chance to learn on the job. Kilgore made his defensive debut against the Las Vegas Raiders following Gardner-Johnson's ejection.
Kilgore totaled 11 snaps as an extra safety. He made a key third-down pass breakup, and he also allowed a touchdown.
The other option is to sign veteran Geno Stone off the practice squad . Stone, who has game experience at both strong and free safety, made 34 consecutive starts for the Cincinnati Bengals prior to signing with the Bills this past March.
In 2023, Stone led all NFL safeties with seven interceptions for the Baltimore Ravens. He has seemingly struggled since then, and it's a bit concerning that he didn't show enough during training camp to not earn a roster spot.
Although head coach Joe Brady has publicly expressed his satisfaction with the Bills' linebacking corps, there's the potential to provide a boost by making an internal change.
"I think you're not a fan of the way our linebackers are playing, based off some of the questions, but I have no issues with the way our linebackers our playing right now," said Brady prior to the Week 6 road game.
Whether it's taking away coverage snaps from either Terrel Bernard or Dorian Williams, it seems like a good time to activate veteran Shaq Thompson off the practice squad . Not re-joining the Bills until after training camp, the former first-round draft pick has presumably spent the season's first six weeks ramping up into playing shape.
If it's not Thompson, then there likely won't be any in-season change to the linebacking corps.
In fact, I'm not even sure there's an impactful enough trade to be made by general manager Brandon Beane, whose best deadline move in recent years is likely securing cornerback Rasul Douglas for the 2023 stretch run.
The Bills are going to have to bank on players continuing to grow into the defense, and Leonhard's ability to maximize the talent available.

title: Panthers Can't Wait Until It's Too Late to Fix Their Cornerback Problem
full_text:
The Panthers should be getting some help at cornerback soon, with Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson both working their way back from injuries . Dave Canales sounded pretty optimistic about where each of them stands, which is obviously good news for a secondary that's been trying to get by without both of its starters.
Even with those two getting closer, I'd still be looking for another corner.
That really doesn't have much to do with what Baker Mayfield did Sunday. He threw for only 64 yards and attempted 11 passes in Tampa Bay's 43-13 win . The Buccaneers didn't need him to do much because they ran for 258 yards and controlled the game that way.
For me, it's more about what Carolina has behind Horn and Jackson and what happens if one of them isn't ready as quickly as expected. We've already seen both starters go down at the same time. I don't think I'd want to take the chance of being in the same spot again later in the season.
There's no question the Panthers are better when Horn and Jackson are on the field. If both come back healthy over the next few weeks, cornerback suddenly looks a whole lot better than it does right now.
The problem is you're putting a lot of faith in both guys staying healthy the rest of the way. Horn has missed time throughout his career, and Jackson is working his way back from groin surgery. Maybe both return and don't miss another game, but I'm not sure that's something I'd want to bet on if I'm Dan Morgan.
Carolina elevated Robert Rochell from the practice squad again for Sunday's game, and he's given the Panthers another option while they've been short-handed. But there's a difference between getting through a few weeks and having enough depth for the rest of the season. Another injury at corner could put Carolina right back in the same situation.
That's why I'd rather see the Panthers address it before they have to.
I'm not talking about giving up a Day 2 pick or chasing some big-name corner just because the Panthers are sitting at 3-3. I wouldn't do that, especially with a team that's still trying to figure out exactly where it stands.
But I'd absolutely make some calls.
If there's a veteran available for a late-round pick, or maybe somebody buried on another depth chart who Carolina thinks can help, that's the type of move I'd be interested in. The Panthers don't need somebody to come in and take Horn's or Jackson's job. They need another corner Evero can trust if one of those guys isn't available.
That might not be the kind of move that gets everybody excited at the trade deadline, but it could matter a lot more a month from now.
If Carolina was sitting at 1-5 right now, I'd probably feel completely different about this. Keep the draft picks, let the younger guys play and use the rest of the season to figure out what you have.
But that's not where the Panthers are. They're 3-3, and as bad as Sunday was, they had won three of four before Tampa Bay came to town. I'm still not completely sure what this team is, but I've seen enough to think there's at least a chance Carolina is playing meaningful football in November and December.
That's why a smaller move at corner makes sense to me. It doesn't mean Morgan has to suddenly act like the Panthers are one player away from a Super Bowl. It just means giving a team that's put itself in a decent position a little more protection at one of the thinnest spots on the roster.
Maybe Horn and Jackson come back, stay healthy and none of this becomes an issue. That's obviously the best-case scenario. But we've already seen what this secondary looks like when both starting corners disappear from the lineup at the same time.
If the Panthers are still hanging around later this season, I'd rather have another corner sitting there and not need him than need one and realize they should've made the move weeks ago.
