title: The Panthers Got Obliterated By the Buccaneers, But These 4 Things Matter
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers got crushed by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. It was an ugly game and a reminder, perhaps, of how far this team still has to go. It's best to forget about this one, but before we do, here are the most important things to remember.
The Panthers invested a ton up front on offense. They spent big on guards Damien Lewis and Robert Hunt. They signed Rasheed Walker and drafted Monroe Freeling. Yet, the offensive line is a mess. It's been bad all year.
Losing Taylor Moton for a second time is a huge blow because he's the only offensive linemen (with the exception of Damien Lewis) who seems capable of doing his job. It's a disaster, and the Panthers invested way too much for that to be the case.
The Panthers lost this game from the top down. You can blame almost everyone for this loss. Dan Morgan refuses to address injury depth issues. Dave Canales hardly ever has this team prepared to play.
Ejiro Evero cannot adjust . Brad Idzik may be innocent, but the offense was pretty bad, too. Some of that is not on him, but he certainly did the team no favors. From the top down, the Panthers failed today.
Yes, this was an ugly one. It's one that's best to forget about as soon as they review the film this week. Just move on and try to put it behind you. What should help is that this is not really a repeatable thing. The Panthers had a perfect concoction of things going wrong that just won't happen again.
The run defense was horrible. The pass protection was bad. Bryce Young was off. The special teams was horrific. Will all of those things happen in the same game again? It's unlikely. Today was just a perfect storm of bad things.
To Carolina's credit, last week was one of those games that allowed the Panthers to claim that they've "arrived." Winning winnable road games to get out to a good start is what good teams do. The Panthers did that, but that wasn't the final opportunity.
Division games matter a lot, even when one team is far behind the other. The Panthers had yet another chance to prove they've made the leap, and they just didn't look ready to do it. It's unfortunate in a very winnable division.

title: 3 Major Takeaways From Panthers' Complete Meltdown Against Buccaneers
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers had a chance Sunday to keep some momentum going after a 25-14 win in Philadelphia. Instead, they turned the ball over four times, couldn't stop the run and were basically out of this one by halftime. Tampa Bay led 33-6 at the break and rolled to a 43-13 win.
There isn't one thing you can point to and say that's why Carolina lost. The Panthers were bad on offense, bad on defense and even special teams got in on it. Tampa Bay didn't need much help, but Carolina gave them plenty anyway.
Here are my three biggest takeaways from a game the Panthers would probably like to forget.
I've defended Bryce Young plenty, and I still think we've seen some good things from him this season. Sunday just wasn't one of those days.
Young finished 14-of-27 for 163 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. He also lost a fumble when Al-Quadin Muhammad got to him in the second quarter, and Calijah Kancey picked it up and returned it 32 yards for a Tampa Bay touchdown. That put Carolina down 17-0, and things never really got any better from there.
The offensive line certainly didn't do Young any favors. Tampa Bay sacked him five times, and there were plenty of snaps where he didn't have much time to do anything. Still, Young made some bad decisions of his own, and three turnovers from your starting quarterback are going to be tough to overcome no matter how well everyone else is playing.
That's probably the frustrating part for me. We've seen Young play better than this, take care of the football and make enough plays to give Carolina a chance. None of that showed up Sunday.
This might be the biggest head-scratcher of the whole game. Carolina had allowed only 81 rushing yards combined over its previous two games, but Tampa Bay had 147 by halftime Sunday and finished with 258.
Bucky Irving went over 100 yards with two touchdowns, Kenny Gainwell added 88 and Sean Tucker broke a 46-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter. The Panthers knew Tampa Bay wanted to run the football, too. Baker Mayfield was back after missing three games with a thumb injury, so there was no reason for the Buccaneers to put the game on his arm if they didn't have to.
They didn't. Mayfield threw the ball just 11 times, and Tampa Bay still won by 30 points. Why throw it when the Panthers couldn't stop the run?
We saw this against Chicago when the Bears ran for 291 yards in the opener. I thought Carolina had gotten away from games like that, especially after what we had seen from the defense lately . Sunday looked way too familiar.
There are games where you get beat, and then there are games where you seem determined to make everything harder on yourself. This was definitely the second one.
David Moore muffed a punt and handed Tampa Bay a short field. Young's fumble turned into a Buccaneers touchdown. Then Carolina finally got something going with a 50-yard touchdown from Young to Darren Waller, only to have the extra point blocked and returned the other way for two points. That pretty much sums up the afternoon.
Then there is the Taylor Moton injury. Moton had just returned last week after missing the first four games of the season, and now Dave Canales says he'll be "out for a while" with a broken fibula. That's a tough loss by itself, but it's even tougher after watching Young get sacked five times.
I'm not ready to throw away everything we saw from Carolina before this game because of one terrible afternoon. The Panthers are 3-3, and we've already seen them look like a completely different team at times this season. But Sunday was a pretty big reminder that they're not there yet.
The good news is it's only one game.
The bad news is there wasn't much about this one worth keeping.

He previously wrote for Greenville Sports Media, where he covered various sports and teams across the Carolinas. His experience includes game coverage, feature stories and interviews.

title: Grading Bryce Young in Carolina Panthers' Horrific Loss to Buccaneers
full_text:
Well, that was ugly. The Carolina Panthers got demolished by the division rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers , falling to 3-3 on the season. Carolina was never in the game, as the Bucs scored 17 unanswered points by the 11-minute mark of the second quarter.
Entering Week 6, Bryce Young was the league leader in passing yards per game, and had an elite turnover ratio of 11-2. That ratio has changed drastically now, after what's easily the worst performance of the season for Young and the Panthers overall.
Young didn't finish the game, being subbed out early in the fourth quarter after the Buccaneers scored their 43rd point.
There are certainly other directions to point the finger at for this loss , but Young was still abysmal.
Bryce Young finished the Week 7 loss completing just 14 of 27 passes, for 163 yards, 1 touchdown, 2 interceptions, and 1 fumble lost.
It doesn't get much worse than that; there's no team that can recover from that many catastrophic mistakes. Young's fumble resulted in a scoop-and-score for the Buccaneers, and his first interception put Tampa Bay deep in Carolina territory.
Bryce Young fumbles and the Buccaneers scoop and score!💥 pic.twitter.com/WmcvairNvy
Young was also sacked 5 times, which isn't fully on him because he was under pressure basically the entire game, being pressured on over 68% of dropbacks.
Part of the inefficiency was his failure to connect with his top receivers. Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker combined for 5 catches and 49 yards on the day, on 10 targets. For context, Darren Waller totaled more receiving yards than both receivers on just one catch: a 50-yard touchdown.
With such a crowded pocket and no time to process, Young looked like a deer in the headlights on a lot of throws.
This performance continues Young's trend of having no success against the Buccaneers, now 1-6 in his career against Tampa Bay. It's essentially the opposite of his dynamic with the Atlanta Falcons, a team he consistently shreds to pieces.
Outside of the 50-yard touchdown pass to Waller, Young's other 13 completions weren't consequential to the game, as the Panthers only had one drive that reached the red zone, and it was in the third quarter, with the game already out of reach.
Even with the Buccaneers totaling 258 rushing yards, Young still contributed significantly to the Panthers' Week 7 loss.
Before Sunday, Young had played as well as any QB in the NFL not named Josh Allen or Brock Purdy, but his performance against Tampa Bay will likely be the worst QB performance of the week.
Preston is an experienced sports writer focusing on NFL, College Football, NBA, and MMA topics. He is a passionate Charlotte and Oklahoma sports fan and graduated from the University of Science and Arts Oklahoma in 2025 with a Bachelor of Arts in Communications degree with a focus in journalism.

title: 4 Winners and 7 Losers from Panthers' Repulsive Showing vs. Buccaneers
full_text:
With games that are over at halftime (27-point deficit), it's best to flush it and move on. Most everyone from the Carolina Panthers was a big loser today, but there were some who stood out more than others. And while it was ugly, there were some decent individual performances, too.
Bobby Okereke's 7 tackles in the first quarter are tied for the most by a Panther in the opening quarter of a game since at least 2000 and the most since Frankie Luvu had 7 in Week 15, 2023.
It wasn't a banner day for everyone on defense, but Bobby Okereke was once again very solid. He made a few big plays on third downs that helped a maligned Panthers defense get off the field in some crucial spots.
The Bucs already have more rushing yards today than the Eagles had against the Panthers last week.
No Emeka Egbuka, and Baker Mayfield has an injured thumb. You and everyone else knew the Buccaneers would pound the run and feed Bucky Irving. Well, either Ejiro Evero didn't realize that , or he just didn't have his defense ready to defend the run with any success. Neither option is an excuse. Oh, and they couldn't tackle, either.
One play makes you a winner today; that's how ugly it was. Darren Waller's 50-yard touchdown, which was a terrific pass from Bryce Young, was really the only highlight, and it briefly gave the Panthers a tiny bit of hope, although that literally evaporated on the extra point.
David Moore is considered the Panthers' "safe punt returner," meaning he goes in to catch the ball on fair catches -- cleanly. Welp.
David Moore has one job. Just one. He has to field punts where a fair catch is needed, and he couldn't even do that. With a chance to flip the momentum back after a big stop on defense, Moore muffed a punt badly. It gave the Buccaneers an immediate second score.
Was Chuba Hubbard as good as he usually is on Sunday? Not at all, though it's partly the fault of the game situation. Still, while the bar for being a winner today is on the floor, Hubbard was pretty solid again for the Panthers.
The veteran right guard's nightmare season continues. Robert Hunt has been abysmal so far this season, and that didn't end on Sunday. The guard was beaten badly on a strip sack that was returned for a touchdown, an early dagger from the Tampa Bay defense.
As with Darren Waller, scoring a touchdown gets you on the list. Tre Tyus took a pitch and followed his blockers into the end zone. It was a good play design (albeit with and against backups), but Tyus was also pretty good on special teams, too.
Nothing special about the #Panthers special teams as of now. Brutal start for that group.
You probably didn't expect to see the special teams coordinator ever land on one of these lists, but once again, special teams were abysmal. The Panthers muffed a punt with their "reliable" returner (how often do teams even have two differentiated returners?) and then had an extra point blocked and run back for two points. Those are huge swings in a divisional matchup.
Guess who was on the side of the Panthers blocked XP?
The Panthers had an ugly day in many aspects, and Rasheed Walker was involved in a couple of big ones. He got beat badly on a sack, and he was responsible for the blown block that led to a blocked extra point (a three-point swing). At that point, it was still in question.
After a point in the first half, Bryce Young was in an untenable situation. Forced to pass every play and facing a defense that knew it opposite a horrible offensive line, Young had an unwinnable task ahead of him. That said, this was his first dud of the year.
and now a Bryce Tremayne drop on 4th and 1 between his numbers, and he puts it on the floor thats bad
A potential touchdown hit Brycen Tremayne in the hands. It was a perfect throw on fourth down with no defender making a play on the ball, and he bobbled and dropped it. He's been reliable this year, and that was Carolina's last-ditch effort to get back into the game. Tremayne just couldn't make the simple play.

title: Panthers Are Getting Crushed by the Buccaneers — And Have Nobody to Blame but Themselves
full_text:
The Panthers got away with making mistake after mistake last week in Philadelphia. They're finding out pretty quickly that you can't live like that every Sunday.
Carolina turned the ball over three times in the first half against Tampa Bay, and the Buccaneers didn't waste many of those opportunities. That's a big reason the Panthers found themselves staring at a 26-6 deficit late in the second quarter, and the frustrating part is Tampa Bay hasn't exactly had to do anything special to build it.
David Moore muffed a punt in the first quarter, giving the Buccaneers the ball at the Carolina 18. A few plays later, Bucky Irving was in the end zone and Carolina was down 7-0. That's about as easy a touchdown drive as you're going to get in the NFL.
Then Bryce Young was stripped by Al-Quadin Muhammad early in the second quarter, and Calijah Kancey scooped it up and returned it 32 yards for a touchdown. Instead of making Tampa Bay drive the field, the Panthers basically handed them seven points. Young threw an interception later in the quarter to give Carolina its third turnover of the half.
You can survive one of those mistakes. Three before halftime is asking for trouble, especially when you're playing a division opponent that doesn't need much help to begin with.
That's what makes this so frustrating after last week's win over Philadelphia. Carolina committed 13 penalties for 149 yards against the Eagles and somehow still found a way to leave with a win. I thought that showed something about this team, but it was also pretty obvious they couldn't keep making those kinds of mistakes and expect to get away with it.
Instead, the Panthers came home and found a completely different way to make life difficult on themselves. The penalties haven't been nearly as ridiculous as they were in Philadelphia, but turnovers are even harder to overcome. Carolina spent most of the first half giving Tampa Bay short fields and extra possessions.
The Buccaneers haven't even needed Baker Mayfield to come back and light up Carolina's secondary. They've been able to run the football, take advantage of Carolina's mistakes and let the Panthers keep digging their own hole.
There's still another half to play, and we've already seen this Carolina team come back from some ugly situations this season. But if the Panthers are going to have any chance of doing it again, the first thing they have to do is pretty simple.
Stop helping Tampa Bay beat them.

title: The Panthers Can't Afford Ejiro Evero's Problems Any Longer
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have a slight coaching problem , but they have a serious defensive coordinator problem. Ejiro Evero's defense is night and day from week to week, but they can no longer afford to stomach that.
For years, Evero got the benefit of the doubt because the Panthers had awful defensive personnel. We can't even really complain about that, because the personnel was truly that bad. Coming into this year, the excuses were gone.
Now, injuries have played a role in what Evero has had to work with, but most of the time, it's not the worst issue. Not having Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson is a killer blow, but that wasn't the problem against the Philadelphia Eagles or the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Evero doesn't seem to have the right game plan every other week. Today, everyone knew that not having Emeka Egbuka and Baker Mayfield wearing a glove on his throwing hand meant the Buccaneers would run the ball.
Yet, it looked like the Panthers were confused by how much Tampa Bay ran on the first drive, leading to an easy score. Then, the Panthers just refused to adjust. Tampa Bay did whatever they wanted on the ground.
Poor tackling reflects on the coaching. Being out of position does, too. Not having players available is one thing, but having the players on the field out of position or missing easy tackles is another. That's coaching.
At times, it seemed like Evero had turned the corner. But he can't keep the consistency from week to week. Everyone rightfully complained that Bryce Young wasn't consistent from week to week, and he has turned it around.
Because of that, this team has a chance to do something. They have a playoff-level offense, but the defense, which was supposed to be a strength this year, can't figure it out every other week. That is the main reason the Panthers aren't better than they are.
Unfortunately, the Panthers are at a loss here. Does firing the defensive coordinator mid-season fix things? Maybe, maybe not. But something has to change, because the Panthers can't afford to not know what sort of defense they're going to get every time they run out of the tunnel.
This week, it wasn't the absence of Jaelan Phillips, Horn, or Jackson. It was terrible preparation and an unwillingness or inability to adjust.
To be outcoached this badly by Zac Robinson, one of the most maligned coordinators in the NFL, is a tough look. It wasn't even his defiant zone coverage scheme that usually bites the Panthers, which is another issue that has come up a lot during his tenure.

title: Panthers Inactives vs. Buccaneers: Another Starter Down as Injuries Keep Piling Up
full_text:
The Panthers haven't had much luck staying healthy this season, and Sunday against Tampa Bay isn't going to be any different.
Carolina already knew it would be without Jaelan Phillips after he aggravated his hamstring against Philadelphia. Thomas Incoom injured his calf in the same game and was placed on injured reserve Saturday, and the Panthers are still waiting on starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson to get back.
It seems like every week Carolina gets somebody back and loses somebody else.
The Panthers announced seven inactive players before Sunday's 1 p.m. kickoff.
Phillips is obviously the big one here. He's been starting on the outside, and with him out, Princely Umanmielen is expected to get the start opposite Patrick Jones II. Carolina also elevated Nick Hampton from the practice squad Saturday to give the Panthers another option on the edge.
That's a group I'm going to be watching against Baker Mayfield. He's back after missing three games with a thumb injury, but his return shouldn't change what Carolina expects from this game . The last thing the Panthers want is to let him get comfortable early.
Incoom is a little different. He hasn't played much on defense, but he's been a big part of Carolina's special teams. The Panthers activated Bam Martin-Scott from injured reserve Saturday, and that's where he should be able to help right away.
The Panthers have already spent the last few weeks without Horn and Jackson after both starting cornerbacks went down in Week 3. Horn is working his way back from a significant quad injury, while Jackson had surgery for a groin injury.
Both remain on injured reserve, but Dave Canales had some encouraging news Friday. He said Horn is ahead of some of the normal timelines for his injury, while Jackson has also started picking up his speed as he works his way back.
That's good news for later. It doesn't help much Sunday.
Robert Rochell was elevated from the practice squad again this week, so Carolina is still having to make things work in the secondary without its two starters. Now Phillips is out, too, which takes another starter away from a defense that's actually been playing some pretty good football lately.
Carolina held Philadelphia to 222 total yards and just 35 on the ground last week . The Panthers have now held two straight opponents under 50 rushing yards, and they've managed to do that while already missing Horn and Jackson.
If there's some good news Sunday, it's Monroe Freeling.
The rookie tackle is active after missing last week's game with a knee injury. He practiced fully all week but was still listed as questionable heading into Sunday. With Stone Forsythe inactive, having Freeling back gives Carolina another option behind Rasheed Walker and Taylor Moton.
Sam Hecht is also inactive, so the Panthers will have Torricelli Simpkins III and Corey Bullock available behind Austin Corbett at center. Both can snap the ball if something happens and Carolina has to shuffle the offensive line again.
Hopefully it doesn't come to that. The Panthers have done enough shuffling already.
They've still managed to win three of their last four, which might be the biggest thing to take away from all of this. Carolina hasn't had the lineup it wants for a while now, but so far it hasn't stopped the Panthers from finding ways to win.
There's more I'd like to see from Carolina against Tampa Bay than just another win , but considering how much shuffling this roster has already done, getting to 4-2 would be a pretty good place to start.
Sunday they'll have to find another way to get it done.

title: Fantasy Football Start or Sit: Bryce Young & Tetairoa McMillan
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have been a virtual gold mine for fantasy managers this year. Bryce Young is way outperforming his ADP. In some leagues, he went undrafted and has been a dream waiver-wire addition for managers.
Tetairoa McMillan was the only Panther who was getting positive press before the season, and he has done nothing to lose that goodwill. He's the WR15 and player57 (with a bye week), which isn't far behind his ADP.
This week against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, should you keep starting these two?
Bryce Young has been absurdly good this season for fantasy football. He's fourth in fantasy points per game at the QB position. He's averaging over 22 points, which is an incredible number to count on weekly.
To put it further in perspective, Young is top-10 in points per game regardless of position. He's been a dream pick for anyone who took a flyer on him. That makes him must-start until further notice. There's really no reason to bench him unless you happen to also have Brock Purdy, Josh Allen, or someone with an absurd matchup (like Jordan Love).
It's still good to know what to expect. The Buccaneers' defense has been solid, but those numbers might be inflated by some bad offenses. They blitz a ton, but Bryce Young is the second-best QB in the NFL against the blitz.
The Bucs also don't get home a lot despite that, with the second-worst pressure rate in the NFL. And it's not like Young struggles against pressure because he's been pressured more than anyone else. Expect Young to keep rolling, even if he doesn't light up the box score to the same degree.
Verdict: Keep starting him until further notice
The Buccaneers do not defend wide receivers all that well. They're 19th against the position in fantasy, so they're below average. That means Tetairoa McMillan will have plenty of opportunities today against this defense.
The Jalen Coker factor means that McMillan will not get a dominant target share, but that doesn't really hamper him too much. He was out-targeted last week and still scored 14.6 PPR points. That's a good number.
As mentioned, Bryce Young should be just fine, so there shouldn't be any reason the Panthers' passing attack slows down. That's good news for McMillan owners, who can expect another double-digit performance this week.

title: Fantasy Football Start or Sit: Jalen Coker, Chuba Hubbard & Darren Waller
full_text:
It's been five games, so it's a big enough sample to say that the Carolina Panthers are an elite fantasy football offense. Every week, they have multiple players worth starting. This would've seemed impossible in the preseason, especially with Jonathon Brooks hurt.
Jalen Coker, Chuba Hubbard, and Darren Waller are among those players. This week, against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, should you start or sit these players?
Jalen Coker is in a difficult spot. He's the WR2 on this roster even though he does kind of match Tetairoa McMillan in production when both are healthy. That gives him a boost in defensive coverage, as he won't often draw the best cornerback.
It also means he's not going to get as much love from Bryce Young, although there will be plenty of weeks in which he does. But ultimately, Coker has produced when he's been healthy, and he is healthy.
The Buccaneers' secondary is not great against wide receivers this year, so Coker is not a bad play unless your wide receiver room is just incredibly deep.
Chuba Hubbard has been one of the best fantasy football running backs this year. He's getting a good amount of yardage and scoring at a ridiculous pace. That might slow, but there's no reason to expect a complete dropoff this week.
The Tampa Bay defense is ridiculously stout against the run. However, they're weak against the pass, and the Panthers have been passing to open up the second-half run game against tired defenses. That should happen here.
Plus, unless you somehow have two top-10 running backs also on your roster, you can't afford to bench Hubbard for a less-than-ideal matchup.
The Panthers have too many tight ends to worry about, making starting Darren Waller on a given week a tough sell. He is the premier passing target among the three, but the Panthers use the other two so much for blocking.
Waller is essentially touchdown-dependent at this point. He is likely to get a few catches, but unless he scores, then six or seven points isn't going to cut it. However, the Buccaneers are a good matchup for tight ends, and the tight end position is notoriously hard to manage in fantasy.
Verdict: Sit unless you're in desperate need of a Hail Mary attempt

title: NFL Insider Confirms 'Aggressive' Bears Have Begun Pursuit of Khalil Mack Trade
full_text:
As Chicago Bears fans dream of a potential Khalil Mack reunion, it appears the team is has already taken a step toward making it happen.
On Sunday, FOX's NFL insider, Jay Glazer, revealed that the Bears have already put in a call to the Los Angeles Chargers to inquire about the availability of Mack.
Glazer also noted that he believes the Bears are going to be the most aggressive team in the NFC North when it comes to making a move at the trade deadline.
"I think of the teams in the NFC North, there's going to be one team that's going to be really aggressive when it comes to the trade deadline. I think that will be the Chicago Bears," he said .
"I know they've already talked to, you know, the Chargers, saying, 'Hey, what about a guy like Khalil Mack?' I think they're going to be very aggressive. Ryan Poles, that's what he does. More aggressive than the other teams in that division."
Glazer's report came on the same day ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport reported that the Bears are expected to have interest in Mack as the deadline approaches.
"There is expected to be interest in Mack from teams such as the Chicago Bears, but the Los Angeles Chargers have given no indication that they are willing to make any trades at this time," the ESPN reporters wrote. "The Chargers (0-6) insist they are trying to win games, but that doesn't mean they're not going to get calls on Mack in the coming weeks."
Trade buzz has been swirling around the Chargers because of the fact that they're 0-6 and going nowhere.
Mack in particular has been widely speculated about because he checks the boxes of someone who could get traded because he's on a one-year contract and may hang up his cleats after 2026.
There are so many reasons why bringing Khalil Mack back makes sense for the Bears. The feeling of nostalgia in bringing a fan-favorite back to Chicago would be overwhelming.
For starters, Chicago needs more depth at edge rusher. The Bears have gotten solid production out of the position this season, but they could certainly use more.
Mack has shown he's got plenty of gas left in the tank with three sacks in six games this season and acquiring him would give the Bears an edge rushers room capable of pushing this defense forward.
Not to mention, we've seen how quickly things can change there in the last few weeks, when the Bears lost Dayo Odeyingbo to injured reserve and Montez Sweat to a suspension.
Thankfully, Kyler Gordon has turned into Reggie White , which has helped cover for their losses. However, Chicago can't depend on that all the time.
Then we have the aspect of how much adding Mack boosts the culture, which is already good to begin with. Mack is a leader and his mere presence just makes this team better.
Lastly, there is no long-term commitment necessary here, which is important to note because the Bears' financial outlook isn't great, with Over The Cap noting the Bears are currently slated to be $1 million over the cap next offseason.
Mack is scheduled to be a free agent in 2027, and there's also a chance he may retire after he mulled doing so after last season .
Add it all up and it's not hard to see why trading for Mack is a no-brainer decision for the Bears. Now, general manager Ryan Poles just has to seal the deal to bring Mack home.
Mike Moraitis is a freelance writer who has covered the NFL for major outlets such as Sports Illustrated and The Sporting News. He has previously written for USA TODAY Sports Media Group and FanSided, and got his start in sports media at Bleacher Report.

title: NFC North Standings: Where Bears Sit After Vikings, Packers & Lions Games in Week 7
full_text:
The Chicago Bears were idle on Sunday after playing their Week 7 game on Thursday night, and that left Chicago watching their division rivals over the course of the day.
Of course, the Bears emerged victorious over the New England Patriots in their Week 7 contest, 30-24, and moved to 5-2. As a result, they were sitting in second place going into the weekend.
The other three NFC North teams were in action on Sunday, with the Minnesota Vikings taking on the Indianapolis Colts and the Green Bay Packers facing the Detroit Lions.
Here's a look at the results of those contests, followed by the updated NFC North standings.
In what was one of the ugliest games of the Sunday slate, the Vikings found a way to beat the lowly Indianapolis Colts, 16-10.
The Vikings managed just 275 yards of total offense and could not get much going on that side of the ball, but Brian Flores' defense is really, really good and shut the Colts down throughout, limiting Indianapolis to just 218 total yards.
With the win, the Vikings moved to 6-0 and Minnesota is the only unbeaten team in the NFC, and one of two unbeaten teams in the NEL, along with the Kansas City Chiefs, who play on Sunday night.
What a bizarre game this was.
Both teams did everything they could to hand the game over to the other and there were countless questionable penalties, especially on the Packers, miscues and terrible coaching decisions (we're looking at you, Dan Campbell).
Nevertheless, the Lions managed to be slightly less awful than the Packers en route to a 20-17 victory on a field goal in the closing seconds.
Fun fact: Packers kicker Trey Smack has two field goal attempts of 35 yards or less that have been missed or blocked and the rest of the league has one combined this entire season, according to ESPN Research .
1. Vikings (6-0 2. Bears (5-2) 3. Lions (4-2) 4. Packers (4-3)
With the Lions beating the Packers, the Bears hold on to second place going into Week 8, but they failed to gain any ground on Minnesota, who has a multi-game lead over Chicago.
Meanwhile, the Packers' loss sends them to the cellar in the division and the Lions move out of that spot into third place.
The Bears draw the Seattle Seahawks on Monday night in Week 8 while the Packers will take on the Carolina Panthers on Thursday night and the Lions will host the Vikings on Sunday.

title: Five Ways the Bears Can Improve Even After Starting Season 5-2
full_text:
Any team can improve, even those among the unbeaten ranks.
The Bears were 24-point losers just three weeks ago at Green Bay and even after consecutive impressive wins they can still find ways to up their performance.
Here are five big ways Caleb Williams and the offense or Dennis Allen's defense can improve after the mini-bye week when they go to Seattle, and when they return home Nov. 8 to play resurgent Tampa Bay.
Bears’ WR Luther Burden III with the fumble and the Panthers recover. pic.twitter.com/T5o12SZuDn
This may easily have escaped the attention of some but only the Chargers and Saints had lost more fumbles than the Bears going into Week 7 games. Last year the Bears lost seven fumbles for the entire season. This year they have already lost six, egregious and otherwise.
Love D'Andre Swift but another fumble? pic.twitter.com/h2qrVLcWOy
This is a recording, stop dropping passes. Yes, Johnson said they had to stop this after the loss to the Rams in the playoffs season. He even got rid of one of their worst perpetrators, Olamide Zaccheaus. Yet, whether it's Rome Odunze or Colston Loveland or one of the backs, someone always seems to come up with a dropped pass. They finished with the fifth-most drops last year with 29. So they have improved -- they had the sixth most dropped passes going into Sunday games.
Colston Loveland with a bad 3rd down drop. One play later makes up for it with a big time catch. Unflappable. First 5 games 13 catches for 110 yds the last two games 13 catches for 134 yards. 📈 #DaBears #Bears pic.twitter.com/H3tsHimRbO
Going into Sunday's games, the Bears had the fifth-most penalties with 53, although they were certain to move down in ranks with some other teams just behind them and still playing this week. They were worst most of last season, but this is still an embarrassing level.
"I'm proud of the fact that right now -- we're not playing very clean football, very disciplined football from a penalty standpoint there's too many pre-snap penalties and there's too many holding penalties right now for us - but despite those, our guys still find a way to get back on track and overcome," Johnson said. "I've been a part of teams where you get one penalty and that just derails the whole drive and that's it. That's not what's happening to us right now. I look forward to the day that we clean those up and see what that looks like.”
🚨 #Bears WR Jahdae Walker was EJECTED from the game after headbutting a defender. 🐻 Completely unnecessary and unacceptable. There’s no room for that kind of mistake, especially in a close game. Chicago HAS to clean up these undisciplined penalties moving forward. #DaBears … pic.twitter.com/2ctc7ICOPP
Typical was the first drive of the game against Atlanta. They went 67 yards for a touchdown on the possession and had three penalties, including a hold on Theo Benedet.
It might seem like missed tackles would be their biggest problem, especially after the way they handled the short Patriots pass before halftime on Thursday. But they actually were tied for 11th fewest missed tackles going into Sunday and stand to be even better after those games. Actually, their problem has been defending deeper throws and no one would be surprised by this after the way they let the Packers complete long throws and even did it against Atlanta the following week. On Thursday, the Patriots tried to test this and Tyrique Stevenson got back to knock one down. Perhaps they are improving or will. According to NFLGSIS statistics, the Bears have given up the fifth highest average gain per completion on deep passes to the right side (16.86), the third highest average gain on deep passes over the middle (29.13), and the 11th highest gain per passes completed against them to the left side (13.69). Their pass defense overall hasn't been great, as rookie safety Dillon Thieneman is their top tackler with 43. If the safety makes the most tackles, it can be a sign things are not going right on defense -- although Dennis Allen does call on his safeties to be all over the field.
Jordan Love updated career vs Bears 136/203 Cmp/Att | 67.0 Cmp% 1,892 Pass Yds | 9.3 Yards/Att +81.8 Total EPA | 0.41 EPA/Play 15 TDs | 2 Ints 7.4 TD% | 1.0 Int% 117.3 Passer Rtg pic.twitter.com/fXuFcGCBJ6 https://t.co/GOajAYrNKC
Even after they improved and were 4-for-5 and 3-for-4 the last two games in the red zone at scoring TDs, the Bears still rated only 19th in TD percentage for the red zone going into Sunday. At the root of their problem is their inability to move the pile in close on runs. D'Andre Swift is tied for the third-most rushing TDs inside the 10 in the NFL with six but he averages 1.85 yards per run inside the 10. Derrick Henry, for instance, has averaged 2.5 yards per rush inside the 10 and leads in TD runs inside the 10. Swift has only 13 yards on 12 carries inside the 5. Kyle Monangai also is below 2.0 yards per run inside the 10, althoug he has been hurt the last two weeks. It's not a terrible problem and they can offset this with short passes or Williams keepers. Other teams have similar issues in close. KC's Kenneth Walker, for instance, averages only 1.6 yards inside the 10. But they can make things much easier for themselves by getting more TD runs inside the 5.
This problem could be over with Williams back healthy, and definitely could be once Monangai is healthy again after toe and finger issues.
In red zone trips with Caleb Williams the Bears are scoring TDs at an 80% rate The only 2 non-TD drives were a fumble and a kneel down https://t.co/cDlVP35TxV

title: Give Ben Johnson Extra Time to Prepare and Here's What Bears Can Expect
full_text:
A day after Ben Johnson's Bears beat one half of the Super Bowl XL teams, he paused to look at what's coming with extra time now to prepare to face the other team from  last year's title game, the Seahawks.
"Thought they did a really nice job; finding a way to get a win like that on a short week," Johnson said of his team. "Takes a lot of mental preparation over the course of a few short days to make sure we download the game plan and put it to life like they did.
"Credit to the staff as well for getting that job done and I’m looking forward to taking a step back and catching our breath here this weekend.  Gives us a chance to evaluate where we're at personnel wise, schematically. Almost like a mini-bye week in a lot of regards also."
Is this necessarily good for the staff, though? The rest always helps players, no doubt. However, Johnson's ability to get the Bears ready for Thursday's win over New England with only a few days of work kept in line with a trend he has shown in coaching.
Now, he faces the opposite situation with the extended mini-bye weekend in his pocket. There's extra time for Seattle to prepare, as well. Seattle's extra time is very limited, though, since they're playing a Sunday night game with the Chiefs, followed by the Monday night game against the Bears.
I owe you honesty. Chicago would be my pick to come out of the NFC today. Can’t apologize for it. Ben Johnson is in his bag, and Caleb Williams may be the most talented QB in the conference. I just lost likability points, didn’t I? pic.twitter.com/ekMBq5kqGi
A couple of trends are at work in this case for Bears fans to consider with their team, and also another with the Seahawks.
The one trend with Seattle is how coach Mike Macdonald has been very good at getting his team ready when given extra time, even if it is just one extra day. Meanwhile, the same cannot entirely be said for Johnson with the Bears.
Macdonald is in his third season as Seattle coach, and during his tenure Seattle is 11-3 when he has more than the normal week to get the team ready for a game.
You know who else has been the villains? The Patriots w/ Brady & The Chiefs w/ Mahomes. They were villains for many years. And I’ve been hoping and praying that I’d get to watch my Bears be the villains one day. 🐻 ⬇️
Considering Seattle missed the playoffs with a 10-7 record in his first year, was 3-3 this season going into Sunday night this season besides their 2025 Super Bowl season,  the11 wins Macdonald has had with extra time accounts for a huge amount of their victories.  Of the wins they've had under Macdonald, 40.7% came during a longer work week. This includes their playoffs and the Super Bowl last season.
The other side, and of more concern for the Bears, is how Johnson's team has done when he had extra time. The Bears are only 3-4 in games when Johnson has extra time to get them ready.
Are they putting too much into game plans? Some of the opponents have been very strong, and that has to be taken into account, but 3-4 when your team is 17-9 in two seasons is not saying much for his ability to use the extra time wisely.
Baldy, can we all agree Ben is a top 3 play caller in the league?
If there is a ray of hope here, it's how Johnson is trending up.
The Bears are 2-0 this season when he had extra time. They were only 1-4 last year.
The only win the Bears had last season when Johnson had extra time was their bye week and they needed a late Jayden Daniels fumble to beat Washington 25-24. They lost to the Rams in the playoffs with one less day to prepare after they had beaten the Packers. They also lost the season opener to Minnesota, their regular-season game to Green Bay following their Black Friday win over the Eagles, and then to the 49ers after they beat the Packers at Soldier Field in the regular season.
However, this year they beat the Eagles with an extra day to prep on Monday night, and also won their opener over Carolina with all offseason and preseason to prepare.
Former NFL Great Mark Schlereth goes all in on Ben Johnson. The league has finally seen behind the fake tough guy curtain. pic.twitter.com/kmxbV12ycP
Much can go into these numbers beyond prep time, of course.  The opponent and how they lost matters. For instance, they lost the game last year at San Francisco but no one is going to blame the way Johnson had the offense prepared. They had 38 points. It was the defense faltering.
Perhaps Johnson just needed time as the head coach to get the trend working his way. Another number says this could be the case. That one is how he did prepping his offense in Detroit when he had an extra day.
Although Johnson wasn't head coach, he was the coordinator who called plays and came up with game plans — with head coach Dan Campbell overseeing, of course.
"The Bears believe in him" @howaboutafresca and @SwollenDome make the case that Ben Johnson is the best head coach in the NFL right now pic.twitter.com/qJft2l644B
The Lions were 13-4 when Johnson was offensive coordinator and had more than a week to prep. In fact, some of Detroit's most impressive offensive efforts occurred while Johnson had extra time to prepare and was a coordinator.
One of their biggest regular-season wins and blowouts was at Dallas in 2024 when they won 47-9 after they had extra time to get ready.
The great majority of Johnson's "40-burgers" over three seasons with Detroit came when he had extra time to get the offense ready. They scored 42 on Seattle, 41 at San Francisco, 42 against the Chargers in L.A., 40 against Carolina, and 41 at home against the Bears with extra time in victories. They also had 42 against Buffalo in a loss.
This could all work the Bears' way on Monday Night Football in Seattle, but something must give because Seahawks will have a similar trend working their way.

title: Bears Linked to Khalil Mack in Latest Trade Rumor From ESPN Insiders
full_text:
There is nothing Chicago Bears fans would love more than to see the team pull off a trade for Los Angeles Chargers edge rusher Khalil Mack.
There's a few reasons why that's the case, with the biggest one being Mack is hugely popular in Chicago after his four seasons with the team before he was traded to Los Angeles.
But the Bears also have a need at edge rusher, where Chicago needs more depth, especially with Dayo Odeyingbo set to miss a few more games due to injury , and with Montez Sweat not having the kind of season Chicago was expecting.
ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport listed off a slew of trade candidates ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline next month and Mack was among them.
Taking it a step further, the NFL insiders said that the Bears are one of the teams "expected" to have interest in Mack, although they also note that the Chargers "have given no indication" of interest in parting ways with Mack.
"There is expected to be interest in Mack from teams such as the Chicago Bears, but the Los Angeles Chargers have given no indication that they are willing to make any trades at this time," the ESPN reporters said. "The Chargers (0-6) insist they are trying to win games, but that doesn't mean they're not going to get calls on Mack in the coming weeks."
It's nice that the Chargers are still trying to win games, but the fact of the matter is they haven't been able to do that entering their bye in Week 7.
Los Angeles' season is cooked and they should be looking to sell off some pieces. Mack is a prime candidate to be one of those pieces for a few reasons.
Not only is he in the final year of his contract, Mack has also contemplated retirement in the past , which makes it more probable he won't be back in L.A. in 2027.
With Mack in the twilight of his career, it's hard to fathom him being keen on playing out the string with the Chargers and it's conceivable he could want a trade to a contender, something Chicago looks like after seven games.
Mack views his time with the Bears fondly , so it's possible he may be intrigued by the opportunity to return, and if that's the case, the Chargers could oblige his desire out of respect for him.
Mack still has plenty left in the tank with three sacks in 2026, so he could definitely provide a boost for the Bears. If he becomes available, Chicago should absolutely bring Mack home.
Mike Moraitis is a freelance writer who has covered the NFL for major outlets such as Sports Illustrated and The Sporting News. He has previously written for USA TODAY Sports Media Group and FanSided, and got his start in sports media at Bleacher Report.

title: Colts Trade Rumors Should Have Bears Making Call to Indianapolis For 2 Players
full_text:
The Chicago Bears need help along the interior of the defensive line and the Indianapolis Colts reportedly may have two good interior defenders available for trade.
According to ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport , the Colts could unload both DeForest Buckner and Grover Stewart before the NFL trade deadline next month.
"Nearly guaranteed to leave Indianapolis after the season, a decision to unload players would almost certainly include Buckner," the NFL insiders wrote.
"Also in the final year of his contract with a base salary that pays him the rest of $11.8 million, Stewart is expected to be a trade target," the ESPN reporters added.
It's not hard to see why the Colts are likely to deal both players.
The Colts look primed for a fire sale this year and a rebuild next year after firing general manager Chris Ballard recently.
Stewart, 33, and Bucker, 32, are both in the final years of their contracts and aren't likely to stick around for a rebuild.
The Colts would be wise to unload both before they leave in free agency for nothing next offseason. The draft capital acquired will assist in the Colts' rebuild, also.
The trade of Gervon Dexter continues to look worse by the week. Losing Dexter has seriously hurt the Bears' interior pass-rush, which has notched just one sack over seven games.
Chicago's run defense hasn't been great, either. Granted, the Bears do have a top-10 unit, but that's misleading because opponents aren't running on them much. Going into Week 7, Chicago had the second-fewest rushing attempts against.
When digging a bit deeper, the Bears are giving up the ninth-most rushing yards per attempt and their run-stop win rate is 27%, which ranks 28th, per ESPN.
Buckner is obviously the more attractive piece given the fact that he's a very good pass-rusher and a solid run defender. Buckner has four sacks in six games, which is three more than Bears interior defenders have in seven.
But with the better option comes a more expensive cost. We can see the Colts getting a third-round pick for Buckner in a trade that sees Indy send a pick back in the deal. If not, a fourth-rounder and then a lower pick sounds about right.
Stewart would be a fine consolation prize. He doesn't offer much in the pass-rush, but he is a gap-filler who can make a dent in the run game. Stewart will probably cost a fifth-round pick, and perhaps a fourth in a deal that involves a pick swap.

title: NFL Hits Caleb Williams and Jahdae Walker with Fines for Falcons Game
full_text:
Jahdae Walker's special teams plays were costly for the Bears against Atlanta in terms of yards lost due to penalties for a Week 6 victory, and they were also costly for him personally.
What quarterback Caleb Williams wore in the game was also costly.
The NFL fined Walker, a second-year Bears receiver, $5,620 for roughing the kicker and also fined him $5,620 more for unnecessary roughness stemming from the use of his helmet when the Bears beat Atlanta 31-23 on Oct. 18.
These were the second and third fines of the season for Walker. In the season opener, the NFL had fined him $5,620 for taunting against the Carolina Panthers.
Walker hit the plant leg of Atlanta punter Jake Bailey with 12:48 left in the third quarter after a punt, and the Bears were penalized on the play, resulting in a first down for the Falcons.
Jahdae Walker screwed up with this headbutt. But he shouldn’t have been ejected. Seems a bit extreme. #DaBears pic.twitter.com/DkA0ubkEqr
The other play involving Walker against Atlanta was a bit more costly. On the first play of the fourth quarter, Walker was involved in kickoff coverage and head-butted Atlanta receiver Chris Blair after the play, directly in front of the officials. He was flagged for unnecessary rougheness/using his helmet. Also, it resulted in Walker being ejected from the game.
If there was any satisfaction at all for Walker in this it was that Blair was also fined by the league, but it was for an earlier play in the game with 8:15 left in the first quarter when he threw a blindside block. The fine for this was $5,972.
Jahdae Walker runs into the punter Ben Johnson is pissed pic.twitter.com/zJGvpyLSLE
The Bears have been relatively free of fines this season but this wasn't their first fine from this game.  The NFL fined Williams $11,941 for wearing Caddix cleats, an NFL dress code violation.  The Caddix cleats have been relatively popular around the league this year and it has been reported about 40 players have been wearing them.
The NFL has contractual agreements  for players to wear adidas, NIKE and Under Armour cleats but not Caddix. Williams, receiver Cooper Kupp, and quarterback Joe Flacco are among the players who have been wearing the Caddix cleats.
It wasn't their first fine for uniform violation of this season. Cornerback Jaylon Johnson was fined $5,971 against the Philadelphia Eagles for wearing an unapproved streamer towel.
Walker's fine was the first for an on-field Bears incident since Tyrique Stevenson was fined $22,342 in Week 2 against the Vikings for using his helmet in a tackle.
Caleb Williams was fined by the NFL over $11K for his Caddix cleats he wore against the Atlanta Falcons for being in violation of the NFL Uniform and Equipment Rules. 📸: Getty pic.twitter.com/wf2F5VeRRu

title: Who Should Bears Fans Root for in Week 7 After Beating the Patriots on Thursday Night?
full_text:
For the first time in the 2026 NFL season, Chicago Bears fans can rest easy going into Sunday. The Bears pulled of a sensational primetime win over the New England Patriots on Thursday Night Football and are now getting some well-deserved rest before their next game, a Monday Night Football showdown with the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks.
Sunday football is always a more carefree viewing experience for fans when their team already has a win in the books. However, there are still some matchups that Bears fans should have a rooting interest in, and that includes more than just division rivalries. With that in mind, here's a Week 7 rooting guide for Bears fans to follow once the action starts on Sunday.
At this point in the season, Bears fans should be rooting against the Green Bay Packers every week, and not just for rivalry reasons. They currently own the tiebreaker over the Bears after Chicago's disastrous Week 5 loss to the Packers , and that could come back to haunt them in what is expected to be a tight NFC Wild Card race. They still have one more game to play against each other, but the Packers could very well win that matchup, too.
The Lions could end up being a greater threat to the Bears' playoffs hopes than the Packers, but for now, Bears fans should root for Detroit.
Despite featuring one of the worst offenses in the NFL, the Vikings keep finding ways to win and at 5-0 they stand atop the NFC North. The rooting interest for Bears fans here is obvious. There's a lot of they need to make up if they're going to make a serious push for a second NFC North division title , and seeing the Vikings fall to 5-1 this week would be a good start.
Unfortunately for Bears fans, that's not likely to happen. The Colts are in complete disarray after an embarrassing Week 6 loss to the Tennessee Titans , and star defensive tackle DeForest Buckner's postgame comments suggested a team that had already given up on the season. Go ahead and root for the Colts, but Colts fans would probably tell you to keep your expectations low.
If the Bears can't win the NFC North this year, they'll be battling for a Wild Card spot in January, and that's where they'll need help from other teams. The Seahawks are currently in a precarious position at just 3-3 on the season and in second place in the NFC West. But it's far too early to count out the defending champs.
Expect Seattle to eventually figure things out and string some wins together. It's crucial for the Bears' playoffs hopes then that they first rack up a few avoidable losses like this one. Plus, the Bears face Seattle next week. Getting the Seahawks when they're in the middle of a slump would only help the Bears' chances.
A former Marine and Purdue Boilermaker, Pete has been covering the Chicago Bears since 2022 as a senior contributor on BearsTalk. He lives with his wife, two kids and loyal dog.

title: Do Bears Play Today? Remaining Schedule, Predictions for Rest of Chicago's 2026 Season
full_text:
The Chicago Bears are sitting at 5-2 after seven games and, going into Sunday, are in second place in the NFC North.
The Bears' latest victory came against the New England Patriots, when quarterback Caleb Williams outdueled fellow young quarterback Drake Maye to a 30-24 finish.
Williams' impressive effort against the Patriots has the national media absolutely in love with what it is seeing from the former No. 1 overall pick, who continues to make the case he should be ranked among the NFL's elite at the position.
Now, a look at the rest-of-season schedule for Chicago as it tries to navigate its way to the postseason in 2026.
No, the Bears are not playing on Sunday.
Chicago already took part in its Week 7 game on Thursday night and the Bears will now enjoy 11 days of rest before their next contest, which will come against the Seattle Seahawks on Monday, Nov. 2.
The long rest is needed, as the Bears have some key players banged-up they are hoping to get back, including running back Kyle Monangai and linebacker T.J. Edwards, both of whom have missed multiple games.
Here's the rest of the Bears' 2026 schedule, along with our win-loss predictions for each game.
Week 8: at Seattle Seahawks - Monday, Nov. 2, 8:15 p.m. ET, ESPN (win)

title: Montez Sweat Returns to Defense Getting Its Sacks From Kyler Gordon
full_text:
On Friday as the Bears bid farewell to tight end Cole Kmet for the season, they welcomed the return of the player with the biggest contract on their roster.
Oh yeah, Montez Sweat. Remember him? He was reinstated by the commissioner after his suspension for a performance enhancing drug policy violation.
Their pass rush hasn't exactly collapsed without the player regarded as their leading pass rusher. If anything can be said for Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen, it's that he knows how to make lemonade out of lemons, and he did it once again by using subs and with blitzes.
Allen went to more blitzing and switched up the fronts repeatedly over the last two weeks without Sweat available, and also with Dayo Odeyingbo on injured reserve with a quad injury. The pressure actually amped up. Largely, it's the result of getting Kyler Gordon back and blitzing their slot cornerback, along with other DBs or linebackers.
I want the record to show that while both QBs played exceptional tonight, Caleb was doing it against a borderline top 5 defense whereas Maye was doing it against Kyler Gordon and The Backyardigans https://t.co/Nz4SwVKFbR
Gordon has four sacks in two games, or as The Athletic's Dan Wiederer pointed out in the locker room after Thursday's win, the Bears DB has four sacks in five days.
It makes you wonder what Gordon can do with 10 games and numerous days still to go. And with Sweat now rejoining the rush to often line up on the same side of the field as Gordon, double-teaming   the edge rusher might not be possible if a team wants to block a blitzing DB.
In case you're counting or thinking of it, the NFL record for sacks by a defensive back in a season is 9 1/2 by Jamal Adams with Seattle in 2020.
Kyler Gordon isn’t just a pass blitzer. He can hold up against tight ends in the run  game. Uncommon blend of strength speed athleticism and quicks. #DaBears #Bears pic.twitter.com/ub2NiPxoKP
"That's only four," Gordon said after Thursday's game. "That's not enough."
It's twice as many as Sweat had in five games, in case anyone is counting. Gordon has tied teammate Austin Booker for the team lead, and it's Allen he has to thank for it.
"I appreciate it man," Gordon said. "I couldn't wait to do this together. I appreciate him putting me in a position to do that and that's just the beginning, so. ..."
Dennis Allen kept the Falcons off balance by using varying his pressure patterns. Here, the Bears run a simple double B-gap blitz with the Mike Hug Rushing the RB. Chicago assumes the TE will stay in the protection because of the pressure and "steal" his defender in the post.… pic.twitter.com/vEwsSXlJ3n
The blitzing Bears are going to be a thing even with Sweat returning. This was apparent in the playoffs last year as Allen finally had Gordon available after only three games played in the 17-game regular season due to injuries.  He turned Gordon loose on the Rams and it worked to a large extent.
While Gordon missed games with a calf injury this year, Allen didn't really say much about his slot cornerback returning before he was ready. Allen just made do with what he had, the same way he has done it without Sweat for two weeks and the way he did it without numerous players in the past.
The Allen defense with more speed now should be aggressive regardless of who they have on the field. They currently rank eighth in sacks per game at 2.7. That's probably a better stat to look at than sack total because some teams have played two less games than the Bears at this point. The positive is their pass rush win rate, which was near or at the bottom of the league most of last year, has risen dramatically. They rank sixth in this ESPN analytic, at 57%.
First 4th down of the game. 8 guys showing blitz, only 4 come. Jackson, Bush, Hicks & Booker drop out. Hardy crashes all the way to the center confusing the RT. Thieneman occupies the confused RT & TE w/ Kyler untouched off the edge. Another patented DA simulated pressure. #Bears pic.twitter.com/z8ei2hppsR
Allen has blitzed the eighth highest percentage at 34.2% through seven games, per Pro Football Reference. Unlike in some other seasons when they supplemented no rush with blitzing, the Bears are getting pressure. They are fifth in pressure percentage at 28%.
"I think these guys, they're really coming in there," coach Ben Johnson said. "I think they're building their confidence, too. I think they know that they can be pretty good.
"When you have these guys running free, I think they believe in the scheme. They see that, ‘Holy cow, DA's doing a great job scheming this stuff up, and we're coming in free for some sacks here.' I think we're heading in the right direction.”
It shows in overall defensive statistics heading into Sunday's games. The Bears are 11th in yards allowed, but it's actually less because they have a game or even two on some teams. They're eighth in points allowed and eighth in scoring on offense. They've allowed the second fewest first downs (107) even though they have played more games than all teams except New England.
The pressure can eventually lead to more takeaways.
D'Marco Jackson PICKS OFF Maye in the end zone. BEARS BALL. NEvsCHI on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/wq8LKTC3lX
Everything hinges on what has been an effective run defense so far. They're sixth against the run a year after they were 27th. Of course, they're not not leading in takeaways like last year, as they're 13th with 10, but Johnson sees that coming if the pressure and the run defense on first and second downs continues at this pace.
"I do think there's an element of the more off schedule we can get offenses on first down, the better off we're going to be in terms of ending their drive," Johnson said. "I hate to look back at last year, but we're a better defense than we were a year ago.
"The biggest difference is we're not taking the ball away quite as much at this point of the season. If we can continue to harp on that ball production and getting those takeaways, I think you're going to see some really good defensive play, some more consistent defensive play."
And it can't hurt getting back their No. 1 pass rusher, even if he is only No. 4 now on the team in sacks with two.
Perhaps now they can used Gordon a little more at what he's there to do, and that's cover slot receivers. But not too much. They don't want to let QBs get too comfortable.
Callers are riled up after Bears defensive end Montez Sweat got hit with a 2-game suspension. "I work for a job, if I get drug tested and I fail, I lose my job," a caller says. "He's a millionaire. It's a wrap. You're a bust. You did nothing for us. Just beat it. Go home." pic.twitter.com/sYQBaxd7Oj

title: Bengals Big Betting Favorites Against Titans, Largest Spread Line of Cincinnati's Season So Far
full_text:
Oddsmakers aren't expecting the Bengals to have much trouble with the Week 8 opponent. Cincinnati is a 10.5-point betting favorite on DraftKings Sportsbook against the Tennessee Titans on Sunday at home. The point total is set at 46.5 overall with Cincinnati -625 on the moneyline.
They are massive betting favorites to win the home game on Sunday. Cincinnati just covered for the first time after three consecutive missed spreads this season.
The Bengals are 3-3 against the spread in 2026, and this marks the largest betting spread they've been favored by since the season began. Another AFC win has to happen against Robert Saleh's 1-6 outfit. This betting line has ballooned to double digits after opening at 6.5 points to start the season.
Cincinnati just beat a much-better team in the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday, albeit without star quarterback Lamar Jackson.
"I think this was a really good team," Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said after a 35-13 win on Sunday. "This is as well-rounded [of] a team as you play in the NFL in all three phases, with the talent and coaches they have. So, I think to go on the road and get a win like this, it just reaffirms that we can be who we think we are. It doesn't mean it's going to happen if we show up next week and don't have a great week of practice, or go lay an egg – then what was this one for?
"So, I am confident that we built this team with the players that understand that and don't need to be reminded of that. They know, 'Hey, this was a great win, but it's one win in 17 games. We have to be able to quickly move on to Tennessee and put together another great performance.'"
Cincinnati is 4-2 on the 2026 campaign and can continue making a contender case this weekend.
They battle the Titans during a 1 p.m. ET kickoff at home on Sunday.

title: 6 Winners and 2 Losers From Bengals' Dominant Comeback Win Over Ravens
full_text:
After an abysmal first half, the Bengals scored 35 unanswered points in the second half to blowout their division rival Ravens 35-13 in Baltimore. They're 4-2 on the season following the win.
Here are six winners and two losers from Sunday's victory.:
Burrow started the game rattled from the Ravens blitz. That changed drastically from the moment the second-half started as he completed 10-straight passes and led 5-straight touchdown drives.
He connected with seven different receivers in the game, finishing 22-of-30 for 292 yards, four touchdowns, no interceptions and a passer rating of 143.3.
A good football team does not look as unprepared coming out of a bye week as the Bengals did on Sunday. Head coach Zac Taylor had two weeks to get this Bengals team prepared to face the Ravens, and instead they looked completely undisciplined.
Throughout the entire first half the offense managed only three first downs and 59 total yards. They only possessed the ball for 7:40. The Ravens had the ball for 22:40.
Tee Higgins did not record a catch in the first half, and it is a major reason why the offense failed to gain any ground to start. That changed in the second half as he recorded four catches in the first 10 minutes of the third quarter for 61 yards and a touchdown.
With the Ravens defense focusing heavily on Ja'Marr Chase, Higgins took advantage with six receptions for 148 yards and a touchdown.
Not once, not twice, but three times the Bengals defense surrendered a first-down on third and long. On the games opening drive, Tyler Huntley found Zay Flowers on 3rd & 9 who diced through the Bengals defense for a 48-yard score.
Later in the first half, Huntley found Flowers again on a 3rd and 16 for a 20-yard catch. The lack of discipline in long third down situations must improve.
The Bengals prized offseason addition showed up in a huge way yet again. Lawrence created havoc for the Ravens offense all day and played a big role in holding Derrick Henry to 45 yards on 17 carries.
He staked his exclamation point on the day with his fourth sack of the season late in the fourth quarter. Lawrence has transformed the defensive line for this team.
Mafe consistently created pressure in this game and proved the Bengals right to pay him in free agency over signing Trey Hendrickson to a lucrative deal. Mafe ended the day with 1.5 sacks, two quarterback hits and a tackle-for-loss.
He looks the part of an ascending player who's ceiling could match Hendrickson's as a pass rusher and possibly beyond considering his ability to defend the run. Hendrickson finished with two quarterback hits, but didn't have a tackle or a sack.
Gesicki only had 12 catches heading into Sunday's game, but he's a reliable red zone threat. That trend continued against the Ravens. He caught the Bengals first touchdown of the day on the opening drive of the third quarter that cut the deficit to 13-7. Gesicki has now hauled in five touchdowns on just 13 receptions, and continues his streak as one of Burrow's favorite red zone targets. He has a touchdown in five of six games.
Howell finally got home for his first NFL sack this week on a critical 3rd & 11. He has routinely created pressure as a true pass-rusher this season, and should only continue to improve with each week that passes.

title: 'I Was Pretty Lights Out' - Joe Burrow Assesses Ravens Performance In Rare Way As MVP Play Continues
full_text:
Joe Burrow is usually pretty coy about his play game-to-game, but there was no hiding his excitement about Sunday's showing. Burrow didn't get many chances in the first half across the 35-13 bullseye on Baltimore, but he lit them up in the second half.
The veteran MVP candidate passed for four TDs in consecutive games to round out 292 yards in the air (22-30 completions). Most of that in the final 30 minutes.
"I think I played really well," Burrow said. "The first half was what it was, and obviously would have liked to have some of those back, but we didn't turn the ball over. That played a big part, and the second half I think I was pretty lights out. Yeah, I'll watch the tape and ask me again on Wednesday, but I think for the most part I was pretty good.
"Just trying to treat every play like it's its own universe and trying to critically think about what's required of me on the play and where the defense is going to tell me to go with the football, and they're going to have to adapt quickly sometimes in a play depending on what the defense is showing or what presents."
According to Sumer Sports, Burrow went 16/18 for 249 yards and 4 touchdowns in the second half against the Ravens. Burrow's 21.24 Total EPA in the second half is the 4th best second-half performance out of 2,204 qualifiers since 2022.
When Cincinnati's back sat firmly on the wall. He answered the call and diced up the home team.
The Bengals had to win that game to keep a majority percentage playoff projection on the board and not fall to the bottom of the division. Add in no Lamar Jackson, and the opportunity was too good not to see vintage Burrow.
His Week 7 outing notched a 92.6 ESPN QBR, the second-best outing of the week so far and good enough to launch him up to third among all QBs on the season tally (77.6 overall).
If he keeps playing like this and the Bengals win at least 12-13 games, keeping the MVP trophy out of his hands will be hard.
"We know who we have to be, and we let our big-time players go and make big-time plays. That's what the NFL is all about. You know you can do all these different things, but at the end of the day, you just gotta go make plays, gotta execute what's called, and that's what we did," Burrow concluded.
Onto Tennessee and Week 8.

title: 'Got To Step This S*** Up' - Ja'Marr Chase Delivers Halftime Speech to Fuel Bengals Win Over Ravens
full_text:
Ja'Marr Chase hammered home his captain traits in a massive winning way on Sunday afternoon. The Bengals trailed Baltimore 13-0 at halftime, and he came into the locker room delivering an impassioned speech to get the offense going.
The team posted its fewest first-half yardage tally since 2018. Then they ripped off nearly 300 yards in the next 30 minutes for a 35-13 win.
It ignited Amariis Mims, Joe Burrow, and more.
"Really fired us up, man. I saw it in his eyes, man," Mims said to FOX 19 and more at his locker. "We were not gonna leave here without going in. And I've always said when One talks and he gets that fire in front of him, everybody needs to shut up and listen. Because, as I said, he is not only the best receiver in the NFL, but probably one of the best players in the NFL, in my opinion.
"So when a guy like that talks, you shut up, and you listen, because it's very important. And we all did hear it, and we all shut up, and we heard it. And it worked, we came back and scored 35 straight points, and they scored zero. So that was definitely a speech that I don't mind him giving every week. If that's the case, if we're gonna do that, we need to give it every week."
Mims had a big smile on his face as Burrow got sacked just one time thanks in large part to arguably the best pass-blocking right tackle in the NFL this season.
Chase delivered with five catches for 62 yards and a score, while Tee Higgins continued his elite efficiency season with six catches for 128 yards and his own end zone trip.
"We had 15 plays, maybe two or three possessions, and it didn't go our way at all," Chase said about the speech reasoning at his locker. "We had opportunities to get the ball out of our hands. Joe was putting up with too much pressure, and I came in here screaming, saying somebody got to make a play. Somebody got to make a play, and I told the offense we can't look at our defense the whole time. We got to step this s*** up and make something work."
“Yeah, Ja’Marr went in there and got after everybody a little bit and got everybody fired up. That certainly plays a part, but at the end of the day, we just executed," Burrow noted.
Cincinnati is up to seventh in the AFC after that win and is right on pace with the rest of the AFC North contenders. The next conference win opportunity awaits against Tennessee at home this week. A team the whole locker room wants to start faster against.

title: 'Just Bread And Butter' - Zac Taylor, Joe Burrow Detail How Bengals Offense Stormed Back Against Baltimore
full_text:
What a difference one break can make.
Cincinnati's offense sputtered in its limited opening chances against Baltimore on Sunday. But then things changed in a big way across the final 30 minutes of a 35-13 win.
The attack hummed through the air and scored five touchdowns to flash the ceiling this whole team can reach. Bengals head coach Zac Taylor and quarterback Joe Burrow dove into the second-half barrage after the rare win.
According to our Jay Morrison, it marked the Bengals' first second-half shutout since Week 14, 2023, in a 34-14 win against the Colts. They trailed 13-0 at the break.
"We got ourselves in rhythm, but we found some things that are just bread and butter, Cincinnati Bengals . We got ourselves in some really good rhythm. Found some really good runs too," Taylor noted. "I thought the backs and the lines did an excellent job in the run game, getting us what we needed. Maybe we didn't have a 15-yard run, but that's not what we needed in this game. We just needed to stay on track so we can come back and try to hit him with another throw."
The throwing hit indeed as the team dropped back 31 times and ran 20.
Burrow carved up the Ravens for 292 yards, four touchdowns, and no turnovers.
"We made some nice adjustments in the second half that I think helped us. And at the end of the day, we just executed and made a lot of plays," Burrow said about the big moments in the final few frames. "We just started calling some of our base stuff. O-line protected great, and really we just got the ball in Ja'Marr (Chase) and Tee's (Higgins) hands as many times as we could."
Cincinnati needed to keep pace in the AFC North as the only team playing in the division this week.
They leave right in the thick of the division race with Pittsburgh and Cleveland. Both of them won on Sunday, while Baltimore fell to last place.
"We know who we are. We know who we have to be, and we let our big-time players go and make big-time plays," Burrow said. "That's what the NFL is all about. You can do all these different things, but at the end of the day, you just gotta go make plays, gotta execute what's called, and that's what we did."
Cincinnati has boosted its playoff odds to over 75% after the win and has the third-best point differential in the AFC now.
Things are clicking with a few below .500 teams up next. The Titans roll into town next Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.
First time the #Bengals have blanked a team in a second half since Week 14, 2023 in a 34-14 win against the Colts.

title: Instant Takeaways: Joe Burrow Leads Bengals' Second-Half Rally in Dominant Win Over Ravens
full_text:
The Bengals rallied from a 13-0 halftime deficit to beat the Ravens 35-13 on Sunday in Baltimore.
Joe Burrow and the offense scored 35-straight points after going scoreless in the first half. He completed 22-of-30 passes for 292 yards and four touchdowns. The Bengals' defense recovered after getting torched in the first half.
Tyler Huntley threw for a career-high 298 yards, but the Bengals' defense sacked him four times and had a second half interception that helped Cincinnati pick up it's fourth win of the season. The Bengals are the 10th team in NFL history to be shutout in the first half and score 35 or more points in the second half.
The Bengals are 4-2 on the year and 1-1 in the division. Here are our instant takeaways from the win:
The Bengals dominated the second half. Burrow took over on offense and the defense shut down  Huntley, Derrick Henry and the Ravens' defense.
Burrow led a 9-play, 66-yard touchdown drive to start the third quarter. He found Mike Gesicki in the corner of the end zone to make it 13-7.
That was the first of 5-straight touchdowns for a Bengals offense that played its best ball of the season.
Burrow completed 16-of-18 passes for 249 yards and four touchdowns in the second half. Joe Flacco finished the game at quarterback.
Burrow has thrown for four touchdowns in back-to-back games.
Tee Higgins was outstanding in the second half. He didn't have a catch in the first half on one target. He caught six passes for 148 yards and the go-ahead touchdown that gave the Bengals the lead for good in the third quarter.
Higgins is off to the best start of his career. He had a 44-yard catch on an off-script play with Burrow that helped the Bengals take control of the game. Higgins averaged 24.7 yards-per-catch.
The Bengals were downright awful in the first half. Burrow completed just 6-of-12 passes for 43 yards. They punted three times. That included two questionable decisions on 4th-and-3 near midfield.
Everything that could go wrong, did go wrong for the Bengals. They did hold the Ravens to field goals on two long drives. That kept Cincinnati within two possessions. That allowed Burrow and the offense to grab control of the game in the third quarter with back-to-back touchdown drives.
Bengals tight end Erick All Jr. suffered a right knee injury in the third quarter and never returned. It's the same knee All suffered a torn ACL in during his rookie campaign. He missed the entire 2025 season due to the injury. Awful news for the third year tighrt end.
Starting safety Bryan Cook went down with a lower leg injury in the fourth quarter. The training staff was using a massage gun on his leg area on the sideline. Veteran Kyle Dugger re-injured his quad in the second half and didn't return. It's an injury he's been battling for weeks.
The Bengals return home to play the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 1 p.m. ET.
