title: Erick All Injures Same Troubled Knee Against Baltimore, Bengals Safety Hurt
full_text:
A brutal injury may have struck the Bengals offense.
Erick All is out for the rest of the Ravens contest with a knee injury after a bad history of knee injuries in his past. He suffered the issue in the second half on Sunday and went to the locker room shortly after. It's the same right knee that he's had those surgeries on in the past.
Bryan Cook got hurt in the second half and had trouble exiting the field, but did not go into the blue medical tent. He's been banged up in recent weeks along with backup safety Kyle Dugger, who went again as a couple of dings stack up late in the game.
"TE Erick All Jr. has a right knee injury. He has been declared out. S Kyle Dugger has a left quadriceps injury. He has been declared out," The team posted on X.
All had been working his way into more snaps for the Bengals recently and now hopefully isn't dealing with something major again.
He dropped major praise on Zac Taylor earlier this month on First Word With James Rapien.
"I look at Zac as that type of coach that's very transparent; he'll tell you how he feels, and it just kind of surprised me hearing 'I'm surprised he hasn't done that with people in the past,'" All said . "Zac's a great coach; if he sees something that he doesn't like or that he wants you to fix, he'll voice it to you whether in practice, game, cameras on, it doesn't matter, and that's what I love about him."
Cincinnati is trying to claw out its third-ever double-digit comeback against Baltimore to get to 4-2 on the season. They extended the lead to 21-13 as the offense has scored 21 unanswered points so far in the second half.
All would love to be part of that again soon with his great physicality.
"With the word physical in the dictionary is a picture of Erick All," Taylor said during OTAs this past summer. "Trying to put his face through somebody's soul."
Cincinnati is in the final minutes of its latest AFC North battle with Baltimore.

title: Sources: Latest on Shemar Stewart's Future Ahead of NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
Bengals defensive end Shemar Stewart was a healthy inactive on Sunday. The move comes just days after ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported that teams could be interested in trading for the former first round pick ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline.
"One surprise name a few teams are tracking is Cincinnati edge rusher Shemar Stewart," Fowler wrote . "The 2025 first-round pick is not a factor in the team's rotation right now. He has played 17 defensive snaps, well behind the total for the fourth defensive end, Cedric Johnson (83). And rookie second-rounder Cashius Howell has been impressive.
"Cincinnati typically doesn't move its young draft picks, but it would be surprising if the Bengals haven't received inquiries on Stewart, whose upside remains high."
Cincinnati selected Stewart 17th overall in the 2025 NFL Draft. He has one sack in three games and has only played 17 snaps on defense this season.
The Bengals are not actively shopping Stewart ahead of the trade deadline, multiple sources have confirmed. Stewart expects to remain in Cincinnati beyond the deadline and the Bengals believe he is going to help them win games this season.
Cincinnati has nine defensive linemen active for Sunday's game: Dexter Lawrence, Jonathan Allen, Kris Jenkins, TJ Slaton, BJ Hill, Myles Murphy, Boye Mafe, Cashius Howell, and Cedric Johnson.
Jenkins and Johnson have both developed and impressed the coaching staff this season. Combine that with Stewart missing all of training camp due to a knee injury he suffered on the first day of practice and the Bengals understand why the former first round pick has fallen out of the rotation.
The Bengals used a first round pick on Stewart for a reason. They knew it would take time for him to reach his full potential. There are coaches and members of the front office that are still very much in on the 22-year-old.
Murphy is set to become a free agent in March. A trio of Mafe, Howell and Stewart makes a lot of sense in 2027.
From a financial standpoint, they've paid him just over 68% of his rookie contract ($13 of $19 million).
The Bengals knew it would take Stewart time to develop. He missed key time in training camp that could've helped that development. Instead, Johnson emerged as DE4.
The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday, Nov. 10. Never say never when it comes to a deal, but the Bengals didn't make Stewart inactive on Sunday because they plan to move on from the former first round pick.
He's very much in their future plans. Of course, that won't stop teams from calling over the next few weeks. A deal is unlikely and the Bengals want Stewart to remain in stripes, but teams will certainly inquire about his availability ahead of the trade deadline.

title: Why Not Another? Browns Kicker Andre Szmyt Comes Up Clutch in Win Over Titans
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns just keep getting the job done.
On Sunday, Oct. 25, the Browns improved to 5-2 on the 2026 campaign, beating the Tennessee Titans on the road from Nissan Stadium 27-24, with a game-winning field goal from kicker Andre Szmyt being the difference maker.
Sunday marked the fifth time this season the Browns have won on a game-winning drive led by quarterback Deshaun Watson, and the third time that Szmyt has been the hero.
This is also Andre Szmyt’s fifth career game-tying or go-ahead FG in the final two minutes, passing Dustin Hopkins (4) for second most by a Browns kicker this century (behind Phil Dawson, 10) [via ESPN Research] https://t.co/nFm1w83K0j
"We got to give the fans something to watch and enjoy. It boosts the NFL ratings, so I know they loving that," Browns Pro Bowl defensive back Denzel Ward said at the conclusion of the game.
Ward also played a major part in the victory, snagging his second interception of the season and 20th in his illustrious career. He also finished with two tackles.
While Ward obviously put it a great way, there were others who echoed his sentiment and shed more light onto the Browns' fifth win of the campaign. Here are three must-hear quotes following the victory:
Of course, wins are going to be wins.
But even though the Browns didn't look the prettiest on Sunday, Monken reiterated that these games haven't looked the same. Whether it's a win or a loss, the Browns are making improvements across the board in different areas.
It would be nice to see the Browns play a clean, near-perfect game, but sometimes you take what you can get.
"That was a fun one," Monken said postgame. "Never looks the same but feels the same."
Browns coach Todd Monken: “That was a fun one. Never looks the same but feels the same.” pic.twitter.com/foodG7IzNx
Monken wasn't going to let KC Concepcion's incredible game go unnoticed.
The rookie finished with eight receptions on 10 targets, going for 129 yards. He averaged 16.1 yards per reception, consistently getting involved in the Browns' offense from the start.
He also tacked on three carries for 23 yards on the ground.
Postgame, Monken complimented Concepcion.
“Real dude, man. He's a real dude," he said. "Coming out of the draft, everyone said that about him. When you visit him and you're around him, like, he's diligent, he's humble, competitive, got unbelievable fight."
Todd Monken on KC Concepcion (career-high 152 scrimmage yards): “He’s a real dude.”
The thoughts from Monken were echoed by Concepcion himself, as he would go on to share that he believed Sunday would be his breakout game.
"I enter every week expecting to have a game like this," he said. "This week it was my breakout game, so I just can't wait to keep stacking weeks."
On the campaign, he now has 30 receptions for 315 yards. He has yet to find the endzone, but if Sunday can be repeated at all down the line, that certainly will change.
Watson finished Sunday's game with a whopping 308 yards through the air on 36 attempts , completing 25 of them in the process. He averaged 8.6 yards per reception, while also throwing one interception.
Besides his lone blemish that came in the first, he had a great game.
However, while the Browns are up to five wins , he doesn't think the team is done just yet.
"We haven't even reached our peak," Watson said postgame.
Browns QB Deshaun Watson: “We haven’t even reached our peak.”
The Browns will look to remain atop the AFC North this coming weekend when they face the Pittsburgh Steelers for the second time this season.
The two sides will collide on Sunday, Nov. 1, at 1:00 p.m. EST from Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: Browns Get Lucky Break As Two Major Defensive Contributors Cleared For Titans Game
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns should be entering Sunday's showdown against the Tennessee Titans with all the momentum in the world.
Following a strong 4-2 start to the 2026 NFL regular season, the Browns have now gained an extra edge as two major defensive contributors were cleared to play.
On Sunday, Oct. 25, just hours before the Browns were set to take on the Titans from Nissan Stadium, the team released the inactive report, with both cornerback Denzel Ward and linebacker Quincy Williams not listed. The two had been dealing with injuries throughout the week and were questionable.
Denzel Ward is ACTIVE (right hand) for #Browns v #Titans Inactives: QB Taylen Green (3QB) LB Justin Jefferson CB Noah Igbinoghene RB Audric Estime DT Mike Hall Jr. C Parker Brailsford
The only inactives are quarterback Taylen Green, linebacker Justin Jefferson, cornerback Noah Igbinoghene, running back Audric Estime , defensive tackle Mike Hall Jr. and center Parker Brailsford.
Each of these comes as no surprise and will likely not have too big of an effect on the outcome.
#Browns CB Denzel Ward (hand) is ACTIVE for today's game against the Titans.
All week long, there was speculation surrounding Estime's involvement on the gridiron on Sunday. He was dealing with a hand injury, specifically something with his finger.
Head coach Todd Monken did expect him to play, though.
"Knowing Denzel, we expect him to play , but we'll see," Monken said during the week.
Ward has been the Browns' most reliable defensive contributor since he arrived way back in 2018.
This season, he has contributed 25 total tackles, three pass deflections, two forced fumbles, one quarterback hit and one interception. While he hasn't had many flashy moments yet, he has stayed healthy and remained a consistent presence on the field.
If he keeps up his current pace, he will set a career-best in total tackles.
Against Cam Ward and a relatively pass-heavy offense, Ward will have a chance to continue his recent streak of good play.
Like Ward, Williams has been en fuego as of late.
Playing in all six games to begin the campaign, Williams has 40 combined tackles with three for a loss. He has also contributed three quarterback hits and one sack, all while routinely putting physical shots on the opposition. He has a team and league best of three forced fumbles.
He has also tacked on two pass deflections.
Whether it is the rushing or passing attack, Williams has found a way to impact both areas of an opposing offense.
Fortunately, all week long, Williams was singing the song that he was going to be playing this weekend. Following the Browns' close-knit win over the Ravens last weekend, he had been dealing with neck soreness.
"Just a little soreness," Williams said on Thursday. "Missed yesterday just for precautionary stuff, get some tests done and everything and I was back out there today moving full speed. Moving, it feels good. Just did a little check right there...good for Sunday."
Having nearly every go-to option back from injury on both sides of the ball gives the Browns the perfect opportunity to improve to 5-2 on the campaign and stay atop the AFC North standings.
The Browns and Titans kick things off at 1:00 p.m. EST.

title: Browns Put Themselves in Unique Position Ahead of Sunday Outing Against Titans
full_text:
It's time to see what the Cleveland Browns can do at pretty much full strength.
Following a slow start to the season in the injury department, Weeks 3 through 6 gave the Browns a lot to be concerned about. Key contributors on both sides of the ball were banged up and held off the gridiron.
But ahead of the Browns' Week 7 matchup with the Tennessee Titans, countless players were deemed healthy enough to suit up.
Of the bunch, the running back room's Dylan Sampson and Quinshon Judkins stand out, as neither has been healthy at the same time this season outside of the first quarter of Week 1. With both back and ready to go , the Browns have a chance to finally get the rushing attack going.
Their returns certainly make things interesting, though, as along the way, backups Jaleel McLaughlin and Audric Estime have held down the fort pretty well.
So, on Sunday, Oct. 25, how will the Browns coaching staff use Sampson, Judkins, McLaughlin and Estime?
According to the official depth chart , Judkins is RB1, with Sampson, McLaughlin and Estime following in that order.
Through the first five games of the 2026 campaign, the second-year back has only posted 221 yards and one score on 73 carries. He is currently averaging a measly 3.0 yards per carry.
Coming off an injury last season, it was expected that he might not have as quick of a bounce, especially out of the gates, but Cleveland's play calling has him running right up the gut quite often. Not only is he not a workhorse, physical back in that capacity, but he also isn't getting the right holes created by the offensive line.
On Sunday, it would be nice to see the Browns limit his snap count, just to keep him healthy, but also give him more time to breathe if that is the way they plan to continue using him.
On Sampson's end, he is the speedster of the running back room.
As they did in 2025, he should continue being the team's go-to receiving back. Last year, he hauled in over 30 receptions for just north of 250 receiving yards and two touchdowns. With the Browns' offense finally becoming a bit more dynamic, he should get some usage by Watson outside in the flats.
Sampson is a player you just have to let get loose.
Just Hours Before Sunday's Game, Estime Was Ruled Inactive
Now, here is where things get interesting for the Browns.
A team very rarely brings two players back from injury and thrusts them immediately into the heavy workload they previously had, especially at the running back positions where hits are taken left, right and center, meaning both McLaughlin and Estime should see time in the backfield Sunday.
Of the two, McLaughlin seems the most fit to see meaningful time on the field, having already made a pretty nice impact in limited opportunities.
He has 11 carries for 72 yards and one touchdown on the ground, while also grabbing four receptions for 14 yards.
Like Sampson, he has tremendous speed, and if he gets loose, he can take even the simplest of looks for six.
Now, if any of Sampson, Judkins or McLaughlin come up short and a goalline punch is needed, that is where Estime could see time on the field.
In his Browns debut last week, he found the end zone on a two-yard carry.
While he may not seem like a realistic option for many reps, he still certainly does have a role in Cleveland's offense. The only question will be what it looks like now with Sampson and Judkins back from injury.
The Browns and Titans will go toe-to-toe on Sunday, Oct. 25, at 1:00 p.m. EST from Nissan Stadium in Nashville. The Browns will look to improve to 5-2 on the young 2026 campaign.

title: Browns Sign Standout DT Maliek Collins To Two-Year Extension Amid Strong Season
full_text:
Veteran defensive tackle Maliek Collins has signed a two-year, $30 million extension with the Cleveland Browns ahead of their Week 7 matchup with the Tennessee Titans .
The deal includes $23 million guaranteed, according to NFL Network insider Ian Rapaport.
Collins, 31, has seemed to have found a home in Cleveland after bouncing around the NFL. Collins was selected by the Dallas Cowboys in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft out of Nebraska. After four seasons in Dallas, he spent one season with the Las Vegas Raiders.
He then went on to play three seasons with the Houston Texans and one with the San Francisco 49ers before signing with Cleveland.
The #Browns and standout DT Maliek Collins have agreed to terms on a 2-year extension for $30M with $23M in total guarantees,  agent Drew Rosenhaus tells me and @AdamSchefter . pic.twitter.com/rIJIcfP2DF
Collins has been a key piece for this Browns defense since signing with the team in 2025. Collins posted a career year in his first season with the Browns before going down with a tricep injury in week 13 that kept him out for the remainder of the season. In 12 full games, Collins posted 25 tackles, 6.5 sacks, and 1 fumble recovery.
Now fully recovered, Collins looks to replicate that impact in 2026.
The Browns' defense has been the catalyst for their unprecedented 4-2 start, and Maliek Collins has played a major role in it. After giving up 34 points in week one against the Jacksonville Jaguars, Mike Rutenberg's unit has allowed just 17.6 points per game.
The unit ranks 4th in the NFL with 65 total pressures and 6th in pressure rate at 40.4%. In addition, the unit has not allowed a 300-yard passer in 50 consecutive regular-season contests.
The Browns' defensive line unit raised many question marks coming into the season following the departure of Myles Garrett. Garrett was traded in the offseason to the Los Angeles Rams after nine seasons in Cleveland.
Through four games, the unit has answered the call by being one of the best units in football. A key reason for this is Maliek Collins' ability to make those around him better. Second-year defensive tackle Mason Graham was finding his stride in his rookie season before Collins's went down with his injury.
Although the sample size was small, Graham's play was noticeably worse following the injury to Collins. Since then, Graham has come into this season playing like one of the best defensive tackles in football.
The impact Maliek Collins brings cannot be overstated. After standing out in the first six weeks of the season, the Browns are rightfully rewarding the veteran, keeping him in Cleveland for the years to come.
Cody Croy joined the BIGPLAY Sports Network in June 2026 to cover the Ohio State Buckeyes and Cleveland Browns On SI.

title: Browns' 2027 NFL Draft Plans Could Change Everything for Shedeur Sanders
full_text:
Coming into the 2026 NFL season, many people thought Shedeur Sanders would be the starting quarterback for the Cleveland Browns by this time, here in week 7.
However, after the resurgence of Deshaun Watson , the Browns are in a unique situation.
The upcoming NFL Draft will be a pivotal moment for the Browns organization's future. With many quarterbacks available in a class that many call "loaded", Cleveland may look for their next guy.
However, would this be overlooking Shedeur Sanders?
In his rookie season, Sanders was named to the Pro Bowl after throwing for 1400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions.
Especially after sitting behind Deshaun Watson so far this season, would it be fair to the former fifth-round pick out of Colorado?
There's one case that I have been arguing since the start of the season.
Watson is currently 31 years old and clearly isn't getting any younger. With his injury history, Watson could very well be done playing football in the next few seasons.
With that being said, wouldn't the Browns want a guy who had the chance to sit and learn the system for months?
Think about how many guys the Browns have had to call up or bring in and start after being on the team for a week.
Cleveland has the chance to get a Pro Bowl caliber quarterback acclimated to their roster, and give him enough time to learn from the bench and eventually some in to be the future of the franchise.
Another way-too-early 2027 NFL Mock Draft from @JustinM_NFL has the Browns selecting... 4. Jeremiah Smith, WR, Ohio State 32. Trinidad Chambliss, QB, Ole Miss Should the Browns target Smith and take a QB with their 2nd 1st round pick next year? (📽️: @NFLPerformances )…
At this moment, the Browns hold 11 draft picks in this years draft.
Out of those, they hold the first-round pick from the Los Angeles Rams after trading away Myles Garrett. Additionally, they have multiple late-round selections.
If the Browns decide not to draft a quarterback, they could definitely use their picks to bolster the roster.
Whether they try to win the draft for a third straight year or package some picks to get players, the options are endless if Cleveland decides Shedeur is their next guy.
Especially after getting their future pass catchers this past year in Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, the Browns really can focus on their weaker units and build up a playoff caliber roster ready for Sanders to take over.
Let's say Cleveland goes through the draft process, sits down with a couple of quarterbacks (you know they will, regardless), and finds a guy they really like.
Let's go further to say the select said guy. What is in store for Sanders?
Well, obviously, after waiting patiently, Sanders and his camp would most likely be unhappy, feel disrespected, and demand a trade out of Cleveland.
I don't see a world where the Browns manage to keep both Sanders and a rookie quarterback unless they decide to part ways with Watson after his contract expires this season.

title: Browns Defensive Leader Cleared To Play Sunday vs. Titans, Team Gets Big Injury Boost
full_text:
The last thing the Cleveland Browns wanted was for injuries to slow down their hot start to the 2026 campaign.
And while earlier in the week, it seemed that banged-up bodies were threatening to put them into Sunday's showdown as underdogs, the team's latest report gave everyone a sigh of relief.
On Saturday, Oct. 24, the Browns released an update on injuries, with corresponding moves made ahead of a Week 7 meeting with the Tennessee Titans on the road in Nashville.
#Browns roster moves: -activated RB Dylan Sampson (knee) from injured reserve. -placed G Teven Jenkins (back) on injured reserve. -elevated DT Sam Kamara from the practice squad. -S Grant Delpit has cleared concussion protocol and has no injury status for tomorrow’s game
The Browns officially activated running back Dylan Sampson off the injured list.
The second-year speedster has missed the last five straight weeks due to a lower-body injury he suffered in the Browns' season opener in Jacksonville. He was injured on a kickoff.
Across the last two campaigns, Sampson has played in 16 games, recording just 175 rushing yards on 65 attempts. However, he makes his impact known in the receiving game, where he took 33 receptions for 271 yards and two scores.
Being dumped down in the flats from time to time, Sampson can make defenders miss with his speed. He did it with then-rookie Shedeur Sanders last season.
If he gets involved in the game plan on Sunday, it will be intriguing to see how the Browns use him, especially with Quinshon also back from injury.
In hopes of keeping the defensive line deep through a few injuries, the front office elevated defensive tackle Sam Kamara. Over the last two weeks, he has been a nuisance for opposing teams, recording eight total tackles, three for a loss, one sack and one quarterback hit.
He will be looked to help out the line as Mason Graham continues to ramp up his involvement since returning from injury.
Finally, the Browns have placed offensive guard Teven Jenkins on the injured reserve list.
He hasn't played all season, having injured his back ahead of the Browns' Week 1 opener in Jacksonville. In his place, rookie Austin Barber has thrived , being listed as one of the league's top rookies through the first few weeks of the season.
To avoid Jenkins rushing back and re-injuring himself, Cleveland made the right move to shut him down through the back half of the season.
If they need him by then, he should be all set to return. If not, the current group can keep doing the job they have been doing.
Safety Grant Delpit was in concussion protocol for most of the week.
But thankfully, it seems one of the Browns' most important defensive leaders will be good to play this weekend.
His six-year career in the Orange and Brown has been exceptional, with him recording 476 tackles and two 100-tackle seasons along the way. He has also added eight interceptions, 7.5 sacks, 26 tackles for a loss, 24 pass deflections and three forced fumbles.
A dynamic safety, Delpit's clearance is great for a Titans passing attack that is going to look to get Tony Pollard and Cam Ward going early. If anything gets outside the hashes, Delpit being on the field will be a good safety blanket for a Browns stop.
The Browns and Titans will play on Sunday, Oct. 25, from Nissan Stadium in Nashville at 1:00 p.m. EST.

title: 5 Players That Need to Step Up for a Browns Victory Against Titans
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns head to Nashville to take on the Tennessee Titans with the chance to improve to 5-2 on the line.
With a win, the Browns will remain in first place in the AFC North, and their playoff chances strengthen considerably. The Titans had one win going into their matchup against the Browns last season and ran the ball down the defense’s throat on their way to a 31-29 win.
These five players will have to step up to ensure a Browns victory.
In all four of the Browns’ victories, Watson has led game-winning drives. He has not put together any sustained success, but has found a way to lead the team at the end. That is a hard way to win in the NFL and bad play will eventually catch up to him. It is a harder way to win when playing on the road as evidenced by their 1-2 record away from Cleveland, which may be 0-3 if not for a two and half hour rain delay.
Watson needs to be sharper and not put the offense in a position where they have to score at the end of the game. He has started games slow by holding on to the ball too long and making decisions too late. The Titans’ defense should be a good opportunity for Watson to focus on getting the ball out of hands on time and making decisive runs.
A big part of the offense’s struggles has been the run game. Judkins should be fresh coming into the game as he missed last week with an injury. He has struggled all season and needs a good game to rejuvenate the offense. Dylan Sampson is also returning from injury and Jaleel McLaughlin showed speed in his limited action.
The trade deadline is approaching and the Browns need a better running attack for any chance at a playoff berth. Judkins needs to turn his season around and the Titans have a great defensive tackle, but outside of Jeffrey Simmons, there should be holes for Judkins to run through. If he can right the ship and the Browns have a successful rushing attack, then they will leave Nashville victorious.
Graham was having a sensational season prior to his leg injury. This will be his first game back and he will be needed to slow down the Titans’ running game. Last season the Titans ran up and down the field against the Browns, allowing them to score 31 points. Cameron Ward has struggled throwing the football in his short career and Graham will be imperative to force him into passing situations.
Ward has shown that he will make bad decisions under duress and Graham can bring pressure up the middle, forcing him to act fast. Graham leads the Browns with four sacks despite missing two games.
Grant Delpit returns after being out with a concussion , but the Browns may want to limit his action and allow him extra time to recover. McNeil-Warren has been steadily improving with each game. He is a physical safety and if he can play well near the line of scrimmage to slow down the run game, then he can play ball hawk on obvious passing downs.
The defense needs to prevent any big-play opportunities and make the Titans offense earn their yards. McNeil-Warren will be the protection over the top that will put an end to any big plays.
Fannin has had an unusual season as he has been really quiet, but it is not entirely his fault. Watson has not had a connection with Fannin and has missed him by a mile on a couple of throws. Fannin has been having to block more this season due to the offensive line’s inability to protect Watson.
He is too good of a pass catcher and play maker to be tied up around the line of scrimmage blocking. Monken and Watson need to find a way to get Fannin the ball and let him make plays. If Fannin can have four to six catches this game, then the offense will be able to move the ball and keep the Titans’ offense off the field.
The Titans should not be overlooked and the Browns should not rely on their record to assume a win. These five players need to have a good game for the Browns to head to Pittsburgh next week in another AFC North showdown for first place.

title: Is Shedeur Sanders in Cleveland in 2027? Exploring His Path Forward With Browns
full_text:
When the 2025 campaign concluded, it seemed that the Cleveland Browns had found their long-term starter.
While he had a lot of work to do to become a reliable starting quarterback in the NFL, then-rookie Shedeur Sanders showed enough to warrant real consideration to be the leader of the Browns moving forward.
However, the moment the front office moved on from head coach Kevin Stefanski and opened a new chapter in the franchise's storied history, that sentiment came crashing down.
After battling for the starting job all offseason, Sanders lost the race to controversial quarterback Deshaun Watson, who has begun the 2026 season off nicely. He has experienced plenty of bumps in the road along the way, but has the Browns atop the AFC North standings with a 4-2 record through six weeks.
While it is obviously great to see the Browns playing competitive football, Watson's success puts the Browns in a difficult situation moving forward.
Watson's currently in the final year of his deal, and with how controversial and rocky his tenure in Cleveland has been since he was traded just a few years back, it seems unlikely that the two sides would work out a return deal.
That means that Sanders could end up becoming the starter yet again.
But is he ready for that? And is the front office even thinking about such a decision?
When the Browns named Watson the starter, both the front office and Monken confirmed it was primarily an experience-based decision.
The 31-year-old has been in the league since 2017, throwing for 19,078 yards and 130 touchdowns along the way. He hasn't played the best since joining the Browns back in 2022, but still commands an offense well and can recognize different tendencies.
Sanders, on the other hand, is still quite raw. He put together a rookie campaign that saw 1,400 passing yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions. The numbers may not show it, but he got himself into trouble quite a few times, throwing the ball into odd situations or scrambling into traffic both into and outside of the pocket. To put it simply, he looked like a first-year signal caller.
From the organization's perspective, starting Watson may have been just the safer option for a team looking to give Monken a chance to succeed in his first year as a head coach. Instead of working out the kinks in Sanders' game on game day, they can do so on the practice field and behind closed doors.
With the Browns being 4-2, it seems like the decision has paid off so far.
However, the bigger question is whether that short-term success aligns with Cleveland's long-term plans.
Keeping Watson ahead of him on the depth chart gives Sanders time to learn, but with the path ahead so murky, things could just continue to get even more complicated, especially if Watson leaves in the offseason.
It seems like a relatively odd question to ask, especially considering the 24-year-old has a lot to prove.
But the last thing the Browns want to do is frustrate or put wrinkles in the timeline of yet another quarterback. It is something they have done time and time again, routinely resetting the quarterback development process in Cleveland.
For a young quarterback trying to establish himself in the NFL, though, the situation he is in is a difficult balancing act. Sitting behind a veteran can provide him with valuable experience, but after getting time to develop on the field in 2025, he now has to do it off it in 2026.
There is no reason to assume Sanders is unhappy with his current situation , but if the Browns keep Watson around in 2027 or make a move for another quarterback to take his place, his long-term outlook in Cleveland will begin to look grim.
Sooner rather than later, the Browns will have to determine whether or not the future revolves around him.
Could the Browns make a move in the 2027 NFL Draft to select a top quarterback? Maybe, but it doesn't seem likely at this point.
The team has gone from quarterback to quarterback over the last few campaigns, and even drafted two back in 2025: Sanders and Dillon Gabriel, and one in 2026: Taylen Green. Drafting yet another would continue to crowd the quarterback room, making it even more difficult for a coaching staff to develop one of them properly.
Instead, it seems far more likely that the Browns, who have two picks in the first round of the upcoming draft, will select pieces to fit alongside one of the quarterbacks they currently have.
No matter what the Browns end up doing with Sanders moving forward, the 2026 campaign will certainly be looked back on with plenty of confusion.
If Cleveland really does believe Sanders is the future, why not start him from Week 1 onward? If they don't think he has what it takes to be a starter in the league, at least not yet, why didn't they just say that?
For now, questions will continue to be asked. And only the guys at the top really know what plan is in motion for 2027.

title: Browns Pro Bowler Lands on Injury Report as Key Contributors Return
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns seem to be on the mend when the injury report for Sunday’s game against the Tennessee Titans came out.
Key contributors are back on the field, but they are still not out of the weeds yet, with one surprising player listed as questionable who can influence the outcome in Nashville.
Denzel Ward was listed as questionable with a hand injury on Friday’s report. He was limited at practice on Friday, and the defense needs him to be healthy. Ward is having an incredible season locking down the offense’s top receiver.
The Titans do not have much to offer on offense, but rookie Carnell Tate is having a solid season with 344 yards, which is only one yard behind Denzel Boston. Todd Monken believes that Ward will play with a finger injury, but advised, “We’ll see”.
When Ward is on the field, quarterbacks generally do not even try to throw his way, but quarterback Cameron Ward can be reckless with the football and throw it his way, leading to a crucial turnover.
The defense cannot allow easy throws for Cam Ward, as he has struggled in his second year , and not giving him momentum will be key. On the other hand, if Denzel Ward has to miss any game this season, Sunday’s game may be the one to do it against a struggling offense.
Another concerning, questionable designation is Quincy Williams with a neck injury. He has been flying around the field in recent weeks, making big hits and causing fumbles. Williams will be key to rushing Cameron Ward and forcing him to make bad decisions leading to errant throws and turnovers.
However, Carson Schwesinger is in the lineup and he is so good that he can make up for Williams’ absence should he be out for the game.
The defense continues to be hobbled as Grant Delpit is also listed as questionable with a concussion. He left last week’s game early with the injury, but has not been ruled for this week.
He is a physical veteran that helps shut down the offense’s running game by playing near the tackle box, but Emmanuel McNeil-Warren has stepped in and is improving every game he is on the field.
The Browns’ stagnant rushing game will get a boost as Dylan Sampson has been upgraded to questionable. He suffered an injury in the first game of the season and has been out since.
The offense relies on his speed to be a change of pace and utilize the screen game in lieu of a traditional running play.
Quinshon Judkins will play against the Titans after missing last week. The offense could finally have the top-two running backs in the backfield that they envisioned when the season started. The Titans have big Jeffery Simmons at defensive tackle and he feasted against the Browns’ offense last season.
The addition of the two running backs can help lift the offense.
The defensive line gets a major boost with the return of Mason Graham. His injury in Week 4 looked bad, but he avoided the worst-case scenario and is back in the lineup after missing two games.
He still leads the team with four sacks and the second-year defensive tackle has made major strides this season in anchoring the aggressive line.
Graham will need to be good, as Michael Hall Jr. continues to remain on the injured list and is out again with an ankle injury. Also on the defensive line, Kalia Davis will not play in the game. The defensive line has caused havoc for other quarterbacks and has shut down the running game.
The Titans’ Tony Pollard has had a solid season running the football, and the line will need to keep him down and make Cameron Ward beat them with his arm.
Also out is Dillon Gabriel and Teven Jenkins. Gabriel has practiced and the Browns will have to make a decision on his injury designation soon or risk shutting him down for the season. Jenkins is out, but rookie Austin Barber has stepped up and has played well for the offensive line.
If a couple of the questionable players can strap it up on Sunday, then the Browns will receive a major boost to help them improve to an AFC North best 5-2.

title: How the Browns Could Change the Game with this Position-Altering Trade
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are 4-2 to begin the 2026 NFL regular season.
Through the first six weeks, there have been plenty of positives for the Browns to be excited about, especially with the defensive side of the ball. But with the positives come some negatives, with many of them unfortunately being on the offensive end.
Starting quarterback Deshaun Watson has been somewhat all over the place, the rushing attack has been absent and the tight end room has become incredibly thin.
In order to capitalize on the momentum they have established, landing a few key pieces at the trade deadline could be the perfect way to round out the roster and fill a few holes.
One player who has stood out as of late is tight end Sam LaPorta of the Detroit Lions, who seems to be frustrated with his current situation. On a recent episode of Pardon My Take, LaPorta shared his frustration with not receiving a contract extension from the Lions.
"You know, like last year, whatever it was, Week 9, Week 10, you know, I break my fucking back for the team," he said, "and then I'm going out there this year, and I'm balling, and maybe they're just not showing the love ... And in three months, if I don't get to wear the Honolulu blue and play for the Lions anymore, it's going to be all good.
"I'll go get paid somewhere else."
Sam LaPorta on not receiving an extension from the Lions, via @PardonMyTake : "You know, like last year, whatever it was, Week 9, Week 10, you know, I break my fucking back for the team and then I'm going out there this year and I'm balling and maybe they're just not showing the… pic.twitter.com/MocZjCmq1f
The last part of LaPorta's quote is eye-opening because the 25-year-old is on the last year of a four-year contract worth nearly $10 million . As one of the league's best tight ends, he is rightfully hoping to see Detroit dish him out some cash to lock him down on a long-term deal.
But that simply hasn't happened yet.
On Thursday, Oct. 22, members of the Lions were open to the media for roughly 45 minutes, but LaPorta did not show up.
Lions TE Sam LaPorta was a "no show" during the 45-minute player media access yesterday, per @freep (h/t @officialctpod ) pic.twitter.com/q4ubT8p0nz
If this situation continues, the Browns should pick up the phone and give the Lions a call.
Very rarely does a franchise have the opportunity to have two of the league's best tight ends on the same roster. And oftentimes, it is hard for a front office to justify paying two players a good chunk of money at that position.
However, the Browns are notorious for running multi-tight end sets.
Under Kevin Stefanski, the team featured a 12 personnel scheme, highlighting two tight ends, two wideouts and a running back. Under Todd Monken, that scheme is maintained, with him also utilizing three-tight-end groupings from time to time.
He also enjoys hitting the deep shot or explosive play if it is open, something LaPorta has thrived with.
He has recorded a long of 38 yards or more in each of the last four seasons, all while averaging a whopping 11.4 yards per reception. Across the last four campaigns, he has totaled 2,420 yards and 23 touchdowns.
According to Free Press, Lions tight end Sam LaPorta HID from media, forcing teammates to answer questions about  what he said. Many Lions declined to answer pic.twitter.com/ZZetKqDdTb
Bringing LaPorta to Cleveland would give the Browns a one-two punch that no one else in the league could match up against.
With the rest of the tight end room featuring Blake Whiteheart, Carsen Ryan, Joe Royer, Jack Stoll and Brendan Bates, landing a go-to option like LaPorta would take less pressure off the depth and instead put it back on those who can handle it.
Fannin Jr. x LaPorta would set the stage for offenses to start investing more in a well-rounded, dynamic offense. Not only would the Browns have two of the best tight ends in the league, but they would also be pairing them with two up-and-coming stars outside the hashes in KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston.
A move like this wouldn't just make the Browns an even better team, but it would change how teams think about the position moving forward.

title: Dak Prescott Topps Trading Card Goes Viral For Overlooked NSFW Message
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys' stock has taken a massive hit in recent weeks, following back-to-back losses on the national stage. Now, the Cowboys are back in the primetime spotlight for a third consecutive week, facing the division rival Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football.

Away from the field, the Prescott market is soaring if you're a trading card collector. That's because a recent Prescott card from the Topps Football Holiday box has gone viral for a very specific reason.
Prescott always shares uplifting messages or writes notes for specific causes on his wrist tape, and one message that made it's way onto the Topps cards had everyone doing a double take.
Topps just printed a Dak Prescott card with an expletive on it, and now it’s immediately raised the price of the card. Reminds me of the Billy Ripken card pic.twitter.com/nmifKEBzFu
On the viral card, Prescott's wrist tape reads, "F*ck Cancer!" Prescott lost his mother, Peggy, to colon cancer when she was just 52 years old. At the time, Prescott was 20 years old and playing college football at Mississippi State.
He has also written messages like "Ask 4 Help," as part of his initiative to encourage people struggling with their mental health to reach out for help in honor of his brother Jace, who died of suicide at age 31.
While the holiday edition of the card is what went viral, the same Prescott image is used on the 2025 Topps Flagship Football cards and is expected to be in the 2026 Topps Chrome Football boxes releasing on November 18.
That gives you more opportunities to get in on the madness.
Yesterday, the same day that news spread of Dak Prescott’s handwritten “F—- Cancer” wrist tape message visible on his 2026 Topps Holiday card, his 1/1 gold vinyl from the product appears to have sold for $1,800. This will be a super popular card. pic.twitter.com/slRD6j0rdy
It's great to see the card getting widespread attention, and also helps to continue pushing out Prescott's message.
Prescott established the Faith Fight Foundation, a non-profit that works to "empower individuals, families, and communities to find strength and resilience through adversity." Two of the core pillars of Prescott's foundation are colon cancer research and prevention, and mental health & suicide prevention.

title: NFL Punishes Tyler Booker, Matthew Golden For Infractions in Cowboys vs. Packers
full_text:
Dallas Cowboys guard Tyler Booker is going to be lighter in the wallet after being punished by the NFL.
The NFL releases its list of fines every Saturday and this time the league revealed that the Cowboys guard was among them.
Booker was hit with a fine of $11,941 for unnecessary roughness (late hit) in the fourth quarter of the Week 6 loss to the Green Bay Packers .
The infraction came at 6:43 in the fourth quarter. Booker did get flagged for the late hit, costing the Cowboys 15 yards. Booker got bailed out on the next play, though, as the Packers committed a roughing the passer penalty on the next play.
Booker wasn't the only player to get hit with a fine, as Packers wide receiver Matthew Golden also took a hit to his bank account for unsportsmanlike conduct (taunting) in the first quarter at 7:47. Golden was flagged, also.
We'll see if both players appeal, but if they choose not to or simply aren't successful, Golden's and Booker's fine money will be donated to two different foundations, the NFL notes.
The Professional Athletes Foundation was created to "support Legends in need," while the NFL Foundation supports "the health, safety and wellness of athletes across all levels, including youth football and the communities that support the game."
On average since 2011, NFL fines have contributed about $4 million per year to those great causes.
Booker had a fantastic rookie season in 2025 and he has picked up right where he left off.
The 2025 first-round pick has posted a pass-blocking grade of 69.8, per Pro Football Focus , and he has yet to allow a sack and has given up just seven pressures. His PFF pass-blocking grade ranks 22nd among guards, and it is currently over seven points higher than his 2025 mark.
Booker has been even better as a run-blocker, with his 80.0 PFF grade ranking 12th at the position. That is also better than his 2025 mark, when he posted a 76.9.
Not only has Booker been an elite guard, he is also one of the team's leaders, as evidenced by his being voted to the team's leadership council during the offseason .
“We knew what we were getting with Tyler,” head coach Brian Schottenheimer said of Booker during the offseason.
“When we drafted him, we knew that he was an elite person, an elite human being," he added. He was all about our five core values of putting the team first, working hard, competing, loving football, and being about the brotherhood.”
Safe to say, Booker has been everything the Cowboys could've hoped for, and then some.

title: NFL Legend Proposes Ridiculous Cowboys Dak Prescott-Justin Herbert Trade
full_text:
Dak Prescott has etched his name in the Dallas Cowboys' record books as the all-time leader in passing yardage and passing touchdowns. He's proven to be a strong leader of the franchise and has guided them to a record of 85-59-1 in his career.
The problem is that he hasn't had success in the postseason . Dallas is just 2-5 with Prescott as the starter during the playoffs, something that has haunted him throughout his career. While Jerry Jones and the front office have always supported Prescott despite the playoff losses, he can't escape the criticism.
Now, Prescott is struggling in the regular season as well , leading Dallas to a record of 9-13-1 since the start of the 2025 season. That had Mike Valenti asking Boomer Esiason if the Cowboys need to move on from Prescott. Esiason didn't outright say it was time, but floated a wild trade idea, that even he admitted isn't likely to happen.
"Did you see Justin Herbert wearing a Dallas Cowboys uniform? Let's just fantasize about that for a second. I can see it. I mean, Justin Herbert goes to the Cowboys and Dak Prescott goes to the Chargers. That would be amazing. That would be great for NFL. That would be great for football," Esiason said on their show, Kickoff with Boomer and Valenti .
"Now, both of these guys probably have no move clauses or no trade clauses in their contracts, but maybe both of the guys are sick and tired of where they are by the time we get to the end of the season. So I think that would be a dream scenario for all of us who cover the NFL. I don't know that would help. And I don't think Dak is going anywhere."
Boomer Esiason says on the Kickoff with Boomer and Valenti, that a Justin Herbert for Dak Prescott trade would be good for the NFL, but doubts Jerry Jones would pull the trigger on it pic.twitter.com/Lm55WpqWod
Aside from the fact that neither team would realistically be able to move on from their star quarterbacks, the trade makes very little sense for either franchise.
For the Chargers, they would be moving on from a 28-year-old quarterback who might be struggling in 2026, but is still in his prime. He might benefit from a fresh start, but Los Angeles wouldn't be willing to swap him for a more expensive player who is 33.
Dallas likely wouldn't be too quick to make the move. Sure, Herbert is younger, but he has the same issues Prescott does. Despite having multiple seasons with double-digit wins, Herbert is just 0-3 in the postseason and had a historically bad performance in 2024 when he threw four interceptions in a loss to the Houston Texans.
You could make an argument that due to his age, Herbert would be a better option. That said, they already know and trust Dak, which makes it far more likely in their minds that they can find success with him at the helm than with a player they don't know.

title: NFL Insiders Link Cowboys to Super Bowl EDGE at Trade Deadline
full_text:
Jerry Jones said he plans to be aggressive at the NFL trade deadline , believing his Dallas Cowboys could make a run at the NFC East title despite their 2-4 start.
Coaching has clearly been an issue, but Jones believes adding more talent will help the team make up for their shortcomings in that area. Whether that would be enough remains to be seen, but what we do know is that Jones is determined to fix the defense.
That's why NFL insiders Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport said the Cowboys are a team to watch at the deadline. The player they see Dallas targeting is Arizona Cardinals outside linebacker Josh Sweat. The Cardinals already traded Marvin Harrison Jr., and the insiders say they could be willing to move on from the former Pro Bowl pass-rusher .
"The Arizona Cardinals already have shown they are willing to trade a player for the right price. In August, general manager Monti Ossenfort said the Cardinals were not interested in trading Sweat. But now the Cardinals are 2-4, and unless they turn it around, they could be willing to listen to meaningful offers," Schefter and Rapoport wrote.
"One team that could explore the possibility of a Sweat trade is the Cowboys, who are trying to salvage their season Monday night in Philadelphia."
Sweat has ties to Christian Parker, going back to their days with the Philadelphia Eagles. Sweat was a fourth-round pick out of Florida State in 2018 and played in Philly for seven years. His last year with the franchise was in 2024, which was Parker's first of two years as their passing game coordinator and defensive backs coach .
Philadelphia went on to win the Super Bowl that season and Sweat was a central figure in their victory. The outside linebacker had six tackles and 2.5 sacks, helping the Eagles defeat the Kansas City Chiefs 40-22.
He turned that success into a massive deal, signing a four-year contract with the Cardinals for $76.4 million with $41 million guaranteed. He had 12 sacks during his first season with the Cardinals, but has been off to a slower start this year. Through six games, Sweat has 14 tackles and two sacks.
He was dealing with a knee injury during the summer, which might have slowed him down to start the season, but has shown signs of turning things around with both of his sacks coming over the past three games. His recent production, assuming it holds up, could be the exact boost Jones is looking for.

title: Cowboys Week 7 Rooting Guide for Fans as Monday Night Football Game vs. Eagles Awaits
full_text:
Dallas Cowboys fans will have to wait a bit longer to see their team take the field in Week 7, as the Cowboys play on Monday night against the Philadelphia Eagles.
This will be the first matchup between the NFC East rivals, both of whom are in complete disarray. We don't need to rehash all of the Cowboys' issues because fans have been beaten over the head with them for the first six games.
The Eagles are down bad, also. Not only is Jalen Hurts lost for the season due to blood clots, but Philly is down a pair of wideouts for this game, with DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks ruled out , which is more good news for the Cowboys' putrid secondary.
Ahead of kickoff on Monday night, here's the games fans should be paying attention to most, and the desired results for each.
Desired result: Texans beat Giants
Despite how terrible the Cowboys have played this season, the NFC East title is still well within reach.
The 2-4 Cowboys enter the week tied for second with the Eagles behind the 3-2-1 New York Giants, who will square off against a hot Houston Texans team that has won two straight.
A Giants loss and Cowboys win wouldn't put Dallas in first place, but it would move the latter one step closer to the top of the division.
Desired result: Lions beat Packers
The Cowboys have the Green Bay Packers' first-round pick due to the Micah Parsons trade, but we also know that the New York Jets will get the higher of the two first-rounders the Cowboys have thanks to the Quinnen Williams trade.
We would bet the Packers are going to finish with a better record than the Cowboys this season (bold, I know), so chances are Dallas will end up keeping the Green Bay pick.
So, it's important that Green Bay loses as much as possible so the Cowboys can still have a solid first-round pick, which would soften the blow of losing the higher one.
The division will almost certainly be the Cowboys' best path to the playoffs, but it's still worth keeping tabs on the wild card and the teams in front of Dallas in the race for those three spots.
It's a steep hill to climb already, though, as the Chicago Bears, Packers, Detroit Lions, Seattle Seahawks, Atlanta Falcons, New Orleans Saints and Eagles are all ahead of them in that order.
Again, because of the draft pick, the Packers losing to the Lions is most ideal, but the result of that game will benefit Dallas either way since the Lions are a spot closer to the Cowboys.
From there, ideally the Cowboys see the Seahawks lose to the Kansas City Chiefs, the Falcons lose to the San Francisco 49ers, and the Saints lose to the Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris. Of course, Dallas can further help itself by beating the Eagles, also.

title: Former Dallas Cowboys Star Rips Joey Porter Jr. for Lack of Discipline
full_text:
In need of help in the secondary, the Dallas Cowboys made a deal with the Pittsburgh Steelers to bring in Joey Porter Jr. The former second-round pick made his debut in Week 4 against the Houston Texans, and shut down his side of the field .
Porter missed Week 5 due to an illness, but was back on the field in Week 6 and again had a strong showing, allowing zero receptions while breaking up two passes. He did draw a pass interference, and former Cowboys cornerback Pacman Jones believes that's something that will be an issue with Porter.
Jones was a guest on the Gridiron Podcast with Skip Bayless and Aqib Talib, and said that Porter will get two pass interference calls every game.
"He is a walking accident, bro. Every play he is gonna grab, he gonna get you two PIs every game," Jones said. He then added that Porter's physicality has always been an issues.
"He gonna give you two penalties down there every other week. If you look at the flags, how many flags he's had, I bet you in the last year and a half, he's in the top two," Jones said.
“Joey Porter Jr is a walking F***** Incident” 😭 Pacman Jones is going off on Joey 👀 #dallascowboys #cowboys #joeyporterjr pic.twitter.com/424UeBnJDX
Jones is correct in saying Porter will draw flags, even though his two per game number is overexagerated. Still, Porter has the most penalties by a defensive player since entering the league in 2023 (36). He also has the most defensive pass interference penalties called against him (14), according to ESPN Insights.
Both Talib and Bayless were quick to come to Porter's defense. Talib said that he might be a physical cornerback, but added that he doesn't give up touchdowns. Bayless then said he's an upgrade over everything they had in Dallas.
Jones conceded that Porter is a good player, but also believes that he benefited from the talent around him in Pittsburgh.
"Joey's a good player. I'm not saying that. But you got to realize, Joey made a lot of plays when he had a lot of pieces around him in Pittsburgh. This defense in Dallas don't have no pieces."
Despite the criticism from Jones, Porter has been able to stand out in Dallas even without any true help around him. As Cowboys On SI's Mike Moraitis wrote, Porter has played 61 snaps in two games and has been targeted just four times and has yet to give up a reception . Porter has forced three incompletions and opposing quarterbacks have a rating of 39.6 when targeting him.
There's some truth to the claim from Jones, but the Cowboys will gladly take the occasional pass interference if it means they can actually get some stops on defense.

title: Cowboys Struggling Secondary Catches Break With Eagles Injury Report
full_text:
Injuries are going to happen in the NFL, and sometimes they can truly impact a team's success. The Dallas Cowboys understand this, as they have been dealing with multiple injuries throughout their defense.
As they prepare to take on the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football in Week 7, the Cowboys are starting to see players return. While not all will be on the field on Monday, the Cowboys have seen cornerback Cobie Durant , safety P.J. Locke , linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, and EDGE Marist Liufau return to practice .
In addition to getting healthier, the Cowboys' defense caught a break this week on the Eagles' injury report . Their secondary, which has allowed 1,396 yards through the air (ranked No. 23), won't have to face wide receivers DeVonta Smith or Dontayvion Wicks, who were both ruled out on Saturday.
Eagles will be without WR DeVonta Smith, WR Dontayvion Wicks & OLB Nolan Smith on Monday night. https://t.co/cPX7DkYoUI
That's huge for the Eagles, who are already without starting quarterback Jalen Hurts. They will again start Tanner McKee as Hurts deals with blood clots in his lungs . McKee struggled against the Carolina Panthers in Week 6, but Cowboys fans know their defense is usually the cure-all for quarterbacks.
This week, McKee will have to try and get his offense on track without their top two pass catchers. Smith leads the team with 26 receptions of 310 yards and two touchdowns while Wicks has 19 catches for 284 yards with one touchdown reception.
Smith has been dealing with a lingering hamstring injury and missed Week 4 and Week 5. He returned in Week 6 and recorded 75 yards on seven receptions, but he has not practiced this week. This will be the first missed game of the year for Wicks, who suffered an ankle injury against Carolina.
Philly could also be without running back Saquon Barkley, who missed the previous two games with a hamstring injury. He's questionable entering the game, and while he hasn't had the explosive season we're accustomed to seeing from him, Barkley will have a favorable matchup should he play.
Dallas is dead last in the NFL in run defense, surrendering 899 yards through six games. Opposing backs are averaging 4.7 yards per attempt and the only times they have fared well has been when starters are out. They held the Houston Texans to 62 yards with David Montgomery sidelined and 57 to the Green Bay Packers who were still without Josh Jacobs.
The Dallas offense also caught a break, with outside linebacker Nolan Smith being ruled out with a concussion. Smith is tied with Jalen Carter for the team lead with three sacks.
Philadelphia still has a dangerous front seven, but the absence of Smith leaves them without one of their more explosive players off the edge.

title: Cowboys-Eagles Final Injury Report Is Great News for George Pickens, DeMarvion Overshown
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys are heading into Week 7's matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles facing what should be viewed as a must-win and should-win game.
Philadelphia is dealing with major injury issues, which includes the concerning blood cot issues for quarterback Jalen Hurt along with wide receiver DeVonta Smith's lingering hamstring injury. Both players will miss Week 7 against Dallas.
The Cowboys had multiple names on the injury report themselves this week, but fortunately, Dallas is looking fairly healthy across the board headed into Monday Night Football.
The Cowboys released their final injury report before Monday Night Football, and some of the team's most important players are good to go for the game.
Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens (shoulder) and cornerback Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) are both without an injury designation and will play against the Eagles.
Both players are in a contract year and still have a lot to prove to the Dallas front office. They can't afford to miss any games both for their individual goals and if the Cowboys want any chance at winning the NFC East.
Additionally, the Cowboys are officially getting back some key players on defense ahead of Week 7.
This includes the return of cornerback Cobie Durant and linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, both of whom have missed multiple weeks due to hamstring injuries. Durant has been out since getting injured in Week 2's win over the Washington Commanders while Overshown suffered his injury in Week 1 against the New York Giants.
Overshown's return had been anticipated during the week, his healthy status is now official on Saturday's injury report. It comes an ideal time for a Dallas defense that will be without starting linebacker Dee Winters due to an Achilles strain. His status will be one to watch headed into Week 8.
Cowboys wide receiver KaVontae Turpin (ribs) and offensive tackle Drew Shelton (hamstring) are also out for the game.
The status of Cowboys safety P.J. Locke (foot) and linebacker Marist Liufau (foreman) are both questionable against the Eagles.
It remains to be seen if they will play, but there's no doubt their presence would help the depth of the Dallas defense, a unit that's been banged up all season long.

title: Broncos' Biggest Winners and Losers From 30-16 Victory Over Cardinals
full_text:
The Denver Broncos defeated the Arizona Cardinals 30-16 on the road to get to 5-2 in the standings. It sure didn't look or sound like an away game, with the overwhelming number of Broncos fans at State Farm Stadium.
With the Kansas City Chiefs losing to the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday night, the stage is set for the Broncos' rematch with Patrick Mahomes and company next week at Mile High. The Broncos have the chance not only to balance the scales against the Chiefs and avenge their Week 1 loss, but also to make headway at the top of the AFC West at the halfway point of the season.
As we sift through the aftermath of the Broncos' fifth victory of the season, let's talk about this team's biggest winners and losers.
Nix finished with 295 yards from scrimmage, but it was his 62-yard touchdown run that seemed to reignite his confidence. He also tossed a 52-yard touchdown pass to RJ Harvey, becoming the fifth player in NFL history to record a rushing and passing touchdown of 50-plus yards in the same game.
Nix finished 15-of-29 passing for 222 yards and a touchdown. After the game, Nix toyed with a local media corps that had been skeptical that he had fully healed from his fractured ankle suffered back in January.
"You believe me now?" Nix asked with a smile from the post-game podium.
BO NIX 62-YARD TOUCHDOWN RUN DENvsAZ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/sxC4uWF33r
Nobody should be questioning Nix's health anymore, and his big game in the desert seemed to salve whatever was ailing him between the ears in his recovery from that serious injury.
Barron deserves a lot of credit for holding down the fort amid Patrick Surtain II's injury, but he had a rough game against the Cardinals. Barron was penalized twice for pass interference, and he allowed four of five targets to be completed for 41 yards.
Barron did finish with five tackles, and while his coverage was sticky, Jacoby Brissett was able to exploit him, especially one-on-one against tight end Trey McBride. Let's hope this game doesn't affect Barron's confidence too much because he's been a plus player over the past month.
The rookie returned from injured reserve and made a huge impact in his first game back. Coleman's burst brought an energy to the Broncos' ground attack that had been missing.
He also did well as a receiver out of the backfield and in pass protection. He finished with 69 yards from scrimmage on 11 touches, and averaged 6.0 yards per carry as a rusher.
The rookie Jonah Coleman making something out of nothing DENvsAZ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/wjeHrq6ZEi
The Broncos' run game is looking up with Coleman back on the field.
Dobbins went from getting 17 carries last week to just six on Sunday, mainly because Coleman was efficient when he was on the field. Alas, Dobbins was only able to generate 23 rushing yards on those carries, though he did find the end zone on a 1-yard touchdown.
Dobbins did have a nice 13-yard run erased by an illegal shift penalty, so he did have a few nice runs. But his burst is nowhere close to that of the rookie.
I expected Sean Payton to balance the running back touches, but not in the rookie's favor. It could be a sign that there's a new RB1 in the Broncos' backfield.
Bonitto was a terror all day long, finishing with a team-high six pressures on Brissett. Alas, Bonitto wasn't able to get home for a sack, but his presence was felt all game long.
With a solid head of steam built up over the past few weeks, it's very possible it could culminate in a big Bonitto night next week against the Chiefs and their undrafted rookie left tackle.
Waddle makes the "losers" side of the ledger, though it wasn't all his fault. As a receiver, he was solid, catching four of his seven targets (team high) for 48 yards, including a long of 27 down the right seam.
Alas, with the Broncos trying to protect a lead and kill the clock late, Payton decided to get cute and run an end-around, and Waddle bobbled the tossed exchange, fumbled it, and then fell on the ball as Josh Sweat landed on top of him, injurying his chest.
The injury didn't look good for Waddle, who was shortly thereafter escorted to the locker room never to return. With how well Coleman was running the ball late, it was an unnessary risk that Payton has already accepted the blame for, calling the play call "dumb." Let's hope Waddle's injury isn't as serious as it looked.
Harvey only carried the ball three times for six yards, but his two catches for 54 yards and a touchdown made a big difference in this game. On his 52-yard touchdown, Payton perfectly timed a screen to exploit the Cardinals' blitz-happy defense, and Nix, Harvey, and the Broncos' offense executed it to a 'T.'
RJ Harvey takes the screen pass 52 yards for a TD! DENvsAZ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/symyT3Qo6D
It was Harvey's first receiving touchdown of the season and well deserved. Given the burst he shows as a runner, he's deserving of more carries than he's gotten of late, but it appears he's going to take a back seat in that department to Coleman and Dobbins.
Singleton finished with a season-high 19 tackles (12 solo), and was a whirling dervish out there. He was penalized for a ticky-tack roughing the passer call, but the veteran linebacker was a difference-maker out there.
In coverage, Singleton didn't hold up so well, allowing four of five targets to be completed for 38 yards, but he cleaned up those plays well. The team captain has a legitimate chance at notching 200 tackles this season.

title: Broncos QB Bo Nix Makes NFL History in Week 7 Win Over Cardinals
full_text:
Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix added another piece of NFL history to his growing legacy in the Mile HIgh City.
In Sunday's win over the Arizona Cardinals , Nix became the fifth player in league history to record passing and rushing touchdowns of at least 50 yards, according to Next Gen Stats.
Nix joins Justin Fields, Lamar Jackson, Cam Newton, and Ace Parker of the 1938 Brooklyn Dodgers as the only players to ever accomplish that feat.
Appearing more confident both as a passer and runner, Nix completed 15-of-29 passes for 222 yards and one touchdown, a 52-yard screen to running back RJ Harvey who took it to the house. Nix also added 73 rushing yards, including a 62-yard scamper in which he went untouched up the middle of Arizona's defense.
"When he's making plays, it gets the whole team juiced," defensive end Zach Allen said in his postgame gathering with reporters.
Nix completed balls to nine different receivers, with Courtland Sutton totaling a team-high three catches for 45 yards. Harvey (54 yards), Marvin Mims (53 yards), and Jaylen Waddle (48 yards) were also all involved.
“Listen, I think for our team, offensively, all those of those things. Yeah, I mean, the confidence inside of the building relative to his ability hadn’t changed at all," head coach Sean Payton said of Nix after the game. "I appreciate some guys, sometimes you’re answering questions about whether or not… and there’s not one time where we were… he’s our guy. And it was good to see him play well and it was good to see us block well and make some plays down the field.”
The Broncos were also aided by the return of rookie running back Jonah Coleman, who converted carries into 54 rushing yards and helped chew clock in the second half, despite Denver losing the overall time-of-possession battle, 33:18-26:42.
Mired in a mental slump to this point, Nix's touchdown run -- the longest such play by a quarterback in franchise history -- might've been the spark he desperately needed to turn around the second half of his season, and lead 5-2 Denver confidently back into the postseason.
It was the get-right game against an inferior opponent that many believed would transpire . He didn't put up Star Wars numbers, but what he did series-to-series passed the smell test in different orders of magntitude compared to past few games.
Now the question becomes: Can Nix and company keep this monentum rolling into Week 8, when they'll meet a familiar foe in Kansas City that presents a much tougher matchup than the hapless Cardinals did.
"I thought we played a good game offensively, but there are still several things we would like to get better at," Nix said after the game.

title: 3 Big Takeaways From Broncos' 30-16 Win Over Cardinals
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are 5-2 after beating the Arizona Cardinals 30-16 on the road.
You'd be forgiven for thinking this game was played at Mile High, though, as the stands at State Farm Stadium were thronged with Broncos Country. Having so many fans at their back on the road seemed to give the Broncos some juice, especially in the second half.
The Broncos can now look ahead to their Week 8 rematch with the Kansas City Chiefs, and gear up for the opportunity to make some headway in the divisional race.
What did we learn from the Broncos' fifth win of the season? Here are three key takeaways.
Nix didn't need a big 300-yard passing game to regain his confidence; it came flooding back on the heels of a 62-yard rushing touchdown. The play came at the bottom of the second quarter, with Arizona's secondary running some match coverage with everyone's backs turned to the ball.
Nix capitalized, showcasing some impressive speed as he nearly went untouched all the way. It was the longest quarterback rushing touchdown in Broncos history and the longest in the NFL since 2022.
BO NIX 62-YARD TOUCHDOWN RUN DENvsAZ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/sxC4uWF33r
Nix finished the day with seven rushes for 73 yards. Generating some success on the field with his legs seemed to spark something in Nix, but he was already looking much better before his big run.
The Broncos challenged Arizona's defense vertically, and while Nix was unable to connect on some of those shots (one of which was a big Troy Franklin drop on a flea-flicker), it showed a refreshingly aggressive mindset, both on the part of the quarterback and Sean Payton, the play-caller.
Nix came just shy of totaling 300 yards from scrimmage. He went 15-of-29 as a passer for 222 yards with a touchdown. His two longest throws of the day were a 47-yard catch-and-run by Marvin Mims Jr. and a 52-yard RJ Harvey touchdown that came on a perfectly timed and well-executed screen to exploit the Cardinals' blitz-happy defense.
Nix's get-right game last season came in Week 7, although the Broncos had to wait until the fourth quarter to see him break loose. There's just something about Week 7 for Nix, it would seem.
This game had to go a long way toward solving the between-the-ears struggles Nix has dealt with this season. Exhale, Broncos Country. Nix is going to be fine.
The Broncos have been linked to Pro Bowl running back Jonathan Taylor in the NFL rumor mill, but with Coleman returning to the field for the first time since Week 2, GM George Paton may be far less motivated to look elsewhere ahead of the trade deadline.
The Broncos have two more games between now and the deadline to ultimately decide on whether to make a trade, but their backfield simply looked different on Sunday. Coleman contributed in every way, catching passes out of the backfield, picking up blitzers in pass protection, and showing some burst and vision to make plays as a runner.
Coleman finished the day with nine carries for 54 yards and two receptions for 15 yards. Just as we saw in Week 2, the rookie was crucial late in the game, helping to keep the chains moving with some tough running as the Broncos protected a multi-score lead.
The rookie Jonah Coleman making something out of nothing DENvsAZ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/wjeHrq6ZEi
J.K. Dobbins was solid, finishing with 23 yards and a touchdown on six carries, while Harvey only carried thrice for six yards. Dobbins's touchdown should have gone to Coleman, by rights, as the rookie did the heavy lifting on that drive at running back. The fantasy folks would say Coleman got "vultured" by Dobbins.
The Broncos' backfield is headed in the right direction. Coleman looks primed to carry the torch as this team's No. 1 running back moving forward, and as Week 7 showed, that still leaves plenty of room for Dobbins and Harvey to have a role.
The Broncos decided not to dress cornerback Patrick Surtain II, downgrading him to out shortly before kickoff . Riley Moss, Jahdae Barron, and Kris Abrams-Draine held down the fort again amid the officiating crew's torrent of yellow laundry. That's a topic for another time.
Late in the game, with the Broncos protecting a two-score lead, Payton called a trick play of sorts, sending wide receiver Jaylen Waddle on an end-around instead of just giving the ball to Coleman, who had been efficient on that drive. Nix tossed the ball to Waddle, but the receiver bobbled it, and fumbled, falling on the ball to save the possession. Alas, Josh Sweat fell on top of Waddle, with the ball seemingly digging into his chest.
Waddle was injured on the play. After a quick trip to the blue tent, he was escorted to the locker room. It was reported as a chest injury, which is an ailment he's been dealing with for the past two weeks. He may have aggravated it.
Waddle finished the day with four receptions for 48 yards, including a great 27-yard catch down the right seam. The Broncos are going to need their newest receiving weapon. Fingers crossed.
If that wasn't scary enough, All-Pro defensive end Zach Allen went down with a hamstring injury late. It takes a lot for the big fella to go down, but Allen was at least able to walk off the field on his own power.
With the Chiefs up next at Mile High, let's hope that it's nothing major for Waddle and Allen. We'll be looking for updates on these injured key players.

title: Broncos' Make Game-Time Decision on Pat Surtain II vs. Cardinals
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are in the desert to take on the Arizona Cardinals .
The game's inactives just dropped. Let's take a look, starting with the Broncos.
Surtain was listed as questionable for this game , but the Broncos are going to play it safe. With Riley Moss fully back in the saddle, and given the rise of Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine, the Broncos can afford to get by without Surtain for one more game. Circle Week 8 for Surtain's return.
Hufanga suffered an ankle injury in Week 5. This will be his second missed game, which is why the Broncos elevated safety Taylor Rapp again from the practice squad. Hopefully, Hufanga can return next week alongside Surtain.
Casey and Bentley are rookie draft picks who've yet to dress this season. They probably won't dress, unless there are injuries ahead of them on their respective depth charts.
Both Jackson and Onyedim being inactive is interesting. It implies the Broncos aren't too worried about Arizona's ground attack. Onyedim, the team's highest draft pick this year, has been a healthy scratch in each game.
At a certain point, you've got to wonder when Onyedim is going to get his shot. Then again, Sai'vion Jones has finally been getting some action on defense, and like Onyedim, he was a third-round pick last year who spent his rookie campaign as a healthy scratch, mostly.
Still, given that Denver ranks 31st against the run and Onyedim was one of the 2026 draft class' best run-defending defensive tackles, his inactivity is curious. The Broncos' defensive line gets after the quarterback like no one else, but they're struggling to stop the run.
As for Ehlinger, he'll dress as the emergency quarterback, but he officially goes down as a healthy scratch. That's one of the newer NFL rules, and the Broncos exploit it every week.
👀 our inactives for #DENvsAZ : 📰 » https://t.co/janx2byozb pic.twitter.com/NXDe4kpAh6
Budda Baker is playing. He was listed as questionable but he's dressing.
The big hits here for Arizona are the absences of Love on offense and Nolen on defense. The Broncos will see a lot of running back Tyler Allgeier, and with Nolen out, there's an even bigger opportunity to get the ground game rolling.
