title: Broncos a Team to Watch in Jonathan Taylor Trade Sweepstakes, Insider Claims
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is little more than two weeks out, and the rumor mill is cranking.
Since the Indianapolis Colts fired their general manager, Chris Ballard, the Denver Broncos have been linked to running back Jonathan Taylor all week in the rumor mill. But on Sunday, as Week 7 got underway, ESPN insider Adam Schefter gave the Taylor-to-Denver rumors a heaping dose of credibility.
"The first player to watch in Indianapolis is Jonathan Taylor. There's going to be a lot of interest in Taylor around the league. Teams like the Seattle Seahawks, the Minnesota Vikings, the Denver Broncos, and the Green Bay Packers, who made a run at Jonathan Taylor a couple of years back. [They] could decide to call Indianapolis again," Schefter said on Sunday NFL Countdown .
If Schefter said it, there's something burning at the source of that smoke, even if it's just an ember. And I think, right now, the Taylor possibility is just that: an ember.
The Broncos are through their first six-week gauntlet, and the schedule is now opening up for them. Meanwhile, they just activated rookie running back Jonah Coleman , and the Broncos believe that the best is yet to come from J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey.
If anything, the 4-2 Broncos will be buyers ahead of the November 10 trade deadline, but that's a big if. For the first time in a while, the Broncos have a full complement of draft picks in 2027, and their roster is starting to age, so infusions of youth will be key for the future.
I'm not sure Sean Payton is trying to hear that right now, though. Not after he came within a single game of leading the Broncos to the Super Bowl — a goal that would have been realized had Bo Nix not suffered his ankle injury in the divisional round.
Payton wants to win now because Nix won't be on his rookie contract forever. The third-year quarterback may be slumping, but the Broncos still view him as the future franchise quarteback.
Payton has said playing quarterback is the toughest thing to do in the NFL if you don't have a run game. The Broncos haven't had a viable run game this season, which has only exacerbated Nix's issues.
Re-signing Dobbins and keeping him healthy was supposed to give Nix the run-game foundation he needed to build on in Year 3. Maybe it was the level of competition those first six weeks, maybe it was the culmination of all Dobbins's serious injuries, but he hasn't looked like the player we saw for 10 games last season.
Coleman could be the answer, but pinning a team's rushing hopes on a rookie returning from injured reserve, regardless of his draft pedigree, would be ill-advised. The Broncos have three games left to decide whether to make a play for Taylor, unless another team beats them to the punch.
Taylor already has 492 rushing yards and seven touchdowns this season, though he is averaging a career-low 4.0 yards per carry. He's one of the best backs in the NFL, though, and would immediately upgrade the Broncos' backfield.
If the Broncos want to beat out other potential Taylor buyers, it might take upwards of a second-round pick, plus more, to pry him off Indy's hands. The Broncos will have to decide whether he'd be worth the cost, and they'd have to absorb his new two-year, $44 million contract.
But Denver would have Taylor all the way up until he hit the 30-year-old mark before having to decide on what to do next. Because he has so many miles on his tires, even at 27, there's a chance the Broncos could get him for a third-rounder plus some 2028 late-round capital. Maybe.
We know the Broncos are interested if Schefter is saying it. Let's see if it motivates the likes of Dobbins, Harvey, and Coleman, starting on Sunday at State Farm Stadium as the Broncos take on the Arizona Cardinals .

title: 5 Bold Broncos Predictions vs. Cardinals: Bo Nix's Reckoning
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are preparing to take on the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. The Cardinals are a feisty 2-4 team and are already exceeding expectations.
This isn't a gimme game, despite what some people say. That being said, the Cardinals aren't exactly a good team either.
The Broncos can't overlook this opponent, but this game is a chance to do some maintenance on offense and get the unit firing on all cylinders.
And now it's time for this week's bold predictions. If the Broncos can realize these predictions, it could put them on the winning track for the rest of the season.
Nix has been seeing ghosts when looking deep after some early interceptions and near turnovers, which explains, in part, the ultra-conservative passing approach we've seen for weeks. This is a good game to work on correcting his hesitancy, as the Cardinals rank 31st in explosive pass-play rate allowed.
The Cardinals suffer multiple coverage breaks per game. They have serious issues with their linebacker coverage, and their secondary isn't the best.
The Broncos have no better opponent remaining on the schedule than Arizona to help Nix break out of his shell. The Nix reckoning is coming.
This pairs with my previous prediction; there is ample opportunity to get Harvey involved in the passing and running game. The Cardinals are the NFL's fourth-worst defense when it comes to covering running backs, despite having one of the lowest rates of targets to backs.
Part of this is due to Arizona's secondary issues. The Cardinals' linebackers will be mismatched covering Harvey, and they struggle against outside runs, which is where the Broncos' second-year back can be used in the ground game.
Harvey finishes with 100-plus receiving and 50-plus rushing yards.
The Cardinals haven't allowed many sacks this year (only 12), and they have the eighth-lowest sack percentage and pressure rate. However, they do allow one of the fastest times to pressure (sixth-fastest).
Given how much pressure the Broncos can generate, as long as they can bring down Brissett, they're poised to have a big day in the sack department. If this prediction comes true, it'll be only the third time in franchise history that the Broncos will have posted three straight games with at least five sacks.
This pass rush is on a roll, and that momentum continues in the desert.
Thanks to the pressure up front and forcing a mistake from Brissett, Barron nabs an interception and returns it to the house. Barron is aggressive in coverage, and it sometimes backfires, but it pays off in this game.
Brissett throws an underneath route under pressure, and Barron jumps it for the first pick-six of his career. He actually had one as a rookie, but it was called back due to a defensive holding penalty far away from the play.
Through the first six games, the Broncos have gotten close to a return touchdown. Harvey in particular has had multiple long returns that were a block or an avoided tackle away from being a touchdown.
The Cardinals have lapses on kickoff coverage, which create the opening for a special teams touchdown. The Broncos have had a third-phase score brewing for weeks, but the stars finally align against Arizona, whether it's Harvey or Marvin Mims Jr.

title: How the Broncos Reshuffled 53-Man Roster Ahead of Week 7
full_text:
The Denver Broncos made a flurry of roster moves on the eve of Sunday's road matchup against the Arizona Cardinals .
The Broncos announced that running back Jonah Coleman and outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper have been activated to the 53-man roster, as expected.
Coleman is returning from a four-game absence on injured reserve while Cooper is eligible to play following a season-long stay on the NFL's commisioner's exempt list.
In corresponding transactions, the Broncos placed outside linebacker Jonah Elliss and running back Tyler Badie on short-term IR. Both players must sit out at least four games before suiting up again.
Denver also promoted safety Taylor Rapp and defensive back Sean Fresch Jr. from the practice squad, their second such elevations in as many weeks.
"It wasn't our first time," defensive coordinator Vance Joseph noted on Thursday. "Those guys played well last year. I think it was half of the Dallas game, the Chiefs, and maybe Houston last year. So I wasn't surprised by how they played. We had a good plan for those kids. They played to it. Obviously, our depth on defense is really in the DB room and outside backer room. So we've been very fortunate losing Coop early to have Q and Jonah step up, and losing Pat and Riley to have KD and Barron step up. It's where our depth was. So it was almost luck to kind of have that group intact."
As Joseph himself noted, Cooper will immediately slide back into his old starting role with Elliss -- who suffered an ankle injury in last week's win over Seattle -- now on the shelf. Behind Cooper and fellow starter Nik Bonitto remain Que Robinson and Dondrea Tillman.
"Well, obviously he's a great pass rusher, but I think the energy he plays with, the toughness he plays with, the edge setting he plays with, it's obviously second to none," Joseph said of Cooper. "With Nik opposite of him, more of a speed rusher, he's more of a power rusher. So you'll see Nik kind of get more opportunities also as the quarterback escapes out of the pocket, and now Nik can make plays. Coop's a big part of what we've done in the past, and it's good to have him back."
Rapp and Fresch Jr. will help offset the loss of starting safety Talanoa Hufanga, who was designated on the injury report as out with ankle issue, and the potential gameday rule-out of All-Pro cornerback Patrick Surtain II, considered questionable for Week 7 with his own ankle malady.
Colemean, meanwhile, will slot in at worst as the No. 3 RB behind J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey. At best, a now-healthy Coleman will begin eating into Dobbins' workload and assume more first- and second-down responsibilities.
"First of all, he's very smart. He's handled the playbook very quickly from day one, rookie minicamp on," offensive coordinator Davis Webb said of Coleman on Thursday. "Every time he's gotten an opportunity, whether that be in a regular-season game, obviously the Jacksonville Jaguars game sticks out, the Atlanta Falcons game in the preseason sticks out. So we're excited to get him back into the fold. I think the last couple weeks, our whole running back room is kind of slowly going up, turning in the right direction."

title: Several Broncos Could Make History Against Cardinals in Week 7
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are looking to extend their winning streak to three games this week as they travel to take on the Arizona Cardinals .
The Broncos have won their past three games against the Cardinals and hold a 10-1-1 all-time head-to-head record. Denver's only loss to the Cardinals came on the road. However, the Broncos are 2-1 this season against NFC West opponents.
At 4-2, the Broncos have everything to play for. The AFC West crown is still very much on the table with 11 games left. The Kansas City Chiefs are undefeated at 5-0, but the toughness of their schedule is just getting started, whereas, for the Broncos, they're already through the worst of it.
The Chiefs have to square off with the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday. Next week, the Broncos return home to rematch the Chiefs at Mile High.
If Denver handles its business against the Cardinals, and the Seahawks do the Broncos a favor, Week 8 could decide the AFC West leader at the halfway-point of the season.
Now, let's not get ahead of ourselves. None of this is to say Denver should be looking past Arizona; I only lay it out to show how important winning this game at State Farm Stadium actually is for the Broncos.
Several individual Broncos have career milestones and records within reach on Sunday. And beyond the ultimate objective of winning the game, the Broncos also have some potential team records at stake.
Let's take a look at what to watch for on Sunday when the Broncos square off with the Cardinals.
The Broncos are coming off back-to-back games with five sacks as a team. If they're able to get Jacoby Brissett to the turn five times and make it three straight games, it'll be the first time the Broncos will have achieved that feat since 1991.
Recording five sacks as a team in three straight games has only ever happened twice before. This is Denver's chance to make it a third time in team history.
Sutton needs just one touchdown catch to tie Riley Odoms for the seventh-most receiving scores in Broncos history. Sutton has caught 40 career touchdowns.
This season, though, Sutton has just one touchdown. It's been a slow start for the two-time Pro Bowler, but with the schedule opening up, don't be surprised to see him suddenly take flight .
Waddle needs triple-digit receiving yardage to become the fifth player in team history to record multiple 100-yard receiving games in his first season as a Bronco. It hasn't happened since 2014 when Emmanuel Sanders first joined the club.
Waddle leads the Broncos in receiving yardage, but his one 100-yard game was way back in Week 2. He's also due for a big day.
With one rushing score, Dobbins would become the eighth Bronco ever to record multiple three-game streaks with at least one touchdown on the ground. He scored his first touchdown of the season in Week 5's road win over the Los Angeles Chargers and followed that up with his second last week against the Seahawks.
If the past two games are any indication, Sean Payton plans to continue feeding Dobbins, so there's a good chance he hits this milestone.
With a half-sack, Allen will become the ninth player in Broncos history to notch at least five sacks in four straight seasons. His 4.5 sacks currently lead the team, and he's been almost unstoppable this season.
Going against the team that drafted him out of Boston College, I would imagine that Allen has a little something special in store for the Cardinals.
Bonitto needs just two sacks to tie Trevor Pryce for the third-most sacks by a Bronco in his first five seasons. Bonitto started the season slow, but he's been on a roll of late, sitting with 3.5 sacks entering Week 7.
The Cardinals' offensive line will have a very difficult time keeping Bonitto and Allen from carving themselves out a piece of Broncos history.
Lutz has 98 career field goals as a Bronco, and one more would tie him with David Treadwell for the sixth-most in team history. Lutz has missed three field-goal attempts this season.
However, when the Broncos needed him in the clutch last week, he nailed a kick from 53 yards out to deliver an overtime win over the Seahawks on Thursday Night Football . He could reach 100 career field goals as a Bronco this week, depending on how the Cardinals game unfolds.

title: Broncos' Riley Moss Is Ready to Cut Loose Against Cardinals
full_text:
Getting healthier can only help the 4-2 Denver Broncos keep rolling.
Sunday's trip to the desert to face the 2-4 Arizona Cardinals might end up being a week too early for cornerback Patrick Surtain II — who returned to practice this week and has been listed as questionable for Week 7 —  the Broncos' young secondary can be relied upon to carry the load, based on what we've seen of late.
Surtain's long-time partner in crime, Riley Moss, has been cleared to return to the starting lineup, and he's relishing the challenge the Cardinals will present on Sunday.
"Yeah, it'll be lit," Moss said this week via Denver Sports ' Andrew Mason . "I'm excited."
Moss sounded relieved to be past the rib injury that sidelined him for a game and a few quarters. Such an injury can make playing cornerback a bit tricky because of how the pain restricts movement.
"The biggest thing is a lot of twisting, a lot of movements like that kind of irritate it and that's kind of my job, and it's tough," Moss said via Mason.
Moss returned to action against the Seattle Seahawks, but his playing time was limited to just 20 snaps . A rib injury can take some time to heal.
"When you're rehabbing, you kind of just have to let it heal. And then you can get into your ramp-up and get rolling," Moss said via Mason. "The good thing is, I wasn't out for too long to lose too much conditioning and stuff, but yeah, we approached it good."
Even without the Surtain in the lineup, Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine have really stepped up and made some big plays for defensive coordinator Vance Joseph.
Barron, the Broncos' 2025 first-round pick, is proving he has the coverage chops to hang on the boundary. The Broncos' cornerback depth has shown up at the most opportune times in each of the past two seasons, but it really saved the day over the past three weeks.
Meanwhile, slot corner Ja'Quan McMillian has also continued to excel, so when Surtain returns to man the perimeter opposite Moss, this unit will be off and running again.
Perhaps seeing the young bucks making a name for themselves made Moss a bit more anxious to get back in the lineup — even if it was only in a limited capacity last week against the Seattle Seahawks.
"I was only in for certain personnel and stuff just to kind of get ramped back up," Moss said. "It was tough because it was a short week, so we didn't really practice."
Either way you slice it, the Broncos have a talented cornerback group, and it’s a dynamic collective that’s possibly the deepest and most talented in the entire league. We'll find out on Sunday whether Surtain is back against the Cardinals.
It wouldn't be a shock to see the Broncos hold Surtain out one more week, to reinsert him at home against the Kansas City Chiefs.

title: Broncos Trade Deadline: 5 Realistic Targets to Move the Needle
full_text:
The Denver Broncos still have three games to go between now and the November 10 NFL trade deadline .
The Broncos have some apparent needs, including running back and offensive line, but the next three weeks could reshape the conversation. If the return of rookie running back Jonah Coleman sparks the Broncos' ground game and J.K. Dobbins snaps out of his funk, the team could be more than content to stand pat at the deadline.
This team did face a ridiculous initial six-game schedule, which could explain why the Broncos' offensive line has looked so lackluster, especially as run blockers. With the schedule easing up for the foreseeable future, it wouldn't be a surprise to see the starting five rubber-band back into the top-five status it had entering the 2026 season.
Some would point to tight end as a need, and while I certainly wouldn't disagree, it doesn't feel like the Broncos see it that way. Even if they did, Bo Nix's middle-of-the-field avoidance in the passing game would make the pursuit of a pass-catching tight end pointless, though the Broncos could still use an upgrade at the Y.
Looking around the league, there are five realistic trade options the Broncos could consider. This is an already well-built veteran roster, so any trade acquisition would have to represent a clear upgrade over what Denver already has at that position.
Let's break down these five players.
The Indianapolis Colts could be poised to hold a fire sale at the trade deadline, having just fired GM Chris Ballard amid the team's disappointing 2-4 start. For now, the Colts are retaining head coach Shane Steichen, but if he survives into next season, this team's next GM could be looking to orchestrate a reboot, which will require draft assets.
Indy's best personnel resources could be put on the trade block. Taylor is certainly one of them.
Although his yards-per-carry average is currently at a career low (4.0), Taylor already has 492 rushing yards and seven touchdowns. He just signed a two-year, $44 million deal before the season started, so the Broncos would have to ensure they could fit his contract under the salary cap.
If Taylor was suddenly traded to Denver, Sean Payton would have to consider putting Bo Nix under center more often, at least on first and second down, instead of in the shotgun. Taylor needs that head of steam that the under-center offense can offer a ball-carrier.
Taylor is one of the NFL's best and most prolific running backs, and while it wouldn't be cheap to acquire him, I doubt it would cost the Broncos anywhere near as much as the San Francisco 49ers once gave to the Carolina Panthers for Christian McCaffrey. Taylor will turn 28 in January and he has a  lot of mileage on his three-time Pro Bowl tires.
Imagine for a moment — if you will — a Broncos offensive line that features Nelson at left guard and Quinn Meinerz at right guard. That would be one heck of a way to spark a run game. Nelson is playing on an expiring contract, which makes him an even more realistic trade candidate for the Colts.
That also helps make Nelson realistic for the Broncos, but the team would have to rethink it's long-term strategy at left guard. Current starter, Ben Powers, is expected to depart in free agency next year, and the Broncos drafted Kage Casey in the fourth round this past spring with an eye on being the future at left guard.
Casey had a really good summer, but he's been a healthy scratch thus far. Would Denver want to give up draft capital and sign a proven All-Pro like Nelson to a lucrative multi-year contract rather than follow through on its plan to develop Casey?
That's the rub, but when it comes to this offensive line's failure to launch, Powers is the least to blame of Denver's trio of culprits. Center Luke Wattenberg and right tackle Mike McGlinchey have been far more problematic, both as run and pass blockers.
As for Nelson, giving up a second-round pick would likely get the job done, but if the market heats up for his services, it wouldn't be a shock to see the Colts ask for more. He's going to be 31 next year, but he's coming off his eighth straight Pro Bowl nod and was a second-team All-Pro last season (for the third time in his career). He's also a three-time first-team All-Pro.
Irving has one more year left on his contract, but the Bucs are headed in the wrong direction. He's rushed for 452 yards and two touchdowns this season, averaging a healthy 4.7 yards per carry.
Irving was Nix's teammate at Oregon for two years, and they entered the NFL draft together in 2024. Nix went to Denver in Round 1 while Irving landed in Tampa in Round 4. They made a lot of hay together in Oregon, so I'd imagine they could hit the ground running as pros.
Irving is only 24, and while he rushed for 1,122 yards and eight touchdowns as a rookie, injuries caused him to finish with half that production in Year 2. He's appeared in every game this season for Tampa, though.
Depending on Tampa's desparation, I would start with a third-round pick for Irving's services. If the Bucs wanted a second-rounder, it might be a bridge too far, given that Denver could find a good running back in the draft next spring. But that wouldn't help them in the present.
While we're talking potential fire sales, Vea has to be in the conversation of realistic targets. He asked for a trade this past summer, but instead of dealing him, the Bucs gave him a one-year, $30 million extension.
The Broncos' defensive line has been okay this season, but when it comes to stopping the run, they've struggled. Only one team has been worse against the run, and one of Denver's biggest issues is the lack of mass up front.
The 6-foot-4, 347-pound Vea would be an immediate solution. The problem? He's about to turn 32 in February, so any team interested in his services would have to be confident that he has plenty left in the tank.
If a third-round pick would get it done, I'd be on the phone right now with the Bucs. At least to check on the possibility.
Barkley has been banged up this year, but the Eagles could be poised to sell off some of their top assets, being in a similar situation as the Colts, minus the firing of their general manager. Barkley turns 30 in February, so any team acquiring him would have to verify his health and feel confident in his long-term viability.
Barkley is under contract for two more years, which could be advantageous for the Broncos. That would give them the chance to make use of his talents now, and give them time to determine whether he's worth re-signing beyond 2028 when his contract expires.
When Barkley is healthy and in the zone, there's no better running back in the NFL. But it would probably take a second-round pick plus perhaps a 2028 Day 3 selection to pry him off Philly's hands.

title: 8 Winners, 3 Losers in Detroit Lions Win Over Packers
full_text:
On Sunday, the Detroit Lions came back after a bye week to start divisional play, taking on the Green Bay Packers.
The Lions forced multiple stops in the first half, en route to a 10-7 halftime lead. The Packers took advantage of a turnover on the Lions’ opening drive of the second half to grab their first lead, but Detroit snapped back and executed when it mattered most, taking up the final three minutes of game clock to kick a game-winner as time expired. Detroit emerged victorious, 20-17.
Here are the winners and losers from the divisional affair.
The Lions All-Pro receiver has been a thorn in the NFC North’s side for nearly a half-decade, but Green Bay seemed to forget about St. Brown in the first half. The receiver found himself having a career day in the first half.
St. Brown started his damage with a simple out and up where his man could not keep up with him. That was the theme of the opening half, as the receiver slid behind coverage. The Packers surrendered 204 receiving yards in the first half, with the USC product accounting for 135 yards on seven catches on eight targets.
The Packers elected to finally cover the Pro Bowl receiver, holding him to 15 yards in the second half. That said, St. Brown finished with his fifth 150-yard receiving game of his career.
The Packers had a rough start to the game, with St. Brown and then Williams burning the secondary on back-to-back plays. Right after the former had an out-and-up for a big gain, Williams was open for another gain, and then was targeted a second time in the flat, which he took for a touchdown.
The Packers clamped up on Williams after that, only allowing one more catch in the first half as St. Brown ran wild. The halftime adjustments to cover St. Brown enabled the Alabama product to get free for two more catches for 40 yards on the Lions’ go-ahead scoring drive.
Williams capped that drive off with his second touchdown of the night, after an eligible Penei Sewell ran routes and helped free up Williams on a hitch route.
Branch made his return to the field on Sunday, and it was quite the successful return. The former Lions second-round pick aided a few defensive stops early. Branch helped the communication throughout the day, along with breaking up a pass.
His biggest play of the night, however, came to open the fourth quarter. Jordan Love took a shot deep with Christian Watson appearing to have a step on Khalil Dorsey. Branch, however, flashed over to high point the ball and ended a chance of a Green Bay go-ahead scoring drive.
Reed was strong on Sunday, despite the Lions allowing nearly 300 yards through the air. The corner made some of the biggest plays of the days when it was needed most. With Green Bay inside the Lions’ 10-yard line on fourth down, Reed sniffed out a screen and dropped Matthew Golden behind the line of scrimmage. That ended an impressive Packers streak, as they had converted their previous nine fourth-down attempts.
Reed also added a pass breakup late, knocking the ball out to force a punt. Most breakdowns on the day did not occur from Reed, and he quietly put together one of his best games in Honolulu Blue.
Hutchinson brought down Jordan Love for the only Lions sack of the game in the second quarter, providing a significant portion of the defensive stops needed. He also nearly picked off Love during the first half.
Hutchinson finished with five quarterback hits , while the rest of the team combined for one hit on the afternoon.
As the fourth quarter wore down, the Lions and Packers each got desperate to make a play. The Lions went for it on fourth down and got stuffed on a Jahmyr Gibbs run , giving the Packers the ball inside the Lions’ 30-yard line. That dragged out the Lions defense, which stood tall and forced a Trey Smack field goal attempt.
Wonnum made arguably the biggest play of the night, with the South Carolina product getting a few fingers on the Smack field goal, deflecting it and pushing it just wide.
While it was not a game that saw Jahmyr Gibbs go for over 150 total yards, Gibbs was quietly doing his role behind the scenes. Sonic finished the game with just over 130 total yards, crossing 100 yards in the final two minutes.
On the opening scoring drive, it was Gibbs picking up a blitz to enable a big play to Jameson Williams, who would follow that up with a score on the next play.
In the final two minutes, Gibbs faced a free touchdown twice and declined it both times, kneeling to make it second-and-2 before taking another kneel after converting a 3rd-and-6 on a toss play. That enabled the Lions to run the clock out and kick a field goal as time expired.
Bates was needed for all eight of his points on Sunday, with the Arkansas product kicking the Lions home to victory as time expired.
None of Bates’s field goals were particularly hard, but he was part of the end product that executed a win. His kickoffs were also strong, with the kicker forcing Green Bay to return the ball and not break their 30-yard-line. Full marks for the former Michigan Panther.
It was a rough opening to the season for Mays. The center was activated for Sunday’s contest after being the star free agent acquisition to the offensive line. In the first half, Mays provided a strong push in the opening series. That was offset by a false start penalty where the entire offense besides Mays moved.
Then, to make matters worse, Mays was knocked into Gibbs, forcing the back to fumble as the Lions were deep in Green Bay territory. It gave the Packers a way to escape, kneeling to end the half.
Mays did not have a strong start to the second half, either. The center had a bad exchange with Goff on the opening series, with the ball bouncing two yards past the line of scrimmage and being recovered by Green Bay. That enabled Green Bay to score a go-ahead touchdown on their ensuing drive.
Barnes had a rough outing Sunday. On two separate fourth-down plays , the Purdue product was tagged for a missed assignment in coverage. The Packers went 3-of-4 on fourth down in the opening half, and Barnes was the primary man giving free conversions to Green Bay.
To make matters worse, Barnes was again the primary man in coverage when the Packers had their go-ahead touchdown in the third quarter, and missed a shoestring tackle attempt as Josh Jacobs ran in for the touchdown.
Additionally, in the fourth quarter, Barnes was whistled for an unnecessary roughness penalty, albeit controversial, with Tom Brady lamenting the call on television.
After a loud week in off-the-field headlines, LaPorta had a quiet game on the field. He went the entire first half without a target, primarily showcasing his blocking. In the third quarter, the Lions faced a lull, and Goff airmailed a swing pass to LaPorta in the flat.
It was a very quiet day for the Iowa product who was coming off his best game of the season before the bye week. That said, when LaPorta was called upon on Sunday, he answered. LaPorta was open on his first target, and made the most of his second target, catching the ball for an 18-yard gain on the game-winning drive for Motown.
Sports writer since 2022. Emmett Matasovsky started covering the Detroit Lions in 2025. He has extensive experience covering Michigan State Spartans athletics, including MSU basketball and football. Has demonstrated passionate, in-depth coverage of college athletics.

title: Everything Dan Campbell Said After Lions Defeated Packers
full_text:
Here is a transcript of everything Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell said after his team defeated the Green Bay Packers to move to 4-2 on the season.
The former NFL tight end shared why he went for it on fourth-down in the fourth quarter and addressed the improved play of the defense, the return of Brian Branch.
“All right. That team's been playing really good football, won three in a row, and we had our hands full. That was a good win, man. I thought our defense really showed up. Everything we talked about -- the way we needed to play this game against that high offense, getting (Packers RB Josh) Jacobs back. We had to try to eliminate or limit what those two receivers (Packers WRs Christian Watson and Matthew Golden) could do and try not to let them behind us. Then I thought our back end, it wasn't perfect, but I thought they played really good back there, man. I thought we played sticky. I thought we were challenging. Some of our guys – I thought (CB Khalil) Dorsey, man, stepped in and did some big things. There was no panic, made some big plays downfield. That's something that has hurt most teams. We talked about it, and (Packers QB Jordan) Love's got the ability to find it. Front was disruptive, you know, we talked about being disruptive, trying to play with violence and trying to make it hard. Ultimately, man, I thought our defense really, really stepped up, and they were the big story of this game. Offensively, we really played pretty good until the two turnovers, and then we had one of those drives that we messed up that was not good, man. We didn't convert on the fourth down, and then the two takeaways. Really, we had some good things going, we just couldn't finish out. And that's frustrating, but at the end of the day, (QB) Jared Goff, one more time, putting it in his hands, man, he's playing at such a high level. We have a tremendous amount of trust. He's just going to take care of the football, do the right thing, make explosive passes when they're there, get it to the right person, manage the game when we need him to manage it, push the ball when we need him to push it. He's playing at such a high level. That offensive line, I thought, protected him very well. It was a good win, you know, it was a good win. Division win number one. Finally got a couple wins here, and now we'll get ready for Minnesota.”
“Well, I thought we would get it, number one. I really believed we would get that. Number two, I knew we would get the ball back if it didn't work out. And those were the key thoughts.”
“Yeah, man, he’s done a lot. You go through an injury like that, the amount of rehab and things that go into all of that to get back to where you're ready to play at a high level in the NFL, top tier talent and to get back to some of what you are. He's not even fully back yet, as far as, just the rust. He's healthy. Every time, every rep he'll take, he's going to get better and better. But it's not an easy road, especially when, -- I mean, he loves the game, man. He's highly competitive. He wants to go. Really, the hard thing was managing him in the first half. He was all over me early and I said, 'Listen, we just got to be smart, see where you're at.' And once we got into halftime, it felt like we're good here. It's a huge play. Everybody loves BB because he's a great teammate and he's a productive football player, man. He just can find the ball. He's got a nose for it. And not only that, he knocked out some of those runs. He's just a heck of a football player.”
“Are you surprised? I could have told you that was going to happen. You know Saint. Saint was ready to go. Saint was ready to go after Arizona. He had to go through a whole Bye, though. He does what he does, and he's reliable. You can count on it. You can count on the production in the run game and the pass game, and he's going to make plays, and he's going to find a way to win a one-on-one and make criticals, and he did it once again today.”
“That was big. We kind of talked about that before this game. We knew where (WR Amon-Ra St. Brown) Saint would be at, and just, Jamo, man. Let's take that next step into the electricity, man. Making some of these catches, taking off with it. That game against Green Bay a year ago, he really took off, and he was kind of like, 'Man, let's find some of these again,' where we can get the ball in his hands and let him cut it loose. He made some huge plays for us. So those two guys, that O-line protecting (Lions QB Jared) Goff, letting Goff deliver these accurate balls for our guys so they could run with it was big.”
“Kind of big spot? Those are enormous, going in and coming out. That's the hardest thing is – we're excited, I'm excited that we won that game, but you can't do that. We were fortunate. Our defense put the fires out there, and we were able to recover, but we just can't do it. We know that because, at the end of the day, we did. We played pretty good football and played, in some regards, some of our best football. But when you put those on there, man, those hurt, and we had a chance to really try to extend the lead there significantly, and we didn't do it.”
“Well, that's our guys. Those guys aren't going to give in or go in the tank or whatever. We were able to overcome, but it takes all three units. I mean, between – everybody had a hand in it. Cover units, (Lions WR DeAndre) Carter was big. How about Carter, man? Carter’s got a little juice. It’s good to have him here. But then just the defense then doing what they needed to do, and offensively, man, we calmed down, we got back in our groove. Found a way to, at the end of the day, let’s drive it all the way down there and finish with the ball in our hands until we hand it to (Lions RB Jahmyr) Gibbs with one second left. It wasn’t perfect, but, man, that’s what it’s about. Defense had done enough to where now it’s time for offense to finish this game out. It’s not fair to ask them to go back out there again after the way they’ve been playing their tails off, and our offense stepped up in a big way to finish the game.”
“Well, the more that you start to make plays with one another and I can see there is a confidence, there is a trust that's building with some of these guys, most of these guys’ areas. And so, when that begins to go up, now your whole level plate and the floor begins to rise here. So, the front's been doing a really good job. The backers have been playing pretty dang good too and the back end in spurts, but these last two games we really stepped up and I feel like they know where their health's at. They're starting to use it, man. Now they're gaining confidence. We're challenging on some of these throws down the field. We're making it hard and there's nothing free, man. We're trying to defend every blade of grass and that's what good defenses do. And so there really is a mindset and an aggressiveness, and so I'm proud of those guys. I feel like they're getting better.”
“We're going to use all those guys, just like we did today. That was the plan coming in. Hey, we're going to use all of our – they're all going to the game. We're using them on special teams, we're going to use them on defense too. Let's roll them. And we also knew those guys had launched some of these, so let's get some fresh bodies in there if we need to. And we'll continue to do that. When guys step on and make plays, we can get more opportunities. That's the bottom line, man. So, did a good job, and there's no reason why he wouldn't get a few more plays.”
“That was big time. Our defense, we talk all the time about putting fires out. The defense put the fire out. And they’re already in field goal range. title: Lions Injury Update Confirms Star Avoided Serious Issue
full_text:
The Detroit Lions secured a massive divisional win over the Green Bay Packers on Sunday.
Playing their first divisional opponent of the season, the Lions overcame some mistakes and were ultimately able to earn a hard-fought 20-17 victory over the Packers to advance to 4-2 on the season.
Running back Jahmyr Gibbs played a pivotal part in the victory, notchng 116 rushing yards on 29 carries. The dynamic running back played a key part on the final drive, as he converted the final third-down to cement the win.
On that game-sealing run, however, Gibbs landed awkwardly trying to slide onto the turf inbounds to keep the clock running and prevent the Packers from getting the ball back. Though the landing wasn't smooth, head coach Dan Campbell stated that he should be okay during his postgame press conference.
"We got him checked. He should be good. That's that whole, is it really worth going down?" Campbell said. "Or should he just go score? Sometimes I question that. Maybe he should've just (scored). But, all good. That's a good win."
Gibbs had slid to the turf two plays prior, on first-down, two yards short of the chains. This was done in an effort to maintain the running clock, but it nearly backfired after the Lions jumped resulting in a five-yard penalty.
However, on third-and-6, quarterback Jared Goff pitched the ball to Gibbs who burst around the left side before sliding after getting the first down. This allowed the Lions to run the clock all the way down to one second before taking a timeout to set up Jake Bates' game-winning field goal.
Campbell's update is a sigh of relief for Detroit, as Gibbs is one of the team's most dynamic talents and one of the league's best running backs. Signed to a three-year contract extension in the offseason, the Alabama product is off to another strong start through six games in 2026.
Detroit's offseason saw the team deal David Montgomery, who was Gibbs' counterpart in the backfield, to the Houston Texans and cement Gibbs as their top running back moving forward. This has come with an increased workload for him, as he has had at least 20 touches in five of the team's six games.
Up to this point, Gibbs has notched 620 rushing yards and nine total touchdowns, with seven on the ground and two as a receiver. Sunday's game against the Packers marked the first one this year where Gibbs was kept out of the end-zone.

title: Key Takeaways From Detroit Lions 20-17 Victory Against Packers
full_text:
The Detroit Lions were only able to win two of their six division games last season. With how important it is to thrive in division play, the game against the Green Bay Packers in Week 7 was another test in one of the toughest divisions in the NFL
Detroit's offense has been tasked with carrying a defense that has many question marks. One aspect of the offense that has been successful has been Jared Goff executing play-action passes.
“I think just from his standpoint, one of the things that makes him so elite in that is his process. It's uncomfortable and you don't do it a ton in college anymore where you turn your back to the defense," said Drew Petzing. "You have to take in a ton of information pre-snap, and you have to know where your eyes need to go and who you need to locate on their side of the ball and on our side of the ball. And I think that's a huge part of the action game.
"He's done it at such a high level that I think even when that happens, he's able to calibrate quickly, figure out what's going on and make the proper decision almost every time. And that's really one of the main reasons I think he's excelled in that area.”
Turnovers were a factor in this contest, as Detroit allowed Green Bay back in the game late in the second-quarter and early in the second half.
After 60 minutes of action, Detroit was able to take advantage late of multiple personal foul calls and mistakes from the Packers, advancing their record to 4-2.
Here are the takeaways from the Lions' 20-17 victory.
Detroit's offense quickly took advantage of an early error by the Packers. After winning the opening coin toss, the Lions chose to defer.
Green Bay was able to march into the red zone, but were not able to punch it in to the end zone. A delay of game penalty forced the Packers to back up five yards, which proved to be costly , as kicker Trey Smack missed an easy field goal try.
Detroit quickly marched down the field for an opening touchdown. Goff found Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams early in the game.
The speedy wideout capped off the six-play, 80-yard drive with a 16-yard touchdown reception.
It was only the second touchdown for the Lions in the first quarter this season, and the first since Jahmyr Gibbs opened the regular season with a one-yard score against the Saints in Week 1.
29 straight games for Goff with TD pass! JAMO pic.twitter.com/9oABAir9TW
The Packers quickly tied the game, with Jordan Love leading his team on a 12-play, 74-yard scoring drive to answer Detroit's opening scoring drive.
Tight end Tucker Kraft proved to be difficult to coverage, as he secured a key fourth-down reception on the Packers second drive for a gain of 22 yards.
With the Packers in the red zone, Jack Campbell fell in coverage and Kraft took advantage. Love scrambled and connected with the talented tight end on a 14-yard touchdown.
Through their first two possessions, Green Bay secured six first-downs and were 2-for-5 on third-down.
Green Bay moved deep into Detroit territory midway through the second quarter, but a huge tackle for loss by cornerback D.J. Reed forced a turnover on downs inside Detroit's red-zone. The Lions would then go on a lengthy drive and looked poised to extend their lead before the half.
Goff connected with Amon-Ra St. Brown multiple times, and the veteran passer surpassed 200 passing yards before halftime. On second-and-10 from the Green Bay 12-yard line with :30 seconds to play, however, Detroit's fortunes changed for the worse.
Jahmyr Gibbs took a handoff for a short gain, but ran into center Cade Mays at the end of his run and the ball was jarred loose. The friendly fire resulted in a fumble that was recovered by Green Bay, ending the Lions' drive and sending the game to halftime with Detroit leading 10-7.
Disaster would strike again on Detroit's first drive of the second half. Mays, who was playing in his first game with the organization after a wrist injury sent him to injured reserve in training camp, had a botched snap exchange with Goff that resulted in another Packers recovery to start the third quarter.
The second fumble would have dire consequences, as the Packers took advantage of the short field and scored on a 25-yard touchdown from Love to Josh Jacobs.
The Packers were called for a couple of penalties that assisted the Lions keep their offensive drive alive in the third-quarter.
Linebacker Brenton Cox Jr. was called for roughing the passer and cornerback Brandon Cisse.
Campbell, similar to LaFleur earlier in the game, decided to go for it on fourth-down deep in the red zone. Unfortunately, Cisse pushed Williams out of bounds in the back of the end zone, keeping the score at 17-14.
Not on Branch’s watch pic.twitter.com/ABGm4f0ZWt
In the second half, Goff narrowly avoided tossing an interception, as the Packers defenders were not able to haul in passes that could have been picked off.
Green Bay was able to tie the score at 17-17.
With the football midway through the fourth-quarter, Campbell decided to go for it again on fourth-down, but this time deep in their own territory.
The Packers defense stuffed Gibbs, forcing a turnover on downs. The Packers failed to capitalize, as Smack missed a 35-yard field goal that was blocked partially by defensive end DJ Wonnum.
1.) Rookie Keith Abney dropped a third-down interception in the end zone after a throwaway toss by Love.
2.)  Goff passed Derek Carr (41,245) for the third-most passing yards through 11-career seasons in NFL history.
3.) Lions fan Cody DeLorenzo completed a 313-mile ultramarathon run for charity from Lambeau Field in Green Bay to Ford Field in Detroit with the game ball. The organization rewarded him with two Super Bowl tickets.
4.) After the Lions took the lead in the third-quarter, Khalil Dorsey and D.J. Reed both made plays on deep shots forcing a three-and-out for the Packers.
5.) Brian Branch earned his first interception of the 2026 season to end a Packers drive early in the fourth quarter.
6.) Lions cornerback Ennis Rakestraw injured his ankle and was listed as questionable to return in the fourth quarter.
7.) The Lions drove 71 yards in 10 plays to win the game, with kicker Jake Bates knocking through a 22-yard field goal as time expired to give the Lions the win.

title: Detroit Lions Second-Year DE Remains Inactive Against Packers
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have officially released their list of players who will not suit up against the Green Bay Packers at Ford Field.
Second-year defensive end Ahmed Hassanein, who posted a social media message that many took as being encouraging about his game status this week, remains inactive.
He has now been ruled inactive for the first six games of the 2026 season, despite having a positive training camp.
Others ruled inactive include Mekhi Wingo, Bishop Fitzgerald, Seth McLaughlin and Jackson Meeks.
Hassanein is seeking at some point to contribute to a defensive line that has had a strong start to the season. Part of the reason for the resurgence has been the play of defensive tackle Alim McNeill.
After returning from a torn ACL last year, McNeill did not perform at the level he expected.
Now fully healed, the 26-year-old is among the top interior defensive linemen in the league.
McNeill's 79.4 PFF grade ranks seventh out of 129 qualifying defensive linemen. Kacy Rodgers has the defensive line ranked fourth in pass block win rate (58%).
“I think this is maybe the best we’ve seen Mac. I mean, the pressure he’s creating up the middle, it’s created a trickle effect for guys around him, to be honest with you," Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard explained to local reporters earlier this week. "He’s winning at a high rate right now, and what it’s doing for guys around him and how selfless he is. But not only the pass rush, that’s kind of what gets glamoured upon, but in the run game.
“What he’s doing in the run game and able to get back to playing stout, especially when he sees double teams and things like that," Sheppard explained further. "I’m just excited for him because I know the frustration he had before not being able to be him kind of his full self.”
The Packers offensive line has struggled to start the season and has deal with many injuries. As a result, Green Bay has been quite ineffective rushing the football.
Green Bay has a run-blocking grade of 47.8, which ranks 31st in the NFL.

title: Setting Lions Fans Expectation for Alim McNeill Against Packers
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have a pivotal matchup on Sunday against the Green Bay Packers.
On Sunday, the Lions will have their first divisional game against their rivals and an opportunity to make a statement. They are looking for their third division crown in four years, and Sunday's matchup is the first of two consecutive division games.
One element that could be a big asset for Detroit is their pass-rush. The defense has ranked poorly in many statistics, but entered Week 7 leading the league with 20 sacks. They've gotten plenty of production from Aidan Hutchinson, D.J. Wonnum and Alim McNeill.
In McNeill's case, it has been a strong start after a down year in 2025. McNeill missed the start of the 2025 season while rehabbing a torn ACL, but has returned to form after a full offseason and recorded 3.5 sacks through the first five games.
Sports Betting Dime 's Drew Ellis feels confident in McNeill's ability to get after the quarterback once again in Week 7. He has tabbed McNeill to record at least a half-sack in Sunday's game as his best bet for the week.
The line for McNeill going over .25 sacks in Sunday's game is currently set at (+229).
"I’m getting a little risky this week. Green Bay has had arguably the worst offensive line play in the league," Ellis told Lions OnSI. His 3.5 sacks is tied for second-most in a season for the veteran defensive tackle."
The Packers have struggled to keep Love upright throughout the start to the season. McNeill could be a massive option for Detroit to put that pressure on him, as his ability to rush from the interior is a difference-making trait.
Entering Sunday's game, the Packers have the ability to challenge Detroit downfield with their passing game. However, if McNeill can put heat on the quarterback , it will take the pressure off of the secondary and could swing the game in Detroit's favor.

title: Key Matchup Detroit Lions Must Win Against Green Bay Packers
full_text:
The Detroit Lions will face arguably their biggest test of the season Sunday afternoon when they take on Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers .
Since the beginning of their three-game win streak in Week 4, the Packers have looked like one of the NFL's very best teams. Notably, they've allowed no more than 14 points each of the past three weeks, and enter Week 7 with the league's 10th-ranked defense (20.8 points allowed/game).
As good as the Packers’ defense has been, though, it's hardly the only part of the team that has stood out in recent weeks. Green Bay, in fact, has also greatly benefited from the emergence of wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden.
Watson and Golden are both easily on the verge of breakout campaigns.
Watson has already compiled as many touchdowns as last season (six) and nearly as many receptions (29) and reception yards as he did a year ago (538). The 2022 second-round pick accumulated 35 catches and 611 yards in 10 games a season ago.
Meanwhile, Golden, Green Bay's first-round pick in 2025, has already exceeded all his receiving totals from his rookie season. He's coming off a 104-yard receiving performance last week against the Dallas Cowboys, and for the season, he's secured 30 catches, 501 yards and three touchdowns. And just like Watson, he's well on his way to notching a 1,000-yard receiving campaign.
Undoubtedly, keeping Watson and Golden in check will be a tough task for Detroit's secondary.
Luckily for Kelvin Sheppard's defense , though, Brian Branch will be active on Sunday for the first time in 2026, after missing the Lions’ first five games while recovering from a torn Achilles.
The Pro Bowl safety's presence alone should elevate the play of Detroit's defensive backfield, which has dealt with its fair share of struggles thus far this season.
“Whenever you gain a player like (Branch) and his caliber back, it's outstanding,” Sheppard told reporters earlier this week. "There are multiple things that player can do to help us, and we'll find the spots that we feel is right and he feels is right for him as we progress.”
When Branch is at his very best, he's a plus defender against both the run and the pass. Just last year, he earned a Pro Football Focus run defense grade of 82.6 and a PFF pass coverage mark of 74.3, both top-13 marks among all qualified safeties last season.
So, he should be a big help when it comes to attempting to curtail the production of Watson and Golden Sunday.
And he could be especially resourceful when it comes to defending Watson. While Watson surely possesses the ability to beat defenders deep, he also does a striking amount of his damage over the middle of the field. In fact, he paces all NFL receivers with 309 receiving yards in the middle part of the field, equating to a staggering 28.1 yards per catch on such targets.
As a result, a strong day in coverage from Branch could go a long way toward preventing Watson from exploding for a big afternoon.
At this present juncture, I'm willing to predict that Watson finishes with six catches for 67 yards in the Week 7 divisional matchup .

title: Roundtable: Lions Week 7 Preview Against Packers
full_text:
The Detroit Lions OnSI staff previews the Detroit Lions Week 7 matchup with the Green Bay Packers.
Vito Chirco: I believe the Lions will be tested all game long against the Packers. To me, Green Bay is a formidable opponent, and might be even stronger now with the return of Pro Bowl running back Josh Jacobs. So, if the Lions play anything less than their “A game,” they're likely going to be in trouble and end up on the losing end. But, I envision a solid enough effort from Dan Campbell's squad in this Week 7 divisional affair. I believe with Brian Branch back in the starting lineup, the Lions will deliver one key stop and Jared Goff and the offense will come through in the fourth quarter. The Lions come out on top in what will be a highly contested game from start to finish.
Emmett Matasovsky: With Cade Mays and Josh Jacobs both active on offense for their respective squads, I foresee a shootout. The Lions get Brian Branch back for some desperately needed help on defense, but the question becomes if that is enough.
The Lions offense, on fresh legs after an extremely strong start to the year, is expected to be deadly. Any given player or star can produce, and it is a battle to stick with Jahmyr Gibbs for the whole event. I see a Motown win at the very end.
Christian Booher : This is a great opportunity for the Lions to prove that they belong in the conversation for the NFC North title. Getting Branch and Mays back will be huge wins, and both players will be able to make a huge impact.
Detroit's defense is the biggest factor in Sunday's game. The Packers have shown that they're not afraid to take deep shot after deep shot, and the Lions' secondary has struggled as one of the league's worst pass defenses. I think it's a shootout, with Green Bay getting one more big play than Detroit and stealing the win.
Chirco : I'm going to go with Jahmyr Gibbs. I know that the Packers’ pass defense is one of the best in the league, so I think the Lions will need a big game from Gibbs in order to secure the Week 7 victory. And I believe Gibbs will deliver just that for Detroit, helping Dan Campbell's team eke out its fourth win of the season.
Matasovsky : The MVP will be Jahmyr Gibbs. Gibbs had 200 yards from scrimmage and got the full week to rest up, along with regaining Cade Mays on the offensive line. Mays is expected to be a tangible upgrade from Juice Scruggs, and the former second-rounder already did an admirable job paving the way to open the year.
Expect at least 150 yards from scrimmage for Sonic, if not over 200 yards.
Booher : I think it will be Aidan Hutchinson. The Michigan product is one of the top pass-rushers in the league, and against a team that could decimate Detroit's secondary, Hutchinson could change the game by getting to Jordan Love. I expect him to have a massive impact against a struggling Packers' offensive line.
Chirco : I think there certainly will be moments. Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are a formidable pass-caching duo, and they've been torching pass defenses for weeks now. And even though it's great to have Brian Branch back, Detroit is still lacking a bonafide No. 1 cornerback. With that said, I expect Watson and Golden to both deliver strong showings in this Week 7 tilt.
Matasovsky : In all passing yards per game statistics, be it from this season or the last three games, the Packers rank among the top 10 in passing yards for the NFL. The Lions secondary, even in one of their best games, let Jacoby Brissett throw for a season-high yardage. The obvious answer is yes.
Brian Branch coming back will be huge, but the Lions have already lost a prime piece that would rotate from the re-activation of Branch, as Avonte Maddox’s season ended from injury. Branch can only be in one place at a time, and when there are multiple missed assignments in coverage each play, breakdowns will happen.
Booher : I do think the Lions are going to struggle on Sunday against Green Bay's passing attack. Green Bay is uniquely designed to give the Lions problems, with an array of weapons like Matthew Golden, Christian Watson and tight end Tucker Kraft.
I believe the Packers are going to test the Lions early, and as a result a big defensive play could help swing momentum. Because the Lions have struggled so much in the secondary, the onus is on the pass-rush to get home and make everyone's life easier.
Chirco : To me, they were very messy and uncalled for. I'll take it a step further and say they were tone deaf. LaPorta has to be able to “read the room” better and know that those comments are only going to piss off the Lions fanbase and make him look like an individual who is out of touch with reality (especially considering the economic issues in today's world). LaPorta lost himself a lot of supporters with those comments, and he just better hope now he “balls out” the rest of the season.
Matasovsky : In the media, it is a scandal. The Iowa product said the quiet part out loud about his frustrating contract negotiations after his best game of the season. It is (justifiably) one of, if not the top, media story of the week.
In the locker room, I do not think there are many eyebrows being raised or heads being turned. Those that are close with LaPorta in Allen Park’s facility have likely heard the same frustrations, probably with more expletives thrown in.
It is messy, but I doubt it is a locker room distraction or the beginning crack of a broken locker room. It is, like I said earlier, a player saying the quiet part out loud about their negotiations.
Booher : I was not expecting those comments because of how the Lions have traditionally handled those conversations. LaPorta does have every right to be upset with the way things are going, but that should be a conversation for the organization, not a larger audience.
I think Mike Valenti's point on it was very accurate. It was a tone-deaf argument from LaPorta and insulting to fans. However, he's justifiably a huge part of the organization with how well he's played since being drafted, and as a result some of his frustrations are understood.
Chirco : I want to see him log “competitive” snaps in his 2026 season debut. And when I say competitive, I mean I want to see him running around the field and being a nuisance against both the run and the pass. When Branch is at his best, that is exactly what he brings to the table. So, if he can make a couple run stops and deflect a pass or two, I think it'd be a solid outing from the Pro Bowl safety.
Matasovsky : Not to set lofty goals, but three interceptions. Just kidding. I want to see a player that has a good range of motion and full trust in his legs when it comes time to plant to jump, or to leave his feet when diving for a tackle.
On top of that, I want to see a more informed secondary in terms of communication with Branch on the field. In coverage, I want to see the Alabama product staying close enough, if not fully stride-for-stride. In essence, I want to see signs of the former Lions second-round pick being healthy.
The final, and most important, thing I want to see from him on Sunday is him walking up the Ford Field tunnel postgame in full pads and with a clean bill of health.
Booher : For me, I would just like to see Branch be able to play and move around in some capacity. My expectations for his first start of the season are relatively low, and I'm not expecting him to be the level of player he was pre-injury right away.
I think Branch will have 1-2 "wow" moments, such as a big hit or an acrobatic deflection, but overall just his presence in the secondary will give a boost of confidence to the group as a whole.

title: Detroit Lions 2026 Week 7 Rooting Guide
