title: Rams Practice Squad Breakdown: Injuries Could Force Unexpected Players Into Action
full_text:
As the Los Angeles Rams enter Week 7, they have been hit hard by the injury bug. Wide receiver Davante Adams, along with defensive linemen Kobie Turner and Poona Ford, was placed on injured reserve this week. Additionally, wide receiver Puka Nacua’s status is uncertain as he manages a calf injury suffered in practice.
It seems as if wherever the Rams turn, another injury pops up. Every day brings another player dealing with some sort of injury. If the Rams are without Nacua and Adams on Sunday, it could force them to go to the practice squad.With injuries forcing the Rams to rely more on their depth, it seemed like a good time to take an updated look at the practice squad. As a reminder, teams are allowed to elevate a player off the practice squad three times during the regular season.
Andersen had some strong moments in the preseason , but it would be surprising to see him on the active roster unless injuries dictate it. That’s especially the case as the Rams re-signed Tanner Ingle to the practice squad after cutting him. With that said, given some of the issues on special teams, Andersen’s tackling ability could be beneficial there at some point. Andersen was one of the better special teams players for the Rams in the preseason.
Nick Andersen picks it up! 📺 @CBSLosAngeles | 📲 https://t.co/R5m5kJYWYi pic.twitter.com/6UOfb3QkEU
While Austin Blaske showed some promise in the preseason, the practice squad is the best spot for him right now. The Rams will continue developing him throughout the season. At some point, he could take Justin Dedich’s role as a reliable depth player on the interior.
Given some of the inconsistencies on special teams, Jack Bouwmeester could absolutely find his way on the active roster at some point. The Rams and special teams coordinator Bubba Ventrone don’t seem sold on Evans, who might be on the hot seat. Bouwmeester is part of the International Player Pathway Program.
The Rams may like what they saw from Fourqurean during the preseason, but he’s behind Cam Lampkin on the practice squad depth chart. When the Rams needed cornerback depth last week against the Cardinals, they went to Lampkin. Still, Fourqurean is a player they’ll continue developing.
Hance is a veteran player who gives the Rams some depth at offensive tackle. The Rams like Bill Murray more, but if they got into an injury pinch, Hance would likely be one of the first players they call up.
Following the Rams placing Poona Ford on injured reserve, they signed Jalen Hunt. Hunt was an undrafted free agent originally signed by the Jacksonville Jaguars after spending seven years in college. He fits the Rams’ profile on the defensive line and will provide depth at that spot with Ford out for the season. Hunt may not see the active roster this season, but the Rams have done well developing players on the defensive line.
JALEN HUNT ALL UP IN THE BACKFIELD 💪 pic.twitter.com/9kV6j1ot6c
The Rams cut Ingle after the game against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 4 given some of the issues on special teams. However, they brought him back to the practice squad . Ingle hasn’t seen the active roster since, but he’s clearly someone the Rams like as they keep bringing him back. Practice Squad Elevations: 1
Heading into Week 7, Nate Landman will be out with a concussion. Kendricks is expected to get called up to the active roster for the game against the Raiders. The Rams signed Kendricks two weeks ago to provide experienced linebacker depth and another player who could contribute on special teams if needed. Kendricks will make his Rams debut on Sunday.
ERIC KENDRICKS KNOCKS IT AWAY 49ERS BALL 😳 SFvsPHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/YS7jtonSGC
Lampkin has spent the last few years developing in the Rams’ system. An argument can be made that he should’ve made the final 53-man roster at the beginning of the season, but the Rams were able to keep him on the practice squad. Lampkin was called up last week with Trent McDuffie injured. He’ll be someone the Rams keep readily available if they need help at cornerback. Practice Squad Elevations: 2
During the first few weeks of the season, the Rams elevated Elias Neal from the practice squad to contribute on special teams. Given that teams are only allowed to elevate players off of the practice squad three times, Neal hasn’t been elevated in a few weeks. It’s potentially why the Rams also signed Kendricks. Neal is someone the Rams will continue developing. Practice Squad Elevations: 2
Nelson was an in-season addition by the Rams as they signed him before last week’s game against the Cardinals. Nelson gives the Rams some depth on the edge with Myles Garrett injured. Josaiah Stewart was also managing an injury at the time. Nelson spent time with the Saints this offseason before getting cut. He has never played in a regular-season game, and that likely won’t change with the Rams.
The Rams have been developing Bill Norton over the last few seasons on the defensive line. He struggled in the preseason, but Norton is a player the Rams have kept around. However, it says a lot that they added Hunt in the wake of Ford going on injured reserve. Norton is still a developmental player at the position.
Over the past two seasons, Brennan Presley has been a standout in the preseason. However, he hasn’t made an appearance on the active roster. If the Rams are without Nacua on Sunday, Presley may get the call. The Rams may still rely on some of their more experienced players, but Presley has shown that he can make plays when he’s gotten a chance.
Ty Simpson delivers a TD strike to Brennan Presley 🔥 Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/5Dc65aRqbk
It was surprising back in Week 4 when the Rams didn’t bring Dan Villari up from the practice squad. The Rams were thin at tight end with Terrance Ferguson and Colby Parkinson out. It’s possible the Rams simply see Villari as a developmental tight end this season.
After the Rams placed Ronnie Rivers on injured reserve, there was some consideration given to bringing up Jordan Waters.. However, the Rams opted for Dean Connors instead. Waters remains a player the Rams like and will continue to develop.
Williams gives the Rams some experienced cornerback depth on the practice squad and was signed last week. Given that the Rams have used up two of Lampkin’s practice squad elevations, Williams could see the active roster at some point. He was a fourth-round pick in 2022 and spent time with the Seahawks in 2024.

title: Forget the NFC West, Can the Rams Even Make the Playoffs?
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are 2-4 entering Week 7 and it can be argued that Sunday’s game against the Las Vegas Raiders is a must-win situation. A win against the Arizona Cardinals last week would have put the Rams in second place in the NFC West, right behind the San Francisco 49ers. Losing that game put them at 0-2 in the NFC West and in last place. At this point, it’s highly unlikely the Rams win the division, especially with the 49ers at 6-0.
Entering Week 7, the Rams have a four percent chance to win the NFC West. However, the playoffs are still within reach. Cue Jim Mora’s “Playoffs?! Playoffs?! You want to talk about playoffs?! I just hope we can win a game!” rant from November of 2000.
Happy 19th anniversary to the Jim Mora 'Playoffs' rant.  You shall be in our lives forever🙏 pic.twitter.com/iKk41mlvog
That’s where the Rams are at right now. It seems ridiculous to talk about the playoffs because they really need to just focus on winning a game. After losing 18-16 to the Cardinals and suffering the amount of injuries they have, the Rams simply need to focus on taking things one week at a time.
Still, that doesn’t mean that we can’t look ahead a little bit. Back in 2023, the Rams came back from a 3-6 start to make the playoffs. In 2024, they came back from a 1-4 start to make the postseason. Making the playoffs isn't completely out of the realm of possibility. The Rams just need to start stringing some wins together.
As it stands, the Rams have a 39 percent chance to make the playoffs via The Athletic . ESPN’s model has them slightly lower at 33 percent. While the Rams are playing an AFC opponent on Sunday, a win is critical to their playoff chances simply because they can’t afford many more losses.
A loss to the Raiders would put the Rams at a 27 percent chance to make the playoffs. Winning on Sunday makes it a near coin-flip at 45 percent. It’s very possible that we are looking at this game as the one that saved or ruined the Rams’ season.
To make the postseason, the Rams may need to finish 11-6 or 10-7. That means they can afford just two or three more losses over their final 11 games. They still have to play the Kansas City Chiefs, Seattle Seahawks twice, the San Francisco 49ers, and the Green Bay Packers. It’s likely the Rams will lose two of those games at minimum.
Looking at ESPN’s model , the biggest threats to the Rams’ playoff chances right now are the second- through fourth-place teams in the NFC North and the Seattle Seahawks. The good news is that the Rams will play the Packers after the bye week and then play the Seahawks twice in the final three weeks of the season.
Unfortunately, the timing may not work in the Rams’ favor, as the Packers have bounced back from their early-season struggles. While the Seahawks are in a rut, they may snap out of it by Week 16.
The Packers, Bears, Lions, Vikings, and Seahawks will all be teams that the Rams will be watching closely. There will likely only be one team to come out of the NFC South and NFC East divisions. However, the NFC North and NFC West could provide multiple playoff teams.
As it stands, the Rams’ most likely record is between 8-9 and 10-7. Since the NFL expanded to a 17-game format in 2021, only the Seattle Seahawks in 2024 missed the playoffs at 10-7. That’s what the Rams are looking at right now with the overall strength of the NFC. An 8-9 team has never made the playoffs as a wild card, and if the Rams were to go 9-8, they would certainly need help. They may need help at 10-7.
Realistically, the Rams are hoping they can finish ahead of the Seahawks in the NFC West and that either the Vikings collapse after starting 5-0 or the Packers lose their form again. There’s very little confidence right now that the Rams can string wins together, but the schedule has set up for it. If the Rams can win each of their next five games, that alone would increase their playoff chances to 77 percent. That would allow the Rams to lose to the Chiefs, the 49ers, and the Seahawks once and still finish 10-7. If that’s the way things play out, the Rams would have an 89 percent chance at the postseason.
They would obviously need certain things to go their way as well. Given the Rams’ poor record in the division, they would not be able to tie with the Seahawks. They would need the Seahawks to finish worse than 10-7 or take the season series and win both games in Week 16 and 18.
It seems likely with their schedules that the Bears and Lions finish with 11 wins. That leaves the Vikings and Packers as teams to monitor.
With the Vikings, they could lose four of their next five games. They play the Lions, Packers, and 49ers on the road and then also play the Bills. The Patriots on the road will be tough and the Panthers have looked good as well. It’s possible the Rams could use some help in later weeks. However, if the Vikings finish 10-7, the Rams would be seeded ahead of them.
Finally, the Rams’ game against the Packers after the bye is a must-win. If the Rams lose that game, it would be very difficult to come back from that. Assuming they win that game, it's possible the Packers could finish 10-7 and behind the Rams in the standings.
When all is said and done, we could be looking at: 1. 49ers 2. Bears 3. Panthers 4. NFC East Winner 5. Lions 6. Rams 7. Packers/Vikings
That would put the Rams in the playoffs and a trip to Carolina in the Wild Card round for a second consecutive season. Given the Rams’ current situation, they would very likely need to win three road playoff games to make the Super Bowl, but if they get healthy and find their stride, they would be a rare team with a good chance of doing that.
The Rams have come back from early-season deficits in the past. That’s certainly not the path they wanted to take this year, but it’s where they find themselves. Still, they need to show they can consistently win games. The Rams may be better than their record says they are, but they are 2-4.
🚨 NFL FRAUD METER - Week 6 🏈 The 6-0 49ers aren't frauds The 5-0 Vikings are... pic.twitter.com/f2gjARxzCJ
In 2024, it was a win against the Raiders in Week 7 that sparked a 9-3 finish. The Rams will hope a win against the Raiders in Week 7 this year does the same. The year before, the Rams lost three straight before a win against the Seahawks sparked them to a 7-1 finish.
However, the difference in both cases was that the Rams were getting healthy and coming off their bye week. At this point in the season, the Rams couldn’t be more hurt at key positions, and they don’t have their bye until Week 11.
Still, Sunday’s game against the Raiders is important. If the Rams are going to turn it around, it starts on Sunday. We can talk about playoff scenarios all we want, but none of it matters if the Rams can’t start winning games. The margins are already small and they get narrower with every loss. If they can get to the bye week with some momentum, the season could look very different. At 2-4, however, they can no longer afford to keep waiting for things to turn around.

title: Rams Week 7 Injury Report: Puka Nacua, Trent McDuffie Questionable vs. Raiders
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams could be without wide receiver Puka Nacua on Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders. Nacua was officially listed as questionable on Friday’s injury report after injuring his calf on Thursday . Also listed as questionable was cornerback Trent McDuffie, who did not practice on Friday. Additionally, linebacker Nate Landman has officially been ruled out.
Nacua was a surprise addition to the injury report on Thursday after he left practice with an apparent calf injury. He did not practice on Friday and will be a game-time decision. According to NFL Media’s Ian Rapoport , Nacua’s calf injury is only minor, but his status is up in the air for Sunday’s game. Rams head coach Sean McVay talked about Nacua’s injury in more detail in his media availability.
“I don't think he knows exactly when it occurred,” said McVay. “You look at it and there's a little minor thing in there. Felt it where he wasn't able to have some of the power and full explosion. Just noticed it, but I don't think he was aware of any sort of specific play that led to it.”
If the Rams are without Nacua, they will rely on depth players such as Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, and Jordan Whittington. The Rams would also likely lean heavily on their tight ends and running backs. Earlier this season without Nacua, Williams had six receptions against the Denver Broncos and became a big part of the passing game.
Landman being ruled out would imply that he didn’t pass through the concussion protocol this week. With Landman unable to go, McVay noted on Friday that the team would bring up linebacker Eric Kendricks from the practice squad, who they signed two weeks ago.
“He's got a veteran presence, real good concept understanding, can play a variety of schemes,” McVay said. “Has had success in a variety of schemes, understands football from a big-picture perspective, has a good vibe about himself.”
McDuffie missing his fourth consecutive practice with a groin injury certainly isn’t a good sign. McVay didn’t provide much of an update on McDuffie, only that he was questionable. McDuffie did work off to the side to an extent during the media portion of practice.
Rams CB Trent McDuffie working with training staff. He is questionable for game against Raiders. pic.twitter.com/993xUzHHPT
The Raiders will be relatively healthy heading into Sunday’s game against the Rams. After being limited on Wednesday with hamstring and calf injuries, tight end Brock Bowers was a full participant on Thursday and Friday and was not given an injury designation. Tonka Hemingway was also cleared.
With that said, the Raiders will be without wide receiver Dont’e Thornton and tight end Carter Runyon. Running back Mike Washington’s status is also up in the air for Sunday. Washington has been used alongside Ashton Jeanty this season and has averaged 4.9 yards per carry. He did not participate in practice the last two days and is listed as questionable.
The Rams were already going to be shorthanded heading into Week 7, but the uncertainty surrounding Nacua and McDuffie only adds to their challenges. With several starters already sidelined, the Rams will need their depth to step up in a significant way if they're going to get back in the win column.

title: Rams vs. Raiders Prediction: Week 7 Preview, Key Matchups, and Players to Watch
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams enter Week 7 desperately needing a win. After losing to the Arizona Cardinals last week, the Rams are at risk of dropping to 2-5 and are set to take on a Las Vegas Raiders team that is much better than in past years.
It’s fair to call Sunday a must-win game for the Rams. A loss to the Raiders would drop their already slim playoff chances even lower. Given where the Rams are, they can’t afford many more losses. At some point, they need to find some consistency and string together some wins, which won’t be easy with all of their injuries.
The Raiders are 3-3 and have lost three games in a row. With that said, two of their three losses are by three points, including last week’s 33-30 loss to the Buffalo Bills. Much like the Cardinals, the Raiders have been feisty this season and quarterback Kirk Cousins has played well. This isn’t a Raiders team that the Rams can afford to overlook.
Through six weeks, the Raiders’ defense ranks 26th in defensive EPA per play, success rate, and points per game allowed. Despite the injury to Davante Adams , the Rams should be able to move the ball. However, the same could’ve been said last week against the Cardinals, and the Rams managed just 16 points. The Raiders are better defending the run than the pass. This season, they are allowing the second-highest average depth of target and 13 passing touchdowns. Matthew Stafford should be able to find success.
With Puka Nacua as the Rams’ only legitimate threat at wide receiver, how the Raiders cover him will be something to watch. That becomes even more important if Nacua is unable to play and the Rams have to rely on Konata Mumpfield.
However, the Rams need to protect Matthew Stafford and keep him clean in the pocket. While McClendon has allowed a 6.8 percent pressure rate this season, Crosby has generated 25 pressures when facing right tackles, the second-most in the NFL. The Raiders also like to drop Crosby into coverage from that spot, which will also be something for the Rams to look out for.
The Raiders and head coach Klint Kubiak will be plenty familiar with Chris Shula and the Rams’ defense. Kubiak comes over from the Seattle Seahawks and was previously with the San Francisco 49ers in 2023. The Raiders have generated the 14th-most yards after the catch, while the Rams have allowed the most. Kubiak is going to dare the Rams’ defensive backs and linebackers to come up and tackle.
The Rams have done well covering tight ends this season. Last week, they held Trey McBride to seven receptions for only 53 yards. It wasn’t his lowest output of the season, but the Rams still managed to keep him in check. Brock Bowers will be another challenge. Bowers adds an explosive element to the Raiders’ offense. If Lake and the Rams can keep Bowers in check, they’ll force the Raiders to win with Tre Tucker and Jalen Nailor at wide receiver.
Despite the Rams losing to the Cardinals in Week 6, playing on the road, and sitting at 2-4, they are favored to beat the Raiders. Still, it’s hard to have any confidence in that happening on Sunday. Even without Adams, the Rams should be able to move the ball on offense, but they have to be able to finish drives. Given the injuries on defense, the Rams may need to score 30 points to win. This is a winnable game despite the injuries, but the Rams haven’t shown enough consistency. Prediction: Raiders 27, Rams 21

title: Rams Get Encouraging Puka Nacua Injury Update, But Week 7 Status Remains Uncertain
full_text:
The injuries just continue to pile up for the Los Angeles Rams. During Thursday’s practice, wide receiver Puka Nacua left early and was listed as limited with a calf injury . While details weren’t immediately available, NFL Media’s Ian Rapoport reported on Friday morning that the injury is believed to be minor.
“My understanding is, after tests, it was more minor than anything else. I wouldn’t say precautionary, because it’s not nothing, but at least not a significant injury,” said Rapoport. What that doesn’t tell us is whether or not Puka Nacua would be able to play.”
From @GMFB : #Rams WR Puka Nacua suffered what is believed to be a minor calf injury, while the #Colts will have a decision to make on RB Jonathan Taylor. pic.twitter.com/lF6yuIEo9I
Rapoport mentioned that it’s safe to say that Nacua’s status is up in the air for Sunday. After placing a handful of players such as wide receiver Davante Adams and defensive lineman Kobie Turner on injured reserve this week , the Rams were hoping to go into Week 7 against the Las Vegas Raiders as healthy as possible.
The Rams took significant hits on defense this week as Turner was placed on injured reserve along with Poona Ford. Additionally, cornerback Trent McDuffie has not practiced at all this week after injuring his groin last Thursday.
Remaining as healthy as they can on the offensive side of the ball as Adams and Terrance Ferguson recover from injuries will be essential to keeping the offense competitive over the next several weeks.
Nacua has already missed two games this season with a groin/hip injury. When Nacua was out, it was Adams who stepped up in his place. With Adams set to miss the next six weeks, the Rams will be relying heavily on Nacua.
If Nacua were to miss Sunday’s game, it would put the Rams’ offense in a very difficult spot. The offense would likely rely on Tutu Atwell, who previously stepped up in place of Nacua in 2024. Players like Konata Mumpfield and Jordan Whittington would be asked to step up as well, and the Rams could look at rookie CJ Daniels. Even with Nacua out, it wouldn’t be surprising to see the Rams bring up Brennan Presley from the practice squad.
The Rams will get information on Nacua later on Friday when the team reports to practice. Nacua will unlikely be a full participant, but head coach Sean McVay should at least be able to provide some more details.
Given the Rams' injury luck over the last few weeks, they can certainly be relieved that Nacua’s calf injury doesn't appear to be serious. However, while the news surrounding Nacua is encouraging, his availability for Sunday remains uncertain. Given the inconsistencies on offense and Adams' absence, the Rams need Nacua available as they look to avoid dropping to 2-5.

title: 3 Overreactions to Raiders' Fourth Consecutive Loss vs. Rams
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders faced the best version of the less-than-healthy Los Angeles Rams and lost their fourth consecutive game, 35-21. It was a competitive game in the second half after the Raiders went down 28-6 at halftime, putting them within 10 points of the lead.
It was another humbling experience for the Rams, who continue to show they are still maturing as a roster and overall franchise. Head coach Klint Kubiak may have them on the right track long term, but the short term feels low. With that in mind, here are some overreactions to Sunday's tough loss to the preseason Super Bowl favorites.
Whether it is the blocking execution up front or the running backs themselves, the Raiders have spiraled downward, becoming the worst rushing offense in football again. Las Vegas was held to under 50 total yards on the ground and 2.8 yards per carry on 17 attempts, with rookie Mike Washington Jr. leading the way with six carries for 27 yards, 21 of them coming from one play.
I'm not sure if there is an easy solution to the Raiders' run game issues. You can see they are trying everything, especially Kubiak and offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko. Yet these problems persist. The Raiders cannot win football games if they can't run the football, period.
For the fourth straight week, defensive coordinator Rob Leonard has allowed at least 30 or more points. 35 more were added in the Raiders' loss to the Rams, and the failures on this front point to a lack of an ample pass rush opposite Crosby and in the middle of the defensive line, and a young secondary that has been thrown in the fire and is learning the hard way.
While Las Vegas does have some good moments on defense, Leonard's unit is starting to become untrustworthy to the naked eye. The Raiders will continue to try to experiment with ways to improve, but again, this is a rebuilding season, which means Leonard will have to roll through the punches.
I applaud Tre Tucker for his performance on Sunday (five catches, 103 yards, one touchdown). He was the best receiver on the field, performance- and impact-wise, for this particular game, creating explosive plays and giving his offense a chance to score or be the one doing the scoring. I wrote earlier in the week that the Raiders should consider trading for Jacksonville Jaguars wideout Brian Thomas Jr., and Tucker silenced my take quickly (for now).
Tucker is emerging as a consistent threat in this high-powered passing offense. Tight ends Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer might be the stars of that show with Kirk Cousins, but Tucker is emerging at the right time as the Raiders head to the Meadowlands to face the New York Jets next weekend.
Jared Feinberg, a native of western North Carolina, has written about NFL football for nearly a decade. He has contributed to several national outlets and is now part of our On SI team as an NFL team reporter. Jared graduated from UNC Asheville with a bachelor's degree in mass communications and later pursued his master's degree at UNC Charlotte. You can follow Jared Feinberg on Twitter at @JRodNFLDraft

title: Winners & Losers: Brutal Truths From Raiders vs. Rams Showdown
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev.—The Las Vegas Raiders (3-4) were beat up - frankly, manhandled - by the Los Angeles Rams (3-4) last night, 35-21, and truthfully, the score wasn’t that close.
I thought the Raiders would win, and with the Rams limping in with multiple injuries, and the NFL Trade Deadline looming , the Raiders, as they have in all four straight losses, cost themselves, and ultimately beat themselves.
Each week I reflect on the game, offering winners and losers, and today will be no exception.
I love that Klint Kubiak is aggressive; when you are an underdog, you have to be. So when he came out, won the toss, and didn’t defer, I liked it. It goes against conventional wisdom, but I thought he was sending his team a message that he expected to win and was putting his offense on the field to start to prove a point.
It seemed as if the Raiders got shell-shocked early; the attacking ceased.
Field goals at the end of the first and second half seemed senseless, and when the Rams continued to punish the Raiders, who could get no pass rush, and attacked the Raiders, playing off giving a future Hall of Fame QB with nearly no mobility the ability to stand back and attack them, I was stunned.
I asked Kubiak after the game if they had considered turning up the aggression and going after Matthew Stafford, the Rams QB; he told me bluntly, “No.”
I appreciate his honesty, but I can tell you that was the Rams' biggest offensive concern coming into the game, and the Raiders, by not changing, were victims all night.
Kubiak and his DC, Rob Leonard, are good first-year young coaches. I have not given up faith at all, not one bit, but on that night, they were outcoached.
Kubiak went into more detail and didn’t pull any punches. His feet are firmly planted in reality, and he spoke the truth on that side of the ball.
"Well, no one's coming to help us. We've got to figure it out ourselves as a coaching staff with the players, and we have to complement each other as well because to we've got to start the game a lot faster offensively."
The Raiders' offensive line was as bad as their defense. But the Rams got up fast, thus making the Raiders a one-dimensional team (They threw 45 times and ran 14 called runs, and Cousins had three scrambles), and you can’t win in this league when a defense forces you to be one-dimensional. A fact Kubiak is well aware of.
"Yeah, well, you can't win in this league having to throw it as much as we're throwing it. We've got to be more competitive in the game early so that we can be balanced. But there's no balance in playing from behind."
QB Kirk Cousins elaborated on how the game changes when teams force you to go one-dimensional, and to his credit, he sugarcoated nothing.
"You certainly had to be a little bit more one-dimensional. I thought we still tried to do some things to stay varied, but yeah, when you get down three scores or whatever it was, then that's the game you got to play, and that's part of football and part of trying to get back in the game."
The Raiders' abysmal red-zone performance continued this week. The Rams were 5/5, while the Raiders were a lowly 1/5. Kubiak told the truth about it.
"Yeah, it's very disappointing, especially with the emphasis we've put on it. When it comes down to it, we have to make plays down there when we have our one-on-one opportunities. We've got to make the throws, we've got to make the catches and it didn't happen."
Matt Gay missed a 51-yard field goal that he should have made, but the truth was that special teams, led by the great Joe DeCamillis, was not good; it was great. While there are no moral victories in the NFL, truth is still truth, and he asked Kubiak about how well they played.
"Yeah, I think that's been a standard throughout the year. Coach Joe [DeCamillis] and Tim [McConnell] and Marquice [Williams] do a phenomenal job, and that's a phase that we continue to rely on."
Kirk Cousins still leads the NFL in touchdown passes, but the 15-year veteran knows the red zone is an Achilles' heel for this team.
"I think it's really a team game, and we just got to all kind of do our part. I got to hit throws when they're there and there's just any number of things that come up. I think of the throw to Cody [White] on -- It was another fourth down. But I have to go back and watch, I felt like they matched Brock [Bowers] in the flat, and maybe if you give it to Brock, it's going to be a catch tackle. But does he able to break that tackle or lean forward for a first down?”
Cousins went deeper, explaining his thought process. “Those are the things that I don't know in real time. But I thought I'll work Cody one-on-one and then wish I had given him a ball that he could have maybe just stopped and gone up for, as opposed to running underneath it. So those are some plays that I think end up looming large at the end of the game."
Ever since the Raiders selected the young man NFL executives ranked as the best NFL QB prospect in the last four years, Fernando Mendoza, questions have come up about when he will play.
That isn’t abnormal, and with the Raiders now riding a four-game losing streak, they will get louder. Cousins knew that coming in and addressed it head-on.
“It's really the same every day that it was in March or April. I mean, nothing changes in the sense that if I'm not the best option, then I don't want to be out there either. I want our football team to have the best chance to win games. And if the first OTA, if that had become apparent, I would have been the first one to say, 'Yeah, you can't play me.' So nothing changes and the organization will do what they feel is best.”
Cousins elaborated even more, “But I feel that Fernando's [Mendoza] done a great job and has a bright future ahead. I'm going to try to go out there and play as well as I possibly can, help us win, and give him a great example to learn from until he does go out there eventually."
WR Jalen Nailor is a high-priced free agent that the Raiders desperately need to break out. He addressed the Silver and Black's lack of execution in plain terms.
"At the end of the day, it's all about executing the X's and O's. We just got to find a way to do that better and complement the defense or special teams. We got to play a whole complete game as a whole team."
Ashton Jeanty may not have had a great night toting the rock, but the Rams and a poor OL performance had more to do with that than he did. Still, Cousins targeted him eight times, and he caught all eight.
Cousins is not the problem, and the sophomore RB bragged on the play of his veteran signal caller.
“He's just super detailed every single week. Obviously, he's been playing this game for a long time, but he also has the confidence in everybody who's out there, running routes, and he gives them the chance to go make plays. You see it week in and week out from him."
This is not the Raiders of old. No one is holding their head down. Nobody is quitting; this team is angry, feisty, and hungry. Superstar Maxx Crosby made that abundantly clear.
"You've got to stay close together. The world is negative in general, the world, the media, all that. That's just part of it. Negativity is what sells, and the fanbase is going to obviously be very upset, and they have every right to be, but you can't feed into that. You can't feed into the negativity. You can't lose confidence in who you are because of noise. There's always going to be noise, good or bad, but you don't let that dictate who you are. You've just got to continue improving on a daily basis."
Nakobe Dean has been a terrific signing for this team, and he held no punches back when talking about his team and how to fix the losing streak.
"Most of it is all controllable; everything is controllable. Even if you making a play, you're not making a play. You got to control it. Just got to be real. It's a performing based league, got to perform. At this point, we know what we not good at as a defense, and we got to pick that up. And like I said, it…

title: 3 Instant Observations After Raiders' Blowout Loss to Rams
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders were hoping to snap their three-game skid on Sunday against the Los Angeles Rams. Quite the opposite happened, as a dormant Raiders' offense failed to get much going against a Rams team missing several critical players.
Sunday was another forgettable outing for Las Vegas, just two weeks after a similarly disappointing Week 5 loss to the New England Patriots. The Raiders' home performance against the Rams on Sunday was confirmation that the season's first seven games were accurate.
The Raiders can beat bad teams and compete with the league's best, but they need nearly everything to go right for them to beat the league's elite. Regardless of opponents' records or injuries, Las Vegas' roster is still a work in progress.
Sunday's loss to the Rams confirmed that their 3-3, and now 3-4, record is exactly what it is. Las Vegas has a high ceiling and a low floor. They are right in between good and bad, which is still an improvement from where they were at the end of last season.
Las Vegas has reason to be cautiously optimistic about things in future seasons, but they are what they are this season. The Raiders are an improved team, but need more additions to their roster to truly compete with the league's best teams.
However, they also made enough changes during this past offseason to no longer be amongst the league's cellar dwellers. They are experiencing the expected growing pains of a team in its first season under a new head coach and a ton of new pieces on both sides of the ball.
Las Vegas is right where they are supposed to be.
Anyone who has followed the Raiders in recent seasons knows John Spytek was tasked with rebuilding one of the league's worst collections of talent. Even with all of the moves Spytek and the Raiders made this offseason, they still needed more.
In terms of roster-building, no team had a more productive offseason than Las Vegas. The rebuild they have embarked on will take multiple offseasons. Still, the Raiders entered the season with several roster holes that needed addressing, but likely cannot be addressed until after this season.
The Raiders have undoubtedly improved on both sides of the ball compared to last season. However, at some point, last season stops becoming the metric by which a team is judged. Halfway through the season is about that point.
As much as they have improved, Las Vegas still needs more pieces on both sides of the ball. The plays that work against the Raiders' defense and the unproductive play of its offense against elite teams are largely due to not having the pieces.
The season's first three games showed the improvement Las Vegas made during the offseason. Their four consecutive losses have confirmed exactly where they need more roster help. The Raiders need help along the offensive line, in their defensive backfield, and at wide receiver.
However, that is no surprise to Spytek and the Raiders' front office. A four-game losing streak is far from ideal, but at least Las Vegas now knows where to improve moving forward.
If the Raiders' entire schedule included teams like the Miami Dolphins, New Orleans Saints, and Los Angeles Chargers, Las Vegas' offense would be among the league's best. However, even serviceable defenses will give this Raiders offense trouble as they refuse to make the one change that could help.
After three games against three of the league's worst teams and three of the best, Las Vegas' Week 7 outing gave them a chance to beat a reeling Rams team. Los Angeles was the first team Las Vegas has played that fell between the bad teams and the elite teams they have faced this season.
The Rams were missing several defensive players, yet the Raiders' offense still struggled to move the ball, let alone score points. Sure, Las Vegas' defense can play better, but what does it matter if their offense scores only six points in three quarters?
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: Raiders Stock Report: Biggest Risers, Fallers After Falling Flat vs. Rams
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders' Week 7 outing against the Los Angeles Rams was flat and reminiscent of their Week 5 blowout loss to the New England Patriots. Few things went the Raiders' way against the Rams.
The Raiders look like an up-and-down team that is slowly becoming inconsistent. Still, even though they are inconsistent, they are still better than they were last season.
Below are the players who are trending up and down after Sunday's loss to the Rams.
Laube had arguably the best game of any Raider on Sunday, as he averaged nearly 40 yards per kickoff return through three quarters. Unfortunately, Las Vegas' offense could not do much of anything on Sunday, even with Laube's solid returns.
Las Vegas' defensive backfield allowed Matthew Stafford to complete nine of his first 10 passes and 12 of his first 14 passes. Stafford is the league's reigning MVP and has had similar games against much better defensive backfields. Still, letting Stafford start the game on a roll is not ideal.
Along with suspect coverage, the unit often missed tackles that could have limited yards after the catch. Las Vegas' defensive backfield was the team's most significant weakness at the start of the season. However, against the Rams and the New England Patriots, the unit left a lot to be desired.
The unit played better in the second half, but Stafford completed 17 of his 19 passes in the first half.
Cousins did not necessarily do anything wrong on Sunday. However, it is undeniable that the offense, as constructed, is limited with Cousins under center. If there is any pressure at all, Cousins' chances of completing a pass attempt decline rapidly and tremendously.
The offense has several other issues overall that continue to negatively impact Cousins. Las Vegas' offensive line has kept sacks to a minimum but has also allowed many pressures this season, which has impacted the time  Cousins has in the pocket. This would negatively impact any quarterback.
However, Kubiak has been tasked with finding ways to win with the roster that he has been given. If the Raiders' offensive line is so bad that Cousins can't succeed behind it, Las Vegas' coaching staff must either change the offensive line or change the quarterback.
Las Vegas has already replaced Jackson Powers-Johnson with Caleb Rogers. They won't bench Kolton Miller or DJ Glaze. Spencer Burford is an option to replace him along the line, but they don't have a dependable replacement, other than potentially rookie offensive lineman Trey Zuhn.
The Raiders spent the offseason moving Zuhn around to different positions along the line. For them not to put him on the field more often while needing better play alog the line speaks volumes about the coaching staff's confidence in their starting lineup.
Considering there is not much more they can do to improve the offensive line this season, the Raiders need a quarterback who can move in the pocket when protection breaks down. The Raiders need a quarterback who can confidently run past the line of scrimmage when it is time to do so.
Las Vegas doesn't have many offensive linemen who can protect Cousins better. Still, they have a quarterback who is mobile enough to make plays with his legs, accurate enough to complete tough passes, and talented enough to do both. In fact, they spent the No. 1 pick in the draft on one!
If the Raiders are content to beat bad teams and either fall a few plays short or completely fall flat against better teams, they should continue to keep Cousins as the starter. If they want to actually win games against good teams and push for a playoff spot, it is time to start Fernando Mendoza.
Or, the past four weeks are exactly what this year's Raiders will be against the league's better teams. Mendoza will struggle at times, but it will be better for the Raiders' long -term future than continuing to start Cousins. Coming close is not the same as winning.
Las Vegas has upcoming games against the San Francisco 49ers, Seattle Seahawks, and the Denver Broncos. Those are all good teams. They need to decide what their goal is this season. If they want to compete, start Cousins. Mendoza gives them a better chance to actually win.
Starting Mendoza does not guarantee anything at all. He will lose games, too. However, I personally believe they have a better shot at winning with Mendoza under center. Even his struggle will help move the rebuild along. It is time.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: Raiders vs. Rams: Week 7 Instant Live Updates and Results
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders and Los Angeles Rams face off today at Allegiant Stadium. Both teams desperately need a win. Even so, Las Vegas is still playing with house money, since the Rams started the season hoping to play in the Super Bowl.
Sunday gives the Raiders a chance to steal a game against a Rams team dealing with several injuries on both sides of the ball. A win on Sunday, with a game against the New York Jets next weekend, would set Las Vegas up well moving forward.
Schedule-wise, Las Vegas has a much more manageable second half. A loss against the Rams wouldn't be the end of the world, but a four-game losing streak would make next Sunday's road matchup against the Jets a must-win for Kubiak's Raiders.
First things first. The Raiders must find a way to beat a Rams team that may be every bit the 2-4 team their record suggests. Las Vegas will have to play their best football on Sunday. Over six games, they have proven that when they do so, they can compete with any team in the league.
The Raiders are working through one of the toughest schedules in the league this season. They are doing so with new pieces across the board. Kubiak believes his team has responded about as well as possible to losing three games in a row.
“Yeah, as professionals, that's part of the price of admission for being here. At least that's what we talk about, and they have to go do it. So you stress things, and you look for team-oriented guys, and you promote team-oriented guys, and you celebrate those things,” Kubiak said earlier this week.
“And so, I do like where we're headed in that regard. But I think a lot of that comes from mom and dad, who those who those people are, and how they were raised, and our scouting department identifying those traits when drafting or signing guys.”
Las Vegas can quickly make up for the past three weeks with a win over the Rams. Yet Sean McVay, Matthew Stafford, and the rest of the Rams still have enough to beat the Raiders, even with all the injuries they enter the game with. The Raiders have to play how they have most of the season.

title: How Raiders' Maxx Crosby Can Make Big Impact Against Rams
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders are trying to get a statement win over the Los Angeles Rams later this afternoon.
In order to beat a powerhouse -- albeit, the Rams are quite injured, but still a powerhouse -- your best players have to show up. For the Raiders, they'll need defensive end Maxx Crosby to step up in a big way.
These are the kinds of games Crosby looks forward to every season: games against some of the top teams in the league, and despite injuries, the Rams are still that, especially considering they have the reigning MVP quarterback Matthew Stafford.
In two games against the Rams, Crosby has recorded seven tackles and two sacks. The Raiders haven't won either game, but they have the chance to pull off the upset at home this afternoon.
Crosby shows up against some of the best teams in the league, and this game should be no exception. He knows much is required of him in this showdown, and he will be ready to answer the call.
It's been an impressive start to the season for the five-time Pro Bowler, generating 35 pressures in six games and recording two sacks. He has logged a 27 percent pass-rush win rate , which is tied for fifth in the NFL.
If he continues to play at this level, Crosby could be looking at his third All-Pro nod and sixth Pro Bowl appearance. His legendary run as one of the greatest players in Silver and Black history has continued this season, and he doesn't want to slow down any time soon.
The Rams do not boast one of the league's best offensive lines, so we could see Crosby wreak havoc this afternoon.
Offensive tackle Alaric Jackson will be back for this game after getting his suspension cut in half, but he may not be enough to slow down Crosby, who will want to do everything in his power to stop the Raiders' three-game losing streak. Crosby may not line up across from him as much, but he would likely win those matchups anyway.
The Rams haven't allowed many sacks this season, but that may change after they face one of the league's best pass-rushing teams: the Raiders. Crosby and his cohorts have done a great job getting after the quarterback, and they'll want to disrupt Stafford all day.
Expect Crosby to have a major impact in this game, just as he has all season. We will see whether that havoc results in a victory against what is supposed to be one of the league's best teams.
Carter Landis studied journalism at Michigan State University where I graduated in May of 2022. He currently is a sports reporter for a local television station, and is a writer covering the Las Vegas Raiders

title: In Make-or-Break Matchup, Raiders Must Lean on Special Teams
full_text:
Sunday afternoon is a great opportunity for the Las Vegas Raiders, and it is a make-or-break game to snap a three-game skid after starting the season unbeaten. Their opponent? The 2-4 Los Angeles Rams, once considered the undoubted Super Bowl favorites with a superteam built, only for injuries and inconsistencies to batter the franchise.
Head coach Klint Kubiak has been coaching an explosive offense led by NFL passing touchdown leader Kirk Cousins. While the Raiders' defense will be the highlight in this matchup, special teams will be the biggest key in this game for both teams. The important third unit could help the Raiders get their fourth win of the year.
For the past two seasons, the Rams’ downfall has been their special teams. Somehow, head coach Sean McVay cannot seem to get this unit right and continues to make bad decisions on this front. Those decisions have led to what we have today, with Los Angeles having maybe the worst special teams unit in the NFL, which has cost them games this season.
Raiders special teams coordinator Joe DeCamillis will play a big role on Sunday as his unit looks to take advantage of the Rams' pitfalls in an important phase. A longtime special teams coach who won a Super Bowl in 2021 with the Rams, DeCamillis has the best punter in the league, AJ Cole, and a steady veteran kicker, Matt Gay.
The key for Las Vegas is being consistent this week, according to DeCamillis, tackling in space, getting bodies around the ball carrier, and going stride for stride with the hang time on punt coverage.
“The one thing we got to improve on is our punt coverage, and that's space tackling,” DeCamillis said. “Got to get better at space tackling. Got to get more population around the ball, and then we've got to match the distance to the hang time, and I think those three things are things we worked on this week, and we got to just keep plugging and trying to get it done."
One thing the Raiders would like to do this weekend is create explosive plays in the return game. Last week, the Buffalo Bills did well to contain the explosive and quick Dylan Laube, Las Vegas’s third-string running back.
“Yeah, we tried to start moving him around,” DeCamillis said. “If you watch that, we tried to do some different things to try to get it to him. [The Bills] did a good job of placing [the ball] where they were. So, we just have to, like you said, be intentional of trying to do that, try to work the formations as much as we can to get him the ball.”
Two of the key players I listed for the Raiders this week were Laube and Mailk Benson, their top two return men. Laube could be the most important, as DeCamillis praised the running back’s downhill toughness on Friday.
“Dylan's done a good job for us. He's a straight line downhill tough kid that hits it hard, and that's what this play requires.”
What Laube also brings is good vision, balance, and open-field short-area quickness to make moves in space. Benson is a lightning-quick and explosive runner himself, and the two could bring a spark for the Raiders' kickoff and punt coverage.
As we saw with the Arizona Cardinals last week, their special teams play, or the terrible play by the Rams, helped them win that game. We could see the same thing at Allegiant Stadium as the Raiders look to improve to 4-3 and create the most disappointing season in recent NFL history for Los Angeles.
Jared Feinberg, a native of western North Carolina, has written about NFL football for nearly a decade. He has contributed to several national outlets and is now part of our On SI team as an NFL team reporter. title: What To Expect From Raiders’ Top Offensive Players vs. Rams
full_text:
A couple of weeks ago, this matchup was labeled a daunting one for the Las Vegas Raiders, as the Los Angeles Rams were once viewed as the class of the NFL.
However, the Rams have been one of the most disappointing teams in the league, entering Sunday with a 2-4 record. Not to mention, Los Angeles is dealing with an onslaught of injuries, with Poona Ford, Kobie Turner, and Davante Adams all out for the foreseeable future. Meanwhile, Puka Nacua is a game-time decision, and Trent McDuffie is questionable.
Despite being viewed as underdogs at home, the Raiders have a legitimate chance of ending their three-game losing streak in Week 7. With the Rams ravaged by injuries, specifically on defense, here's how Las Vegas' top offensive players can perform on Sunday.
Although the Raiders are in the midst of a three-game skid, Cousins has been more than serviceable. Now, there have been times when his immobility has been exposed, but that won't be a problem on Sunday. Los Angeles' defense has recorded eight sacks this season and will be without Ford, Turner, and Myles Garrett.
Cousins will have all the time in the world to operate in a clean pocket, which is all he needs to dissect an opposing defense. The Rams' secondary could also be short-handed if McDuffie is ruled out. While Cousins isn't supported by a bona fide WR1, the 38-year-old quarterback has more than enough to expose Los Angeles’ defense. You should expect an impressive outing from the 15-year veteran.
Jeanty has been underwhelming this season, averaging 3.2 yards per carry and rushing for one touchdown in six games. However, the 22-year-old running back has been battling through injuries during that stretch. While those injuries may still be present, the Rams' defensive line isn't.
At this point, Los Angeles' front line is a makeshift unit, with Aaron Donald headlining the group. Jeanty has an opportunity for a breakout game, but Mike Washington Jr. should carve into his workload, which is why I project a modest carry count for the second-year running back.
Regardless, Jeanty should surpass his production from the last two weeks, in which he's compiled 49 yards and one touchdown on 20 attempts.
Despite not recording his first reception until the third quarter last week, Bowers finished the game with four receptions for 70 yards. It's safe to assume that the 23-year-old tight end will be involved much earlier on Sunday.
If Cousins and Bowers have a rapport early in the game, the superstar tight end will have a monster outing. He's eclipsed 100 yards in two of four games this season; achieving that feat for the third time in 2026 is definitely in play.

title: One Raiders Player Who Could Surprisingly Be Traded Before Deadline
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders' front office spent the offseason making wholesale moves to improve its roster in its first season under head coach Klint Kubiak. John Spytek and the Raiders dished out big bucks to improve nearly every position group on the team.
The only two positions the Raiders didn't add talent to were the two positions where they have two of the league's best players: tight end and punter. Even though Las Vegas made plenty of progress this offseason, its roster rebuild will take years to finish. This matters for multiple reasons.
Las Vegas made enough progress on its roster in one offseason that it has little room to add more talent this season without it hurting them in one aspect or another. If the Raiders trade a player away, it could impact the foundation Kubiak and his staff are building.
After the roster changes the Raiders made and the work the team put in on the field this offseason, I don't believe the Raiders should trade away any player, even when the deadline arrives on Nov. 10. To do so would be hasty. After the season would be a different story.
Of course, if the Raiders get a big offer for a major draft haul or players in return, it goes without saying that they should consider it and probably make the trade. However, they should refuse anything except an offer they cannot refuse.
Still, the trade deadline is approaching, and teams will undoubtedly keep discussing offers. Spytek has said in the past that he is open to hearing trade offers, both big and small. Even during his first season at the helm, Las Vegas struck a deal for a contributor in exchange for an often-injured player.
Spytek was also close to pulling off the trade of the offseason, ahead of having the best free-agency signing period and one of the best draft hauls in the league. I do not believe they should make a trade, but it is unquestionably on the table, as the Raiders sit at 3-3 on the season.
Las Vegas has lost three straight games . Two of those three losses came against the Kansas City Chiefs and the Buffalo Bills by six points combined. The Raiders' two losses to the Chiefs and Bills showed how close they are to regularly competing against, and eventually beating. the league's elite.
Their loss to the New England Patriots showed how far they are from doing so. All three losses make it fair for the front office to consider a trade. However, Kubiak knows the Raiders do not take the field on Sundays to almost win . A trade could help Las Vegas take an even bigger step this season.
“It's such a competitive game, and if you're just hoping to keep it close in the fourth quarter, that's not a winning mindset. So, just having the mindset when you have an opportunity to make a play, when you're playing complementary football on one side of the ball, special teams gives you good field position, you got to go score on that drive,” Kubiak said earlier this week.
“Defense gets a turnover; you got to go score on that drive. If there's a sudden change defensively, then we got to get a stop. So, just having the ultimate competitor's mindset of not being okay with having the game be close in the fourth quarter. That's not what we're here to do.”
Technically, one player who could be traded - and it would be a significant surprise - is offensive tackle Kolton Miller. Yet the way his contract is structured for both this season and next season eliminates him from the conversation.
The bigger surprise would be to see offensive lineman Jackson Powers-Johnson traded. Offseason rumblings and Caleb Rogers starting over Powers-Johnson in Week 6 may make this seem like less of a surprise. He is a very tradeable piece, but it would still be a surprise because of the timing.
Yet if those reasons make him potentially being traded not a surprise, Las Vegas trading him before the trade deadline, with the depth they have at the offensive guard position without Powers-Johnson, should outweigh those offseason rumblings and Rogers starting last week by a large margin.
He has plenty to improve upon, but teams in the league have a backup offensive guard as good as Powers-Johnson. Maybe adding a high-end veteran guard and another serviceable guard after the season, while continuing to develop Powers-Johnson, is the answer.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: Five Instant Overreactions to the Dolphins-Jets Matchup
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins grabbed their first win of the season against the New York Jets. Their 28 to 25 victory marks the first of Jeff Hafley's Miami tenure, which means it's time to overreact to this game.
After not holding a single lead over the course of their first five games, Miami never trailed against the Jets. They remained in control through an ugly second half, and started what could be one of the craziest stories in NFL history.
On a very real note, the Miami Dolphins grabbed a win that required every ounce of effort they could muster. From a stellar offensive first half closed out by some masterful clock management to a timely fourth-down conversion to seal the victory, Jeff Hafley’s unit never wavered and won several crucial momentum-swinging moments. This win adds an exclamation point to a first half of a season that has felt about as promising as 1-5 can feel.
Malik Willis played what was easily his best game as a member of the Miami Dolphins, going 14 of 21 passing for 208 yards and two touchdowns, and adding another 37 yards and a score on the ground. His decision-making was consistently positive, as he understood when to take off, when to move off of his progressions, and when to fire into some tight windows.
On Miami’s first scoring drive, Willis made multiple throws late in the progression, including the first of two touchdown passes to Caleb Douglas. Just as important, though, was what we didn’t see on the stat sheet: turnovers. Miami won the takeaway battle on Sunday, and while Geno Smith threw an early pick to Michael Taaffe, Willis kept the ball out of harm’s way.
Willis looked like a completely different player than what we saw against the Cincinnati Bengals, and if he can start to stack strong performances, his window as the Dolphins’ franchise quarterback will remain cracked open.
One of Miami’s most promising rookies made his triumphant return on Sunday, and Caleb Douglas’ impact on the health of the Dolphins’ passing game is palpable.
His two catches, both of which went for touchdowns, showcased an element Miami simply doesn’t have with any of their other weapons. In the first quarter, Douglas dusted cornerback Azareye'h Thomas, pressing into his toes and snapping off a gorgeous route to the inside. Then, when Miami’s offense struggled to remain explosive late in the game, Douglas hit Minkah Fitzpatrick with a mean stutter-step, and followed it up with a tightrope act that resulted in a 63-yard score.
Even when he wasn’t making plays, it's clear that Douglas’ size and talent put the rest of the Dolphins’ receiving weapons in a more natural spot. Greg Dulcich had one of his best games, and Malik Washington made multiple nice plays underneath. Douglas’ impact cannot be understated, and his presence was key in Miami grabbing their first win.
The Dolphins’ rookies have largely met expectations, and one who has far exceeded them is safety Michael Taaffe.
Taaffe grabbed his second interception of the season against the Jets, triggering down on a crossing route by Jeremy Ruckert. It was an excellent play, and one Taaffe continues to make this season, trusting his instincts to fly towards the football.
Even as a rookie, there are a couple of plays in each game where it seems like Taaffe knows what the offense is running before it happens. His football IQ has made an immediate impact on the back end, and in a year where the primary goal is assessing talent, the former fifth-round pick looks like a gem.
In what ended up as potentially the biggest play of the game, former Miami Dolphins kicker Jason Sanders missed a 40-yard field goal for the New York Jets, and for the first time all year, the Dolphins played what looked like a clean game in the third phase.
In the first game after Jeff Hafley not-so-subtly called out Riley Patterson for not being able to get the ball into the end zone, Patterson’s replacement, veteran Zane Gonzalez and punter Bradley Pinion took turns on kickoffs and had the distance to eliminate the Jets’ potential returns. Gonzalez also went four for four on extra points.
Pinion had a mediocre punt that was salvaged by a nice bounce, but overall, special teams wasn’t a glaring negative, and that’s the first time all season that I’ve been able to say that.
Tyler DeSena is currently a journalism student at the University of Central Florida. Prior to joining Dolphins On SI in 2026, DeSena worked with dolphinstalk.com, and created independent social media content on X, YouTube and TikTok.

title: Miami Dolphins Week 7 Instant Takeaways: Willis, Douglas Make Sure to End Winless Foolishness
full_text:
OK, everybody can forget about this idea — farfetched as it was — that the Miami Dolphins were going to finish the 2026 season at 0-7 and we can at least hit the pause button on this idea that the Malik Willis experiment already should be deemed a failure.
The Dolphins got that elusive first victory of the Jeff Hafley era Sunday and of course it was going to come against the New York Jets, just has it had in 2007 after Miami started off 0-7.
And while there were plenty of stars on this day — welcome back, Caleb Douglas — Willis absolutely was front and center.
His final passing numbers weren't necessarily overwhelming as he finished with 208 yards on 14 completions, but he provided exactly the kind of quarterback we saw during his stints with the Green Bay Packers that convinced Hafley and Jon-Eric Sullivan to bring him over.
It was the kind of performance that would make the Dolphins look to another position with their first-round pick in the 2027 NFL draft, a pick that still figures to be pretty high, and maybe we can stop debating — at least for a little while — whether it should be Drew Mestermaker or Arch Manning or Darian Mensah.
All along, we said Willis deserved the benefit of the doubt and a longer look before making definitive judgements about his viability as a starting quarterback, but if nothing else he bought himself more time with that performance — not that we would suggest he's cemented anything, either, just off one game.
As for the win and that silly notion the Dolphins could go 0-17, did anybody really think the Dolphins wouldn't be able to improve as the season moved along.
And, as we pointed out on numerous occasions, if the 2019 Dolphins could win five games after being outscored 163-26 (basically an average of 41-7) in their four games, yeah the 2026 Dolphins pretty safely were going to win a game here and there.
-- Douglas had only two catches in his return after missing three games with an ankle injury, but they both showed why he's the most exciting player on offense (outside of Willis) with De'Von Achane on IR. His first touchdown showed off his route-running ability as he faked the Jets cornerback out of his cleats with a quick jerky movement and then there was the fabulous YAC work on what became the game-winning touchdown. And how sweet was it that the Jets player he beat to turn a short reception into a long touchdown was none other than Minkah Fitzpatrick.
-- Major hats off to the running game for being able to close out the win after the Jets cut their lead with 3:24 left. It was five straight runs that produced two first downs, starting with a 14-yarder by Ollie Gordon II and punctuated by Malik Willis' sneak on fourth-and-1 where Gordon played a big role with his push of Willis. And even though it was risky, we tweeted before the call that the Dolphins should go for the win on that fourth-and-1 instead of going the conservative route and trying to pin the Jets deep. That's the kind of aggressiveness we want to see from Hafley moving forward.
-- Since we already mentioned Gordon, he continues to shine in the absence of De'Von Achane and looks like a feature back himself.
-- A couple of changes we noticed with the offense was that there weren't as man deep shots as in previous weeks, and that led to a better completion percentage for Willis. His decision-making was better, his scrambling again was a big factor, and he showed great awareness with his slide in bounds near the end of the first half to make sure the Jets wouldn't have much time left after they scored to make it 21-7.
-- It's pretty refreshing that we won't be talking about bad special teams play this week, isn't it?
-- It's actually ironic that the Dolphins ended up winning by three and the only missed field goal came from former Miami kicker Jason Sanders.
-- The Dolphins' new kicker Zane Gonzalez did a good job of putting the ball into the end zone on kickoffs, which limited the Jets' kickoff return opportunities and we'll take the defense starting at the 35.
-- The pass defense again wasn't great, but the secondary is the youngest unit on defense, so maybe it's to be expected to a certain degree. And that was a big-time veteran play by safety Michael Taaffe on his pick when he totally read the eyes of Geno Smith as he was scrambling.
-- Another big reason for the three-point win, of course, was the goal-line stand culminated by Chop Robinson's third-down sack when he absolutely didn't bite on Smith's play fake and Zayne Anderson took away Smith's short outlet. But it was Zach Sieler who made the big first-down tackle to start the whole thing, part of a really good performance by the D-tackle.
-- Yes, we have to factor in the quality (or lack thereof) of the opposition when dissecting this first Dolphins win, but then we also have to look at the quality of the teams against which they lost. So it works both ways. The Dolphins step up again in competition next week when they play host to the New England Patriots, but we'll continue to say the Dolphins will win a game or two this season that they're not supposed to win.
-- This game again the Jets was one of those that was deemed most winnable for the Dolphins, and that's how it played out. Now we don't have to hear anymore about going 0-17, we can table the draft talk for a bit because who knows exactly how high they'll wind up picking in the first round, and maybe most importantly we can just sit back and continue watching the development of the players before making premature determinations.

title: The Five Dolphins Players in the Spotlight in Week 7
full_text:
The MIami Dolphins will be back in action against the New York Jets on Sunday, and the mission will remain the same.
The Dolphins still are looking for their first victory of the season, but more importantly want to see progress and improvement, particularly after the disappointing showing in the last outing against the Cincinnati Bengals.
The matchup against the Jets, who also are in rebuilding mode though further ahead than the Dolphins, represents a good opportunity for Miami to get its first win of the season and end all talk of a winless season.
Most importantly, the Dolphins need for their young players to get better and organically that will give them a better chance to win as the season progresses.
With that in mind, here are the five players we'll be watching closely against the Jets:
QB Malik Willis — There might come a time when this no longer applies because it will have become apparent that the Dolphins need to look elsewhere to find a quarterback for the long run, but we're not there yet — even though a lot of fans already have given up on him. It's very obvious that Willis hasn't played well enough so far in 2026, but every game is a new opportunity and at some point the entire offense (hopefully) will start jelling a bit more.
WR Caleb Douglas — It's not often that the return of a rookie third-round pick is as anticipated as Douglas being back against the Jets, but this is where we are with the Dolphins. The clear lack of playmakers on offense was exacerbated by the loss of De'Von Achane to his season-ending knee injury and Douglas' performance in the Week 1 game against Las Vegas provided cause for excitement. Having said that, it's also probably not fair to expect big numbers from Douglas right away after he missed three games with an ankle injury, but there should be some kind of impact.
RB Ollie Gordon II — Gordon has averaged 94 yards in his two games since taking over as the starter, and now he'll be facing a run defense that's had some tough outings. Gordon could become the most important player on offense before this season is over.
LB Jacob Rodriguez — The second-round pick is off to a great start in his rookie season as a tackle machine, but he'll be challenged again in the pass game because the Jets have an uber athletic rookie first-round pick at tight end with Kenyon Sadiq, whose backup is another good young pass-catching tight end, Mason Taylor (son of Dolphins legend Jason Taylor). It won't be all on Rodriguez to limit the damage from the tight ends, but he'll be involved and will need to clamp down.
EDGE Chop Robinson — Jets quarterback Geno Smith has been very good this year at avoiding turnovers, but he'll also been criticized for taking too many sacks. This is where Robinson has to come in. Some of his analytics in the pass-rushing department are very good, but they haven't translated into enough impact plays. This is where he's got to make it happen.

title: Dolphins Saturday Mailbag: Why Fans Should Want to See Victories
full_text:
Part 1 of the pre-Jets game Miami Dolphins On SI mailbag:
So me and my sons are flying up for the game. Even though we want a top draft pick next year, can you give us a reason to root for a win?
Hey Mark, because the biggest thing you should want to see this season is progress from the young players, namely all the recent draft picks, as well as from Malik Willis. And the Dolphins starting to win some games certainly would be a sign of progress, which might provide more optimism than winding up with a higher draft pick in 2027 than with more and more losses.
Hello Alain, which of the Dolphins and Jets has the better future outlook with their current QB situation? Or is the present irrelevant, and both are likely to find themselves in a future competition to acquire the best prospect that might provide hope in challenging the top of the division?
Hey Ricky, this is a very good question and the answer will come down to whether Malik Willis can take that step and establish himself as a bona fide long-term answer so the Dolphins can use their resources in other areas. If we’re looking at the totality of the roster, I think the Jets actually might be a bit ahead at this time, though it’s pretty close, but Geno Smith clearly is a stopgap for them. Also remember that the Jets have three first-round picks again next year and if they can nail the quarterback, that could set them up for a pretty drastic turnaround sooner rather than later.
I don’t see everything that you say, but I’ve yet to hear you proclaim what you would do, only what you would not do, with the first overall pick. So that being said, as things stand right now and we’ll pretend like the Dolphins have the No. 1 pick and not the Chargers. Who would you select at this very moment with the No. 1 overall pick for the Miami Dolphins?
Hey Dana, you haven’t missed anything because my take always has been that I don’t like the idea of Jeremiah Smith first overall because of positional value (or lack thereof) and I’ve also said that I need the season to play out in college football before I decide which prospect I would prefer. To answer your question, my first preference at No. 1 would be trading down, hopefully not too far down, and picking up additional draft picks. If that’s off the table, based on what I know right now and subject to change, I’d be inclined to go with either Texas edge defender Colin Simmons and might even consider Leonard Moore, the cornerback from Notre Dame. I still don’t have a QB prospect that screams “must take” right now.
Hey Davis, if you’re asking why the Dolphins waived him in terms of this being a big surprise, my answer to you would be that it shouldn’t have been a big surprise. While Duck did show potential at times for the Dolphins in 2024 and in training camp last year, it’s not like he was an established player. And that Miami decided he didn’t rank higher than any of the three newcomers they have — Jaylin Simpson, Marcellas Dial Jr. and Reece Taylor, all of them claimed off waivers, mind you — and that should tell you all you need to know.
Greetings Alain! Had to take an emergency trip to Central Florida last week & on way back was caught in one of the infamous traffic jams around Miami area, so I listened to the Collective.  I then noticed I was in the stadium area & I was creeping along & y'all were talking about the season; the irony wasn't lost on me. This season is meant to creep along, but it gets lost on us fans sometimes. Not sure if he's been asked, but do you think Hafley regrets no 7 on 7's to build some chemistry between QB/receivers? Also to get receivers better familiar with proper routes? Final question: Is Chris Bell's lack of separation due to still recovering from knee injury? Not knowing the assignments? Something else? As always, look forward to both All Dolphins and Dolphins Collective podcasts (best out there) and all the great written content on Miami Dolphins on SI.Com.
Thanks as always, Dave. I don’t think there’s any question that Bell’s knee injury still factors in his ability to separate at the time, but it’s also fair to ask what his ceiling is in that department once the injury is a thing of the past because I don’t think that ever was considered his forte. Hafley explained his disdain for 7-on-7 work in training camp as not being representative of what players will do in games, and I’m thinking he wouldn’t be about to second-guess himself there. And if that 7-on-7 that wasn’t done was replaced by 11-on-11 sessions, then the Dolphins didn’t miss out on that kind of work.
Do you think the Dolphins' staff will be less likely to activate or play injured players due to the history of injuries at that crap field?
Hey Lloyd, it’s a very interesting point you raise because MetLife Stadium historically has been rough on players, for sure. That said, no, I don’t think decisions will be made specifically because of that surface. If the Dolphins decide, for example, that Caleb Douglas is ready to go, I don’t think Jeff Hafley wants to go down the road of being afraid of something bad happening because the game is at MetLife Stadium.
I need your honest opinion here. Do the Miami Dolphins have the smallest shoulders for a coach and general manager duo in the NFL?
First off, I always give my honest opinion. Never a need to preface a question with that. Second … huh? Smallest shoulders? You mean, Jon-Eric Sullivan and Jeff Hafley are not physically imposing? So? And I haven’t studied or examined other coach/GM combos to see where they stand among their peers.
What weapon not named Ollie Gordon steps up on offense on Sunday?
I think Malik Willis comes back from the bye with his best performance of the season. If you’re asking for somebody other than the QB, then maybe I go with Greg Dulcich, who’s due to have a big performance in the passing game.
