title: Breaking Down the Louis News and the other Week 7 Dolphins Saturday Moves
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins will get a second rookie back when they face the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on Sunday.
Safety Kyle Louis was activated off injured reserve Saturday, meaning he'll be ready to return to action for the first time since sustaining a knee injury in the season opener against the Las Vegas Raiders. Louis' availability had been trending positively all week, culminated by his full participation in practice Friday, though he remained listed as questionable on the final injury report of the week.
Along with activating Louis, the Dolphins also made their two weekly practice squad elevations, this time with edge defender Max Llewellyn and kicker Zane Gonzalez.
The move with Gonzalez basically was a given since the Dolphins don't have a kicker on the 53-man roster after releasing Riley Patterson on Tuesday, while the move with Llewellyn suggests that Rob Beal Jr. will miss a fourth consecutive game because of the hamstring injury he sustained in the Week 2 loss against the San Francisco 49ers. He was listed as doubtful on the Dolphins' final injury report of the week.
Llewellyn, the rookie seventh-round pick out of Iowa, will be making his second appearance. He played five snaps in the 35-13 loss at Levi's Stadium.
Louis will become the fifth safety on the active roster, joining Dante Trader Jr., rookie Michael Taaffe, Zayne Anderson and Julius Wood.
A linebacker at the University of Pittsburgh, Louis was switched to safety at some in training camp and in an ideal world he could become a good nickel defender because of his coverage ability. Before he was injured, Louis also had become a gunner on the punt team.
Given that he hasn't played since the opener, it's probably fair to expect Louis to play mostly, if not exclusively, on special teams against the Jets.
But regardless it's great to have him back.
He is the third player the Dolphins have designated to return from IR so far this season after DT Kenneth Grant and LB Trey Moore. Grant also has returned to the active roster, while Moore remains on IR and was designated to return on the day of the cuts to 53 to preserve a roster spot for somebody else.

title: Three Bold Predictions for the Miami Dolphins Against New York Jets
full_text:
The 0-5 Miami Dolphins take on the 2-4 New York Jets in Miami’s first divisional game of the 2026 season. Both teams are looking to keep their seasons from going completely off the rails, so let’s make some predictions for this Week 7 matchup.
Sunday will mark the return of rookie receiver Caleb Douglas, who has missed the past three games with an ankle injury. Adding his size to the top of the depth chart should bump everyone else to a more natural position, and there may be no bigger benefactor than Malik Washington.
Washington has quietly put together an impressive third season, tallying 50 or more scrimmage yards in four of his first five games. He has also established himself as a favorite target of quarterback Malik Willis, who has thrown his way 36 times this year (more than double the second-place mark).
As Miami looks for sustainability, targeting Washington underneath seems like a potential solution, and he has the agility to make defenders miss in space. His ascension, Douglas’ return, and Willis likely needing quick answers against a Jets defense that ranks eighth in blitz percentage is a recipe for a big day for Miami’s most experienced receiver.
This matchup features two passers who have done a poor job mitigating pressure this season. Both rank top 12 in time to throw, top three in pressure rate allowed, and top five in sack percentage.
The Jets are well equipped to take advantage of Malik Willis’ indecision. Their defense ranks in the top eight in pressure rate, and is tied for sixth in total sacks through six weeks.
The Dolphins, on the other hand, have been inept up front. Their four sacks are half the next-lowest team in the NFL, and all four came against Kyler Murray and the Minnesota Vikings in Week 4.
With two weeks to prepare, a quarterback who is willing to hang in the pocket, and the potentially dumb luck that Miami’s sacks have come in a bunch, this feels like a perfect opportunity for the Dolphins’ defensive front to make its mark, even if Malik Willis’ play leads to a similar outcome on the opposite side of the ball.
Ollie Gordon's development in year two has been a revelation. His footwork looks substantially better than it did in 2025, and he’s made the most of his elevated opportunity. Gordon’s rushing yards over expected per attempt is ninth among qualified rushers, per NextGenStats.
The Jets have a very sound defense on a per-run basis. Their EPA per rush allowed is tied for third best in football, and they’re right around the middle of the pack in terms of yards-per-attempt. They have, however, struggled to stop runs in the backfield. Their stuffed run rate is seventh-lowest, and they’re allowing over a yard and a half before contact per carry, which ranks ninth-worst.
Miami’s massive offensive line has opened up big lanes for Gordon in recent weeks. He has a 20+ yard carry in each of the last two games. Now, against a defense that particularly struggles to generate displacement, it wouldn’t be shocking to see the left-side duo of Paul and Proctor give Gordon a runway that he can use to get downhill and put his massive frame to work against New York’s defensive backs.
Tyler DeSena is currently a journalism student at the University of Central Florida. Prior to joining Dolphins On SI in 2026, DeSena worked with dolphinstalk.com, and created independent social media content on X, YouTube and TikTok.

title: Great Douglas News Highlights Positive Final Week 7 Dolphins Injury Report
full_text:
After some extensive time off in the form of a bye week, the Miami Dolphins won't be completely healthy when they take on the New York Jets, but they're getting there.
But they will get back a big piece of their offense for the Week 7 matchup against the New York Jets, with wide receiver Caleb Douglas off the injury report after being a full participant in practice Friday.
Douglas missed the past three games because of an ankle injury he sustained in the Week 2 loss against the San Francisco 49ers and the Dolphins clearly missed him.
It's not ridiculous to say the outlook of this game changes with the return of Douglas. The Dolphins passing offense was one-dimensional without him, with only Malik Washington and Greg Dulcich being consistent targets for Malik Willis, but even that's pushing it.
Despite missing three games, Douglas STILL has the third-most receiving yards of any target on the Dolphins with 113.
Miami is lacking a wide receiver that has as much upside as Douglas has shown so far, even with limited snaps due to the injury. His ability to separate from defenders is unmatched on the roster right now, combined with his speed and agility to get open in a hurry. His return brings size back to the position, with his 6-4 frame being taller than any other wide receiver.
The Dolphins currently average 153.6 passing yards per game, the second-fewest in the NFL, just 0.1 yards ahead of the Tennessee Titans. The group could use a splash of youth to energize it against a Jets secondary that allows only 185 yards per game, the fourth-fewest in the NFL.
Douglas isn't the only Dolphins rookie who could make his return against the Jets.
Safety Kyle Louis was listed as questionable for Sunday even though he's currently on the IR, but the encouraging sign here is that he was a full participant in practice Friday after being limited the previous two days. This could be a sign he's ready to return in his first week of eligibility after missing the required four games.
Normally, activating someone from the IR would require a corresponding roster move to stay within the 53-player limit, but the Dolphins are currently at 52.
Running back Jaylen Wright, who's been dealing with a nagging foot injury, also was cleared to play. With that said, Wright has struggled to make an impact as Ollie Gordon's backup, but the Jets' defense hasn't had the best success against rushing offenses - 123 yards per game given up. This could be his best chance yet to contribute.
Rookie tight end Will Kacmarek, who has been dealing with a hamstring injury, specifically noted on Thursday that he'll be ready to play Sunday, and he was cleared on Friday. As mentioned earlier with Wright, attacking the ground might be key for Miami's offense, and Kacmarek has impressed as a run blocker for Gordon thus far.
However, there are a few players on defense who might not play this game. That includes edge rusher Rob Beal Jr., who is listed as doubtful. He had to exit the San Francisco game with a hamstring injury. Before that, he recorded a single tackle against Las Vegas in the season opener.
It's also confirmed that cornerback Reese Taylor will not play Sunday because of a quad injury; he was ruled out.
Linebacker Willie Gay Jr. was back at practice Friday after being out one day with an illness, and he was listed as questionable after being a limited participant.
On the other side, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn is dealing with a significantly larger number of questions in terms of who's playing in this game. The most significant player on the list is running back Breece Hall, who was listed as questionable. He's been dealing with a quad injury suffered against Detroit in Week 3.
Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said that he'd be surprised if Hall didn't play in this game, but the Jets might not want to rush things with Hall, especially because his replacement, Braelon Allen, has done such a great job in his wake with 314 yards and two touchdowns.
A big boost to the Jets' receiver corps will be the return of wide receiver Adonai Mitchell, who is expected to play while dealing with a broken finger. It'll be the first time that Mitchell, Garrett Wilson and rookie first-round pick Omar Cooper Jr. will all be ready to go in the same game since their season opener.
Nose tackle T'Vondre Sweat is dealing with a knee injury but is expected to play Sunday. He's been reliable when healthy, with 15 tackles in six games played. It's a solid contribution for a player who was acquired from Tennessee in a trade that sent Jermaine Johnson to the Titans.
There are a few players officially ruled out: linebacker Kiko Mauigoa (quad), edge rusher Joseph Ossai (ankle), and offensive lineman Max Mitchell (concussion).
Left guard Dylan Parham is questionable to play in this game with a knee injury that has sidelined him for three games. His backup, Jordan Meredith, has played well in his absence, but it would mean a lot for the Jets to get one of their top linemen healthy once again.
Kene Nwangwu is also listed as questionable, which is a big blow for the special teams. He's been a decent kick returner with 251 yards on 11 attempts but hasn't had an opportunity to break a long run yet this season. If he can't go, Isaiah Williams will likely have to shoulder returning once again for the Jets. It should be noted that Williams had a 78-yard punt return for a touchdown for the Jets' only score in the Dolphins' 34-10 victory at MetLife Stadium last December.

full_text:
The Miami Dolphins again will be looking for their first victory of the Jon-Eric Sullivan/Jeff Hafley era when they return from their bye to face the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on Sunday.
Here's all the pertinent info for this Week 7 Dolphins-Jets matchup:

The Jets, much like the Dolphins, still are in rebuilding mode two years removed from ending the failed Aaron Rodgers experiment. This is a relatively young team under second-year head coach Aaron Glenn, though the Jets appear on the right track with the promising early returns on their three rookie first-round picks — edge David Bailey, tight end Kenyon Sadiq, and wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. The Jets have another three first-round picks next year and it's widely expected that's how they hope to land their quarterback of the future. In the meantime, it's 36-year-old veteran Geno Smith running the offense in his second stint with the team after first arriving as a second-round pick in 2013.
-------------------------------------------------------------------
The best place to start here is that the Dolphins have owned the Jets lately, winning 14 of the past 17 matchups, including a season sweep last year. The Jets might be a better team than they were in 2025 when they struggled offensively with Justin Fields at quarterback, but they still rank in the bottom third of every significant offensive statistical category. While Smith has an impressive passer rating, he's also taken an awful lot of sacks. The Dolphins are coming off two good performances with their running game and the Jets have been very inconsistent with their run defense.
-------------------------------------------------------------------
When a team is 0-5, the reasons a team could lose should be obvious. While the bye may have helped the Dolphins in many ways, this remains a very young team lacking in talent across the roster. The Jets defense doesn't have the big names anymore after the trades of Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams, but they can play good football at times, evidenced by the fact New York held three of first six opponents to under 200 total yards.
This game was highlighted from the start as one of those best opportunities for the Dolphins during this full-blown rebuilding season, and nothing has changed that outlook. The Jets — to borrow an expression — pretty much are who we thought they were, a young team that's not good enough to compete for a playoff spot, good enough to be a tough out but also never an overwhelming opponent. The Dolphins haven't played since that disappointing Week 5 loss against Cincinnati when they took a step back after competitive games against Kansas City and Minnesota, so it's difficult to gauge what kind of performance they'll offer. The Dolphins will defeat the Jets this season, but we're thinking it'll happen in the rematch in five weeks. Final Prediction: Jets 19, Dolphins 17

title: Dolphins Opponent Intel: Jets Insider Dishes on Minkah, Mason Taylor, Geno Smith and More
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins’ Week 7 matchup against the New York Jets will feature a matchup of AFC East in rebuilding situations.
While the Dolphins will head into the game with an 0-5 record, the Jets will come with a 2-4 mark that isn’t exciting, but clearly better than last year when New York started off 0-7 on their way to “earning” the second overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft.
The Dolphins swept the Jets last season, winning a close game at Hard Rock Stadium in the Week 4 Monday night matchup and blowing out the Jets at MetLife Stadium in December.
While it’s clear the Dolphins aren’t as talented as they were last season, the Jets are a bit more of a mystery.
On an episode of the All Dolphins Podcast earlier this week, New York Daily News reporter Antwan Staley helped provide some inside info on the Jets.
Here were some of the highlights of our conversation with Staley:
On an overall outlook for the season:
"What I would say is the good news is they're not 0-7 like they were last year. The Jets still aren't a good team, but I feel like they've gone from a really bad team to now a mediocre team, one that you know it's gonna be in games there, and it's gonna pressure opposing teams and all that stuff. We saw it against the Patriots there. I felt like they had some grit, had some fight. They just did. They’re just not talented enough to be able to overcome the mistakes that they have. Whether you talk about you know clock management or you know drops or penalties and things of that nature. So I think we're just seeing a team that was really young last year, they're the third-youngest team in football. Now they added some veterans there, Minkah Fitzpatrick, Demario Davis, among others, and now they're just trying to get from a mediocre team to a playoff team. And it might be another year before that happens too. But you know, they're a team that's probably going to be in every single game this year for the most part. But lack of talent is still evident in a few spots."
On Geno Smith’s performance this season and how legit is his 101.8 passer rating:
"Yeah, he's held the ball too long at times. Obviously, him being 36 years old now, like he doesn't have the same athleticism that he once had. Doesn't have necessarily the quick release like he once had. So I think he gets in trouble where you know he can hold on to the ball a little bit longer, waiting for his receivers to get open, and thenI think teams now — kind of what you found in the Patriots game — speed him up, like get him processing a little bit faster. That way he can possibly make mistakes. We've seen him fumble the ball a few times. He's only had one interception, but he's had a few fumble losses as well. So it's been up and down. It's been better than what it was last year with Justin Fields, which is a very low bar. But you know, I think Geno has given them opportunities to win games. He just hasn't always played well, so I think the quarterback rating is a bit of a mirage too.”
On whether head coach Aaron Glenn is on his way to solidifying his spot as Jets head coach for the future after a shaky first season, or is that still way up in the air:
"Yeah, that's still to be determined. The positive again is the Jets are fighting; they're in these games. They're showing grit. They're not just laying down and letting teams beat them by 30 points, like you saw sometimes last year. So it looks a lot different. However, they're just not closing games the way that they should be, and it seems like it's the same mistakes that are happening all over again. It seems like it's some kind of boneheaded penalty. It seems like it's some kind of mistake as far as play calling as well. … And I think ultimately the biggest thing, the damning stat on Aaron Glenn is this: opponents have outscored the Jets right before halftime within the last two minutes 90-6 throughout his tenure. And then him being 0-7 in the AFC East. Those are the two damning stats on Aaron Glenn. So until those change, then yeah, it's gonna be up in the air whether he comes back for 2027 or not. It starts there. You have to be able to take care of the division. Forget about New England and Buffalo for a minute, but you cannot get swept by the Dolphins and expect to keep your job this year. So this is a critical game for him. I'm sure it's a critical game for Jeff Hafley and the Dolphins organization too. The loser is going to be in really bad shape, especially if it's the Jets, because people were already calling for Aaron Glenn to be fired even before the season started. If you lose to the Dolphins, then it's hard to kind of overcome that."
On the play so far of two-time Dolphins safety Minkah Fitzpatrick, who they traded to the Jets this offseason for a seventh-round pick:
"I mean, he's been solid. He actually recorded their first interception. They broke the drought, so he'scome in and done the things that they expected him to do: be a quarterback for the defense, be a ball hog. Really helped young safety Dane Belton, who I think has been one of the biggest surprises of the Jets too this year. So I think Minkah is doing a really good job, especially since coming back (from a hamstring injury). He's not the same player that he once was when he was younger, but I think the Jets still benefit from his intelligence and just be able to see just diagnose what the offense is trying to do on a down-to-down basis."
On how Mason Taylor, the son of Dolphins Hall of Famer Jason Taylor, is doing in his second season as a Jets tight end after the team drafted fellow tight end Kenyon Sadiq in the first round of the 2026 draft:
“Well, he had a thumb injury, which kind of kept him out for a little bit, and then since coming back, think he's become more of a safety valve for Geno Smith, especially with Breece Hall being out the lineup too. If you're getting opponents pressuring you and blitzing you regularly, then you need somebody that can kind of get you out of those situations. That's something Mason Taylor can do, kind of find those soft spots in the zone, get some 4- or 5-yard catches and just kind of move the chains down the fiel. He has a different kind of athleticism than Kenyon Sadiq. I think Sadiq is more of a genetic freak, running 4.3, where I think Mason Taylor is more that guy that can move the chains, is just going to be a possession guy, and there's nothing wrong with that. "
On this idea that Malik Willis is very similar to former Jets starter Justin Fields:
“Here's the thing. Like, at least Malik is not afraid to throw the ball down the field. Now, hethere's times where he shouldn't, but he's not afraid to take those chances down the field. I feel like Justin Fields was very scared and hesitant to throw the ball past 10 yards. I don't see the comparison whatsoever. Justin was very cautious, like overly cautious of taking the football, protecting the football. Malik, I don't think it's that at all. He should be sometimes, but I don't think he is. So, no, I don't think that's a good comparison at all.”

title: 3 Studs & 2 Duds From Vikings' Week 7 Win Against the Colts
full_text:
The Vikings gave fans a scare in Week 7 . Coming into the game against the Colts with a 5-0 record, the Purple and Gold trailed until the fourth quarter, when the team was able to outscore their opponents 10-0.
The 16-10 victory over the Colts keeps the Vikings undefeated, but it took a team effort with several key players stepping up when others struggled to have a positive impact on the outcome of Sunday's game.
The defense once again did its job. Although it allowed a rushing touchdown to superstar running back Jonathan Taylor, defensive coordinator Brian Flores's unit continues its streak of not allowing a touchdown in the fourth quarter and finishing games strong.
It was a lot of fun watching defensive lineman Jalen Redmond work against the Colts' offensive line. He had a huge day for Minnesota, finishing with five tackles and a half-sack while registering a hit on Indianapolis quarterback Daniel Jones.
Redmond will be a priority restricted free agent after this season. The 27-year-old defender is making an extremely strong case this season to earn a huge payday to re-sign with the Purple and Gold while allowing the rookie defensive linemen time to develop.
Speaking of rookie defensive linemen, it is great that the Vikings are being patient with Caleb Banks , but now that Minnesota is seven weeks into the season, it is time to see more from the No. 18 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
Banks— who also limped off the field at one point (h/t ESPN 's Kevin Seifert)—finished the game against the Colts with one tackle. It is time to start expecting more from a first-round pick to start feeling good about his future instead of wondering when he will finally make an impact on a game.
Rookie DL Caleb Banks has been limping and is now coming off the field for medical attention.
Welcome back to the Vikings, Jordan Mason. His presence on Sunday was huge, since Aaron Jones has been a workhorse while dealing with a sprained ACL and left the game against the Colts after aggravating his knee .
Mason was the only running back besides Jones to take a snap against Indianapolis. He carried the ball 17 times for 68 yards, averaging 3.4 yards per carry. With him back in the lineup, Jones should have time to heal and rest.
The Vikings' starting center has been good this season despite a shaky training camp, but he struggled to protect starting quarterback Kyler Murray and create space in the run game against the Colts.
A 34-yard pass from Murray to Jordan Addison was erased in the fourth quarter due to a holding call. That penalty could have been disastrous for the Vikings if they hadn't turned it into a 52-yard Will Reichard field goal.
The MVP of this game was linebacker Blake Cashman. He did it all for the Vikings against Indianapolis.   leading the team with 12 tackles while defending four passes and hitting the opposing quarterback three times, registering two sacks.
Cashman was everywhere on the field on Sunday. In fact, the Vikings shared on X that he is the first player in over 20 years to have four pass defenses and two sacks in a game. The last time that happened was Alex Brown of the Bears in 2005.

title: Anthony Richardson Trade Is Worth Vikings' Consideration Under the Right Conditions
full_text:
After firing general manager Chris Ballard, the Colts have emerged as a potential trade partner for the Vikings in recent weeks. That said, there's no better time than now for the Vikings to try to acquire quarterback Anthony Richardson.
The Purple and Gold face uncertainty when it comes to the QB room past the 2026 NFL season since Kyler Murray is on a one-year deal and could benefit from adding a young quarterback with proven potential and starter experience.
Earlier this month, court records showed that Richardson was arrested on a misdemeanor marijuana possession charge following a traffic stop in Carmel, IN, on Oct. 12. He already slid down the Colts' depth chart after Daniel Jones's arrival, but this latest situation could be the straw that broke the camel's back.
For starters, unlike Indiana, Minnesota is a state where it is legal to consume recreational cannabis. This arrest wouldn't be a big deal for the Vikings, but it could significantly decrease the cost of trading for the former No. 4 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft.
Richardson hasn't started a game for the Colts since Week 15 of the 2024 season. Since then, he's played only 14 snaps for Indianapolis and doesn't seem to be in a position to work his way back into a starting role the Colts anytime soon.
On the other hand, having Richardson in the Vikings' quarterback room would add competition for whoever Minnesota brings in during the offseason—either via trade, free agency or the 2027 NFL Draft—and raise the floor for the future of the position.
As a pro, Richardson has been a flop. He completes only 50.6% of his passes and has thrown 11 touchdowns to 13 interceptions while being sacked 21 times for a 144-yard loss. Still, his mobility has been on display, as he's rushed for 634 yards and 10 touchdowns on 115 carries. In 2024, he was a top-10 QB when it came to rushing yards per game (45.4, 3rd), rushing TDs (six, T-3rd) and yards per carry (5.8, 9th) despite playing only 11 games.
Richardson will be an unrestricted free agent after the Colts declined the fifth-year option on his rookie deal. If they don't intend to bring him back, the Vikings should be interested in the potential success an experiment could bring.
Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell would need to take Richardson on as a project and keep developing him. Based on the potential that led to him being a top draft pick, there is hope he could turn his career around in Minnesota, especially if he's inspired by the Purple and Gold's ongoing success.
If O'Connell and the Vikings still believe, they need to talk to Colts interim GM Ed Dodds about acquiring Richardson for a potential Day 2 or 3 pick in next year's draft. They need to strike while his value is at an all-time low, and anything higher would be an issue.
Perhaps it was foreshadowing, but O'Connell's words to Richardson after the Vikings' 21–13 victory over the Colts on Nov. 3, 2024, suggest that he believes the young quarterback has the talent to become a great player in the league, despite his struggles.
O'Connell might be able to put that faith to the test first-hand soon.

title: Vikings Week 7 Report Card: Grading Every Position After Sunday's Win Over Colts
full_text:
If it ain't broke, well, maybe try and fix it a little bit. The Vikings—once again— extended their perfect season thanks to an elite defense and a good enough offense against the Colts on Sunday.
Minnesota defensive coordinator Brian Flores's unit showed why it is the best in the league, while the offense still looks to be figuring things out in the 16-10 victory. Still, a win is a win, and the Vikings move to 6-0 on the year with few complaints from the Purple and Gold's fanbase.
As is tradition around here, let's get into some grades for the polarizing team.
Kyler Murray looked a bit out of sorts coming out of the bye, missing multiple throws throughout the day. Still, despite the off-target throws and pedestrian 150 yards through the air, Murray saved his afternoon with 39 yards on the ground, including a late 35-yard bomb that led to the only touchdown of the day.
The offense with Murray under center is still a work in progress, it seems, and a generational defense has allowed them to take their sweet time. Still, at some point field goals aren't going to be enough, and Murray will have to bring his best with the high-octane Lions and Bills up next.
Jordan Mason returned and looked like he did exactly what he was supposed to do: move the chains and grind away at the defense. His long was just 12 yards, though, and the Vikings are still lacking that explosive playmaker in the backfield who would take the offense to the next level. Aaron Jones was mostly stymied on the day until slashing through on a late 17-yard rush that also sent him to the blue medical tent.
Jonathan Taylor, meanwhile, gashed the Vikings with a 5.3-yard average and gave them a potential glimpse of what a possible trade could look like . Mason and Jones form a solid duo, but with Mason's lack of explosion and Jones' knee hanging on by a thread, the ice is thinning in Minnesota's backfield.
We had a Jauan Jennings sighting, who doubled his catches and quadrupled his yards for the season in one afternoon. Whether or not the two-catch game was enough for the Vikings to hang up on any general managers who come calling , though, is another question, but it was a nice rebound out of the bye.
Justin Jefferson still has yet to notch 100 yards in a game this season after reeling in just 44 against the Colts, and either Murray or head coach Kevin O'Connell (or both) needs to remedy that soon.
T.J. Hockenson and Gavin Bartholomew are forming a nice little duo at the tight end position. Without Josh Oliver, the Vikings haven't missed a beat, and Hockenson is clearly a favorite of Murray's. He snagged the only touchdown of the day for the Vikings and is slowly building a case to return again in 2027.
Hockenson is first on the team in catches and second in yards after six games.
The interior of the Vikings' line struggled with the Colts' defensive front. Will Fries is cruising for a one-way ticket out of Minnesota next season after another rocky game, and Joe Huber may not be the final answer at left guard with the trade deadline approaching. The Minnesota front has allowed three or more sacks in five games this season, and the run game hasn't been especially fruitful either.
The Colts attacked the Vikings' run defense and enjoyed some decent success, racking up 154 yards on the day. Their best run—a 38-yard Taylor TD—went right at rookies Domonique Orange and Caleb Banks, who got blasted out of the way.
Jalen Redmond is still clearly head and shoulders above the rest of the D-line , and if there were a weakness on defense, their depth here might be it.
Blake Cashman might be the best linebacker in football right now.
Twelve tackles, two sacks and a near interception against Indy propelled the Vikings to a dominating defensive performance. While Dallas Turner may get the national spotlight, Cashman is on track to be a first-team All-Pro. Kyle Van Noy added valuable reserve snaps once again with a TFL and has been the best signing of the summer.
The Vikings' secondary wasn't really tested by Daniel Jones and the Colts, but Harrison Smith called game with a fourth-quarter interception (h/t NFL)—his 40th of his career and Jones's seventh of the year.
HARRISON SMITH GETS THE INT! VIKINGS ARE 6-0 ‼️ pic.twitter.com/stul8J8hWe
The Vikings still have yet to allow a fourth-quarter touchdown this season, and Smith ensured that streak continues into Week 8.
All dreams come to an end eventually, and Will Reichard's epic field-goal streak came to an end on a blocked kick in the second half. Still, his leg has won more games for the Vikings this year than the entire offense, and he'll continue to be one of the most important players on the roster. Myles Price shook off a brief injury scare, but had a mostly quiet day outside of his opening 46-yard return.

title: 3 Things That Mattered Most in Vikings' 16-10 Win Over Colts in Week 7
full_text:
MINNEAPOLIS, M.N. — The bye week came and went, leaving the Vikings to make their return to action on a chilly Sunday afternoon.
Legendary play-by-play announcer Paul Allen sounded the Gjallarhorn as the Vikings kicked off their third home game of the season in pursuit of their first 6-0 start since 2009. Former Vikings safety Cam Bynum received a warm welcome in his first game back at U.S. Bank Stadium after leaving for Indy in free agency in 2025. That said, the Vikings' 16-10 win over the Colts on Sunday was defined by another lackluster showing from the offense, as defense and special teams once again carried the team to victory.
As the perfect season continues, here's what mattered most in a game that left more questions than answers as the Vikings improved to 6-0 with a win against a potential trade partner .
If you were hoping that Sunday’s game would build on the hints of promise shown in Week 5’s matchup against the Saints, you certainly walked away disappointed.
The first drive of the game would paint a picture of what was to come, as the Vikings wasted a great opening kick return from Myles Price by unsuccessfully running four times in a row for a turnover on downs in Colts’ territory. Luckily, the O did just enough in the fourth quarter to secure the win. Kyler Murray flashed his legs on a 35-yard scramble before finding T.J. Hockenson in the end zone (h/t NFL) to celebrate National Tight End Day.
A TD for T.J. Hockenson on National Tight Ends Day 😌 INDvsMIN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/E0aOAL9M10
It’s hard to tell whether head coach Kevin O’Connell has become too cautious as a play caller or if Murray is being too cautious as a quarterback, but something has to change if the Vikings' offense wants to compete with some of the best teams in the league in November.
Can defensive coordinator Brian Flores win NFL Coach of the Year? No, but the Assistant Coach of the Year award may already have his name stamped on it.
Minnesota's defense stole the show once again, taking a quick break to allow potential future Viking Jonathan Taylor a chance to check out the U.S. Bank Stadium end zone. After that, the defense locked in, bringing a relentless attack on Daniel Jones all afternoon, resulting in four sacks and a total of 44 yards for the Colts’ offense. Veteran linebacker Blake Cashman in particular had a monster day (h/t NFL), with two sacks and nine tackles on the afternoon.
Blake Cashman steps up for the sack 😤 INDvsMIN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/MSl2dfO6k7
The Vikings’ defense continues to prove itself as a championship-level group. The only question is whether the offense can carry its own weight when Minnesota matches up against some of the NFL's top offensive units.
Kicker Will Reichard officially passed Gary Anderson’s franchise record of 35 straight successful field goals on Sunday, further proving the immense value he’s brought to the team since being drafted in 2024. On his next attempt, the third-year kicker had a 59-yarder blocked that left the home crowd in shock.
While Reichard’s heroics this season have been a fan favorite storyline, it’s further proof of the offense’s inability to consistently find the end zone. This trend desperately needs to shift if this team wants to contend in January. In the meantime, Vikings fans should hope that Reichard’s miss leads to a new streak that carries him clean through the playoffs.

title: Demond Claiborne Faces a Harsh Reality After Vikings Release Week 7 Inactive List
full_text:
The Vikings' offense looks as healthy as it's been in a long time ahead of Sunday afternoon's clash with potential trade deadline partners , the Colts. Jordan Mason's return from injured reserve headlines Minnesota's clean bill of health, and the veteran running back's presence has already impacted another member of the backfield.
The Vikings released their Week 7 inactive list on Sunday morning , featuring the usual sidelined suspects (rookies Jakobe Thomas and Elijah Williams, quarterback Max Brosmer, etc.). Interestingly, though, rookie RB Demond Claiborne was among the latest inactives, marking his first missed game since the season-opening victory over the Packers.
Sunday's #Vikings inactives pic.twitter.com/f4hmml99eT
Sixth-round picks don't usually carry high expectations in Year 1, but that hasn't been the case for Claiborne, a Vikings fan favorite throughout the offseason . Unfortunately, the summertime fanfare hasn't led to regular-season results, and the latest development has put his rookie season in jeopardy.
It isn't surprising to see Claiborne returning to the inactive list based on how his rookie season has unfolded so far.
Despite the opportunity to step into Mason's role and alleviate some of the pressure on lead RB Aaron Jones Sr., the Wake Forest product has been as unproductive as can be. Claiborne has turned six carries into 13 rushing yards (eight yards from one carry) and eight receiving yards on two catches. His 55.2 rushing grade ranks 87th among 105 RBs on Pro Football Focus .
So it isn't surprising the Vikings want to return Mason as the RB2 at the earliest opportunity. The Gallatin, TN, native should provide Jones and the backfield with immediate help, already showing what he can do by rushing for 59 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries in Week 1.
Not only is Mason's return bad news for his future in the backfield, but Claiborne's outlook is taking another hit with DeeJay Dallas being active for Sunday's matchup against the Colts (h/t The Athletic 's Alec Lewis). The Vikings released Dallas before re-signing him to the practice squad earlier this week, so the fact that they still preferred to have him over Claiborne in the lineup (perhaps because of Dallas's special teams contributions) is telling.
Whatever happens on Sunday afternoon, Vikings fans should have a better idea of Day 3 rookie's future.
If each member of the Jones-Mason-Dallas trio does their part, the Vikings might finally have a solution to their backfield problem, giving less of a reason to reinsert Claiborne. That could also lead to Dallas being re-signed to the 53-man roster when his elevations run out, which would likely mean releasing the first-year runner before attempting to bring him back to the practice squad. According to Spotrac , a release would save Minnesota $885,000 this season—with dead cap hits of $205,185 and $73,407 in 2026 and 2027, respectively.
The Vikings could also dangle Claiborne in trade discussions as the Nov. 10 deadline approaches . He might not be right for Minnesota, but another team desperate for RB help might be willing to send general manager Nolan Teasley a seventh-round pick, especially if they're worried about competing with other suitors after a potential release.
Claiborne demonstrated a ton of promise by using his speed, racking up 2,542 rushing yards and 26 TDs over his last three seasons at Wake Forest. Hopefully, his inactive status serves as a wake-up call and gets him to a place where he can use those talents to succeed at the NFL level.
Otherwise, his time with the Vikings could end sooner rather than later.

title: Another Colts Playmaker Is Worth Vikings' Attention for a Potential Trade This Weekend
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts play the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, and a lot is on the line heading into this game. The Purple and Gold are undefeated through their first five games and hope to keep that winning streak alive after their Week 6 bye.
While the Vikings are 5-0, the Colts are coming off an embarrassing loss to the Tennessee Titans that led to general manager Chris Ballard being relieved of his duties. Now, Indianapolis will likely look to rebuild the franchise under a new leader's vision.
Ed Dodds has been named the interim general manager of the Vikings' opponent this weekend. It is his job to prepare the Colts for when the franchise hires a new leader in the front office. Until then, the team could look to acquire draft picks ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
While Vikings fans are daydreaming about acquiring All-Pro players like running back Jonathan Taylor or offensive lineman Quenton Nelson, a more likely trade target for Minnesota is wide receiver Josh Downs.
Downs was a third-round pick in the 2023 NFL Draft. The former North Carolina standout has played in 53 games for the Colts, starting 32. As a pro, he has caught 222 passes for 2,429 yards and 11 touchdowns.
Minnesota is still waiting to get production from free agent signing Jauan Jennings, who has struggled to be an offensive asset this season. He has caught only two passes for nine yards as the team's WR3 while playing 201 offensive snaps.
On the other hand, Downs has played 332 offensive snaps this season and has 24 receptions for 289 yards despite the inconsistent quarterback play from the Colts this year. Daniel Jones is making it tough for any pass-catcher to have a good season, completing only 59.6 percent of his passes for 1,290 yards, four touchdowns, and six interceptions.
Acquiring Downs in a trade would cost significantly less than Taylor or Nelson and could have a major effect on Minnesota's offense. Downs is in the final year of his rookie deal , making him a free agent in the offseason. The Vikings are ranked 29th in the NFL in passing yards per game (167) and could use someone to take pressure off Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, and T.J. Hockenson.
Nonetheless, when the Colts take on the Vikings on Sunday, Minnesota general manager Nolan Teasley needs to keep an eye on the 25-year-old wide receiver to evaluate his potential fit in a Kyler Murray-led offense that desperately needs a competent WR3.

title: Vikings vs. Colts: Who Wins and Why in Week 7
full_text:
Just a year ago, the Indianapolis Colts pushed all their chips in, giving quarterback Daniel Jones a monster extension, and doling out two-first round picks for cornerback Sauce Gardner. Life comes at you fast, though, and the 2-4 Colts have now fired the man responsible for those decisions in long-time general manager Chris Ballard after the team lost to the previously winless Titans in Week 6.
But despite hitting rock bottom, Indy still has some nice pieces on both sides of the ball, and Minnesota would be foolish to overlook them on their quest for 6-0. It's the Vikings and Colts in Week 7, so let's get into who wins and why in this Midwest battle.
Outside of guard Donovan Jackson, who is out for the season with a knee injury, the Vikings enter this matchup at near full strength, something that hasn't been the case since Week 1.
Justin Jefferson and the now healthy Jordan Addison have played just 18 snaps together this season, while Jordan Mason is finally back after spending four weeks on injured reserve. The stage is set for what could be the best offensive performance of the year.
The Colts defense will also be without their best player, as Gardner couldn't get his calf right in time to suit up. That's good news for the Vikings pass-catchers, who need to find some momentum soon, and bad news for a Colts team that has allowed 30 or more points four times this season. Mason and Aaron Jones should be in line for big days too, as the Colts have already allowed three 100-yard rushers this season despite an impressive interior defensive line.
Cam Bynum, the former Viking, and ironically, the one player this defense could really use right now, has five interceptions since joining Indianapolis last season and could be the X-factor on defense.
Ultimately, the Vikings are an ascending unit on offense, and the Colts haven't shown the ability to stop anyone besides a third-string Commanders quarterback so far this season.
Vikings legend Daniel Jones hasn't lived up to his expensive contract this season, and ranks near the bottom in most major quarterback metrics. Over the past three weeks, he's completed just 54% of his passes and thrown one touchdown to three interceptions. His nine total turnovers and 15 sacks on the year certainly don't stack up well to a Viking defense elite at creating both.
Star rusher Jonathan Taylor has seven rushing touchdowns, but still has yet to notch a 100-yard game this season with his pedestrian four yards per carry. Meanwhile, the Vikings defense has allowed more than 50 yards to a rusher just once all season. Taylor has been linked to the Vikings as a potential trade candidate, and Minnesota will get an up-close-and-personal look this Sunday.
The Vikings league best +6 turnover margin and the Colts' league worst -8 will likely tell the story of this game, and Indy will have to play clean game to find a win in Minneapolis. That, or hope Spencer Shrader can continue his perfect season with a multiple 50+ yard field goals.

title: Ivan Pace Jr.'s Time With the Vikings Could End Sooner Rather Than Later
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings' defense is thriving under coordinator Brian Flores, and a significant reason for that success is the linebacker play. Starting interior linebackers Blake Cashman and Eric Wilson are playing so well that it is hard to take them off the field, which has led to a drastic decrease in snaps for Ivan Pace Jr.
Pace has played in all five games for the Vikings this season, but he has only participated in 45 of 295 possible defensive snaps. Even scarier is that he has played a total of seven defensive snaps in the last two games, getting only two against the New Orleans Saints in Week 5.
Eventually, rookie linebacker Jake Golday will start cutting into those snaps as well. The 23-year-old second-round draft pick has been getting a lot of experience by playing 95 special teams snaps in his first five games, but has been limited on defense, getting only seven defensive snaps.
Pace is only 25 years old but is in his fourth season in the NFL. His snap count on defense has decreased with every passing season since being signed as an undrafted free agent in 2023, but it can't get much lower than the 16 percent that he is playing this season.
It was a little surprising when the Vikings signed Pace to a one-year extensio n this offseason worth $3.52 million to stay in Minnesota for the 2026 NFL season, since the team was going to move forward with Cashman and Wilson as starters and drafted Golday with an early selection.
For now, Pace is essentially earning $3.52 million for his work on special teams. However, even his work in that phase of the game is shrinking, and he had his lowest special teams snap count of the season (17) in Week 5 against the Saints.
With Pace on a one-year deal and his role on defense and special teams shrinking, it is difficult not to feel like the clock is ticking on his future with the Vikings.
If a team with a need for an interior linebacker called with a mid-to-late-round draft pick as a trade offer for him, Minnesota general manager Nolan Teasley would be foolish not to listen to the pitch and consider the offer.
Otherwise, he may continue to be phased out of Minnesota's plans until he is eventually inactive on game day.

title: Vikings Week 7: Potential Trade Targets Among Most Important Things to Watch for vs. Colts
full_text:
Fans will once again fill the stands at U.S. Bank Stadium on Sunday as the Vikings return from a much-needed bye week break to host a Colts team desperate to turn their season around .
While everything suggests this should be a straightforward matchup for Minnesota, longtime fans know they can never write off an opponent . Let’s break down three key things to watch as the Vikings look to achieve their first 6-0 start since 2009.
The NFL trade deadline is rapidly approaching, and the Vikings are possible buyers. The Colts, meanwhile, fired their general manager six weeks into the season, signaling that anything short of a rapid change of fortune on the field could lead to a fire sale .
The Colts have several players who could be targets for a contender like the Vikings. Names floated over blogs, podcasts and social media include defensive tackle DeForest Buckner, left guard Quenton Nelson and even a possible reunion with former Vikings safety Cam Bynum.
The hottest name, though, is three-time Pro Bowl running back Jonathan Taylor.
While Minnesota may have no interest in acquiring any of the players listed, Sunday’s game gives general manager Nolan Teasley a chance to evaluate whether he wants to take a swing or two. If Teasley likes what he sees, a decisive Vikings win may be the nudge the Colts need to start answering phone calls.
Minnesota’s offense finally showed some life before the bye week, and the return of some familiar faces may take it to the next level. Thursday’s injury report listed every player on the 53-man roster as a full participant, providing a massive sigh of relief for Vikings fans everywhere (h/t: Vikings).
Barring setbacks, the team should see the return of Christian Darrisaw, Jordan Addison, Jordan Mason, and T.J. Hockenson.
Thursday's #Vikings injury report pic.twitter.com/EVmLOt2D49
While Minnesota is still dealing with the season-long losses of Donovan Jackson and Josh Oliver, Sunday will be the closest the offense has been to “full strength” since Week 1. The opportunity for the offense to gel against a spotty defense could not come at a better time as they prepare to face a gauntlet of top-end teams over November.
If the offense looks sluggish with a full slate of weapons, it may be time to worry about how sustainable that side of the ball could be.
Muhammad Ali and Joe Frazier. Magic Johnson and Larry Bird. Tom Brady and Peyton Manning. These are just some of the greatest matchups in sports history, and Sunday’s Colts-Vikings game will feature the next great battle of titans, as kickers Spencer Shrader and Will Reichard battle for supremacy.
In all seriousness, this game could very likely turn into a special teams shootout. Shrader and Reichard are both at the top of their craft, with Shrader’s 66 points scored through six games currently leading the NFL. His 11 points per game put him just above Reichard’s average of 10.6 over five games played (h/t: NFL Films ).
Don't mess with Will the Thrill 😮‍💨 @Vikings | @InsideTheNFL pic.twitter.com/n1CmRxSRje
Reichard’s 34-made-field-goal streak dating back to last season puts him just two kicks away from breaking Gary Anderson’s franchise record of 35. Hall of Fame kicker Adam Vinatieri holds the NFL record with 44.

title: Vikings Have No Excuse to Keep Sidelining Forgotten Rookie Amid Safety Concerns
full_text:
The Vikings have a real problem at safety . Veterans Harrison Smith and Josh Metellus are ranked among the ten worst safeties in the NFL this season, ranking dead last and sixth-worst, respectively, on Pro Football Focus . Despite the success of defensive coordinator Brian Flores's unit, a change is needed.
That said, the answer to Minnesota's safety issues might already be on the team's roster—a 2026 NFL Draft pick has yet to make an impact this season.
The Vikings selected Jakobe Thomas with the 98th overall pick in April, yet he hasn't played a single snap this season. The 6'1", 211-lb defensive back was inactive for each of Minnesota's five games before the bye, which doesn't bode well for his chances against the Colts in Week 7 .
Thomas played in one preseason game after working hard to recover from a back injury sustained during training camp. In that exhibition game against the Broncos, he had five tackles, three of which were solo efforts. His 79.4 tackling grade ranked second-best among Vikings defenders that game, according to PFF , while his 66.0 run defense grade was seventh-best.
Now that he's healthy and the safety room needs all the help it can get, Thomas needs to be active on game day.
Even if he only gets started on special teams, getting the former Miami (FL) and Tennessee defensive back some on-field experience could go a long way in preparing him for the future.
On Friday, Andrew Krammer of the Minnesota Star Tribune shared an article about Thomas that included a quote from Vikings special teams coordinator Matt Daniels. Apparently, the rookie safety has been asking when he will finally get on the field in a regular-season game.
The 23-year-old safety is chomping at the bit to get some reps this season. Considering how Smith and Metellus have struggled this season , it is imperative that the Vikings find a way to take pressure off Theo Jackson.
Jackson has played 191 defensive snaps for Minnesota this season and has the highest PFF grade among Vikings safeties this year, at 63.7. That's still not great, since it ranks him 41st out of 98 qualifying safeties across the NFL.
It is time to see Thomas finally play some snaps for the Vikings, and that should start in Week 7. He needs to be active on game day to prepare for a future where he steps into a defensive role for the Purple and Gold and helps keep Flores's defense among the NFL's most feared units.

title: Most Important Patriots Postgame From Week 7 — And What They Mean Going Forward
full_text:
Sitting at 4-3, the New England Patriots aren't lighting the NFL on fire. But they've played well in their wins, and in their Thursday Night Football loss to the Chicago Bears , they also had enough chances to try and win the game.
Instead, a Superman effort from the Bears offense — mainly Caleb Williams and Luther Burden III — sent the Patriots home with a 30-24 defeat. It was a game that the Patriots could have pulled away in, but too many opportunities went to the wayside.
"I think it's hard to say, 'Shoulda. Woulda. Coulda.' I definitely think we — I'm proud of the guys for the effort," Drake Maye said. "I think we did some good things and we got a lot of stuff to clean up. And we got to get back from the rest this weekend and get back after we had another one on the road, a division game."
Here are some of the biggest postgame quotes from the Patriots , both from the podium and inside the locker room, after their primetime loss to Caleb Williams and the Bears.
For most of the game, the Patriots trailed. They got behind big in the first half, but Rhamondre Stevenson's heroics to close the opening frame got them within a score. But the Bears roared out of the locker room to another scoring drive. It continued to be back-and-forth, but the Patriots were just one step away for most of the game.
Mike Vrabel on the offense's productivity: "We moved it however we needed to move it and sometimes you are going to have days like that. I thought we'd be able to run it a little better. We didn't, but then our best players were putting the ball in good spots most of the time and making good decisions. That's how it goes, we'd have liked to run the ball a little bit better. But, it didn't happen tonight."
Drake Maye on his end zone interception: "Yeah, I mean, we hit the same thing, the same exact play, it was later in the game. So, I like my chances in there and just — yeah, it's frustrating. So I know that was a big turning point in the game and I know I let my team down."
Christian Gonzalez on dealing with an illness throughout the game: "I woke up and I though it was allergies, and it was a lot more. ... It ain't none at the end of the day."
Hunter Henry on rookie tight end Eli Raridon: "(He's) great, man. Just continuing to get better and growing that confidence. A lot of fun to play with."
A.J. Brown on how he saw Chicago's defense attack him: "I think they did a really good job. Early on, (offensive coordinator) Josh (McDaniels) tried to do a really good job of getting me involved and Drake just was taking what they were giving. They were trying to take me away early on, and that's just kind of how the game played."
Charles Woods on the difficulty of defending Caleb Williams: "Anytime a quarterback that's mobile as him gets out the pocket, they definitely put stress on DBs. Then we have to cover the second play."
The Patriots played two games in five days, and looked worn down — especially after all the injuries that struck. They certainly needed the three days off that they were given this weekend.
But now a new challenge emerges, and it's about bouncing back to play a winnable game against the Miami Dolphins. As it stands right now, the Dolphins sit in the cellar of the AFC East with a 0-5 record and really don't look like they have anything going for them long term.
After a loss against a Super Bowl-like team in Chicago, the Patriots can't afford to look past a team that should beat without any issues. It starts with Maye playing clean football again, the defense wrapping up and making the tackles they need to and the offense capitalizing on their opportunities.
We'll see in a week's time if the Patriots were able to flush the primetime loss and get back into the win column.

title: Patriots Legend Pokes Fun at Christian Gonzalez's Uniform Number
full_text:
There might not be a position for the New England Patriots that's so consistently good every single season more than the cornerback position. Ever since their days in the American Football League, the Patriots have always seemed to have a shutdown cornerback.
That trend has carried over to the present day, as Christian Gonzalez has cemented himsrlf as the latest addition to the shutdown cornerback lineage. But still, there's one thing that makes him stand out from the rest ... and it's drawn some jokes from another member of that cornerback fraternity.
Ty Law, arguably the greatest Patriots cornerback of all time and a Pro Football Hall of Fame inductee, kicked off the team's unofficial theme of the top cornerback wearing No. 24. Since Law donned the number as the Patriot's first round draft choice in 1995, Super Bowl champions Darrelle Revis (2014) and Stephon Gilmore (2017-2020) also wore it.
It's become part of the fabric of New England. Instead of retiring the number for Law, the Patriots have had it passed on. But Gonzalez — who certainly could stack up — blazed his own path, choosing No. 0 as his jersey in 2024.
That drew some jokes from Law this week.
On the fourth episode of "Forged in Foxborough," Law spoke about Gonzalez — who was seen signing his record-setting four-year, $135 million contract extension — and his choice of uniform numbers.
"Because of the success that I had with the number, 24, everybody's always gonna compare to me," said Law, who was inducted into the Patriots Hall of Fame in 2014.
"Then you had Darrelle Revis. He come in, 24. Super Bowl. Then you got Stephon Gilmore, 24. We were all those type of corners and we just happened to all be wearing the same number. Christian Gonzalez, yeah, he broke the rule dammit, you supposed to be wearing 24 Christian."
Gonzalez's career has been filled with a lot of uniform numbers. After being assigned No. 50 during his first training camp, he donned No. 19 in the preseason. Then the regular season hit, and he wore No. 6 for the first few games of his career.
He would miss most of the season with a torn labrum, and then become the first Patriots player ever to wear No. 0 the following year. When Gonzalez was drafted in 2023, Joshuah Bledsoe was wearing No. 24. He'd be released the following summer and undrafted rookie Dell Pettus would end up taking it (he's still wearing it to this day).
"He's making his name on his own right being the same type of player," Law continued. "Outside of Christian not wearing 24, that's a bad boy. He's gon' start his own thing."
Gonzalez has been off to a great start to his 2026 season, playing in five games and racking up 15 tackles and five pass breakups. He's yet to grab his first interception, but limited stars Jaxon Smith-Njigba and D.K. Metcalf in his matchups against them.
He's been a major part of a Patriots defense that's been the best part of the team seven weeks in. His contract extension, the largest in franchise history, got done before Week 1 in Seattle — helping set the tone for how the team wants to lock down their homegrown talents.
"We're excited to have him for hopefully a long time," head coach Mike Vrabel said.
Law, Revis and Gilmore all won Super Bowls with the Patriots, and now it's up to Gonzalez to join that elite group — this time with his own uniform number.

title: 3 Positions the Patriots May Address at the Trade Deadline
full_text:
After seven weeks, the New England Patriots are sitting in the thick of the AFC postseason race. They're 4-3, coming off a hard-fought TNF game against the Chicago Bears and now have a long break before their divisional battle with the Miami Dolphins.
But this team is far from perfect, and there are some holes that could be plugged up by the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Could the Patriots swing a trade to add some new help for the late-season push?
Here are three positions that the Patriots could potentially look at to bring a new face in via trade.
The Patriots have three running backs on the roster right now, so it might not make a lot of sense to add another one to the mix. But other than Rhamondre Stevenson, the Patriots haven't been able to get consistent week-after-week production from their backups.
TreVeyon Henderson, who was expected to have a large role this year in the passing attack, has really struggled on the ground — and carried the ball just three times on Thursday. Corey Kiner, a hard runner, just doesn't have the NFL experience yet for a larger workload.
So maybe the Patriots look to find some help with a receiving option. Tony Pollard, who was rumored to potentially join the Patriots through a trade last season, has 349 yards and one touchdown on a bad Tennessee Titans team. He fits the mold of a Josh McDaniels running back in this offense.
Injuries have depleted the interior of New England's offensive line . Mike Onwenu broke his ankle, Greg Van Roten was placed on IR one week later, Aliijah Vera-Tucker was just placed on IR this week and Ben Brown is dealing with an ankle injury. It's not a deep unit right now.
The Patriots have gotten inspiring play from backups Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse, but that pair — one that wasn't even with the team during the preseason — could be improved on ahead of the postseason. So maybe the Patriots try to swing for the fences with a new starter.
This one might be a pipe dream, but Quenton Nelson has been one of the league's top guards since being drafted by the Indianapolis Colts. If the Patriots want to try and get some additional protection for Drake Maye once the weather turns colder, finding a starting guard could help.
Another position banged up, the Patriots were without Carlton Davis , Channing Canada and Karon Prunty against the Bears. Charles Woods has stepped up in Davis' absence, and both Marcus Jones and Christian Gonzalez have been their usual selves. Kindle Vildor is also on the 53-man roster, rounding out that position group for now.
There is always room to try and bring in some new blood to shut down some of the receivers coming up on the Patriots' schedule. They're tasked to go against Justin Jefferson, Jaylen Waddle, D.J. Moore, Christian Watson and Garrett Wilson later this year, and while those guys will certainly be lined up against Gonzalez, another injury could be dangerous.
There are several guys who have seen their names tossed around trade talks, including Philadelphia's Kelee Ringo and Riq Woolen, Tampa Bay's Zyon McCollum and Los Angeles' Donte Jackson. A lot of this would depend on the health of Davis , who's dealt with a neck injury for the last few games.

title: Patriots Week 7 Snap Count Analysis: Why Didn't TreVeyon Henderson Play As Much?
full_text:
The New England Patriots ' three game-winning streak was snapped on Thursday night, as they lost to the Chicago Bears 30-24 at Soldier Field . It was a weird game, as the Patriots played well enough to find ways to find the game. But ultimately, they struggled on both sides of the ball to make the one extra winning play.
"It's a thin margin when you play good teams," Mike Vrabel said postgame. "We did some good things. But again, didn't do enough. We didn't get enough stops in the red zone and we didn't convert our red zone opportunity the one time, so. That's probably the difference in the game."

title: An Oral History Of Patriots WR Kyle Dixon's 'Twisted' Collegiate Baseball Career
full_text:
Kyle Dixon , the 26-year-old wide receiver from Carlinville, Illinois, was a multi-sport athlete in high school. He was a fantastic wide receiver, a fantastic defensive back and an even better pitcher.
His journey out of Carlinville High School started on the mound. It's now taken him onto the sidelines for the New England Patriots .
How in the world did that happen?
When you ask Dixon — now on the Patriots practice squad — he still doesn't really know. He can try to explain his winding road to the NFL, but there's so many stops along the way that sometimes he forgets a few things. So here's everyone else he's crossed paths with to help fill in the puzzle.
Kyle, born in 2001 to Tim and Monica Dixon, played baseball, football and wrestled in high school. He was excellent in everything he did. His coaches rave about his athletic abilities, almost to a fault.
Don Borgini, former Carlinville baseball head coach: "He was a fierce competitor."
Monica Dixon, Kyle's mother: "He excelled in all of his sports, but was looking for ways to improve his skills. He was always looking online for new training techniques."
Kyle Dixon: "Baseball was a little bit more special for me."
Maybe it was just the athletic juices in his veins, but Kyle always lived for the moment. The homemade pitchers mound that Kyle and his grandfather made in his backyard certainly helped. Once high school rolled around, baseball is where he found his groove.
Borgini: "Every coach on Earth wants a kid that wants the ball in the moment, and Kyle is certainly that guy."
Monica Dixon: "When he did get to pitch, I had a lot of anxiety. His dad could always handle that pressure better than me."
Kyle Dixon: "It was something I really enjoyed a lot."
Borgini: "In a sectional game, he had 19 strikeouts of the 21 batters and it was a tremendous performance by him that I won't forget. ... It is the top (game) for me as far as a pitcher goes (that I've ever seen)."
Kyle Dixon: "It might have been the last game I ever played (in high school). ... We ended up losing that game."
Borgini: "He was attracting a lot of attention."
Monica Dixon: "As parents, it was nice to see his hard work pay off when he got his scholarship. He earned it."
Kyle officially committed to Southern Illinois after a coach at a local JUCO help connect the two parties. But he had committed when Ken Henderson was the head coach. Henderson was fired and the abrupt change caught Kyle — who was on his way to vacation — off guard. Still, from the first day on campus, he stood out.
Lance Rhodes, Southern Illinois baseball head coach: "He wasn't the typical high school-sized kid that was coming to college. He was very put together, just a good looking kid. He definitely looked the part."
Kyle Dixon: "You don't really know what to expect as a freshman, especially with the new staff that didn't recruit you. It was an interesting start to college."
Rhodes: "He (was) just as big as the seniors. He had a ton of ability and he threw extremely hard."
Kyle Dixon: "I was off to a pretty good start my freshman year and then we stopped. We couldn't go into our facility to train with it being COVID. We couldn't go to a lot of the gyms or anything to work out."
His freshman year was mangled by the pandemic, where he only played in eight games. He pitched in four more as a sophomore, but a 22.50 earned run average plagued him. It was a pair of trying years for Dixon. He watched pro pitchers like Max Scherzer and Aroldis Chapman to try and figure out his form.
Kyle Dixon: "I became very focused on looking at MLB pitchers' mechanics and then trying to figure out how I wanted mine to look in regards to that. ... I think I became too focused on mechanics."
Monica Dixon: "I think he started putting more pressure on himself to be perfect and it just wasn't happening. As a parent, it was hard to watch."
Rhodes: "Kyle was always one of those guys that the feel of pitching was something that he needed to develop and work on, and I really think the COVID break in action ... was probably the toughest thing for him."
Kyle Dixon: "I kept thinking if I just keep figuring out whatever mechanical thing it is, then it's gonna play, then it's gonna click. The reality, that was the problem in and of itself."
He didn't want to stick around. After his scholarship was pulled, Southern Illinois Edwardsville — who did research on him coming out of high school — came calling.
Sean Lyons, SIUE baseball head coach: "I had a local umpire stop by our baseball office, come in and tell our staff there's this really good arm pitching, high school kid, not too far from here. ... When Kyle decided to transfer from (Southern Illinois) Carbondale, we kind of had a connection."
Monica Dixon: "We just went with the flow. He would always talk to us about moving and the reasoning for it."
Kyle Dixon: "Ironically, the pitching coach there was the one who recruited me to Carbondale. I was really comfortable with him."
But that coach would later take the head coaching gig for SIUE's softball program, and so Dixon was left with another surprising staff change. Still, his stuff on the mound never left.
Lyons: "He could throw the baseball in the lower-to-mid 90s. Sometimes command and where the location of that was sometimes a mystery for him. But when it was right, man, it was really good."
Kyle Dixon: "I wouldn't say I had a good year, but it was a better year. It wasn't good, but it was progress compared to the year before."
Lyons: "He had a skillset on the mound that could have possibly given him the option ... to play professionally as a baseball player."
Kyle Dixon: "Without a doubt."
Maybe it was time to get out of Illinois. Kyle called Lyons to let him know that he would be entering the transfer portal, a decision that he think took his coach by surprise. After having some summer league teammates hype up Georgia Gwinnett, Kyle then made the trip down south to a team that would go on to make eight-straight NAIA World Series appearances, a streak still active.
Jeremy Sheetinger, former Georgia Gwinnett baseball head coach: "When you see a kid that looks like Kyle and he's built like an Adonis, you know that there's something in there. ... We just feel like sometimes Division I schools, if a kid doesn't gave it, they get pushed to the side. We could spent a little bit more time with them."
Braxton Meguiar, former Georgia Gwinnett second baseman (who played baseball with Mike Vrabel's son, Carter, at Wabash Valley Community College in 2021): "I always remember Kyle's work ethic being different. He never changed. He never wavered, even when he wasn't having success."
Like the previous two schools, it just wasn't in the cards. Kyle had the yips, most commonly associated when throwing a baseball accurately becomes a chore. He'd walk away from sports entirely at the end of the season.
Kyle Dixon: "I was still kind of holding out optimism that I was going to be able to figure it out and turn it around."
Sheetinger: "He was good for a hit an inning, a strikeout an inning and a walk an inning. ... Kyle didn't make our postseason roster."
Meguiar: "He was having some control problems."

title: 4 Postive Takeaways From Patriots' Thursday Night Loss to Bears
full_text:
After falling to the Chicago Bears (5-2) on Thursday Night Football, many are quick to pick apart what went wrong for the New England Patriots and what needs to improve. Those conversations are centered around third down defense, tackling, wide receiver play, and other scrutinies from the Patriots 30-24 let down.
However, like most games, the Patriots still put out good tape, despite the outcome. Here's what New England did well on Thursday night and what we learned about this team moving forward:
With a diminished wide receiver room, the Patriots had to rely on other skill position players to push the ball through the passing game. One of the few that stepped up on Thursday was rookie tight end Eli Raridon.
Raridon hauled in 3 catches for 56 yards, including a 30-yard touchdown reception on a seam route in the third quarter. Maye targeted Raridon earlier in the game but was intercepted in the redzone.
Raridon now has more receiving yards (168) and touchdowns (two) this season than Kyle Williams, Efton Chism III, and A.J. Brown. The third-round pick out of Notre Dame has turned out to be a great investment by the Pats, and will carry the team's pass game well after Hunter Henry retires or moves on from New England.
The Patriots are among the top teams in the NFL for players listed as inactive on reserve lists. Entering Thursday night, the Patriots had 22 players on reserve lists, with nine of those players being starters.
Most notably, the Patriots were missing four guards on Thursday, and were forced to start Walter Rouse and Matt Pryor . While the two players struggled, New England's offensive line had a decent performance, only allowing two sacks on quarterback Drake Maye.
Additionally, the Patriots had three inactive cornerbacks on Thursday, including starter Carlton Davis. Christian Gonzalez was also listed as questionable ahead of the game with an illness, but played every defensive snap.
Lastly, the Pats were limited to just four wide receievers, with Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs on the injured reserve.
With Chicago being one of the NFL's top teams, and last year's second ranked NFC team, New England's competitive showing was impressive, considering the diverse roster they were forced to use.
Similar to the last point, injuries have been a major hurdle the Patriots have had to overcome this season. Each game, the Pats leave with more diagnoses than they entered with.
Last night, the Patriots stayed relatively healthy. With depth being an issue, the health of New England's team was crucial to staying in yesterday's game.
The only significant injury was suffered by defensive linemen Christian Barmore, who appeared to sustain an upper-body injury after sacking Caleb Williams late in the game.
With 10 days until they travel to Miami, Patriots players will have plenty of time to recover from past injuries.
Running back Rhamondre Stevenson was one of the best players on the field Thursday night, and was crucial to New England's ability to stay in the game.
The sixth-year player only ran for 22 yards against the Bears defense, but carried the ball six times, which is twice the amount of his counterpart, TreVeyon Henderson.
Most notably, Stevenson impacted the game through his pass-catching. He hauled in 5 receptions for 93 yards and was New England's leading receiver. His 48-yard touchdown reception to end the first half kept the Patriots within scoring distance of the Bears for the rest of the game.
RHAMONDRE STEVENSON‼️ 📺 Prime Video pic.twitter.com/heXDiTFnzW
This season, Stevenson has 25 more carries than Henderson and has notched 82 more yards than the second-year player. While Henderson has dealt with an ankle injury over the past two weeks, the only action he's missed was Week 1 against Seattle.
Stevenson's production and usage points to continued increase in carries and impact plays from the veteran Patriot.

title: Drake Maye's Interception Wasn't The Reason The Patriots Lost
full_text:
CHICAGO — The New England Patriots didn't win on Thursday Night Football, and yet, their quarterback had yet another great performance.
Drake Maye threw for 300 yards for the second time in three weeks, scored 3+ total touchdowns for the fourth-straight game and used his legs to extend plenty of plays behind a banged-up offensive line.
Did he throw a bad interception in the first half that took points off the board? Yes.
Was that play the biggest reason for the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Chicago Bears ? Nope.
Maye was hard on himself after the game, taking the brunt of the blame for the bad interception he threw to Bears linebacker D'Marco Jackson. He was trying to hit Eli Raridon for a touchdown to cut into Chicago's 13-7 lead. Instead, he didn't put enough air on the throw and it was turned over.
“It definitely was a huge point in the game. It’s those plays, I talk about all the time," Maye said. "And those plays that can swing the game, can impact the game, and that was definitely one of them right there. I wish I definitely had that one back and a lot of plays.
"But got to give credit to them. They had a good plan on a short week and they got after us. ...  I know that was a big turning point in the game and I know I let my team down."
But the Patriots had a bigger reason for the loss, and it was from the other side of the ball. The Patriots really couldn't tackle all night, and according to Pro Football Focus, they missed 16 tackles. That's the most they've had in a single game since Super Bowl LX. Marcus Jones led the Patriots with five.
Chicago controlled the ground game with D'Andre Swift (22 carries, 78 yards, 1 rushing touchdown) and beat the Patriots' zone coverages all night.
“The tackling wasn’t good enough, not against this team," head coach Mike Vrabel said. "We knew coming in, certainly against this team, whether it’s Swift, (Luther) Burden, the quarterback. It just leads to extra yards and conversions. But, we fought. I would say that we need to turn the ball over and tackle better and those are fundamental skills."
Caleb Williams hit eight passes for 20+ yards, really stressing the secondary that was down three cornerbacks coming into the game.
Ultimately, the Patriots lost the game, not because of Maye's play, but because of everything around it. There wasn't a lot of production from the ground game or the wide receivers, penalties ran rampant and the defense struggled to bring anyone down.
And yet, Maye kept them in it. He shouldn't be the one receiving the pointed finger.
"He gave us a chance. He competed and I know he’d like to have that throw back to Eli but, I thought he really competed," Vrabel said. "Whether that was running around and scrambling or finding good places to go with the football. He gave us a chance. I know he’d like to have that one back and he’ll learn from it like he always does. I’m glad he’s ours."
