title: Three Key Matchups the Giants Must Win to Upset the Texans
full_text:
After two weeks of mixed offensive performances and disappointing results, John Harbaugh and the New York Giants are switching things up at quarterback, with J.J. McCarthy taking over for Jameis Winston ahead of a pivotal matchup with the Houston Texans.
The Giants are hoping McCarthy’s presence will spark an offense that lost some of its luster when Jaxson Dart went down and became too one-dimensional in its previous two games against the Washington Commanders and New Orleans Saints, behind Winston’s inconsistent decision-making and an unestablished running game.
That said, New York will need more than its new starter’s efforts to leave Houston with a huge win. Here are the three key matchups the Giants must dominate to stun the Texans and improve to 4-2-1 before their bye week.
The Giants are constantly reminded of just how important their two starting offensive tackles, Andrew Thomas and Jermaine Eluemunor, are to the offense functioning at its highest potential.
For the first time this season, Big Blue faced the Saints’ defense in Week 6 without its stalwart bookends playing every snap. Eluemunor missed the game with a calf injury he sustained against Washington.
Thomas opened on the left side despite a lingering groin ailment, then left in the fourth quarter after the NFL’s medical spotter pulled him for a concussion evaluation.
Without either veteran on the field, the Giants offense faced much more pressure from the New Orleans front, which tallied nine total pressures in the 34-27 loss. Those numbers might pale in comparison to what the Texans’ pass rush could deliver with its dynamic duo of Anderson and Danielle Hunter.
Per the team’s injury report following Friday’s practice, Thomas had no game status and appears to be a full go despite his ongoing groin injury.
Eluemunor, who leads all offensive tackles with a 96.7% pass-block win rate (min. 150 snaps), was listed as questionable, though Harbaugh seemed optimistic he could suit up and play.
The Texans typically flip Anderson, who leads the NFL with 7.5 sacks and holds a 14.1% win rate in his 208 pass-rushing snaps this season, to either side of the formation.
Anderson is a super-talented bull rusher with the power to drive opposing offensive linemen backward into the quarterback and blow up the play before receivers can progress through their routes.
The 6-foot-3, 243-pound defensive end has torn up his immediate matchups in recent weeks, collecting two or more sacks three times and five or more pressures in four of the Texans’ last five games. He can also crash interior gaps quickly, leading to 21 run stops in six starts.
That could pose a problem for either tackle (if they do indeed play) and for anyone who can’t anchor against Anderson’s bull rush.
The Giants are hoping to give McCarthy enough time to operate in the pocket and run extended RPO plays with his dual-threat skill set. If Thomas can’t perform up to par against Anderson, they could have to resort to quick throws instead of betting on a few chunk plays with the quarterback’s impressive arm.
One of the most enjoyable storylines from the Giants’ first six games has been the obvious turnaround in cornerback Deonte Banks’ performance since Dennard Wilson took over the defense.
Banks, a lame-duck starter since the Giants declined his fifth-year rookie option in May, has largely quieted the fan base’s complaints about his coverage with a much-improved 50% opponent catch rate allowed. He is tied with Greg Newsome II for the most pass deflections in the secondary (4).
Some old shades of Banks’ miscues have reared their ugly heads in recent weeks. He has drawn a penalty in three straight games and has allowed completions on 60% or more of targets against him since Week 4.
That includes last Sunday against Chris Olave and the Saints, when the former first-round pick out of Maryland allowed three catches on five targets for 36 yards, with a long of 18 yards, and fell asleep, letting Olave cash in one grab for a touchdown in the Saints’ win.
One week later, Banks’ newest assignment will be a much tougher one as he braces to slow down Texans wide receiver Nico Collins, who has wreaked havoc on opposing secondaries. Houston’s defense, meanwhile, is banged up.
Collins has been one of the most productive pass-catchers this season, averaging a team-high 80.8 yards per contest with a 78.6% catch rate , third-best among receivers with at least 25 targets.
The 6-foot-4, 222-pound Collins hasn’t been much of a deep-threat weapon for Houston’s offense, but he’s been efficient against press coverage, a staple of Wilson’s system. He has hauled in 83.3% of his targets against man coverage, including a perfect 2-for-2 on contested catches.
Banks has shown some strong flashes as an aggressive ballhawk and has helped the Giants flip the endings of a couple of games by getting his hands in front of the pass.
He’ll need to do a lot better against a craftier receiver like Collins, who might try to counteract the peskier coverage by drawing costly penalties against Banks.
That is the last thing his team needs when facing a Texans offense that ranks 15th in third-down conversions and will look to pile on points to pressure McCarthy and the Giants offense.
If Banks can shut Collins down, Houston can’t rely on its ground game to carry the load, as it sits in the bottom third of the league in both attempts and yards.
Giants receiver Malik Nabers promised to get open for his new starting quarterback against the Texans, but that might not be as easy if he has to spar with Derek Stingley Jr.
Nabers has found his groove after a long, grueling ACL rehab that began in Week 5 of last season, and he showed flashes of the dominant pass catcher he can be with three straight 100-plus-yard receiving outings.
Since Week 5, the 23-year-old Nabers has racked up 23 catches for 286 yards and a touchdown, despite Winston's errant throws.
The Giants star really exploded once McCarthy took over in the fourth quarter against the Saints, posting a season-high 12 catches for 165 yards and his fourth game with at least one contested catch.
Given the Giants’ unimpressive receiving depth and sputtering run game, Nabers will likely need to be a major factor in moving the ball through the air and attacking the Texans’ defense, which wants to stunt his confidence with its relentless pass rush.
Nabers’ speed and hands could be a huge asset if the Giants need to prioritize short throws and low crossing routes to counteract the blitz. It wouldn’t be surprising if the Texans call upon Stingley to be their own aggressive cornerback who frustrates the opponent’s top target.
Since 2024, Stingley has been one of the NFL’s stingiest perimeter defenders, allowing an average 52% completion rate in that span.
He excels at getting his hands on the football and cutting off direct throws that could become forced turnovers, leading to interceptions and 23 pass deflections. As bold as McCarthy can be with his decisive throws, he’ll need to be extra careful about ball placement to avoid Stingley bruising his stat sheet with turnovers.
Stingley will also make it tough for Nabers or any other receiver to gain extra yards after the catch, given his strong run-stopping play and fewer than 10 missed tackles in four of his first five seasons.
The Texans could even call on him as a pressure guy in select packages or have him crash the line of scrimmage to stop the run game they’re hoping to revive this week.
All that said, most of the Giants’ passing production has come through the heroics of Nabers and Isaiah Likely. McCarthy will look for his guys, and they’re vowing to be reliable.
Nabers’ reliability will depend on finding ways to beat Stingley off the snap and create separation that pushes the ball toward the end zone, where they’ll need to score to keep up with Houston’s fiery offense.

title: 3 Jets Look Like Bigger Trade Candidates After Humiliating Loss to Dolphins
full_text:
There's no way to put it nicely: Sunday afternoon's 28-25 loss to the Dolphins was nothing short of humiliating for the Jets. After all, the rival Dolphins entered Week 7 winless and among the NFL's laughing stocks, seemingly the perfect opportunity for head coach Aaron Glenn & Co. to claw within one game of a .500 record.
Instead of beating up on an easily beatable opponent, the Jets trailed the entire game as miscues on both sides of the ball suddenly had the Dolphins looking like the opposite of the AFC East's worst team. It's the type of defeat that likely not only defined Gang Green's season, but also Glenn's time in Gotham.
Heading into Week 8 with a 2-5 record, Jets general manager Darren Mougey will likely be doing much more selling rather than the buying fans wanted ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline . A roster retooling is needed to turn things around, after all, so don't be surprised if these three players become even bigger trade candidates after losing to the Dolphins.
A strong preseason performance led to Jarvis Brownlee Jr. having a big role with the Jets early in the 2026 season. He started the year off strong, too, with the veteran slot defender picking up Pro Football Foc us coverage grades of 82.0 and 70.0 in his first two games , all while playing 79 defensive snaps.
Unfortunately, that's as good as it's gotten so far.
Since then, Brownlee has finished with a grade of 59.4 or worse in each of his last four games, allowing 14 catches on 19 targets (73.7%) for 128 yards and a touchdown without any pass breakups or interceptions. The downward-trending performance forced Glenn to make a change on Sunday, scratching Brownlee while rookie CB D'Angelo Ponds took his spot in the lineup.
Although the Jets didn't win, Ponds looked solid, finishing with a 68.6 defensive grade while playing a season-high 30 snaps (32 combined in three previous games). He only allowed one five-yard catch and a 56.3 passer rating on two targets, giving the Jets even more reason to keep playing him over Brownlee.
Two years remain with cap hits of $1.08 million and $1.19 million on his contract , per Spotrac; Brownlee could easily be moved by the Jets before the trade deadline. It's becoming clear that he isn't a long-term solution in Gotham, so New York might as well see what it can get in a potential deal— especially if the team wants to fully unleash Ponds .
The Jets' wide receiver room has become healthier in recent weeks, with Tim Patrick, Omar Cooper Jr. and Adonai Mitchell all healing up since October began. While that's good news for New York's passing outlook, it's bad news for Isaiah Williams's hopes to get (and stay) on the field.
It's been a quiet season for Williams, who's done nothing of note since recording 73 receiving yards and a touchdown against the Bears in Week 4. The former undrafted playmaker recorded one 16-yard catch the following week and has now gone the last two appearances without a single target. Making matters worse, he only saw 22 offensive snaps in those games after averaging 46.6 in the five previous games.
He isn't even much of a factor on special teams anymore. After returning nine kicks and five punts in the Jets' first three games, Williams sits at two and five, respectively, in the last four.
Set to hit restricted free agency in March, it's hard to imagine Williams sticking around. That's even more true if Cooper continues to put up 100-yard performances while Mitchell gets his footing back. With his cap hit just over $1 million and there's no real loss by moving on from him, the Jets could explore a potential Williams trade in the coming weeks.
The 2026 season is a big year for veteran safety Andre Cisco, who's due to become an unrestricted free agent this winter. That said, an early injury to offseason arrival Minkah Fitzpatrick seemingly opened the door for Cisco to prove himself last month , whether that meant securing an extension with the Jets or impressing another team that could target him in March.
Much to his dismay, Cisco's outlook was dealt a major blow once Fitzpatrick returned to begin October. Since Week 4, the former Jaguars third-rounder has played only three, one, two and nine defensive snaps. It doesn't help that he's struggled to capitalize on the diminished opportunities, finishing with the worst coverage (28.8) and overall defensive (27.8) grades among Jets defenders in Week 7, per PFF .
It's clear that Cisco has fallen out of favor, and it's hard to see him turning things around as long as Fitzpatrick and Dane Belton hold on to their starting roles. A $2.2 million cap hit means the Jets shouldn't have an issue moving on from Cisco via trade, and doing so would allow them to see what they've got with certain defensive backs on the taxi squad, including Mory Bamba, Jordan Clark and Sam Womack III.

title: 4 Studs & 4 Duds in Jets' Week 7 Loss to Dolphins: Glenn Crumbles, Cooper Shines & More From Sunday
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — Just when you think the Jets season couldn't get any lower, they find a way to hit rock bottom.
On Sunday, rock bottom was found, and there may not be an opportunity to get back up in the future.
The Jets were desperate for a win against their AFC East rival Dolphins . Instead, the 0-5 Dolphins came away with a shocking 28-25 victory within the confines of MetLife Stadium, dropping the Jets to 2-5.
Perhaps it was a bad omen of things to come when the Dolphins offense came out firing with a seven-play touchdown drive to open the game. They scored on three of their first four offensive drives of the game, including one at the end of the first half that ate up over seven minutes of game action to take a 21-7 lead going into the break.
The Jets made it a game in the second half, cutting the deficit to four going into the final quarter. But a 63-yard touchdown pass, coupled with a clutch fourth-down conversion late in the contest, sealed the team's fate.
As always, there's plenty of studs and duds to look through after a loss like that. Let's go through those now.
Few things actually looked good for the Jets on Sunday. One of their bright spots came from second-year tight end Mason Taylor. The LSU product outjumped an opposing corner in the first quarter to muscle his way for a 13-yard touchdown (h/t NFL).
It's National Tight Ends Day and Mason Taylor is joining the party MIAvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/F72SqDOTVz
It was the kind of play that highlighted the effectiveness of Taylor—someone who can make plays in the receiving end while also using his abilities as a blocker to make a positive impact. He made almost the exact same play late in the game to cut the deficit to three.
In total, Taylor finished with five catches, 62 yards receiving and two scores. It was his first two-touchdown game of his career.
Taylor is a good player. One the Jets can use in the future.
There's no sugarcoating it. This was a disaster for Jets head coach Aaron Glenn . The loss drops him to 0-8 in the AFC East. It was also a game in which he was going against a first-time head coach and a team without a win. Instead of coming out inspired, the Jets looked flat in all areas of the game.
Glenn touted his play-calling prowess during the offseason, but the Dolphins were prepared for everything he threw at them. A team that did not have a lead going into the game yet this season had a comfortable lead throughout the contest.
It's not like the team could point to player execution either. New York did not call a timeout once in the first half despite having multiple opportunities to give the ball back to their offense with a chance for last-minute points. After not calling a timeout in the first half, Glenn inexplicably called a timeout within the first five minutes of the second half to save his offense from a delay of game.
And when the team needed a stop most, the Jets gave up a 63-yard touchdown to close out the game. The loss moved the Jets and Glenn to 0-8 against AFC East opponents.
A loss like this feels more like the beginning of the end for Glenn's tenure. The team believes in him, but in a results-driven business, the Jets are simply not good with him at the helm. And it might be time to start looking elsewhere.
New York's best offensive player on Sunday, besides the work of Mason Taylor, was wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. The first-round rookie caught five passes for 115 yards and a touchdown (h/t NFL). He became the first Jets receiver with 100 yards in back-to-back games since Al Toon in 1985.
The @nyjets rookie Omar Cooper Jr. finds the end zone for the second-straight week MIAvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/TqzjdFlxY4
Much will be made about the Jets' inability to get Garrett Wilson the ball (and we'll get to that shortly), but Cooper seems to be a star in the making. One that the Jets will be able to use to great affect in their offense.
General manager Darren Mougey should be thrilled he was able to trade up for the Indiana star. He's become vital to this offense.
Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich has been around many great receivers over his playing and coaching career. Never before have we seen a staff be unable to get the football to a star receiver like this .
New York's offense targeted Wilson just three times on Sunday and watched the star catch two passes for 26 yards. After the game, Geno Smith said the Dolphins were keying on Wilson throughout the game and making sure they wouldn't beat him, but that isn't necessarily what happened either. New York simply didn't manufacture touches for him.
Whether it was the team's screen calls to Adonai Mitchell, Cooper or Allen, the Jets opted not to try to force the ball to Wilson. The fact that they seem to be the one team in the NFL that simply doesn't know how to get the ball to their best player is disheartening.
And that's before the Jets bungled many other play-calling opportunities, including needing to kick a field goal despite having a first-and-goal at the opponent's one-yard line during the game.
Reich has not been up to the task so far this season. With the amount of talent the Jets have, this is arguably one of the more disappointing staff breakdowns over the last few years.
New York has a very uncomfortable conversation to have in the near future. While star running back Breece Hall has been out with an injury, Braelon Allen has become one of the franchise's best players. On Sunday, he ran for 104 yards on 17 carries for a whopping 6.1 yards per carry average.
Allen still lacks breakaway speed and there were a couple of plays that could have been long touchdowns if he were faster, but he remains a bell cow for this offense. When Hall does return, New York will have to start splitting carries between the two RBs . There's simply no feasible reason they can take Allen off the field anymore.
Sunday was a disaster for the Jets organization. One group was worse than any other, though, and that was the team's defense. New York gave up 28 points to a Dolphins team that had one of the worst offenses in football. They couldn't stop the run, gave up back-breaking penalties and missed key tackles as well.
Going into Sunday, the Dolphins were the only team that had played without a lead for the first six games of the season. They led for a majority of the game against the Jets, recorded over five yards per play, and controlled the ball for nearly 35 minutes.
Worst of all was the run defense. New York has given up 304 combined rushing yards in the last two weeks. It may get worse with the Chiefs and Bills waiting on Gang Green's schedule.
This group has to play a lot better going forward.
New York struggled to get any consistent pressure on Malik Willis on Sunday. While David Bailey and Kingsley Enagbare shared a sack, it was Nate Lynn, a free-agent pickup during the preseason , who made the most of his chance to make an impact.
Lynn recorded his first sack of the season on a key third down in the second half to give the Jets a chance to take the lead late. New York may have squandered that opportunity, but Lynn is a player who clearly needs to be a part of the defensive line rotation going forward.
The numbers show an efficient and successful day for Geno Smith and the Jets offense.
Smith ended the game with 23-for-30 passing, 287 yards and three touchdowns to go along with a first-quarter interception, implying Smith was perfectly fine on Sunday.
The tape will tell a different story.
Reich gets blamed for not getting Wilson the ball, but Sunday had more to do with Smith not targeting him than the actual play calls. Throughout Sunday, Wilson was running open over the middle of the field on several routes. For whatever reason, Smith didn't throw the ball. He also held onto the ball too long and seemed happier to check the ball down rather than get it to an open target.
Simply put, while the numbers showed he had a good game, the tape…

title: 3 Matchups That Will Decide Jets’ Week 7 Game Against Dolphins
full_text:
After coming up short in a game where they had every opportunity to win against the Patriots , the Jets will look to bounce back in Week 7's matchup versus the Dolphins.
New York hasn't had much success against Miami in recent years, going 2-8 since 2020. However, the Dolphins hit the reset button this offseason and are in the midst of a major rebuild, going winless in their first five games.
Although the matchup appears favorable for the Jets, this won’t be a cakewalk . The hardest games to win are the division ones, and so far, New York is 0-7 against the AFC East in the Aaron Glenn era.
But if Gang Green can prioritize winning these three matchups, they’ll come away with a win against the Dolphins.
De’Von Achane was one of the few talented players the Dolphins retained after undergoing a major offseason overhaul. With much of the roster gutted, the former 2023 third-round selection was expected to lead Miami’s offense after combining for over 1,800 scrimmage yards and earning a Pro Bowl selection.
However, those plans took a major hit when Achane suffered a torn ACL in Week 3, forcing the Dolphins to turn to second-year running back Ollie Gordon II to help fill the void. Over the last three games, Gordon has rushed for 229 yards, averaging 5.2 yards per carry and has scored a touchdown in each contest.
With Gordon stepping up in Achane’s absence and emerging as a key contributor to Miami’s offense, the Jets must prioritize limiting him. However, this will be a challenge for New York.
Despite shutting down the run in their first two games, giving up just 131 yards, Gang Green’s run defense has struggled mightily over the past four weeks, allowing 607 rushing yards. During this time, the Jets have gone 1-3, and in all three of their losses, the defense gave up over 100 rushing yards.
Meanwhile, New York’s lone win came when it held the Browns to just 94 rushing yards.
With the Dolphins lacking a functional passing attack, ranking 31st in passing yards per game (153.6), the Jets’ defense must focus on containing Gordon.
While the emphasis should be on clogging the gaps and maintaining outside leverage, New York’s defense should prioritize getting to and tackling Gordon early. He shares a similar play style to Braelon Allen, with both being physical, big-bodied runners who are hard to take down.
Like Allen, Gordon makes defenses pay for not tackling him early, as he’s had eight explosive rushes of 10 yards or more in the last three games. If the Jets can prevent him from breaking tackles and turning short gains into explosive plays, they can force Miami to rely more heavily on its struggling passing game.
That will be critical to slowing the Dolphins’ offense and giving New York a chance to come away with a win.
The Jets’ offensive game plan against the Dolphins should be simple: throw the ball to No. 5.
Garrett Wilson has been New York’s most productive receiver by a mile, leading the team in catches (35), receiving yards (418), and touchdowns (three). Trailing him is rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq, who’s hauled in 15 receptions for 158 yards and a touchdown.
When the Jets feed Wilson, they improve their chances of winning , according to NFL Next Gen Stats . When Wilson’s target share is over 29%, New York is 2-1, but when it’s below that mark, they are 0-3.
In New York’s two wins, Wilson averages 93 yards, whereas in the losses he averages 58.8.
With Gang Green’s offense going three straight games without scoring more than 20 points, offensive coordinator Frank Reich must prioritize getting the ball in Wilson’s hands early and often, especially against Miami’s weak pass defense.
The Dolphins rank 14th in passing yards allowed per game (219.2); however, they are tied for 23rd in passing touchdowns allowed (11) and rank 27th in yards gained per pass attempt (7.8).
Reich must optimize Wilson’s dynamic playmaking as he did against Cleveland. On the first drive, Wilson registered three catches (four targets) for 70 yards, ending the drive with a 32-yard touchdown.
Part of that success was Reich deploying Wilson all over the field, creating different looks and opportunities for the star receiver to make plays. That versatility should be a priority in this matchup, particularly by moving Wilson in the slot more frequently. In both of his 100-yard games, Wilson has logged double-digit snaps from the slot.
Moving him around to create favorable matchups and opportunities to make plays with the ball should be the primary focus against the Dolphins, especially because they don’t have a corner capable of containing Wilson.
One area the Jets’ defense has improved in is generating pressure. Gang Green’s pass rush posted the second-fewest sacks (26) last season. This season, meanwhile, the unit is tied for fifth with 17 sacks.
As the head coach and defensive play-caller, Glenn, along with the team’s new additions, particularly No. 2 overall pick David Bailey, deserve credit for the team’s turnaround. With Glenn’s aggressive play-calling, New York ranks fifth in blitz rate (36%) and 10th in pressure rate (24.3%), consistently putting opposing quarterbacks under duress.
Bailey has played a significant part in this , leading the team in pressures (23) and sacks (5). The rookie edge rusher from Texas Tech had his breakout game in Week 5 against Cleveland, sacking quarterback Deshaun Watson three times and finishing with nine total pressures.
Against the Dolphins, however, Glenn must dial the blitzes down against quarterback Malik Willis. The former Titans and Packers quarterback has struggled this season, but his numbers have been poor when defenses don’t blitz.
When teams send pressure, he’s completed just 55.6% of his passes for a touchdown, posting an 84.3 passer rating. Against no blitz, Willis has completed 56.5% of his passes for a touchdown, throwing four interceptions and posting a 60 passer rating.
Willis’s struggles against four-man pressure are partially due to Miami’s difficulties creating separation. Besides Malik Washington, the Dolphins’ pass catchers have struggled to consistently get open. As a result, Willis has held the ball too long while trying to find an open receiver. Other times, he scrambles out of the pocket trying to make a play, only to be brought down before he can get back to the line of scrimmage.
Willis rarely throws the ball away, but to his credit, that stems from the team always being down and him trying to make a play. Although Miami’s offensive line deserves some of the blame, it isn’t responsible for all the sacks. Over five games, the unit has given up seven sacks, while the other seven come from Willis’ own wrongdoing.
While Glenn shouldn’t hesitate to blitz Willis, he should primarily focus on generating pressure with four pass rushers. This allows more defenders to drop into coverage and limit downfield opportunities.
With the Dolphins’ receiving corps unable to create separation, Willis could be forced to take shots, especially when they’re trailing. This could give New York’s secondary opportunities to come away with interceptions.
Glenn should save his creative blitzes for obvious passing situations, particularly third-and-long, when he can disguise them more effectively. Rushing four also allows the Jets to focus on containing Willis in the pocket and limiting his ability to hurt them with his legs. He already has 186 yards and two touchdowns on the ground this season.
Keeping Willis in the pocket and forcing him to make plays with his arm instead of his legs will be one of the critical keys to a win.

title: 3 Pending Jets Free Agents Already Deserving of Contract Extensions
full_text:
The Jets may only be 2-4 in Week 7, but there is still plenty of talent on the roster to feel good about for the future .
While much of that talent is on rookie contracts, some veteran Jets are scheduled to hit free agency at the end of the season. The Jets will need to decide whether they want to extend those players before that happens, or if they are content with letting them walk.
If New York is smart, three names in particular will be extended by general manager Darren Mougey over the course of the next few months. Let's go through them now.
The first one is easy. Dane Belton has been one of the better free-agent signings the Jets have enjoyed over the last several seasons. Since coming from the Giants, Belton has been graded as a top-20 safety in the league by Pro Football Focus (74.2, 17th) while fitting many different roles.
"How impressed I was that (Dane) can come in and he can play basically the same role that Minkah (Fitzpatrick) had of being able to play the big nickel, playing safety," Glenn said in September. "He’s an impressive player. Intelligent, smart, and he can take up that slack.”
Belton's versatility is something that the Jets cannot let walk in free agency.
The 2026 season has not been a very good year for Harrison Phillips. The aging defensive tackle is ranked as the 103rd-best defensive lineman in the league this year by PFF . For reference, that number is out of 129 players.
Phillips's biggest issue is a lack of pass rush that has crippled the Jets' defense for a majority of the year. At 30 years old, it's fair to wonder whether Phillips can get back to his quality starter days of past years.
Despite the struggles, he's still worth an extension for next year and beyond.
The Jets need bodies along the interior of their defensive line, and Phillips is a locker room leader. It's hard to move off captains who say the right things and keep everyone else in line. He may not get the kind of long-term deal many tackles hope for, but it's still a smart move for the Jets to bring Phillips back.
New York is going to draft a quarterback in 2027 . Armed with three first-round picks, it's more likely the Jets will try to pair a young quarterback with another top playmaker as well.
But the Jets still need Geno Smith. The veteran signal-caller has been quite solid this year , completing 69% of his passes with seven touchdowns and just one interception to boot. He's been everything the team could have hoped for and more this year.
It would be in the Jets' best interest to bring Smith back on an extension and use him as a veteran presence for the incoming rookie. Instead of throwing an inexperienced player at quarterback to begin the year, they could bring Smith back and allow the incoming rookie QB to develop at his own pace.
Not only would it keep a viable starting quarterback on the field for the team, but it would also give Gang Green a quality bridge to their future franchise quarterback. Smith won't cost as much as other starting quarterbacks in the league, but his presence will be just as important going into next year.
It's worth bringing Smith back for another year or two.

title: Jets Have Obvious Offensive Change to Make to Unlock Unit's Full Potential
full_text:
Elite offenses in the NFL can adapt to the personnel they have. In 2024, the Eagles opted to become a run-first team and ended up winning the Super Bowl in the same year.
The following season, the Seahawks focused all their efforts on getting the ball to their top receiver—Jaxon Smith-Njigba—en route to a Super Bowl win. Other organizations like the 49ers and Rams have found sustained success by altering their game plan to fit the players they have.
So why haven't the Jets done that yet?
In the last three games, Gang Green has enjoyed a run-first philosophy that has brought some semblance of success. Braelon Allen has recorded 253 yards on over 4.5 yards per carry .
New York's records in those games? 1-2. The offense has failed to score more than 20 points in each game as well.
If the Jets want to find success for the remainder of the year, they will need to transition from their run-first goals into a more spread-out unit—one that is willing to shred opposing defenses through the air. The Jets have the talent to do so.
Now it's time for the coaching staff to let it go.
Since he was first hired to the team, head coach Aaron Glenn has always wanted to build an offense that was predicated on running the ball. Through his first year and a half with the team, that mindset simply has not turned into wins.
Instead of committing to the run game in a losing effort, the Jets must adapt by passing the ball.
Glenn confirmed to reporters Friday morning that wide receiver AD Mitchell would play in Sunday's Week 7 contest against the Dolphins . He joins a receiving room with Garrett Wilson, Omar Cooper Jr., Kenyon Sadiq, and Mason Taylor, all of whom found past success.
New York's passing unit has all the talent in the world to get the job done now with their final piece healthy and ready to play. As such, Glenn must put his money where his mouth is.
Unlike in the past, the Jets actually have a quarterback who can spread the ball around.
Geno Smith has enjoyed a bounce-back season of sorts, completing 69% of his passes for over 1,300 yards and seven touchdowns. Because of Smith's strong start to the season, the Jets need to rely on him even more.
In last week's game against the Patriots, Smith threw the ball 30 times compared to 27 run plays called. This season, New York is close to a 50-50 run vs. pass call discrepancy, but that isn't conducive to what the roster has at its disposal, though.
If the Jets want to beat the Dolphins on Sunday and rack up wins down the road, they need to become a pass-first team. That's what their roster is best suited for, and boasting enough talent to put opposing defenses in a difficult spot.

title: 2 Winners & 1 Loser for Jets With Adonai Mitchell Officially Returning From Injury
full_text:
Coming off another divisional loss to the Patriots last Sunday, the Jets prepare for the first of back-to-back home games as the winless Dolphins come to town for a Week 7 clash at MetLife Stadium.
While this should be an opportunity for the Jets to get right and for head coach Aaron Glenn to correct some issues with his seat only getting hotter , getting healthy and not beating themselves will be key to avoiding the upset on Sunday.
The execution will have to wait until the game kicks off, but some positive news is already on the way in the form of Adonai Mitchell. Although ESPN 's Rich Cimini confirmed on Friday that running back Breece Hall "will be limited in practice and will be listed as questionable, per Glenn," Mitchell was a full participant in practice and "will play Sunday" after missing four games with a finger injury.
Breece Hall will be limited in practice today and will be listed as questionable, per Glenn. AD Mitchell is full practice and will play Sunday. He missed four games with a finger injury. #Jets
With rookie WR Omar Cooper Jr. having already returned from a high ankle sprain one week earlier, the top-three Jets wideouts will finally be on the field together for the first time since Week 1.
With that in mind, his upcoming return isn't good news for everyone. Here are two winners and one loser as Mitchell finally makes his return to the field this weekend.
One of Geno Smith's biggest weaknesses in his career has been turnovers, but he has made huge strides in that area in his return to Gotham. The veteran has thrown at least one touchdown in each of the last five games and only one interception, which took place in the Week 6 loss to the Patriots when the Jets had just got past midfield trailing by 10 in the fourth quarter.
Smith is averaging 7.5 yards per attempt and has not played poorly, but a 21st-ranked QBR (53.8) and lack of success in the red zone has been concerning. He's only 10-of-16 for 49 yards and two TDs from inside the 20, but his 2.9 yards per attempt speaks more to the coaching staff's reluctance to turn him loose and let him cook when points are within reach .
A lot of that has been without all three of his starting wideouts on the field, though.
Cooper, Mitchell and Garrett Wilson have only been on the field together for four Week 1 snaps, so the weapons have been lacking in the passing game. Now that all three of them will be at Smith's disposal against the Dolphins' 24th-ranked passing defense (26.4 ppg) and one that has also allowed the sixth-most yards per reception (7.8) this season.
Assuming he can have the time to throw, which has become an issue with the offensive line giving up at least three sacks in five of the six games, Smith could be poised for success against Miami as some more favorable matchups could present themselves with the top-three wideouts taking the field together.
With so many injuries taking place in the early going, the Jets had some holes to fill to account for those absences. One player who seemed to be in prime position to benefit was Isaiah Williams, who has primarily been a return specialist in his career.
Despite the rash of injuries, Williams has not done anything to help his case moving forward.
Williams received season-highs in targets (six) and receptions (six) in the Week 2 overtime loss to the Packers, but he also fumbled twice in that game and failed to deliver on the looks that were coming his way. Aside from that game, he has had no more than two catches in a single game this season after entering the season with high expectations as someone who was viewed as the "heartbeat" of the offense .
Granted, Williams did haul in two catches for a season-high 73 yards in the Week 4 loss to the Bears, including a 58-yard TD reception in the fourth quarter (h/t NFL) that really gave the Jets their only spark of the game when the offensive was relatively nonexistent.
Isaiah Williams 58-yard TD! NYJvsCHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/TRgGogeLyP
Williams is easily the biggest loser since he failed to capitalize on Mitchell's absence and is now looking at an even smaller role with the WR room healthier than ever.
Back to players who could benefit from Mitchell's return, look no further than the WR1.
While he has the ninth-most receptions (35) and 14th-most receptions (418), Garrett Wilson was only targeted twice in the first three quarters against the Patriots and has hardly been the focal point of Gang Green's game plan under offensive coordinator Frank Reich .
With Cooper coming off a sensational return after recording six catches for 103 yards and a TD, Wilson was already in position to be the Jets' biggest winner assuming Cooper's breakout carries over. If the rookie can continue to show that he is capable of going off for 100 yards on any given week, that alone would force opposing defenses to pay closer attention to him and take some of the attention off Wilson.
When you now include Mitchell in the mix, there is every reason to believe that Wilson could be a huge beneficiary. After all, the third-year WR has put up at least 60 yards in both games he has appeared in this season and has averaged 13.7 yards per reception. He has still not truly had a breakout performance since his eight-catch, 102-yard showing vs. the Falcons in Week 13 last season, but his availability should attract some additional attention and free up Wilson even more.
Keep in mind, Wilson has 39 catches for 436 yards and two TDs in seven all-time meetings against the Dolphins, so he is no stranger to having success against them. His frustration could eventually boil over if the Jets don't walk a fine line with his targets, but there is no doubt he is one of the biggest winners to emerge with Mitchell returning to the lineup.

title: Isaiah Davis's Jets Future on the Line With Breece Hall Officially Questionable vs. Dolphins
full_text:
Even though Isaiah Davis didn't enter the 2026 NFL season with high expectations, it's safe to say that his start to the campaign has been a disappointment. The former 2024 fifth-round pick went from rarely being used early in the season to being unproductive when he finally got the ball in his hands last week, leaving his future in the Jets' lineup up in the air, to say the least.
Davis has been operating as the Jets' RB2 behind Braelon Allen during Breece Hall's absence, but it's safe to say that he could be bumped down the pecking order soon. Hall has been back at practice this week (albeit in a limited fashion) as he battles back from a quadriceps injury, and even though he's still questionable, head coach Aaron Glenn left the door open for New York's RB1 to play in Week 7 (h/t SNY Jets ).
"We'll take it all the way to Sunday and see how (Breece) feels," Glenn told reporters on Friday.
AD Mitchell is a full go and will play on Sunday Breece Hall will practice again today and the Jets will "take it all the way to Sunday to see how he feels" pic.twitter.com/fU5qQaTFc0
Whether or not Hall plays against the Dolphins, one thing is clear: Davis is running out of time to soldify his role in the Jets' backfield. If he can't find a way to showcase his value on Sunday afternoon, it might be time for Glenn and general manager Darren Mougey to think about turning the page.
After four touchless appearances to begin the season, the Jets finally trusted Davis with nine carries between Weeks 5 and 6.
Unfortunately, he was anything but productive, averaging just 2.7 yards per attempt—a significant drop-off from the 5.6 yards he averaged in his first two seasons with Gang Green. Allen has thrived as the lead rusher in Hall's absence, amassing 253 rushing yards and a touchdown on 55 carries in his last three starts. It would be foolish not to continue using him even when Hall returns, adding to the uphill battle ahead of Davis.
Although Davis's 19 receiving yards on two catches aren't abysmal, the pass-catching opportunities out of the backfield will be sparse (or even nonexistent) once Hall returns and takes back the bulk of them. After all, Hall is averaging 4.4 targets per game in his career, and his 10 targets this season are almost as many as Davis and Allen have combined (16) despite not having played since Week 3.
It's pretty clear Davis is in danger of being on the outside looking in, underscoring the importance of maximizing his opportunities against the Dolphins this weekend. He could have a decent chance to do so, given that Miami allows the 17th-most rushing yards on the fourth-most rushing attempts per game this season.
No matter who's on the field this weekend, it's crucial for Davis to show the Jets the best that he has to offer. The South Dakota State product will be heading to free agency in less than two years, and given his limited role, he needs to make the most of every touch he gets to show New York that he needs to be part of its long-term plans.
If Davis continues to disappoint, though, it might be time for the Jets to consider replacement options.
For example, Kene Nwangwu has played exclusively on special teams this season, but the Jets could consider throwing a few carries his way if Davis's struggles persist. His stats weren't eye-popping, but Nwangwu did have 49 rushing yards and two first downs on 13 carries for New York last season.
There's also undrafted rookie RB Al-Jay Henderson on the practice squad . The 23-year-old runner hasn't been elevated from the taxi squad yet, but he is an interesting option after recording 1,833 rushing yards on 386 carries, 419 receiving yards on 44 catches and 17 total TDs in his last two seasons at the University of Buffalo.
Outside help is also an option as the 2026 NFL trade deadline looms on Tuesday, Nov. 10. They likely won't be chasing a big name like Colts RB Jonathan Taylor, but more realistic-yet-effective targets like the Buccaneers' Kenneth Gainwell or the Titans' Tyjae Spears could be on the table. That's without even mentioning how more targets could become available over the next two weeks.
At the end of the day, the Jets have multiple options—both internal and external—if Davis's inefficiency continues. Sunday's matchup against the Dolphins might be his last chance to prove his worth, and if he can't step up then, there might not be much runway left for Davis in Gotham.

title: Frank Reich's Latest Comments Amplify Concerns About Jets' Biggest Offensive Issue
full_text:
Spoiler alert: Garrett Wilson is an excellent receiver and the Jets' best offensive player .
Just make sure Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich is aware.
New York's play-caller has watched his offense stay stagnant across the board despite an increase in talent at his disposal. Geno Smith is a quality quarterback, and there are several quality pieces around him to make the unit just as respectable as any other in the NFL.
Despite all the talent, the Jets rank 23rd in passing and 27th in points scored.
Part of the disconnect has been New York's inconsistencies, stemming from Wilson's lack of targets .
But don't worry, Reich made it clear on Thursday that getting the ball to his best player is always in the back of his head... when someone else brings it up.
In the Jets' 26-19 loss to the Patriots, Gang Green threw Wilson six of the team's 30 passes. For a roster in need of points, you would think they would target their star significantly more than anyone else.
Never fear, though. Reich spoke to reporters on Thursday, saying that he's always reminded of that... by head coach Aaron Glenn.
It's good for a head coach and offensive coordinator to be in lockstep, as Glenn and Reich are. But it should not take Glenn's comments to remind Reich how important it is to get Wilson the ball . It isn't quite a coincidence that the Jets' three best offensive games of the year saw Wilson as the unit's top target man.
Wilson helps stabilize the unit and gets them going early.
An offensive coordinator not understanding that—or not focusing the game plan specifically on that—is one that seems focused on trying to outsmart the opposition rather than actually scoring points. In the modern NFL, those play-callers seldom find success.
So it shouldn't surprise everyone that the Jets are 2-4 with their offense failing to put up 20 points in each of their last three games.
The good news is that Reich's game plan hasn't been too much of a hindrance to Wilson's mindset. While many star receivers can be outspoken and "diva-like," he's remained committed to the Jets, even during the offensive unit's recent struggles .
“You have that confidence to be productive when you’re called upon again, and then just kind of showing, reminding everyone that this is why I’m at this point,” Wilson said. “And it sounds stupid because it’s like a reminder, but everyone is good, obviously, at this point, but it’s real now. Your teammates feel that, your coaches feel that, and they think they can call upon you again.
Eventually, though, Wilson's patience needs to be rewarded. And that falls on Reich to accomplish.
It's time for the Jets' play-caller to step up and stop trying to outsmart the competition. All Reich has to do is get the ball to the team's best player. Good things tend to happen when that goal is accomplished.

title: Confidence Meter: How Close I Feel the Jets Are to Firing Aaron Glenn in Week 7
full_text:
The Jets were historically bad in 2025, finishing 3-14 and becoming the first team in NFL history to finish a season without recording a single interception. Despite this, New York opted to give head coach Aaron Glenn another year.
New York didn’t let him off the hook easily. By replacing 12 of his 22 assistants from last year’s staff and making roster additions across the board, it’s evident that the Jets’ brass wants to see improvement under Glenn.
Improvement was Glenn’s goal entering his second season , and so far, New York has made some progress.
Through six weeks, Gang Green currently sits in third place in the AFC East with a 2-4 record. The Jets have been far more competitive than last season, with all but one of their losses having been tightly contested, and the defense has shown improvement.
However, some issues remain, with poor coaching decisions and trouble executing in the final two minutes of the first half among the most concerning.
Although the team doesn’t look as bad as it did last year, Glenn must fix these issues if he wants to remain the head coach. Here's how I'm feeling about the Jets head coach's outlook and whether a potential firing is on the horizon.
One of the biggest changes from last year is that Glenn has taken over defensive play-calling duties. So far, the decision has appeared to pay off.
Under Glenn’s aggressive approach, the defense has significantly improved at generating pressure, tying for fifth in sacks (17) and ranking 10th in pressure rating (24.3%). Additionally, the Jets have impressed against the pass, ranking fourth in passing yards allowed per game (185) and 11th in air yards allowed (662).
New additions David Bailey and Dane Belton have been key contributors to the unit’s success.
Bailey has been New York’s most consistent pass rusher, leading the team in pressures (23) and sacks (5). Meanwhile, Belton continues to make plays all over the field and has stood out against the run, earning an 89.7 run-defense grade , per Pro Football Focus, ranking third among 98 qualifying safeties.
Glenn’s defensive improvements have kept the Jets in games. Through six games, the defense ranks seventh in points allowed per game (20.7) and has given up more than 30 points only once. Last year, New York allowed 30 points or more three times in its first six games and eight times in the season.
The defense’s success has played a critical role in New York’s two victories, allowing just 10 points to the Titans and 12 to the Browns.
While the Jets still have plenty of issues to address, the defense’s progress is an encouraging sign for Glenn in his second season. Although they need to do a better job of creating turnovers and containing the run, the unit has taken a step forward.
If Glenn wants to remain in New York, he needs the defense to maintain a similar level of play moving forward.
For the most part, Glenn has done well on the defensive side. Still, he’s made several questionable decisions, which have arguably cost the Jets a win or two.
In last week’s game against the Patriots, Glenn opted to go for it on fourth down twice instead of kicking from 48 and 57 yards. It’s one thing to be aggressive later on when the game is getting out of hand and nothing is working, but passing up potential points in the second quarter while trailing by a touchdown is another story.
It didn’t help that offensive coordinator Frank Reich— who's also drawn criticism this year —dialed up a run in shotgun formation on fourth-and-one and a quarterback sneak.
Another questionable decision by Glenn in this game came on New England’s 42-yard touchdown pass to receiver Romeo Doubs (h/t NFL). On the play, Glenn rushed just three players and dropped David Bailey into coverage.
42-yard touchdown from Maye to Doubs! NYJvsNE on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/tKpDzX136o
This gave Patriots quarterback Drake Maye seemingly all the time in the world to find the open Doubs, punishing Glenn for the terrible call.
Glenn’s game management hasn’t been much better either. The Jets’ inability to execute in the final two minutes of the first half has been one of the team’s biggest weaknesses since Glenn’s arrival.
Through six games this season, New York has been outscored 20-0 in this situation. The problem extends beyond this season, as this has been a recurring problem since Glenn joined. In his 23 games as head coach, the Jets have been outscored 100-6 in the first half's final two minutes (h/t ESPN 's Rich Cimini).
To break this down further, they’ve been outscored in the final two minutes of the first half, 100-6, over Glenn’s 23 games. Next closest team: Packers, -40 pt differential. https://t.co/GTMDrAvwAD
Whether it’s clock management, play-calling, or execution, the Jets struggle in moments where every possession matters. Finding ways to score in these situations has to be a priority moving forward, especially given how close their games have been.
The other major concern is that the offense hasn’t improved under Reich. New York brought in the former head coach of the Colts and Panthers, hoping that his experience would help turn things around on offense. However, he’s been extremely underwhelming.
The Jets have scored just 112 points this season, fewer than the 123 they scored through their first six games in 2025. Given all the additions and changes to the coaching staff and roster, their lack of progress on offense has been disappointing.
Reich has failed to use Garrett Wilson consistently , targeting him heavily in some games while turning away from him in others. Wilson has had more than seven targets in just two games and must find a way to get the ball to their star receiver more often, especially in the red zone.
Through six games, New York ranks last in red zone touchdown efficiency (37.5%).
While Reich deserves his share of the blame, Glenn deserves scrutiny for the offense’s continued struggles as well. As head coach, he is responsible for holding his coordinators accountable and ensuring the team improves in its weakest areas. Glenn’s continued public support of Reich raises questions about whether the coaching staff is doing enough to address the offense’s problems.
Despite the Jets’ struggles, I don’t believe Glenn is on the verge of being fired. Even if the numbers don’t back up the offense, the team has improved from a talent and execution standpoint and is significantly more competitive than last season.
However, I do believe Glenn’s seat is undoubtedly getting warmer. With the offense continuing to underperform, it’s held them back and cost them some games. Just look back at their Week 2 loss against the Packers.
After taking a 10-point lead, the Jets managed just one first down before punting. They later failed to convert on fourth-and-1 near midfield. After taking two sacks in overtime, they punted, allowing Green Bay to drive down the field for the game-winning field goal.
Even as the team continues to make mistakes, Glenn remains confident in the team’s direction, comparing the Jets’ competitive stamina to the 2022 Lions, who started 1-6 before finishing 9-8. While this comparison offers some optimism, New York must turn its competitiveness into wins.
That’s why this week’s upcoming matchup against the Dolphins could be an important test. It’s a game they should win against an inferior team, but a loss would add to the mounting pressure on Glenn and his coaching staff.
I don’t believe Jets owner Woody Johnson and the Jets’ brass would move on from Glenn mid-season. However, if the team doesn’t progress and poor coaching decisions continue, his long-term future in New York will become increasingly uncertain.
For now, Glenn’s seat is warm, but there’s still plenty of football left for him to turn things around—or make his situation worse.

title: 3 Pending Eagles Free Agents Already Deserve Contract Extensions
full_text:
With a 2-4 record in Week 7, it isn't too early to start thinking about the future in Philadelphia. After all, the Eagles have a plethora of players heading to free agency over the offseason, with Spotrac listing 22 pending unrestricted free agents .
Many of those players won't be back in Philadelphia. That's just the way the business of the NFL works. Roster turnover is inevitable. However, a few upcoming UFAs have shown Eagles general manager Howie Roseman that they're worth bringing back based on what we've seen early this season.
Moro Ojomo is currently playing in the final year of the four-year rookie contract that he signed in 2023, and he's a guy that the Eagles should certainly consider bringing back.
Over the course of his current contract, Ojomo has developed into a key contributor for Philadelphia, even though he's often overshadowed on the line by star defensive tackles Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis. He has appeared in 40 straight games for the Eagles over the last three seasons and he's tallied 20 quarterback hits, eight tackles for a loss and six sacks during that span. He's a reliable rotation piece who can come and provide support on the D-Line without the production of the unit falling off.
That's valuable for a team to have.
But just because the Eagles should try to retain Ojomo doesn't mean they will be able to. The Eagles already have a ton of money tied up in the defensive line between Carter and Davis, and they have a bunch of other areas that they'll also need to address. So, there's a possibility that keeping Ojomo won't be financially feasible for Philly. The Texas product will assuredly have other suitors in free agency.
It's a new era for the offensive line in Philadelphia. Mainstays Lane Johnson (retired) and Cam Jurgens ( traded to the Ravens ) are gone, and Landon Dickerson seems unsure about his own future in Philly. So the Eagles need to start building for the future on the line, and retaining a guy who has started in 26 games for them and showed a lot of promise would be a good start.
Tyler Steen moved into a starting spot with the Eagles last season after receiving limited opportunities during his first two years. He's been solid in the role and has posted respectable Pro Football Focus grades , despite struggles elsewhere on the line.
At just 26, Steen should have plenty of productive play ahead of him, and it would be good if he could do so in an Eagles uniform.
Veteran offensive tackle Fred Johnson signed a one-year, relatively cheap deal with the Eagles in free agency in March, and the Eagles could potentially look to sign him to another such deal in free agency next offseason to retain inexpensive, experienced depth on the offensive line.
Johnson has only played 14 offensive snaps so far this season, but he played nearly 60% of snaps last season and over 40% when the Eagles won the Super Bowl two years ago. He isn't exciting and doesn't necessarily offer much upside, but he does offer a decent depth piece at good value. Every team needs guys like those.
The Eagles will assuredly address the offensive line in the 2027 NFL Draft, but a few returning faces wouldn't hurt.

title: 'Players Over Plays:' Nick Sirianni Hinting at a Return to Roots Is Already Benefiting One Eagle
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — The much-ballyhooed shift to a Shanahan/McVay-like offensive scheme has been a dud early in the 2026 season for the Eagles.
And there are subtle hints that head coach Nick Sirianni is about to rewind to his broader philosophy of “players over plays.”
The lip service toward offensive coordinator Sean Mannion’s watered-down version of the hybrid West Coast philosophy now claims some kind of all-inclusive adaptability.
Quarterback Tanner McKee— in for the sidelined Jalen Hurts —said the team’s offensive system aligns with his skill set because of that “adaptability," something that in theory allows coaches to adjust week to week without being locked into one approach.
“I think there’s a lot of different ways that this offense could be run,” McKee said. “I’ve said it before, it’s really wordy. Sean wants to be able to have the freedom to change different things in the game, week to week, whatever it is. And so he’s not trapped into one way of calling plays, running the offense, whatever it is. And so that’s freeing as a player.”
McKee emphasized that the freedom places added responsibility on the players.
Sirianni has described a similar philosophy of balancing a foundational system with in-season adjustments tailored to available personnel and opposing defenses.
“Your job is to go out and to try to win every game the best way that you can,” Sirianni said. “Yes, you want to have a system in place to be the bones of your operation, but while also understanding that you want to attack the defense of what they’re playing and with the strengths of your players,” Sirianni said. “That’s always a fine line. We know we have good players that can execute a lot of different things, but ultimately, it always is players over plays.
“It will always be players over plays.”
Sirianni added that the core values of a program have to be a constant; in his case, that’s the “tough, detailed, together” mindset that the Eagles have adopted.
Everything else—schemes, schedules, and practices—can change.
“We’ve adjusted some things because we’re doing everything we can on our end to be able to go out there and be successful,” said Sirianni.
McKee noted that each week the Eagles' offense targets defensive weaknesses alongside the strengths of the current personnel and the plays the unit has practiced most.
“Each week you attack defenses in a different way. Each week you attack, obviously, the weaknesses of the defense of that week, but also the strengths of the offense,” he said. “What guys are available, what plays do we like, what plays do we run well, what plays do we have a lot of reps on. That was one thing that me and Jalen talked a ton about."
Reviewing tape from his Week 6 start in a loss to the Panthers , McKee identified areas of focus that fit the need for precision within a variable system.
“Communication needs to be at a premium, especially at the quarterback position. I think when anybody is not on the same page, doesn’t know what to do, I feel like there’s always part of that goes on the quarterback,” the Stanford product said. “And then I think settling down a little bit, a little bit quicker. I think I got quick with my feet a couple times at the beginning of the game, trying to get the ball out, being a little rushed. And so I think just trusting my footwork, trusting my reads, getting through progressions, will ultimately benefit me.”
McKee also stressed better efficiency, particularly under center and against the blitz, and his part in that.
“I think efficiency. Efficiency and being on the same page. Staying on schedule,” McKee said when discussing needed improvements. “There are times if it’s a bad play, don’t make a bad play worse. Obviously, taking care of the ball. Sometimes as a quarterback, the best play is to throw the ball away and not take a sack.
“As a quarterback, I think you have to have some damage control. There are plays that, you know, sometimes the defense just gets you. … And so, as a quarterback, you have to be able to diagnose that, have some damage control, and live to see the next down.”

title: Hollywood Brown's Eagles Future Could Be Clear After Week 7 MNF vs. Cowboys
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — Things haven’t worked out the way Hollywood Brown expected when he signed a one-year deal with $5 million in guaranteed money from the Eagles back in the spring.
During the team’s disappointing 2-4 start, the 29-year-old veteran has been buried on the depth chart behind starters DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, as well as first-round pick Makai Lemon and second-year upstart Darius Cooper.
With the NFL trade deadline approaching on Tuesday, Nov. 10 , Brown has been a popular name on the rumor circuit among the league’s national “insiders” as a potential trade candidate. It makes sense: Smith and Wicks are entrenched as the foundation of the Eagles' wide receiver room, the organization is clearly invested in Lemon, and Cooper appears to have played his way out of the undrafted label and into the team’s plans.
Brown, however, is expected to finally get a meaningful opportunity against the Cowboys on Monday night , with Smith (hamstring) and Wicks (ankle) ruled out due to injury. The Eagles will lean on Lemon, Cooper, Brown, and Elijah Moore in an offense that has used 11 personnel the majority of the time, meaning all four should see significant snaps in prime time.
Speaking at his locker on Friday, Brown—who has played in just one game and logged only 17 offensive snaps—admitted he expected a larger role but has remained a true professional, refusing to dwell on the lack of playing time.
“Yeah, I did [expect a larger role],” Brown said. “But I do understand. Stuff happens. I mean, you can’t take nothing personal in this business, so you kind of just got to go about your process and when that time happens, whatever happens, you just got to be ready for it.”
Some of that limited opportunity to date stemmed from an ankle injury Brown suffered in practice ahead of the Eagles’ Week 3 loss to the Rams.
A 2019 first-round pick by the Ravens out of Oklahoma, Brown acknowledged he wouldn’t have always handled the situation so well.
Over his first seven NFL seasons, the speedy wideout was once a major part of the offense in Baltimore, peaking as a 90-catch, 1,000-yard receiver in 2021. Overall, Brown has 371 receptions for 4,322 yards and 33 touchdowns—the kind of experience that seemed potentially valuable for a team that traded A.J. Brown in the offseason.
Yet Brown has yet to catch a pass in Philadelphia, though he did have two rushes for 12 yards against the Titans in Week 2 when offensive coordinator Sean Mannion tried to manufacture touches for him.
With the trade deadline nearing, Brown was asked about his future .
“I’m here right now just trying to play,” Brown said. “I mean, of course, you want to be somewhere where you play, but ultimately, at the end of the day, it’s not my plan. So, I might want to play, I might contribute, but if that’s not the plan for me, you know, I can’t dwell on it too much. You’ll be unhappy, and you’re taking that back home. I can’t take that back home to the wife and kids. I’ve got to try to stay as positive as I can.”
The frustration is real, however.
“Some days better than others,” Brown admitted. “But like I said, it’s a good group here from my teammates. If I’m frustrated, I can go talk to the coach. Everybody hears me out. So it’s not really a bad thing. It’s kind of like, we’re all dealing with something, and we’re dealing with something as a team. So I don’t want to add that extra stress.”
Eagles on SI asked head coach Nick Sirianni on Saturday how Brown had handled things behind the scenes.
“(Hollywood) is a great pro, comes to work every day, just working to get better and paying attention in meetings,” Sirianni said. “He made a catch at practice yesterday. I told him it was one of the best catches I’ve seen in routes on air, the way he adjusted to the ball. He’s highly talented and will bring some great speed to our team. But I’ve just seen the consistency from him of being the same guy every single day, regardless of the circumstances. I’m looking forward to him continuing to develop and add to this football team.”
While Brown may not be in the Eagles’ long-term plans—given the investments in others—a strong performance against the Cowboys could still earn him a meaningful opportunity elsewhere before the trade deadline.
Contending teams looking for a proven, speedy veteran receiver to bolster their offense could view Monday night’s game as a final showcase, potentially turning Brown’s limited role in Philadelphia into a late-season chance to contribute and chase a ring with a new club.

title: 3 Eagles Lineup Decisions I'd Make If I Were Nick Sirianni in Week 7
full_text:
Vibes are low in the City of Brotherly Love. Quarterback Jalen Hurts' injury and a four-game losing streak have Eagles fans questioning what's to come . Three divisional matchups and the NFL trade deadline await before Philadelphia's Week 10 bye. There's no more waiting around to right the ship.
The Eagles have a chance to get back on track when they host the Dallas Cowboys on Monday Night Football in Week 7. The NFC East rivals each enter with a 2-4 record and have split their last 10 head-to-head showdowns. Philadelphia has beaten Dallas in four straight at Lincoln Financial Field, though.
It's clear that changes need to be made if the Eagles want to compete for a division title . There have been too many three-and-outs on offense, which leads to a tired defense spending too much time on the field. With that being said, here are three lineup decisions I would make if I were Nick Sirianni.
This is a decision Sirianni has to make: whether he wants to or not. Wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) are banged up. Neither one was present at Philadelphia's final practice of the week on Saturday, and they have been officially ruled out for Monday night.
Makai Lemon has shown glimpses of what he can do, posting a 13-plus yard reception in five of his six games played. The USC product was selected in the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft after showcasing incredible route-running skills and an ability to rack up yards after the catch in college.
Using Lemon in bubble screens with inexperienced blockers is not going to build his confidence. The Cowboys rank among the bottom 10 defenses in opponent completion percentage and yards per completion. Quarterback Tanner McKee should be looking for Lemon over the middle early and often.
Dallas Goedert's red-zone dominance saved the Eagles' offense time and time again in 2025. The veteran tight end led the team with 18 red-zone targets and a stellar 11 touchdowns. A redesigned offensive scheme and a knee issue have not allowed Goedert to find that same success in 2026.
Goedert's only two red-zone targets this season came in Week 1, when he logged two touchdowns in a victory over the Commanders. Take note that he also drew a defensive interference penalty that set up Dameon Pierce's two-yard touchdown in Week 6. Good things happen when Goedert is the focus.
That first score feeling >>> pic.twitter.com/WpOA9mI0Ky
Sirianni and offensive coordinator Sean Mannion would benefit from using Goedert's 6'5", 250-pound frame to their advantage. Crafty pre-snap motions could draw mismatches near the end zone. Relying on a tried-and-true method would help an offense averaging a dismal 17.7 points per game.
Dallas' lackluster defense is offset by a dangerous offense. Quarterback Dak Prescott, wide receiver CeeDee Lamb, and wide receiver George Pickens have the skills to frustrate defenses. However, the blueprint to shutting down the Cowboys' offense has come to light during their past two losses.
Dallas was held to 50 rushing yards on 13 carries (3.8 average) against the Buccaneers in Week 5 and was limited to 48 rushing yards on 15 carries (3.2 average) against the Packers in Week 6. Running back Javonte Williams has yet to find a groove, forcing the Cowboys to become one-dimensional.
It's crucial for Philly defensive coordinator Vic Fangio to stress discipline in the trenches. Closing running lanes and finishing tackles would put pressure on Prescott to convert long third downs. All it takes is one tipped pass or bad throw to come up with a game-changing takeaway in those spots.

title: Jalyx Hunt's New Injury Comments Show How Lucky Eagles Are
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – Players left the field at halftime for their respective locker rooms at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium two weeks ago. All of them except Jalyx Hunt. Finally, a cart came out to take the Eagles' outside linebacker off the field.
It looked bad , with one leg bending awkwardly behind him and getting stuck there while helping stop the Jaguars on fourth-and-goal from inside the five as time expired on the second quarter.
Hunt wanted nothing to do with the cart. He waved it off. Hunt can laugh about it now, and he did at his locker earlier this week as the Eagles prepare for a Week 7 visit from the Dallas Cowboys on Monday Night Football .
“The group (text) chat was like, ‘Man, if you took that cart off, we would've been on your (butt),’” he said. “I don't know what it is; maybe it's an unwritten rule, but I'm only taking that cart if I physically cannot walk or I feel as if the season's over. So, I felt like I had enough strength to at least hobble off, so I was gonna do it.”
“Because that cart off, man, I've seen some, I've seen some nasty things happen. So, no, I didn't wanna be on with that group.”
Hunt hobbled, helped off with arms around a pair of trainers’ shoulders.
Presumably, the text chat included some teammates. Either way, Hunt was able to stand at his locker and meet with reporters, which indicates his season is not over. He was listed as a limited participant for the first two days of practice this week, which speaks volumes, as does the fact that he was not placed on injured reserve.
It all means that Hunt, incredibly, will return, and in an Eagles season that has absorbed one body blow after another with injury, that is encouraging. The moment it happened, however, was frightening – “Terrifying” was his word.
“I haven't experienced an injury like that before in my football career; thank God I can say that,” he said. “I heard a pop, went down like that, felt how awkward the position was, knowing that's not a normal position for your body to be in. It was really scary. And then having to get that X-ray at the field and feeling how I was feeling, it was scary.”
Hunt then gave a shout out to his Pilates flexibility program for limiting the severity of the injury.
What ensued from that moment in London was sending out texts to family and friends to, he said, “to put prayer warriors out. My mom was praying for me, Dad was praying; it was scary.”
He then boarded the flight back to the U.S. It was one of the most uncomfortable flight she had ever endured, with his leg elevated and booted.
Uncertainty remains about when he will be able to play again, but at least it looks like it will be this season, and not in 2027.

title: Eagles vs. Cowboys MNF: Who Wins and Why in Week 7 NFC East Showdown
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — This wasn’t what the NFL schedule makers had in mind when they decided to stick Eagles-Cowboys on Monday Night Football in Week 7 . Neither team has been what everyone thought they would be.
Both are 2-4 as of Saturday morning, but not far behind the NFC East-leading Giants, who are 3-2-1. The Eagles have lost four in a row for the first time since Doug Pederson was in charge back in 2020, while the Cowboys have lost two straight.
The Eagles have won three of the last four meetings against the Cowboys dating back to Philly’s Super Bowl championship season of 2024.
That said, here's a closer look at this weekend's most key matchups:
Michael Clay’s units have given up a 52-yard kickoff return that cost the Eagles a victory in London and, a week later, they allowed a punt to be partially blocked that gave the Panthers the ball at their own 48 midway through the fourth quarter, which gave Carolina good field position that they turned into a decisive touchdown drive last week.
In fairness to Clay, injuries have had a trickledown effect on who is playing on special teams for him.
For Dallas, dangerous return man KeVontae Turpin isn’t expected to play after injuring rib cartilage on the opening kickoff against the Packers in Week 6.
Parker is the Eagles’ former defensive backs coach, helping shape Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean into Associated Press first-team All-Pros and was hired to be the Cowboys’ defensive coordinator in the offseason.
Dallas’s defensive struggles date back a year and haven't changed under Parker. It ranks 30th in total defense thanks in part to a run defense that is dead last in defending the run, allowing nearly 150 yards per game. Of course, the Eagles played a Panthers defense last week that was giving up 168 yards per game and managed just 32.
The Cowboys brought in veteran defensive coach Mike Pettine last week as a consultant to help Parker try to turn around the defense.
Rookie safety Caleb Downs leads Dallas in tackles with 43.
Saquon Barkley is expected to return, which should give the Eagles a big boost to their ground game. Also, receiver DeVonta Smith and quarterback Tanner McKee showed chemistry last week as Smith returned from a two-game absence, catching seven passes for 75 yards and a 19-yard touchdown.
Cowboys QB Dak Prescott and his offense ranked second in passing production last year, but there has been some slippage, and they are now ranked sixth. It’s not much of a drop, but enough that it hasn’t seen them light up the scoreboard as much this year as they did last, having scored 16 and 13 points, respectively, in their last two losses.
The Eagles’ defense has had its share of struggles with Cooper DeJean struggling to make tackles, safety Drew Mukuba having a hard time in pass defense, and a revolving door at linebacker with Jihaad Campbell and Jeremiah Trotter, Jr. now splitting reps.

title: ‘Guys Gotta Step Up:’ Saquon Barkley Sends Message to Eagles Ahead of MNF Return
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — Top-tier athletes are often hardest on themselves, a common trait among high achievers. There is a fine line, though, between productive self-scouting and slipping into a negative mindset.
Eagles star running back Saquon Barkley, expected to return Monday night against the Cowboys after missing two games with a hamstring injury, has worked to manage that balance as his NFL career has progressed.
Barkley, who recently took up golf, used that sport as an example.
“Some of you guys are golfers. When you think about the next shot after a bad one, you’re just like, ‘Oh, no. No.’ You stand no chance,” Barkley explained. “Someone was playing with Tiger Woods, and even he was hard on himself. It was never in a negative way. He always had a mindset that the next putt’s gonna go in or the next shot’s gonna be great. … You gotta take that to the field, right? And that’s just like the game.
As poorly as the Eagles played offensively against the Panthers in Week 6, Barkley noted they were one drive away from flipping the script in what ended as a 25-14 loss.
“We did not put together our best game on offense, and before you know it, we were one drive away,” Barkley said. “After we just scored a touchdown, the defense made a stop. We had a great special teams play, and we got the ball back in our hands.
“Then on that drive we had a missed snap, and just like that it was second-and-21. We keep doing stuff like that to put us behind the sticks.”
Barkley’s point was that the game was still there if the offense had executed better.
“Going into that drive, that game was right there for the taking, ready for us to win,” the Eagles' RB1 said. “We can’t lose sight of that, and that’s just how the NFL works. At any moment it can change, and we got the guys for it. I’m excited. I love the install that we have in for Dallas. I think Tanner [McKee’s] a great leader of men also.”
While acknowledging the adversity of losing players like starting tackle Lane Johnson to retirement and franchise quarterback Jalen Hurts to blood clots , Barkley said it’s time for others to step up.
“It’s time," Barkley said. "Guys gotta grow up. Guys gotta step up. That’s why this is a big-boy league, and we have the guys, and I’m excited for it.”
