title: One Eagles Rookie Could Be the Next Late-Round Pick to Break Out
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — Rookie Keyshawn James-Newby doesn’t have to look very far to see the success a seventh-round draft pick can make. All the Eagles' outside linebacker needs to do is walk a few stalls deeper into the locker room where Moro Ojomo stows his gear.
Further toward the back of the locker room is another former seventh-rounder—left tackle Jordan Mailata from 2018, who is already on his third contract with the Eagles. Ojomo was a seventh-round pick in 2023 and is playing himself into a second contract that should pay him handsomely, either back in Philly or in another city.
The Eagles have had some recent success mining talent in the final round of the draft, and James-Newby could be the latest to emerge. There could also be some success stories in waiting, considering the Eagles drafted two others in the seventh round last spring – defensive tackle Uar Bernard and safety Cole Wisniewski, both of whom were taken earlier in the round ahead of James-Newby.
“Whether you're first or seventh or a free agent, everyone has odds to beat,” James-Newby said at his locker earlier this week. “It doesn't really matter where you're at, you know? Everyone has odds to beat. … I can't look in the future, I can't look in the past, and I just gotta continue forward and take it day by day.”
The Eagles didn’t have seventh-round picks in 2022, 2024 or 2025. In 2021, they selected Patrick Johnson, who played 58 games with two starts in five years in Philly. He is still in the league, playing a big special teams role for the Raiders.
James-Newby—who is 6'1", 240 lbs—burst onto the scene last week against the Panthers after being elevated from the practice squad for the first time this year. He played 48 snaps (61%) on defense and 24 more (83%) on special teams, earning praise from both the defensive and special teams coordinators.
It was a huge jump for James-Newby, as it was after he was released at the end of training camp. General manager Howie Roseman said he was concerned that his seventh-round pick would be claimed, but James-Newby wasn’t and was added back to the practice squad.
“It's kind of a credit to him being a rookie, first time really playing in a big game, and I thought he did a solid job, and he's going to keep getting better and better the more times he's able to go out there and do it,” said ST coordinator Michael Clay. “I thought he did a fairly good job for us being that first time, and there's always things to improve on.”
Added defensive coordinator Vic Fangio: “He’s a pretty good athlete. He's got some speed to him. I think he'll even do better now that he's got his feet wet more than he expected, or we expected. I do like him, and I think hopefully we'll see steady progress from him the more he gets to play.”
James-Newby made only one tackle but showed enough in other areas to earn another elevation, or even a roster spot, as the Eagles prepare to host the Cowboys on Monday Night Football.
James-Newby played more than he probably expected after Nolan Smith left last week’s game with a concussion . The outside linebacker was in concussion protocol to start the week.
“Keyshawn has never once, no matter the circumstance, gotten down on himself,” outside linebacker Jalyx Hunt said. “You can tell some things frustrate him, but it doesn't change the fact that he's coming back out. He's gonna go 100 miles an hour whenever he can. He's gonna ask questions when he doesn't know something, and he's gonna work to be the best at what he can do.”
KJN spent time at three different colleges: Montana Tech, Idaho, and New Mexico, where he spent his final season before the draft. At New Mexico, he made 15 tackles for loss with nine sacks.
He understands that the NFL is a different level, and there are things he needs to do to become the next Ojomo or Mailata.
“I wouldn't say necessarily work on,” James-Newby said. “I would just say get better at some specific moves. I only have a couple of moves, and those moves are the moves I always like to use, and I always will continue to use. I just have to become more accurate with them, and it'll work out in my favor.”

title: Joe Milton Left Cowboys for Eagles With Starting Job in His Sights
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A.  — For the foreseeable future, Tanner McKee will have an opportunity to try to stabilize a struggling Eagles offense .
The next in line from there may be Joe Milton, the lengthy, cannon-armed Michigan Man turned Tennessee Volunteer who has been working behind the scenes with New England and Dallas over the past two-plus seasons as a developmental quarterback.
The call came from Philadelphia while Milton was still on the Cowboys' practice squad. His agent mentioned the Eagles were interested in adding him after it became clear Jalen Hurts would be headed to injured reserve . Milton went through a normal day of work, got in his car afterward and realized everything had changed.
“I was just like, ‘What am I gonna do? Am I gonna stay on practice squad or should I show up for my opportunity?’ I’m here, so,” Milton told Eagles On SI .
The 6-foot-5 Sunshine State native chose the clearer opportunity.
The Eagles officially signed Milton off Dallas’s practice squad and put him on their 53-man roster before the Week 6 game against Carolina after Hurts was sidelined indefinitely with pulmonary blood clots.
McKee is the starter for now, with Milton joining the room alongside rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton. The move puts Milton on a potential collision course with his former team when the Cowboys visit Lincoln Financial Field on Monday Night Football.
Milton was surprised it was a rival who called.
“Yeah. Just because it is a rival, and it was just like, you know, dang, like no way,” Milton said. “But my agent called me and mentioned it to me.”
At first Milton compartmentalized.
“I went to practice like it was a normal day and just tried to operate as a Dallas Cowboy at the time, and I went home.”
From there, Milton quickly understood the direction he should go.
The timing is imperfect for everyone involved. Milton offered prayers for Hurts, noting he had spoken with the Eagles quarterback a couple of times while still in college.
“Obviously, I talked to (Jalen) a couple times before I even got here, like when I was in college, so we don’t have a strong relationship, but I’d talked to him before, so all prayers out to him for sure,” Milton said.
Milton's development in Dallas had been going well, and he has leaned on that foundation while absorbing a new system.
“My development was going well in Dallas. I feel like I’ve learned a lot, especially coming here and talking with the coaches and hearing this offense now. … I definitely learned a lot over there,” Milton said. “So shout out to [the Cowboys] for that. But development-wise it’s going great. It’s amazing. I love to learn, so here taking notes again and learning a new offense, so it’s amazing.”
Milton described what’s been a whirlwind process: “Plug in and play.”
That means getting the concepts down, understanding how runs are called, how the offense operates, and how the coordinator calls plays.
“So it was great to hear that on game day [against the Panthers],” Milton said.
Being on the other side of the Cowboys-Eagles rivalry feels different for Milton.
“Obviously I’m in another color now. And that’s a rival, but hey, can’t wear blue this week. I’m totally fine on that,” he said.
Milton downplayed the idea that he is here to offer up intel on the Cowboys' dynamic offense led by QB1 Dak Prescott.
For fans who do not know his style, Milton offered up a straightforward self-scouting report.
“Let things come to me and operate efficiently. Run enough, run if I have to,” he said.
Early impressions of the staff have been positive for Milton, particularly quarterbacks coach Parks Frazier, who has made a strong first impression.
“Oh, I love Parks, man. I love [OC] Sean [Mannion] too, but I love Parks. Parks was the first person, first coach I met here, and it’s pretty much, he took me under his wing,” said Milton. “He did what a coach is supposed to do in the right way, and he’s still doing it to this day.”
Milton arrived in Philadelphia with limited regular-season experience—no starts, 37 completions on 53 attempts for 424 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions—plus some rushing production, along with a strong preseason in Dallas.
Whether the opportunity with the Eagles leads to snaps against the Cowboys , or beyond, depends on how quickly he absorbs the offense and how the depth chart shakes out behind McKee. For now, Milton is focused on showing up and proving he belongs.
“Going on my second week, so yeah, man, I love what they’re doing upstairs. It’s great,” Milton said. “They come with the right energy every day. And shoot, they got the right mindset, and that’s what you need as a quarterback. And just take it with a grain of salt, but at the same time, Parks and Sean, they do a great job coaching and explaining why a play is in and what’s the definition of those plays for sure.”

title: 5 Eagles Who Will Likely Be Inactive vs. Cowboys in Week 7
full_text:
The Eagles could be getting a major contributor back for their Week 7 showdown with the rival Cowboys on Monday Night Football.
After missing the past two games for Philly due to a hamstring injury, star running back Saquon Barkley returned to the practice field ahead of the game against Dallas, and he's expected to be good to go for the game, barring a setback. While Barkley might be available for the Eagles, several other players likely won't be.
Here's a look at five Eagles players who are likely to be inactive for the seventh game of the season.
Safety Michael Carter II suffered an abdominal injury in London in Week 5 against the Jaguars that sidelined him for the remainder of the game. He then missed Philadelphia's Week 6 loss to the Panthers due to the injury, and he also missed the first practice of the week ahead of the Dallas game.
Barring a quick turnaround, it seems like Carter is trending towards a second consecutive absence for Philadelphia.
Nolan Smith tallied his third sack of the season in the first half of Philadelphia's game against Carolina last weekend. Unfortunately, he exited the game with a concussion shortly thereafter and didn't return.
Smith was placed in the league's concussion protocol, and he'll have to pass through it before he's cleared to return to the field for Philadelphia. It remains to be seen whether that happens or not. He didn't participate in the first practice of the week.
Landon Dickerson has missed five straight games for Philadelphia after being placed on the IR list with a knee injury following the first game of the season. The Eagles opened up the practice window for Dickerson last week, paving a path for him to return, but he didn't play in Week 6, and it remains to be seen if he'll play in Week 7, as he's now dealing with two separate injuries.
In addition to the knee issue, Dickerson is now apparently dealing with a pectoral injury as well.
Joe Milton is still getting acclimated to Philadelphia's playbook after being signed by the team last week, but it's unlikely that he'll be active for the game against his former franchise. The Eagles aren't likely to have three QBs on the active roster, so Milton will probably be the odd man out.
With Tanner McKee as the starter and Cole Payton as the backup, Milton was likely to serve as the emergency third quarterback, as he did in Week 6.
The Hollywood Brown experiment hasn't really worked out well in Philadelphia .
The speedy receiver has only appeared in one game for the Eagles on the campaign, and he hasn't registered a single catch. He missed several games due to an ankle injury, but he was a healthy scratch in Week 6. He could be in for a similar fate in Week 7,

title: Steelers Can No Longer Avoid CB Troubles
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers held the New Orleans Saints to just 10 points during their international contest in Paris, France. The performance helped earn the team's fifth victory of the season and a temporary share of the AFC North divisional lead.
Since the defense surrendered just 10 points, the Steelers defense is in great shape, right? In many ways, the identity of this team lives and dies with their pass rush and defensive line. After disrupting Saints quarterback Tyler Shough, it's clear that their front seven is dangerous.
Contrarily, the secondary is still in flux. The team gave up their lone touchdown thanks to being outmatched by the Saints' speed on the outside. Since the team traded Joey Porter Jr., the team has lacked another capable boundary corner. The defense has attempted to weather the storm, but they need to add a cornerback via trade immediately.
The additions of guys like Sean Murphy-Bunting and Terrell Smith were smart ones. With injuries running through the secondary, adding that depth gave the team some breathing room over the past few weeks. Sadly, that hasn't solved the issues in the pass defense. If anything, it's kicked the can on addressing a problem that's been brewing for months.
The Steelers have to address their inefficiencies at cornerback through a trade. It's not the ideal situation for finding that player, but they need another starter to pair with Jamel Dean, preferably one who has the speed and physicality that defensive coordinator Patrick Graham yearns for.
There are a few paths the Steelers can take if a trade must happen. Whatever direction they go, they must target the type of player they lost when they traded Porter Jr. - someone who is excels in man-to-man coverage schemes and can be a disruptive force in tight.
A commonly named trade target right now is Philadelphia Eagles veteran Riq Woolen. A big-bodied, physical cornerback who won a Super Bowl with the Seattle Seahawks last season, Woolen provides a ton of what the Steelers are missing right now.
Another low-cost option that I would encourage the Steelers to look toward is Washington Commanders veteran Rasul Douglas. Douglas is a former 2017 NFL Draft pick who has excelled with multiple organizations. The 31-year-old defended 13 passes last year with the Miami Dolphins, and he's already recorded an interception and five pass breakups with the Commanders this season.
For a seventh-round draft pick, the Steelers could add a player who makes that stop at the goal line against the Saints.
There are bigger names to target, instead, if the Steelers want to add a bona fide starter for 2026 and beyond. One player they recently faced could be a solution. Tampa Bay Buccaneers Zyon McCollum is a former fifth-round pick, but he's been a steady starter for several seasons.
Following his rookie contract, he signed an extension that pays him an average salary of $!6 million through the 2028 season. That's only a few more million per season than they currently pay Jamel Dean, so it stands to reason that the organization would happily take on McCollum's remaining deal.
The Bucs are also going through changes. Their salary cap situation skyrockets with quarterback Baker Mayfield's extension taking effect in 2027. The team will need to shed some salary, and the Steelers might be the beneficiaries of Tampa's troubling situation.
A big swing or a quick addition, it doesn't really matter. The Steelers cannot ignore their issues at cornerback any longer. They have to add immediately to give their defense a complete lineup for the first time in 2026.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: How Aaron Rodgers Helped Payton Wilson Make Crucial Play in Steelers Win
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers need both sides of the ball to have success if they want to have a strong season and both sides have shown they'll do what it takes to achieve that.
The Steelers got a big win over the New Orleans Saints in Paris, France in Week 7, with the defense playing an important role in the 19-10 victory.
Linebacker Payton Wilson made one of the best plays in the Steelers' win with an interception in the third quarter, as the Saints were threatening to score.
Wilson doesn't make this play without the help of none other than Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers, showing the camaraderie between the offense and defense.
The Saints were just 10 yards out from a big touchdown to start the second half, which would've given them their first lead over the Steelers in the game.
Saints quarterback Tyler Shough tried to find wide receiver Chris Olave on 2nd-and-7, but Wilson cut the route and made the interception, giving the Steelers possession and keeping them in the lead, 13-10 midway through the third quarter.
We'll be taking that 😏 @payton_wilson21 pic.twitter.com/SPSaIHFNGT
After the game, Rodgers made sure to point out how he may have helped Wilson come up with that interception. How? Wilson made that play because of his work in practice.
"Did it help that he picked me off in practice on a very similar play this week?" Rodgers joked.
AWESOME: Aaron Rodgers asked #Steelers LB Payton Wilson if intercepting him on a similar play in practice helped him make today’s game-changing interception. Wilson said it did, then joked he took the practice pick to the house. Great back and forth 😂😂 pic.twitter.com/A7WtqYz4yv
“That’s honestly just a credit to our coaches and what we do every day in practice," Wilson said on his interception. "I mean, I’ve repped that play, no lie, more than 20 times now."
“And Coach Simo' [Jason Simmons], PG [Patrick Graham], Scott [McCurley], they all do a really good job of that space away from three, two-by-two. Pretty much all throughout the NFL, that’s where they’re gonna attack.
“So just gambling a little bit and undercutting it, having to defend that play against him [Rodgers] a lot throughout training camp and just in practice has really helped. So, just credit to those guys, put me in those situations enough to trust myself to go do it.”
The Steelers offense had a decent game, but wasn't effective enough to beat the Saints on their own, forcing the defense to show they could do what was needed.
Pittsburgh was fantastic against the run, allowing just 18 yards on 17 rushes from New Orleans, shutting down a big part of their offense.
Shough did have a solid game, completing 30-of-38 passes for 278 yards, but threw just one touchdown, and the Steelers held the Saints scoreless in the second half.
The Steelers almost had two fumble recoveries, but both were overturned , which would've made their own performance more special.
Steelers linebacker Patrick Queen came up big with a huge sack on 3rd-and-10 with 6:40 remaining in the fourth quarter, which represented the Saints' final drive of the game.

title: Where Steelers Stand in AFC North After Saints Win
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers continued their strong 2026 season with another win, which is important for their standing in the AFC North.
The Steelers stood strong defensively and defeated the New Orleans Saints 16-10 in Paris, France, for a big Week 7 victory.
Pittsburgh improved to 5-2 on the season and has won its past three games, which include victories over the Indianapolis Colts at Acrisure Stadium, 34-22 in Week 5, and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , 26-19 at Raymond James Stadium in Week 6.
The Steelers are winning consistently at a crucial part of the season, but they aren't the only AFC North team doing well.
Cleveland Browns* (Tiebreaker)
The Steelers are tied for first place in the AFC North with the Cleveland Browns, who are also 5-2 in 2026.
Cleveland leads the AFC North, as they defeated Pittsburgh 27-24 at Huntington Bank Field in Week 4, and hold the tiebreaker.
The Browns got another 27-24 win, as Andre Smzyt hit a 32-yard field goal as time expired for the road victory over the Tennessee Titans.
All five of the Browns' wins this season have come within one score, and they now have back-to-back wins after beating the Baltimore Ravens at home 13-10 in Week 6.
The Cincinnati Bengals scored 35 unanswered points and defeated the Ravens 35-13 on the road for a big Week 7 win.
Cincinnati scored all 35 points in the second half and also has back-to-back wins, defeating the Miami Dolphins 31-24 on the road in Week 5.
The Ravens have lost back-to-back games after starting 4-1, with quarterback Lamar Jackson missing these last three games.
The Steelers and Browns face off for the second time in 2026, with Acrisure Stadium as the location for this historic rivalry in Week 8.
Cleveland hasn't won in Pittsburgh since a 48-37 victory in the AFC Wild Card Round on Jan. 10, 2021, and they haven't won a regular season game there since Oct. 5, 2003, 22 straight defeats.
It should be a battle of both defenses, and the Steelers almost beat the Browns, tying it up at 24 late after trailing 21-7, so expect revenge to play a factor for the Steelers in this one.
The Bengals play the Titans and will also look to add to their winning streak and stay near the top of the AFC North.
Baltimore has a tougher challenge, travelling to face the Buffalo Bills, which would also be harder if Jackson is still out injured.

title: 6 Winners, 3 Losers From Steelers Win Over Saints
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are rolling .
With their 16-10 victory over the New Orleans Saints at the Stade de France in Paris, the Steelers are now 5-2 and in the midst of a three-game win streak.
Pittsburgh still has some issues it has to clean up, but it's hard not to feel good about the way things are trending heading into Week 8.
With that, here are the Steelers ' winners and losers as they fly back home.
Though Watt didn't earn credit for his forced fumble on a sack of Tyler Shough in the second quarter after the call on the field was overturned after review, the 32-year-old was still stellar for the Steelers.
Along with his takedown of Shough, Watt finished the day with four pressures (per SumerSports ) and was getting into the backfield consistently while also helping out against the run, per usual.
Fautanu's gone through some struggles in his move from right tackle to left tackle this season.
Chase Young gave the 2024 first-round pick all he could handle and then some, with Fautanu allowing a total of four pressures and two sacks to the former AP Defensive Rookie of the Year (per SumerSports).
That makes it back-to-back rough outings for Fautanu, who was also far from his sharpest in Pittsburgh's Week 6 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Wilson's made some serious strides in Patrick Graham's defense.
The 26-year-old's biggest play of the day came on an interception of Shough in the red zone with the Steelers leading 13-10 about halfway through the third quarter.
New Orleans did not score for the rest of the contest, and Wilson deserves plenty of credit in that regard. Not just for his pick, though, but his support in the run game as well.
Wilson wasn't the only inside linebacker who showed out in this one.
Queen hadn't exactly been living up to expectations this season, with that continuing from a disappointing 2025 campaign.
He turned the time against the Saints, though, coming up with a drive-ending sack on New Orleans' last series of the game while also leading the Steelers with 10 tackles and making more of an impact than usual against the run.
Queen nearly hauled in an interception on the Saints' first drive of the contest too.
Ramsey was instrumental in helping lead Pittsburgh to a comeback win over the Bucs , though he took a step back in France.
He was still helpful as a blitzer and against the run, though he had some lapses in coverage. In total, Ramsey allowed 70 yards and a touchdown in coverage (per SumerSports).
With Sebastian Joseph-Day (triceps) having been placed on the reserve/injured list this week while Derrick Harmon (foot) had already been on IR for two weeks, the Steelers really needed Benton to step up along the interior of the defensive line.
He did exactly that, batting down a pass at the line and posting two tackles for loss to go with two pressures.
Rico Dowdle deserves his flowers, posting a total of 86 yards on 15 touches, though it was Warren who once again stole the show out of the backfield for Pittsburgh.
He continues to prove that he's one of the NFL's elite running backs, rushing for 101 yards on 18 carries to go with three catches for 36 yards for a total of 137 yards from scrimmage.
Freiermuth did convert a 3rd-and-9 with an 11-yard catch in the third quarter, though he also dropped a great throw from Aaron Rodgers down to around the 10-yard line just a few plays later.
Freiermuth had just 20 yards over two catches as five other Steelers finished with more receiving yards than he did.
Rodgers kept building on what's been an incredibly solid final season for the future Hall of Famer.
He went 19-of-30 for 212 yards and a touchdown through the air while also showing off his wheels a bit, picking up a first down with an eight-yard run on third down that essentially clinched the win for Pittsburgh during the final drive of the contest.

title: Referee Grades: Steelers vs. Saints Was Tough to Watch
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints battled in an historic international contest, giving the Paris, France, crowd their first taste of NFL action.
The Steelers, for the second year in a row, were part of the NFL's inaugural contest in another country. As the league expands its global footprint, the Steelers have been right at the forefront.
Unlike the Steelers' win over the Minnesota Vikings in Dublin, Ireland, in 2025, this year's international game is likely to be overshadowed by the officiating crew's performance.
Once again, the referees controlled another contest for the wrong reasons. Both teams were frustrated with the officiating crew, and a deeper dive reveals they were justified.
It was a day to forget for the officials, who should receive a failing grade for their performance in the latest Steelers' win.
Today’s Steelers-Saints game marks the first time Bill Vinovich has officiated a Saints game since the infamous no-call in the NFC Championship Game more than 7 years ago. The Saints are playing in Paris. pic.twitter.com/vHoQOz8Fp9
Things didn't get off on the right foot between the Steelers and the officials, right from the first offensive series.
Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers tried to connect with wide receiver DK Metcalf on a fade route toward the end zone. Metcalf and the Saints cornerback engaged in hand-fighting and physicality as the route developed, but what most saw was the defensive back's free hand tugging on Metcalf's chest plate.
Now, Metcalf was still able to get both hands up in an attempt to get the ball, and the officials can point to that after the fact.
Despite this, being in a one-on-one matchup and having a free hand on the receiver's equipment as he goes up for the ball usually draws a flag automatically.
This time it didn't, incensing Rodgers and effectively putting a target on their back for the remainder of the contest.
For that, the refs received a D-, and they should feel thankful they avoided an outright fail.
Did I love watching left guard Mason McCormick leaping on top of the pile as rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard picked up 20 yards late in the first half?
Did the officials make the right call, flagging the guard for joining the pile too late?
Once upon a time, this was a common practice in the NFL, but it's one of the plays the league wants completely eliminated due to injury risk. Sadly for McCormick, this was an A+ call and the right one.
Two of the most egregious calls against the Steelers were unnecessary roughness calls levied against wide receiver Brandon Smith and linebacker Payton Wilson.
Let's start with Smith, who was blocking a Saints defensive back in the first half. As the play ended, the two continued jawing at one another. The Saints defender pushed Smith back, and in response, the Steelers receiver pushed his facemask into his opponent's.
What made the call feel so off was that the action hardly felt like an escalation. More likely, it was the reaction that the officials caught. Either way, it was not worthy of throwing the flag.
They could have redeemed themselves in the second half, but instead they made another pair of awful calls against both teams. During the first series, they called rookie Saints guard Jeremiah Wright for a personal foul.
Here's the thing: he didn't do anything unnecessary. He was battling Keeanu Benton one-on-one, and he finished the block all the way to the ground. It's how he's been taught to play his entire life, but suddenly it was a penalty.
On the very next play, the Steelers were on the receiving end of a blunderous call. Linebacker Payton Wilson tracked down Saints running back Alvin Kamara and forced him out of bounds.
Wilson began the tackle along the sidelines, and the two fell into the Steelers' bench, but Wilson was called for a personal foul.
All three of these calls were terrible. Not one met the criteria for a personal foul, and each was a normal, routine football play. That's an undeniable failure for the crew on those calls.
As the third quarter wound down, there was a hiccup in the flow of the game. The Steelers' offensive drive was halted after Saints edge rusher Chase Young sacked Rodgers.
That forced the field-goal unit out for a 39-yard attempt, but it took several minutes before kicker Chris Boswell could knock his third field goal of the day through the uprights.
The reason for the delay was that the officials and the scoreboard operations team were struggling to get on the same page.
Head official Bill Vinovich had to stop the play on separate occasions before the snap, so he could correct the game and the play clock.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers vs. Saints Takeaways: Pittsburgh's Getting Dangerous
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers move to 5-2 on the season and 2-0 in the last two years playing overseas.
Their 16-10 win over the New Orleans Saints was exciting from start to finish. Both sides of the ball had moments when they flashed, and moments when they struggled, and it led to a thriller in France.
Now, they head back home with the Cleveland Browns up next and a shot at first place in the AFC North.
But let's not get ahead of ourselves. It's time to dive into some takeaways.
The Steelers offensive line is finally finding its groove, and the upside is evident - and significant. This group is made up of young, high-potential players. It took some time for them to begin to click, but now that they are, it's exciting.
Mason McCormick has been the team's best offensive lineman throughout the season. The transition from the right to the left side was effortless, and the production has been there from the jump. But Troy Fautanu hasn't been as smooth.
In this game, it looked like things were finally starting to work, until it wasn't. Fautanu looked great in first half of play, keeping Chase Young under wraps and leading the way for multiple Jaylen Warren runs.
In the second half, Fautanu fell apart. Young got to Aaron Rodgers twice, and the former first-round left tackle started to slow down. Once it started, he couldn't reverse it, which has been a trend for Fautanu this season. One that needs to change.
Brock Hoffman and Max Iheanachor held their own on the right side, and it opened the gaps for Warren and Rico Dowdle to lead the way to a win.
And then, there's Zach Frazier. Not much needs to be said. Just watch.
Look at this finish from #54 https://t.co/D0IZGu7xme pic.twitter.com/8iAKVwMdle
If this line is clicking, the offense is as well. And Paris was the first time this group felt like they were headed in the right direction for most of the game. They need to finish strong, but it's a step in the right direction.
The Steelers need to figure out a plan for Jalen Ramsey. He simply can't keep up in coverage, but is a human missile when playing the run and blitzing. Against teams like the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 6, he was the difference-maker because of his ability to get into the backfield and disrupt the quarterback.
Against the Saints, he was a liability.
Ramsey simply doesn't have the speed to keep up in coverage anymore. It forces him to play off the ball further than he would normally and then try to keep up with underneath routes. But as soon as a receiver makes a cut, Ramsey is a step behind, and the longer the route, the further behind he falls.
It might be impossible, but the Steelers need to figure out a plan for Ramsey. They don't have another cornerback to put in the slot, but keeping him in coverage on crucial downs doesn't work.
What will? Who knows. But the Steelers need to start thinking and stop accepting that Ramsey is just a problem against the pass.
The Steelers' best inside linebacker is Payton Wilson and it's not particularly close.
Wilson has taken a significant step forward in the last two games. He's explosive toward the ball, isn't afraid to take on a block, and is winning a lot of them, and is improving in the passing game. All around, you're seeing the development of Wilson take shape, and it's something the Steelers desperately needed.
Wilson's interception against Tyler Shough in the red zone during the third quarter might've been the play that sealed the win for the Steelers. Pittsburgh's defense needed some momentum in the second half and Wilson gave them that.
He also set up the offense for a field goal.
We'll be taking that 😏 @payton_wilson21 pic.twitter.com/SPSaIHFNGT
Wilson's emergence is exciting for Pittsburgh. This team needs a true starting inside linebacker, especially with Patrick Queen's back-and-forth play. Maybe they have one in Wilson.
Mike McCarthy loves to try and get his guys involved. And it's almost always a mistake.
In this game, Jaylen Warren was the clear superstar for the Steelers. Which is no surprise if you've watched any Pittsburgh game this season. But time and time again, McCarthy was taking Warren off the field to try and generate plays for Rico Dowdle.
Warren finished the game 18 rushes 101 yards. Dowdle finished with nine rushes for 41 yards.
It's the same thing with DK Metcalf.
The Steelers are always trying to force the football to Metcalf, whether it's through fades during crucial third downs or in the red zone, or by designing quick passes to him with the hope he'll beat a man and make a play.
Rarely do they work. And meanwhile, Germie Bernard is sitting there with three receptions for 27 yards.
The forced touches for certain players need to end. It only costs the offense momentum and opportunity. Especially when they have stars like Bernard and Warren waiting for plays.
The Steelers head back to the United States of America with a chance to claim the top spot in the AFC North come Week 8. With a battle against the Cleveland Browns next on their schedule, this team did exactly what they needed to in Paris - win.
Now, it's about returning to a normal week and trying to get revenge against their AFC North rival. If they do, the race for the division gets more exciting, with the black and gold leading the way.
Noah Strackbein is a Publisher for On SI, covering the Pittsburgh Steelers since 2019. A Jessup, PA native, Noah attended Point Park University, where he fell in love with the Steel City and everything it has to offer. You can find Noah's work at Steelers On SI and weekdays as the hosts of All Steelers Talk.

title: Steelers QBs Dress Up Like Peaky Blinders for Paris Game
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers ' quarterbacks arrived to their Week 7 game in style.
As they get ready to face the New Orleans Saints at the Stade de France in Paris , all four of the Steelers' signal callers, as well as quarterbacks coach Tom Arth, coordinated their outfits with a "Peaky Blinders"-esque style.
By order of the Peaky Blinders pic.twitter.com/mwuwMFfooM
Though "Peaky Blinders" may be set in England instead of France, the Steelers' quarterbacks seemingly were paying homage to the popular Netflix show while over in Europe this week.
Sitting at 4-2 for a fourth straight year after making the postseason in each of the last three seasons, Pittsburgh is in an advantageous spot in the standings at the moment.
The black and gold are in a three-way tie atop the AFC North, though the Cleveland Browns hold the tiebreaker over both them and the Baltimore Ravens due to their 2-0 record in the division. In the Wild Card race, the Steelers currently own the No. 6 seed.
Pittsburgh won't have a respite upon returning home this upcoming week, instead facing Cleveland for the second and final time this season at Acrisure Stadium before going on bye in Week 9.
Given how tight the standings are both in the AFC North and in the hunt for one of three Wild Card spots in the conference, the Steelers have to take full advantage of these next two weeks.
It's still early in the season, but Pittsburgh's schedule gets noticeably tougher once it resumes action following its bye week.
From a trip to Cinicinnati for Sunday Night Football in Week 10 to a road game against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 11 before hosting the Denver Broncos on Black Friday in Week 12, welcoming the Houston Texans to Acrisure Stadium for Sunday Night Football in Week 13 and taking on the Jacksonville Jaguars on the road on Monday Night Football in Week 14, the Steelers ' five-game stretch immediately following their bye is an absolute gauntlet.
That doesn't take into account that Pittsburgh has to play the Ravens twice within the final four weeks of the campaign, either.
As a result, Pittsburgh cannot let its matchup against New Orleans slip through its hands.
The Saints aren't going to just roll over, and they do offer a bit of a challenge given that their offense averages the 11th-most points per game in the league with 25.3.
At the same time, New Orleans is 2-4 for a reason and has one of the worst defenses in the NFL, allowing 29.7 points per game (tied for most in the league) and 377.7 yards per game (fourth-most).
The Steelers also have to find a way to take down a Browns team that defeated them on Thursday Night Football in Week 4.
Cleveland is as formidable as it has been since its last trip to the playoffs in 2023, but that's still a contest Pittsburgh should win at Acrisure Stadium.
As long as the Steelers win their next two and push their win streak out to four games while moving to 6-2 heading into their bye week, they'll be in fantastic shape.
Being 5-3 while splitting its matchups with the Saints and the Browns won't put its season in danger by any means, but it would significantly lower Pittsburgh's margin for error moving forward with how difficult its schedule will soon become.
If they lose both, however, than the Steelers would be in serious danger.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers RB Good to Go vs. Saints Despite Knee Injury
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are in Paris, France, set to take on the New Orleans Saints in Week 7. Their second international game in two years is a battle of two offensive-minded head coaches, and for Mike McCarthy, he'll have one of his top pieces available.
The Steelers announced their Week 7 inactives, which did not include running back Rico Dowdle. Dowdle came into the weekend listed as questionable with a knee injury after being limited in practice throughout the week.
It was his second lower-body injury of the season after missing three games with a dislocated toe earlier in the year.
The rest of their inactives include:
WR Ben Skowronek QB Drew Allar QB Will Howard CB Brandin Echols RB Eli Heidenreich CB Terell Smith
Howard will serve as the emergency third quarterback, allowing him to dress for the game but not be allowed to be used unless Aaron Rodgers and Mason Rudolph are injured.
Echols (hamstring) and Skowronek (calf) were ruled out prior to the team's trip to Paris. They are the only injured players on the inactive list.
Dowdle is coming off his first game since Week 2, when the toe injury happened. He rushed seven times for 40 yards against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 6, holding a 5.7 yards per carry average as he helped Pittsburgh earn their fourth victory of the season.
Dowdle will continue to work as the 1B option behind Jaylen Warren in the backfield. Travis Homer and Lew Nichols round out the group in Week 7 with Heidenreich being inactive.
The Steelers have also cleared safety DeShon Elliott to play against the Saints. This will be Elliott's first game of the 2026 season after being activated off of Injured Reserve just yesterday.
Elliott missed the end of the 2025 season with a lower-body injury. He returned during training camp and played in a preseason game but was placed back on IR to start the year because the team didn't feel he was fully ready to return.
After returning to practice nearly three weeks ago, Elliott is back in the lineup for his first game of the season. He'll join Jaquan Brisker and Roberts Spears-Jennings in the safety room, and will likely take back the starting role alongside Brisker.
Last year, when the Steelers played internationally in Dublin, Ireland, Elliott recorded six tackles, a sack, a forced fumble and an interception.
Pittsburgh will hope that magic returns againt the Saints.
Noah Strackbein is a Publisher for On SI, covering the Pittsburgh Steelers since 2019. A Jessup, PA native, Noah attended Point Park University, where he fell in love with the Steel City and everything it has to offer. You can find Noah's work at Steelers On SI and weekdays as the hosts of All Steelers Talk.

title: 3 Reasons Steelers Will Beat Saints in Paris
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers will defeat the New Orleans Saints in their international Week 7 meeting. The Steelers meet the Saints in Paris, France, looking for their fifth victory of the season.
To secure that win, the Steelers have to play a much better game than they did in Week 6. For three quarters, the Steelers gave the Tampa Bay Buccaneers every chance possible to win. Finally, they found their footing in the fourth quarter and pulled out the win.
That can't happen again in front of the French crowd against an easy to underestimate Saints team. Thankfully, the Steelers are in a much better position entering Week 7. Due to these three reasons, Pittsburgh will exit Stade de France with their fifth victory of the season.
Running back Jaylen Warren is coming off a disappointing outing compared to his previous three monstrous performances, but he's set for a rebound against the Saints. The biggest reason for this is because New Orleans has not produced a good run defense in 2026.
Through their first six contests, the Saints are allowing 138 rushing yards per game. That figure ranks as the third-worst in the NFL so far. The Saints are one of the worst-performing defenses so far in 2026, but they are especially vulnerable against the run. That's a perfect scenario for Warren to return to his 100-yard rushing form and possibly even more.
Another factor is the health of Rico Dowdle. He enters Week 7 questionable with a knee injury. If he can't go at 100%, the Steelers will be heavily reliant on Warren.
After outside linebacker Nick Herbig exploded in Week 6, recording two sacks in the win, the Steelers are expecting a game-wrecker to appear once again in Paris.
Herbig lived up to his big contract extension against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, but the Steelers are counting on him to bring that production against the Saints as well. Not only because he has momentum, but because both T.J. Watt and Alex Highsmith are dealing with minor injuries ahead of the matchup.
Herbig is healthy and raring to go. That's trouble for Saints quarterback Tyler Shough.
DeShon Elliott is back on the Steelers' active roster after nearly a year due to a major knee injury. The star defender has been sorely missed by the Steelers' defense, and his possible return comes at the perfect time.
The Steelers have been a solid, but imperfect defense in 2026. They started red-hot, but after a couple of tough weeks, they have issues that can be exploited.
One of those blemishes is the safety position. The team released veteran Rayshawn Jenkins after two weeks of playing nearly zero snaps, leaving Jaquan Brisker, Robert Spears-Jennings and Jalen Ramsey as the only safeties on the active roster.
With Elliott back in the mix, the safety position suddenly shifts from worrisome to the position that sets the tone on defense. The Saints will find that out first-hand.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Elevated Two WRs for Saints Game
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are bringing up multiple wide receiver from their practice squad.
Before their Week 7 game against the New Orleans Saints in Paris at the Stade de France, the Steelers added Brandon Smith and Brandon Johnson to their game day roster.
Smith had previously been brought up from the practice squad in Weeks 5 and 6, meaning he is now out of elevations for the year while Johnson has one remaining.
With Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger) on the reserve/injured list, with the former having missed two games thus far while the latter has been out for one, Pittsburgh has been in clear need of receiver depth.
Add in the fact that Ben Skowronek (calf) will miss a second-straight contest as well , and Smith in particular has become somewhat of a key piece for the Steelers' offense after a strong summer.
Smith turned some heads during training camp and even earned some first-team reps during the Steelers' stay at Saint Vincent College in Latrobe.
He didn't get much of an opportunity to prove himself during the preseason, though, as he suffered a lower-body injury in the opener against the Green Bay Packers and remained out for Pittsburgh's final two exhibition games.
Smith was later released at the roster cutdown deadline on August 30 before re-signing to the Steelers' practice squad.
He was first elevated for the team's Week 5 matchup with the Indianapolis Colts after Pittman Jr. was placed on IR. Smith ended up playing 16 offensive snaps in that contest after Wilson and Skowronek went down in the first half, and while he didn't record a catch, he did help out as a blocker on Jaylen Warren's 50-yard touchdown run in a 34-22 win for Pittsburgh.
Smith came up from the practice squad once again , this time alongside Johnson, for the Steelers' Week 6 bout with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Once again, Smith did not log a reception. He did, however, record 41 snaps on offense as the team's third receiver behind DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard in addition to garnering 18 special teams reps (per Pro Football Focus ).
There's a lot up in the air for Pittsburgh in regards to its receiver room.
It's unknown when, or if, Pittman Jr. will be activated off IR, as there seems to be some concern that he could miss the rest of the season.
At the very least, though, it feels incredibly unlikely that he'll return at the earliest possible date, which would be in Week 10 after he misses the required minimum of four games while on IR.
Wilson appears to be in better shape when it comes to making a swifter recovery for the Steelers, though he still won't be eligible to play until Week 11.
With questions about when Skowronek will be ready to take the field again as well, Pittsburgh's receiver depth is being pushed to the limit. Smith is a solid short-term answer if he were to end up signing to the 53-man roster now that he can no longer be elevated beyond this week, though general manager Omar Khan may also have to get aggressive in finding another solution from outside the organization.
Perhaps Marquez Valdes-Scantling will scratch that itch in his return to the Steelers via the practice squad given his connection with Aaron Rodgers , but he didn't show much in his five games with the team last season and is now 32-years-old.
It's possible Smith's spot will be taken by Valdes-Scantling since he has elevations left, and he may also lose out on some opportunities once Skowronek is back as well.
It also becomes even tougher to envision Smith sticking around (if he were to sign to the 53-man roster) once Wilson and/or Pittman Jr. come back, and the possibility of a trade for a receiver ahead of the November 10 deadline may still be alive.
As such, Smith likely has to take advantage of his current role in order to convince Pittsburgh to keep him around and play him again this season, which would require adding him to the 53-man roster after this week.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: 3 Observations from Seahawks Win Over Chiefs
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are impressing the NFL after becoming the first team to beat the Kansas City Chiefs this season.
They dominated Patrick Mahomes, Kenneth Walker III and the Chiefs , beating them handily by a score of 20-3. Here's a look at three observations from the game.
The Seahawks' defense came into the game as the top-ranked unit in the league, but they were definitely going to be tested against the number one offense in the league. The Chiefs came into the game averaging 414 yards per contest, but they managed to gain just 213 yards throughout the game. Meanwhile, the Seahawks had 410 yards of offense and clearly were the winner in this one.
It's further proof that the Seahawks' defense is the best in the league. If they can shut down the Chiefs, they could give every team in the league the same treatment. That should be a warning to the rest of the NFL that the Seahawks are not going away quite yet.
Jaxon Smith-Njigba continued his ascent as the league's top receiver. He led by over 130 yards for the receiving title going into the game and likely just extended that lead. He added another 150 yards to his total, along with a touchdown.
With 867 yards on the season in just seven games, he's on a remarkable pace and very well could be in the mix to not just be the Offensive Player of the Year but also the league MVP.
The one true blemish on the Seahawks for this game came late in the second quarter, when the team was driving and nearly had a touchdown in their grasp. An interception thrown by Sam Darnold to Chiefs cornerback Nohl Williams could have gone a lot worse.
Williams tried returning the ball all the way from one end zone to another and got a decent return off it, making it all the way to the Seattle 44-yard line. Had he gotten a few yards closer, the Chiefs could have kicked the field goal and made it a one-score game going into halftime. He also could have taken it to the house and really flipped the entire game.
Darnold was lucky that the damage was not worse on that pick, and it is something that could haunt them down the line in future games if he's not careful enough.

title: How the Seahawks Shut the Lights Off on Kenneth Walker III
full_text:
Former Seattle Seahawks and current Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III ran wild over five games . Then he ran back into the brick wall that he used to practice against every day.
Stopping Walker was the primary emphasis for the Seahawks’ league-best defense in their 20-3 win over the Chiefs on Sunday, and they exceeded all expectations in pursuit of that goal.
“We [had] to play in waves, because he’s still going to break tackles,” Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said postgame. “I’m sure he broke a host of tackles, because that’s what he does. So, we had to get people to the football, and that gave us the best chance. I felt the guys play like that; I felt like we played great team defense today.”
Walker entered the game with six rushing touchdowns and a per-game average of 133 rushing yards. The Seahawks hadn’t allowed a 100-yard rusher in 25 games — a streak that goes back to midway through the 2024 season.
The former Seahawks second-round pick had been unstoppable, but the Chiefs hadn’t faced a truly elite defense yet this season. Seattle is not just a good run defense; it may be the best in the NFL.
Defense prevailed. Walker turned 14 carries into just 36 rushing yards and added four catches for 21 yards. Neither Walker nor the Chiefs found the end zone the entire game.
Some Kenneth Walker III stats from tonight: - lowest success rate of any game this season (29%) and lowest yds/carry (2.6) - lowest rate of stacked boxes (7%) - lowest number of explosive runs (0) Seattle’s defense, man 😮‍💨
“Just getting after him, man,” Seahawks linebacker Ernest Jones IV said of how they stopped Walker in his tracks. “We knew, I mean, of course he’s been here. We know what type of running back was coming in here. But we don’t allow people to run through our defense, and that’s just us, and we were able to execute against a really good running back today and hold him to minimal yards in that category.”
On the other side, Seahawks running back Emanuel Wilson had his best game of the season with 24 carries for 100 yards and a touchdown (4.2 yards per carry). Wilson had averaged just 3.5 yards per carry on 87 carries coming into the game.
The Seahawks’ defense proved it could completely nullify their former teammate, who is currently an Offensive Player of the Year and MVP candidate, and the offense showed that they didn’t need to keep him to win games. Those are major victories for this Seahawks team after snapping a two-game losing streak .
Seattle’s defense was still playing great during the losing streak, but this is another performance their confidence can fall back on as they reach the middle of the season.
“We can play. We can play. We go out there, and that’s our goal: shut you down, shut your lights out,” Jones said of the defense. “So, I think that’s big ups to the defense today. We came out there, executed, and we were able to go out there and stop a real good offense.”

title: 5 Winners, 1 Loser in Seahawks Big Win vs. Chiefs
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are making a statement with their 20-3 win against the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 7's edition of Sunday Night Football.
After back-to-back losses, the Seahawks needed to bounce back strong , and they did just that against the Chiefs. Here's a look at the winners and losers from the matchup.
Jaxon Smith-Njigba looked dominant once again against the Chiefs. The NFL's leading receiver added to his total with 150 yards on nine catches and a touchdown.
JSN continues to establish himself as the best wideout in the game, and doing so against a really good defense like the Chiefs' only solidifies that.
The front seven stifled the Chiefs' offense all day long. Kenneth Walker III came into the game averaging 133 rushing yards per contest, but he managed to only gain 36 yards on the ground on 14 carries, good for 2.6 yards per carry.
By taking out Kansas City's top weapon, the Seahawks were able to take control of the game from there.
While Walker struggled for the Chiefs, his replacement, Emanuel Wilson, had one of his best showings of the season. Wilson gained 82 yards on 20 carries and had a touchdown of his own in the fourth quarter to secure the victory.
Wilson might concede some carries in the coming weeks to Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price as they return from their injuries, but he looks like someone who deserves a role within the offense.
Seahawks defensive back Ty Okada had the Seahawks' lone turnover of the evening. His interception in the second quarter, as the Chiefs were entering Seahawks territory, took away a bunch of momentum, and Seattle was able to capitalize with a touchdown on the ensuing drive. Okada's big play put the Seahawks on a path to victory, and he should be commended for it.
On a night when a lot of things went the Seahawks' way, Rashid Shaheed is the lone loser in the matchup. Shaheed suffered a knee injury that knocked him out for the rest of the game.
It remains to be seen how long Shaheed will be out, but his absence is definitely a loss for the Seahawks' offense.

title: Charles Cross Injury Update: Seahawks Left Tackle Leaves In Fourth
full_text:
Right now, things are going according to plan for the Seattle Seahawks. They hold a 13-3 lead, have the ball in scoring range, and there are less than five minutes left in the fourth quarter. However, the positive vibes of the moment were momentarily halted when Charles Cross exited with an injury. He walked off, but the severity of the injury is to be determined.
The star tackle, who was given a nine-figure contract extension last year, has been off to a strong start to 2026, if perhaps not quite perfect. Without him, Josh Jones takes the field, a position that he’s succeeded in before, and held his own last year for the Seahawks when Charles Cross missed a few weeks near the end of the season.
The Seahawks were able to score a touchdown to extend the lead to three scores without him, and with less than four minutes remaining now it's unlikely the team needs Cross to return, even if he can. This is one position where the Seahawks can feel relatively secure in their depth. However, Cross is a staple on a line that is just trying to get continuity back after Bradford's injury.
Cross looked to be in some pain and discomfort as he came off the field and onto the sideline. Whether that makes the injury serious is unknown as of now, but we likely won't find out until tomorrow at this point. Seattle may need to go to the practice squad for a week or two to give themselves some depth. Logan Brown is a frontrunner.
Again, the real issue is in the broken opportunity to continue to build familiarity with the offensive line all playing together. That is the main thing this unit has going for it, but so far they've had very limited opportunities to gel together because of injuries. Anthony Bradford was out from week two to now, and the Seahawks replaced him with a rotation of guards.
The Seahawks are about to run out the clock on a victory, so again, there's no real reason for Cross to go back in. Josh Jones is more than good enough to handle the responsibilities of the last few minutes of this one. But ultimately, this offense has little chance to be what it can be without Cross playing, and playing well.

title: Rashid Shaheed Injury Update: Seahawks WR Leaves Early In Third Quarter
full_text:
The Seahawks are leading 10-0 in the third quarter and are looking to expand that lead in the coming minutes, but they’ll have to try that expansion without Rashid Shaheed. The receiver exited the game with a knee injury, being labeled questionable to return by the team. He’s missed at least a few plays here, so the wound is at least of note.
Shaheed has been mostly quiet so far today, with two catches for one yard as the team has attempted to get him involved via bubble screens. He has, however, gotten one big punt return that sparked a scoring drive that wasn’t right before halftime. In his absence, the Seahawks will turn to Tory Horton, Cooper Kupp, and (of course) Jaxon Smith-Njigba.
Shaheed has been isolated as one of the big disappointments so far this season for the Seahawks, having not yet been implemented as a reliable and significant part of the offense. Plenty of people believe that Horton deserves snaps over him, so to those people, this may not be much of a loss at all. But his impact on special teams is always felt, and he represents a downfield threat.
Shaheed was seen going to the locker room with a trainer. He gave a thumbs up on his way, so it doesn't seem particularly dire, but it could easily be enough to keep him out the rest of the night. Noting that we don't have much information to work with yet, I don't get the sense that it's going to be overly long-term, but it's so hard to make such evaluations right now.
The injury will certainly compel the Seahawks to commit to the run even harder than they already have. Through the first two and a half quarters, Seattle has run a lot, especially on early downs. Losing a big play receiver will likely exacerbate that, although holding a lead in the second half is also a powerful motivatior. I believe this team will be fine without him for now.
If Seattle can find their way to just one more score and get things into the fourth, Shaheed wouldn't figure much into the gameplan anyway. Although I'll always wonder about his viability as a pitch play specialist out of the backfield.

title: 7 Seahawks Ruled Inactive vs. Chiefs, Including Zach Charbonnet
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are warming up for their Week 7 matchup on Sunday Night Football against the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs, who are led by Patrick Mahomes and last year's Super Bowl MVP and former friend Kenneth Walker III.
The Seahawks had a long injury report going into the matchup, so many people are intrigued by who will be inactive for the Seahawks against the Chiefs . Here's a look at what they ultimately decided on.
Lock has been limited in practice throughout the week with a right elbow injury. The team is opting to make him the emergency third quarterback for the game against the Chiefs. This means he'll only come in if Sam Darnold and second-year pro Jalen Milroe suffer an injury.
Charbonnet was put onto the 53-man roster this week, sparking hopes that he will return to the field soon. The Seahawks are keeping him out for the game against the Chiefs as he continues to recover from his knee injury, which he suffered during the NFC Divisional Round matchup against the San Francisco 49ers back in January.
Thomas is missing his third straight game for the Seahawks with an ankle injury. He has yet to return to practice and could face a longer absence.
Henry has yet to make his debut for the Seahawks after being signed to the active roster from the Washington Commanders' practice squad in Week 4.
Surratt is dealing with a calf injury that has held him out for most of the season. His last game took place in Week 3 against the Washington Commanders.
O'Toole popped up on the injury report with a hamstring injury but was limited in practice on Friday after sitting out on Wednesday and Thursday. Unfortunately for him, he did not make enough progress to be on the active roster for the game.
Stephens, a fifth-round pick out of Iowa, is the lone healthy scratch for the Seahawks, with Anthony Bradford back in the mix for the team.
Kickoff between the Chiefs and Seahawks is scheduled for 5:20 pm PT inside Lumen Field. Fans can watch the game on NBC or streaming on Peacock.

title: Seahawks Reportedly Considering  Trade for Colts RB Jonathan Taylor
full_text:
It’s getting to that time of year when rumors are heating up. Some teams are becoming buyers to improve their roster, while other teams are sellers to help the rebuilding process. The Seattle Seahawks look to be at the top of the buyers list as they desperately need to improve a portion of their roster.
​The Indianapolis Colts, on the other hand, are on the verge of nearly a complete rebuild after firing general manager Chris Ballard. Based on reports from ESPN’s Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter , the Colts are putting many of their best players on the trade block. This is an opportunity for the Colts to start over and the Seahawks should be among their biggest trade partners .
The Seahawks are one of four prime teams to be connected to Colts running back and three-time Pro-Bowler Jonathan Taylor. He should be one of the best players who are realistically on the trade block. Taylor is on a two-year, $44 million deal that he signed before the season because the franchise thought the team would be more competitive than a 2-4 record and coming off a bad loss to the Tennessee Titans.
​Taylor is in the prime of his career at 27 years old. Through six games this season, he rushed for 492 yards and seven touchdowns on 122 carries. He also caught 15 receptions for 163 yards. Taylor has a chance to replicate another stellar season no matter who he plays for. He rushed for 3,016 yards and 29 touchdowns on 626 carries and 64 receptions for 514 yards and three touchdowns.
​The Seahawks are a mess on the offensive side of the ball due to a lack of explosiveness in the run game, poor play-calling or development and the high number of turnovers, especially from quarterback Sam Darnold . The Seahawks had Darnold take 51 passing attempts, take five sacks and a couple of runs escaping the pocket in the Week 6 loss to the Denver Broncos.
Seattle has no explosiveness in the run game behind power backs Emanuel Wilson and George Holani. Rookie Jadarian Price is still on IR with a chest injury and there’s no indication when he will return. Meanwhile, veteran Zach Charbonnet practiced as a full participant this week, but he ended up being ruled out for Sunday night’s game versus the Kansas City Chiefs.
​The Seahawks need immediate help with the running game and need to save the season before the lack of a run game causes them to lose more games. Taylor could get his second-ever playoff appearance and possibly get his first playoff win. He would also be a perfect fit for the Seahawks’ run game and offensive coordinator Brian Fleury.
​The Seahawks might be interested in Taylor, but he might not be the only player they are targeting from the Colts. Seattle would be a great place for 30-year-old guard and eight-time Pro-Bowler Quenton Nelson to be sent to. Nelson would be the leader of a talented Seahawks offensive line that has regressed from an impressive season last year .
​Nelson could be the starting guard, which leaves questions over Anthony Bradford, who is back after missing five games for Seattle but is in the final year of his rookie contract. There are questions over Grey Zabel, who has struggled significantly in his second year in the league. Nelson’s addition would easily answer one of the questions and dramatically improve the run game and the pass protection.
​The Seahawks shouldn’t think of Nelson as a backup option, but more of a 1-B option. If general manager John Schneider wanted to shake things up in the NFL, he could trade for both Taylor and Nelson and have them stay as teammates. Seattle would’ve had to give up a lot for both players, but this is a chance for the team to get back into the playoff standings and the NFC West Division.

title: Seahawks-Chiefs Week 7 Showdown Features Two Must-Watch Player Battles
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks have a tough test on Sunday Night Football in Week 7 as they host the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs . There will be no shortage of intriguing matchups to watch between the defending champions and the AFC juggernaut.
One key will be seeing how the defensive-minded Mike Macdonald handles the offensive genius Andy Reid. There will also be the matchup between the Seahawks front seven and their former star running back, Kenneth Walker III.
As interesting as those battles will be, PFF's Bradley Locker has two individual matchups on his mind for this showdown. Locker named the best player matchups in Week 7 , and two of those will take place on Sunday Night Football.
There's no player on either side of the ball that means more to the Seahawks' success than Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Even when their defense is absolutely shutting opponents down, the only way they win is if JSN shows up and gives them a solid performance. The good news for Seattle is that he does that with unreal consistency.
The defending NFL Offensive Player of the Year is again playing out of his mind and Locker says his matchup with stellar rookie Mansoor Delane will be one of the top matchups to watch this year. Normally, a veteran such as JSN would have his way with a rookie, but Delane has not been an ordinary first-year player.
"Smith-Njigba looks like a player seriously vying for his second straight Offensive Player of the Year award. His 92.3 PFF receiving grade ties for the positional lead, while his 3.55 yards per route run are second among receivers. Moreover, Smith-Njigba ranks in the top 10 in yards per route run against both man and zone looks, indicating that there’s no surefire way to slow him down," Locker wrote.
"Delane has been everything the Chiefs could’ve hoped to start his pro campaign. The sixth overall pick has compiled an 81.4 PFF coverage grade, the fifth-highest among cornerbacks with at least 120 coverage snaps. Delane has permitted only a 63.8 passer rating when targeted as well."
Through six games, JSN has 49 receptions for 717 yards and seven touchdowns. Cooper Kupp is second in receptions (16) and yardage (179) and no other receiver has more than one touchdown. Smith-Njigba is the offense right now and if Delane can slow him down, that would be a huge help for the road team.
Leonard Williams might be 32 years old, but you could never tell by how he's playing this season. The big man has been wildly disruptive and as Locker says, he's had a ton of success over the right guard. That means Trey Smith will need to be at his best to slow Williams down.
"Williams has taken 103 snaps over the Right A-B gaps and 100 over the Left, which means he should get reps against both Smith and left guard Kingsley Suamataia. He’s been more effective rushing the passer against right guards, generating a 71.2 PFF pass-rush grade in those situations — making his battle with Smith all the more fascinating," Locker wrote.
This one will be a lot of fun to watch, but the same could be said of Byron Murphy II against either Smith or Kingsley Suamataia. The Chiefs have a strong interior line, especially with Creed Humphrey in the mix at center. This will be strength vs. strength, which leaves fans as the biggest winners.

title: Seahawks Confidence Meter: Was the Mini-Bye Taken Seriously?
full_text:
Every great team has some struggles during a portion of a season. The Seattle Seahawks (3-3) are currently in a serious struggle after losing three of their last four games , including the 17-14 road loss to the Denver Broncos on Thursday Night Football in Week 6. The reigning Super Bowl champions wouldn’t make the playoffs if the season ended before Sunday.
The Seahawks have to face the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs (5-0) on Sunday Night Football. Kansas City has the momentum and a better run game led by former Seahawks running back Kenneth Walker III. The Seahawks might have the home field advantage and the recent Super Bowl success, but that won’t matter on Sunday. There is one thing that should help the Seahawks, however.
​The Seahawks are a mess right now due to their lack of efficiency in the run game and the turnovers that have cost them three victories. The coaching staff has been unable to fix the team between games, especially the four-day gap after the San Francisco 49ers and before the Broncos.
​Seattle, however, has no excuse now as they have the Week 7 preparation and the three extra days following the loss to Denver. They need to show how much better the Seahawks have become and how more efficient on offense through the mini-bye. The Seahawks had more time to figure out and change some of the foundations of their offense. They had more time to prepare for the Chiefs than they did with the Seahawks.
​The Seahawks are somehow favorites versus the Chiefs despite having no momentum, no signs of a run game with veteran Zach Charbonnet still out and losing three of the last four games. Quarterback Sam Darnold has been at the center of the Seahawks’ losses by throwing seven interceptions in the four games played.
​The Seahawks have talked about how the team needs to improve from their mistakes, but they’ve been promising since the horrible loss to the Washington Commanders in Week 3. At some point, words are meaningless and if the offensive coaching staff continues to play the less-explosive and less-efficient players at running back, the offensive line continues to get bullied in bursts and Darnold turns the ball over in key moments, then it shows the team isn’t taking their season seriously.
​Head coach Mike Macdonald has to lead the team to urgency or otherwise, the Seahawks could be 3-4 after Week 7. There is a great chance the Seahawks could fall to 3-5 after Week 8’s Monday Night Football matchup at the Chicago Bears (5-2). It will take a team effort to prove the Seahawks can get back into the playoff conversation, or no trade for running back Jonathan Taylor or guard Quenton Nelson will save them.

title: Seahawks Are Not Showing Real Concerns After Charbonnet's News
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks (3-3) have a must-win game in Week 7 as they host the Kansas City Chiefs (5-0) on Sunday Night Football. This has to be the Seahawks' get -right game, or they will be under .500% past Week 3 for the first time since the 2024 season. One of the biggest things that the Seahawks must fix is their lack of impact from the running game, player utilization and turnovers.
​The Seahawks were preparing for veteran running back Zach Charbonnet to return on the field for the first time since tearing his ACL in last season’s Divisional Round over the San Francisco 49ers. He was a full participant in practices, but on Friday, he was ruled out. This comes at horrible timing as the Seahawks are now left with a depleted and talentless backfield before taking on an undefeated team.
​To go from a full participant in practices to now being out is highly questionable. The only two suggestions are that the Seahawks are putting Charbonnet on the trade block for another running back like the Indianapolis Colts’ Jonathan Taylor . The other theory is that they are taking one more week for him to fully get in shape and take a huge amount of carries.
This isn’t the time for a 3-3 Seahawks team going into Week 7 to be playing games. If the 2026 NFL Season ended now, the Seahawks would be left out of the playoffs and they still have to host the undefeated Chiefs and then go on the road to take on the Chicago Bears (5-2) for Monday Night Football. There is a real chance that the Seahawks could be 3-5 by the time they head into Week 9 .
​They’ve rarely taken opportunities to improve their run game. Outside of signing undrafted rookie Robert Henry Jr. off the Washington Commanders practice squad, the front office hasn’t added another valuable running back to the roster. The Seahawks worked out former two-time Pro-Bowler Joe Mixon, but they didn’t like his physical.
​In the first two games of the season, the Seahawks averaged 129.5 rushing yards. They accomplished this by mixing Price with a power back like Wilson and Holani. The Seahawks only averaged 96 yards through the last four games when the turnovers increased and Price was put on IR after Week 3. Seattle put their entire running game on Wilson and Holani, who are both short-yardage running backs with no power or explosiveness.
​As a result of the running game being less efficient, the Seahawks have put too much pressure on quarterback Sam Darnold, who has regressed in his turnovers and decision-making . Darnold had 51 passing attempts, escaped several times for runs and was sacked five times. The Seahawks need a reliable run game in some way on Sunday night for a chance at winning.
​The Seahawks’ coaching staff seemed scared to utilize new schemes or new players. Wide receiver Rashid Shaheed took a pitch handoff for a 28-yard touchdown in the Week 4 win over the Los Angeles Chargers and he had only one rushing attempt in the losses to the San Francisco 49ers and the Denver Broncos. Veteran Velus Jones Jr. is a faster running back, but he only had four carries for 20 yards against the Broncos. Meanwhile, Henry has yet to play a game for the Seahawks.
​If the Seahawks want to create a more balanced offense, they need to have their offensive line create more push at the line of scrimmage. They also need to be smart about who gets the carries. This means fewer carries for Wilson and Holani and more for Jones and Henry. The more the Seahawks don’t take their running game issues seriously, the worse the team’s chances for the playoffs get.

title: 3 Reasons for Optimism After 49ers Loss to Falcons
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers' 29-20 loss to the Atlanta Falcons was not pretty . However, there are some positive spins that can be taken away from the game. What can 49ers fans lean on after the loss?
The schedule makers did not make life easy on the 49ers. First, they gave them a Monday Night Football game at home, which is helpful. However, the downside to that is a short week ahead. The 49ers not only had a short week, but they also had to travel across the country and play the game at 10 AM on the West Coast.
So, due to the game being played 32 hours after the Falcons, the team could not acclimate as quickly. More than that, the 49ers had the bye week to look ahead to. It would be easy to rest some players that had questionable injuries due to the inconvenience and lack of time to heal.
It is easy to see how the game got away from them.
San Francisco could have had a few names come back this week, but the short turnaround and bye week made it easy to rest players. Beyond that, they had a three-game lead in the division entering the day. So, they could take things easy this week. The plus side to that is they should come out of the bye week much healthier.
Nick Bosa, Deebo Samuel, and Mike Evans should all be back. Demarcus Robinson and Marques Sigle are likely not too far behind. Plus, guys like George Kittle, Christian McCaffrey, and Trent Williams get a week to reset. The bye week was well-timed for the 49ers this year.
The loss is not going to stop the 49ers from buying. If anything, it exposed a few holes that might need to be plugged. The team is going to need some defensive line help. Wide receiver is also an expected addition at the deadline. Still, left guard has not been talked about much, but it has been established as a need.
The lack of cornerback depth was also exposed in the 49ers loss. These are positions that were not discussed and could have bitten them down the line. Now, the 49ers can address it at the trade deadline.
