title: Two New 49ers' Trade Needs Exposed in Falcons Loss
full_text:
There have been three needs for the San Francisco 49ers that have been discussed for weeks. Most would agree that if San Francisco makes a move at the trade deadline, it will be a wide receiver, an edge rusher, or an interior defensive lineman.
However, after the 49ers lost 29-20 to the Atlanta Falcons in Week 7, there have been a few more needs that are starting to emerge. What else can the 49ers do at the trade deadline?
The team has been able to get by with Connor Colby for the past few weeks, but now it is starting to look like it is becoming a problem. Colby looked like he had taken a step in year two, but as the competition improved, he struggled.
It started against Byron Murphy and Leonard Williams against Seattle. Then, Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw got the best of him on Monday Night Football. The Falcons' interior is not great, but Gervon Dexter beat Colby consistently.
The 49ers have Carver Willis, but he is a rookie, and he has been hurt for most of the regular season. That would be a risk to put him in, even with a bye week to adjust.
Landon Dickerson of the Philadelphia Eagles and Quenton Nelson of the Indianapolis Colts could surprisingly be available. The 49ers might have to make a move.
Coming into the season, the 49ers secondary looked deeper than past years. Injuries have not helped, but the group is starting to get exposed. It might force a deadline move. Upton Stout and Marques Sigle are expected to come back soon, and that can remedy some of the issues.
However, San Francisco has had to play dime with Stout out, and their extra defensive back continues to be an issue. Jack Jones has been awful when the team plays dime. With Stout out, he started on the outside, and Deommodore Lenoir moved into the slot. It did not go well.
However, their other option is sticking safety Ashtyn Davis in the slot, and that does not work either.
Malik Mustapha was benched to start the season, Sigle was benched last year. Ji’Ayir Brown has played so poorly he will likely get benched when Sigle is back. All three are ahead of Davis, who is playing now. Whether it be a depth cornerback or safety, they could make a move.

title: 49ers' Grades After 29-20 Loss to the Falcons: Brock Purdy Loses the Game
full_text:
ATLANTA -- The San Francisco 49ers just lost 29-20 to the Atlanta Falcons . Here are the 49ers' grades for this performance.
Brock Purdy lost this game. To be fair, he didn't have his top-six wide receivers (Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, Demarcus Robinson, De'Zhaun Stribling, Ricky Pearsall and Brandon Aiyuk). Still, he had George Kittle, Christian McCaffrey and Kyle Shanahan. Plus, Purdy had Jordan Watkins, who had a terrific game (more on him in a minute). If Purdy had put more air underneath his deep pass to Watkins, he would have scored a touchdown instead of getting tackled after a gain of 35 yards. In addition, Purdy threw two picks -- the first to a safety while trying to throw the ball out of bounds, and the second to a linebacker right in front of him whom he never saw. Finally, Purdy also turned the ball over on downs when he took a sack on fourth down. Purdy is still a good quarterback, but he can probably forget about the MVP Award after this performance. We thought he had improved, but it turns out he simply plays much better when Mike Evans is on the field (who doesn't?).
Christian McCaffrey was outstanding despite missing most of the first half with a quad injury. Kaelon Black also played well, minus his fumble. That was a crucial play in the game. Jordan James also fumbled, but the 49ers recovered. And Kyle Juszczyk caught a touchdown pass near the goal line. Overall, this position is not the reason the 49ers lost.
George Kittle caught eight passes for 88 yards despite the Falcons bracketing him most of the game, but also fumbled on the final drive. To be fair, the 49ers already had essentially lost at that point. Still, it's unusual to see Kittle put the ball on the ground.
Sure, they're a bunch of backups, but none of these guys turned the ball over. Of course, Christian Kirk did nothing -- I still don't know why the 49ers signed him. But Jacob Cowing was decent, and Jordan Watkins was good. He finished with three catches for 56 yards. One of those catches should have been a long touchdown, but Purdy underthrew him. He also had another play in which he was wide open deep, but Purdy never saw him. Finally, Watkins nearly made an incredible touchdown catch, but he didn't control the ball after hitting the ground. The emergence of Watkins as a legitimate threat is one of the main silver linings from this loss. The 49ers have to get him more involved in the offense after the bye week.
They gave up two sacks, but also helped pave the way for the offense to gain a whopping 5.3 yards per carry. This position group is the least of the 49ers' issues as they approach the trade deadline.
They limited Bijan Robinson to just 3.2 yards per carry, which is extremely impressive, but they also recorded zero sacks against a subpar quarterback who doesn't move particularly well. The 49ers just let him stand still unbothered all game like he was watching waves at the beach. They really need to trade for DeForest Buckner as soon as possible. They need more pass rushers.
Fred Warner had 13 tackles and Dre Greenlaw had 12. Impressive. And they didn't hit anyone helmet-to-helmet or out of bounds, which is even more impressive for them.
They gave up three touchdown passes and a 118.9 passer rating to Michael Freaking Penix Jr., which never should happen. Granted, the 49ers had no pass rush. Still, the coverage was so soft, it was hard for the defensive linemen to get home. That's because Upton Stout missed the game with a shoulder injury, and his replacement was Jack Jones, who's awful. When the Falcons picked on him, the 49ers replaced him with Ahstyn Davis, who's worse. Finally, the 49ers put Ephesians Prysock in the game, which was smart -- he's better than Jones and Davis. Strange it took the 49ers so long to figure that out.
They gave up multiple long kickoff returns, and Eddy Pineiro missed his fourth extra point of the season and his seventh kick in seven games. He is one of the worst extra-point kickers the league has seen since it moved back the extra point roughly 10 years ago. Too bad the 49ers gave him a four-year extension this offseason, because he's gotta go. The 49ers need to replace him before he costs them any more games. Because as poorly as the 49ers played, they would have been down just one score on the final possession if Pineiro hadn't missed an extra point earlier in the game. Cut him.
Raheem Morris' defense wasn't great, but it succeeded in its main objective, which was keeping Bijan Robinson in check. He never scored. The biggest reason the 49ers lost, other than their kicker missing yet another extra point, was the offense. It stunk. It turned the ball over five times -- two interceptions, two fumbles and one turnover on downs. The running game was working, and the 49ers had the lead in the second half, and yet Kyle Shanahan fell in love with the passing game, just like last week. He called 42 passes and just 21 runs, which is inexplicable considering the 49ers were missing so many wide receivers. Fortunately, the 49ers still are 6-1, and they have a bye week coming up, so Shanahan can look himself in the mirror, acknowledge that he coached poorly the past two weeks, and fix his mistakes. The Super Bowl run depends on it.

title: 8 Biggest Takeaways From 49ers' Week 7 Loss to Falcons
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers suffered their first defeat of the season to the Atlanta Falcons , 29-20. It was an ugly performance by the 49ers, with so many self-inflicted wounds. Let's dive into the eight biggest takeaways from their Week 7 loss.
You would've thought that the 49ers took melatonin before they played the Falcons. They looked so drowsy for the majority of this game, but it was to be expected, as I predicted they would lose here .
The 49ers have played in tough back-to-back games and had to fly to the East Coast to play the Falcons, who have a rest advantage.
Their sloppiness proved it. The penalties were egregious, the turnovers were high, and the star players didn't show up consistently. The Bye Week is arriving at the perfect time for the 49ers.
The 49ers opened up the game with a heavy workload for Christian McCaffrey. It was working well until he suffered a quad injury, forcing him to leave in the first half.
Thankfully, he returned to the game and didn't seem hampered by it. McCaffrey was getting worked on extensively on the sideline to help loosen his muscles.
However, that's been the case in every game this season. The broadcast pans to McCaffrey with a trainer or a massage gun to help keep him loose, indicating that his body can no longer handle a heavy workload.
It was an amazing start to the game for rookie Kaleon Black. He was on the verge of a breakout game, and it still kind of was. Unfortunately, Black lost a fumble that set up a scoring drive for the Falcons.
After that fumble, the 49ers' offense was never the same. As solid as Black performed, his fumble overshadowed it all. The 49ers wouldn't feature the rookie much after that.
The first-half game plan for the 49ers was a heavy dose of running the football. Even though Kyle Shanahan has the "MVP" quarterback, he elected to run the ball more often than not.
It's proof that Shanahan hates his wide receivers. It wasn't until the 49ers were trailing in the second half that he started to dial up more pass plays, and it actually worked to a degree.
Jordan Watkins almost had a couple of amazing plays, but needs to learn how to keep the ball secured. In any case, the 49ers will have one or two of their injured receivers back after the Bye Week.
It's starting to look like the real MVP is Mike Evans, not Brock Purdy. Without Evans, the 49ers' offense is a shell of itself. In the last six quarters without Evans, they've only mustered 23 points.
Of those 23 points, only one came from a passing touchdown. Meanwhile, Purdy has thrown two interceptions. An MVP quarterback shouldn't need to rely on one player, but Purdy clearly does.
A performance like this should quiet down the ridiculous MVP talk with Purdy. He's a terrific player, but MVP? It's October. Anyone engaging in MVP discussions this early in the season is delusional. Let's wait until December before pushing this narrative.
For crying out loud, please get cornerback Jack Jones off the field for good. Every time he's out there, he's flagged for a penalty. He's essentially a penalty machine.
The Falcons made it a point to target whoever Jones was in coverage against, knowing that they could either win the rep or most likely earn a penalty in their favor.
I'd rather see rookie Ephesians Prysock than Jones. At least Prysock gives the 49ers long-term value with growth through reps played. Jones is a liability and should never see the field again.
The 49ers must go for two points after scoring a touchdown. Kicker Eddy Pineiro is unreliable. He's had the yips all season, with zero signs of getting out of it.
Maybe the Bye Week is arriving at a perfect time for him to reset. But I imagine the 49ers will look at which kickers they could bring in while they're off. Enough is enough.
Speaking of moves the 49ers can make, an edge rusher trade is needed. Their pass rush wasn't a factor in this game, and I know the entire defense was drowsy, but this is what their pass rush is.
John Lynch needs to call the Los Angeles Chargers for Khalil Mack or the Indianapolis Colts to bring DeForest Buckner back. As long as they add an impactful player there, it'll be huge for them.

title: 49ers LT Trent Williams Hints at Delaying Potential Retirement Plans
full_text:
This offseason left tackle Trent Williams implied his new contract could very well be his last with the San Francisco 49ers.
Williams has proven year after year in recent seasons that age is just a number. At 38, he’s still playing like one of the best offensive linemen in the league. It’s incredible to witness .
But he's hinted that he might stay longer.
Williams' contract expires after the 2027 season, stating when signed it could very well be his last.
“I still feel like I’ve got some good football left in me, and I’d rather walk away while I’m still playing at a high level than get run out of the league," shared Williams at the time of the new contract.
"It’s been a long journey. My daughter was born a few months before I got drafted, and now I’m heading into Year 17 while she’s about to turn 17 herself.
"As a father, you look up and realize how much time has passed. In a lot of ways, it feels like I’ve watched her grow up from a distance because of the demands of this job.
"Part of me thinks about being there when she goes off to college in a couple of years. I want to be accessible. I don’t want to hover, but I want to be close. I don’t want to be at a joint practice somewhere when she’s moving into school or going through those big life moments."
And that reason makes plenty of sense. Now, he's revealed a prior conversation with her that could lead to a change of heart and continue to compete for longer.
“I learned to just shut up and let it go,” Williams told NBC Sports Bay Area . “[Micah]’s like, I'm living a dream. Why would I cut it off? Why would I wake up if I don't have to?”
“God has blessed me and as long as he gives me the strength and the ability to do it at a high level, I don’t want to be doing myself a disservice if I didn't maximize everything I was blessed with.
“Just athletic ability, just mentality, these things are out of my control,” Williams said. “Things that God blessed me with that have allowed me to propel my name into the upper echelon of my position throughout history. If I have that much of a blessing, what am I doing trying to figure out when should I turn it off?"
He gave a three-word response when asked about staying longer and eventually joining the 49ers’ famous 10-year club, something tight end George Kittle and fullback Kyle Juszczyk achieved this year.
“Never say never,” Williams said, reportedly with a "sly smile."
Whatever he decides, he's had a truly incredible career and should decide on his own terms.

title: 49ers Expected to Pursue a Trade for Colts DT DeForest Buckner
full_text:
The 49ers almost certainly will make a big move before the NFL's trade deadline next month.
And that move, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter , could be to trade for the Pro Bowl defensive tackle the 49ers traded to the Colts in 2020. Yes, we're talking DeForest Buckner.
Buckner told the media after the Colts' latest loss that he's tired of the "same old song and dance," and the Colts reportedly are open to trading some of their star players, including Buckner, after firing general manager Chris Ballard a few days ago.
The 49ers drafted Buckner with the 7th pick in the 2016 draft, and he played for them through the 2019 season. Then, after losing the Super Bowl to the Chiefs in February 2020, they traded Buckner to the Colts for a first-round pick, which they used to draft Javon Kinlaw. =
The 49ers did this so they could extend Arik Armstead and Jimmie Ward, neither of whom is still on the team.
Now, the 49ers seem to want Buckner back. Of course they do. He's still a great player who should have spent his entire career with the 49ers, and they currently need a defensive tackle.
Technically, they need players at lots of positions because, once again, they're among the most injured teams in the NFL. But lots of their injured players are supposed to come back soon. That's why they might not trade for a wide receiver. Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, Demarcus Robinson and De'Zhaun Stribling all are supposed to come back soon.
Defensive tackle is another story. The 49ers lost Alfred Collins for the season -- he's not coming back until 2027. And he might never make a full recovery, considering he tore his patellar tendon. Former 49ers draft pick Drake Jackson tore his patellar tendon in February of 2025 and has appeared in just four games since then.
Which brings us back to Buckner. He would fill the 49ers' biggest need, he's available, and they could get him probably for a third-round draft pick. Plus, he's still in his prime. He has four sacks in six games this season. He would give the 49ers a closer on their defensive line in case Nick Bosa doesn't make a full recovery this season. And then, the 49ers could give Buckner an extension during the offseason, considering he'll be a free agent.
At this point, I fully expect the 49ers to trade for Buckner. That's because they know they're legitimate Super Bowl contenders, and the right move could put them over the top. Plus, the Seattle Seahawks might trade for Colts running back Jonathan Taylor, so the 49ers better do something big.

title: Why the 49ers Will Lose to the Falcons in Week 7
full_text:
A chance at 7-0 is staring the San Francisco 49ers square in the face.
All they have to do is take care of business on the road against the Atlanta Falcons . Then, they can rest easy during their Bye Week, knowing they’ve won an incredible seven games in a row.
However, defeating the Falcons will be a lot tougher than most people probably think. In fact, I think that the 49ers will lose to the Falcons in Week 7 and suffer their first defeat of the year.
This is not a normal week for the 49ers. A lot of factors are against them. For starters, the rest and travel disadvantage. The Falcons have a day's rest over the 49ers, who played on Monday night.
That game also went down to the wire, with the defense needing to be on the field a bunch, which makes it back-to-back games they’ve needed to do that. It wouldn’t be shocking if they’re reeling going into Week 7.
It's also an East Coast game, which means their body clocks will be at 10 a.m. PST. It only adds to the strain. I’d expect them to have a slow start and/or a sluggish finish.
To make matters worse, they don’t have any impactful wide receivers available. Mike Evans is out with an Achilles injury that he aggravated last week. Brock Purdy will not have his most reliable target.
They were already thin with Deebo Samuel (hamstring), Demarcus Robinson (ankle), and rookie De’Zhaun Stribling (ankle) out. San Francisco will face the Falcons with a depleted receiver group .
Purdy will have Jacob Cowing, Jordan Watkins, and veteran Brandin Cooks, who barely joined the team the other week. Of course, he’ll have George Kittle and Christian McCaffrey, so it’s not a total disaster.
Nevertheless, this game will demand that Purdy live up to his MVP narrative. That means taking care of the football, making plays out of structure when necessary, and trying to make the receivers around him better.
Easier said than done, of course. It’ll also require Raheem Morris to make this a revenge, which I’m sure he will. No one likes being canned from a place, essentially being told “you’re not good enough” for the job.
Morris may play it down, but he’s absolutely gunning to embarrass the Falcons. He’ll need his defense to come up with some turnovers to help the 49ers’ offense out.
Otherwise, it’ll make it a tight game, and given the battles the 49ers have fought in recent weeks, especially with the rest and travel disadvantage, they’re poised to drop this game.
The 49ers know they have the Bye Week after, and losing to the Falcons isn’t the end of the world. They can drop this game and still be a top team in the NFC and their division.
It won’t be detrimental to their season's success unless they completely free-fall coming out of the Bye or late in the season. The Falcons aren’t a great team.
But with several factors against the 49ers, it’s enough to see them lose their first game of the season.

title: 49ers Must Trade for an Edge Rusher After Latest Nick Bosa Update
full_text:
Nick Bosa thought he’d be able to play in Week 7 against the Atlanta Falcons .
Turns out, he never had a chance. The San Francisco 49ers ruled out Bosa and five other players for Sunday's contest in Atlanta. This makes five consecutive games that Bosa will have missed due to a calf injury.
The writing was on the wall when Bosa missed every practice this week. Strangely, he would tell reporters he thought he could play or would have a strong chance to, but it seems he was getting ahead of himself.
“I just think he was a little too optimistic, especially for Bosa because he's pretty accurate,” Kyle Shanahan said. “He doesn't say stuff like that unless it's accurate. I just think it surprised him.
“He worked out, after he said that to you guys, and the next day he was just a little sore, which surprised all of us. That wasn't a great sign, especially going to play on turf and stuff this week, so I think it was more he was just a little too optimistic.”
So, Bosa thought his calf was progressing, and once he tested it, he still felt issues. After this latest update, the 49ers must trade for an edge rusher .
There’s no way Bosa will stay healthy for the rest of the year. Whenever he returns, he will be under an indefinite microscope for the remainder of the season. Things could be fine for him on his return; then, after four games played, he’s inactive again.
No one should feel confident in Bosa’s status. The 49ers can’t place all of their chips on him anymore, waiting for him to help take their defense to the next level. They need to go get Khalil Mack from the Los Angeles Chargers .
Even reuniting with DeForest Buckner would be great. All they need is another defensive lineman who can come in and give them a boost. It has to be a player who offenses will make sure to game plan for. That way, the rest of the defensive linemen will have an easier time.
The entire defensive front has been lights out in the last two games. Their collective efforts have been a joy to watch. However, they’ll benefit greatly from an alpha in their ranks to take them to the next level.
That’s what makes Bosa’s looming return highly anticipated. But they can’t place all, if any, of their hope on him anymore. Not when they have a clear shot at a serious Super Bowl run.
Make a trade as soon as possible.

title: Grading The Buccaneers Dominating Win Over The Carolina Panthers
full_text:
It was one of the most dominant games in franchise history as the Tampa Bay Buccaneers coasted to a 43-13 win over the Carolina Panthers.
Many deserve credit for this victory, and we will be going over all of it in this one. Let's go over the top grades for the Bucs' Week 7 win.
Baker Mayfield did not do a lot in his return game, and he didn't need to. However, he did finish with 64 passing yards and a passing touchdown, with zero turnovers on the day and a 109.7 quarterback rating. He was the handoff king in this game, and that's 100% okay.
It was one of the best rushing games in franchise history for the Buccaneers. Bucky Irving had 24 carries for 106 yards and two touchdowns; Kenny Gainwell had 14 carries for 88 yards, and even Sean Tucker had seven carries for 52 yards and a touchdown as well.
This is what a peak Zac Robinson game can look like, as he was able to generate some great rushing teams while serving as offensive coordinator of the Atlanta Falcons. Here's hoping for more of this in the future.
Emeka Egbuka missed this game with a concussion, and there is not much else to speak about here. Tez Johnson was the best thing for this group, as he finished with three receptions for 47 yards and a touchdown. Chris Godwin also finished with four catches for 27 yards.
The tight end room gets this grade purely off of their blocking ability. Cade Otton, Payne Durham and Bauer Sharp were instrumental in the Bucs having a gigantic game on the ground, and they deserve plenty of credit for that.
These guys were absolute units in this one. When you lead the charge for an offense that generates 258 rushing yards and three touchdowns, you are getting a good grade. This group rose to the occasion in spades, and that's with Benjamin Chukwuma filling in for the injured Luke Goedeke in this matchup.
The players in this group were absolute all-stars in this game. Yaya Diaby led the way with three sacks, putting him second on the team this season. Vita Vea had a sack as well, and Al-Quadin Muhammad had a sack that forced a fumble, which was recovered by Calijah Kancey for the touchdown.
Overall, the Bucs defense finished with six quarterback hits, eight tackles for loss and five sacks on Panthers quarterback Bryce Young.
Josiah Trotter was solid in this game and led the Bucs with 10 total tackles on the day and a pass deflection. However, Anzalone still struggles to make tackles, and SirVocea Dennis got beat on a 50-yard touchdown in this game. With Christian Rozeboom on the injured reserve with a finger injury, Trotter is the saving grace of this group.
The defensive line wasn't the only group that had fun today. Tykee Smith had seven total tackles, one pass deflection, and an interception. Rookie Keionte Scott had a blocked extra point that fellow corner Zyon McCollum returned for two points. Speaking of McCollum, he also had an interception in this game as well as a pass deflection. Jacob Parrish got involved as well, with good coverage and a pass deflection.
Danny Smith has this special teams unit humming lately. There was a muffed punt return by former Buccaneers receiver David Moore that was recovered by Bucs special teamer Ko Keift. There was also the blocked extra point by Keionte Scott that was returned for two points by Zyon McCollum.
Finally, kicker Chase McLaughlin continues to be the best thing about the team and made all of his kicks for 11 points.

title: The Good, Bad and Ugly From Buccaneers' 43-13 Victory Over Panthers
full_text:
Through the first six weeks of the NFL season, we've had a lot of bad and ugly topics to discuss as it relates to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .
Week 7 was a different story, though, as the Buccaneers looked like the team that most people envisioned coming into the season. On Sunday, the Bucs completely dominated the Carolina Panthers in every facet of the game en route to a 43-13 victory on the road against the top team in the NFC South.
In a game the Buccaneers absolutely had to have, they finally executed with consistency and performed up to expectations.
Let's take a closer look at the good, the bad, and the ugly that we saw from the Buccaneers in their most impressive win of the season so far.
From the very start of the game, Bucky Irving established himself as the most dynamic offensive player on the field. Irving was patient, elusive, and explosive in space while rushing for 106 yards and 2 TD's on 24 carries.  Irving's unique ability to manipulate defenders by playing cat-and-mouse behind his blockers, and  then turning on the jets at the exact right moment to creative chunk plays was on full display in this game.
It wasn't just Bucky Irving, as both Sean Tucker and Kenneth Gainwell had plenty of success in their opportunities as well. The one constant? The offensive line. The entire unit was exceptional in this game, paving lanes in the run game while dominating the Panthers' defensive line.
The interior of Bredeson, Barton and Mauch really came to play in this contest, and they were clearly on the same page with whatever blocking scheme was being executed on a particular run.
Speaking of stepping up, even without Luke Goedeke in the lineup, Ben Chukwuma showed up in a big way by holding down the right side of the line, and his development as a quality reserve tackle so early in his career is a major positive for this team moving forward.
Bucs OL with one of the great first halves you’ll ever see. Obliterated Carolina on the ground and bought Baker a lot of time to make a couple out of structure plays
The Buccaneers' new offensive coordinator has taken plenty of heat, and rightfully so, for the team's poor offensive performance so far this year. That being said, it's important to give credit where credit is due, and Robinson deserves his flowers for sticking with what worked in Carolina.
It didn't take long for the Buccaneers' offense to assert their dominance in the run game, and Robinson had no problem sticking with that approach for the rest of the game as the Buccaneers rushed  for 49 times for a total of 258 yards on the ground, averaging over 5 yards per carry.
Not only did this allow the Bucs to control the clock and protect their lead, but it also ensured that Mayfield — nursing a recently dislocated thumb on his throwing hand — could, for the most part, stay out of harm's way.
Todd Bowles' defense looked like one of the NFL's best on this day. The vision Bowles has for his defense is a pressure applying group of front, backed up by a flock of ball hawks in the secondary, and that's exactly what we saw today, even without Antoine Winfield in the lineup.
Both Tykee Smith and Zyon McCollum came away with interceptions on the back end. Meanwhile, Calijah Kancey provided a scopp and score, which helped give the Buccaneers even more breathing room in the first half.
Sunday's game marks the first time that Tampa Bay's defense has amassed 5.0+ sacks and four-or-more takeaways in a single game since 10/26/25 at New Orleans.
Speaking of splash plays, the Bucs' gained some serious advantages in the special teams department today, with the punt coverage group recovering a fumble deep in Panthers' territory early in the game. Shortly thereafter, Tykee Smith blocked an extra point attempt, which McCollum then recovered and returned the length of the field for a rare 2-point addition to the scoreboard.
BLOCKED THE EXTRA POINT & TO THE HOUSE FOR ✌️ 📺: #TBvsCAR on FOX pic.twitter.com/G5ITN0VTcA
The Buccaneers defensive line had Bryce Young under serious duress for a good chunk of this game. When it was all said and done, the Bucs got home for 5 sacks on the day, with 3 of those coming from Yaya Diaby, who had a much needed breakout game in the sack department.
Al Quadin-Muhammad and Vita Vea supplied the other two QB sacks for the Bucs, and Kancey nearly got another one. The Buccaneers' offseason vision of a impactful committee of versatile defensive linemen applying pressure consistently materialized in this game, and would provide a big boost to the team if it continues in the weeks to come.
This is downright unfair considering the Bucs put up 43 points in a game where Mayfield was playing with a recently dislocated thumb, but if I have to nitpick, it would point to the lack of production through the air. Mayfield was 7/11 for 64 yards passing in this game, and although the team was wise to stick with the ground game, they'll need to develop a more balanced attack moving forward, which will require the passing game to wake up at some point.
Panthers really getting annihilated by a team that can barely throw a forward pass. NFC South is incredible
The trio of Irving, Gainwell and Sean Tucker made the Panthers' defenders at every level look downright silly in this game. As much as those Bucs' RB's ran with determination and elusiveness in this game, any time a team rushes for 250+ yards against an NFL defense, there's a problem.
Whether it was along the defensive line, the second level, or the secondary, Panthers' defenders simply could not bring down Buccaneer ball-carriers, and both the stats and tape will tell the same story.

title: Overreactions From Buccaneers' Blowout Win Over Panthers
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers needed a win on Sunday to stay alive and keep their season afloat, and boy, did they.
The Bucs absolutely routed the Carolina Panthers, drubbing their division rivals 43-13 on Sunday. The Bucs move to 2-5 on the year, and now, they're not too far off the NFC South lead as they head into Week 8.
Here are our three overreactions from the victory over Carolina:
Tampa Bay's entire secondary has been excellent so far in 2026 — a rare bright spot for the team. But that unit has been anchored by Zyon McCollum, and week in and week out, he continues to show everyone why.
McCollum has allowed just 9.6 per depth of target attempted, and he got his first interception on Sunday against the Panthers and Bryce Young. He also returned a blocked field goal for two points, giving him a score on the year as well.
McCollum has been a lockdown corner all year, and he had his best game Sunday. He's probably not in All-Pro contention with how bad the Bucs are and his lack of picks, but if he strings together a few more turnovers, he may be impossible to ignore — he's playing to the level right now.
The Buccaneers still have plenty of struggles, and they're unlikely to make the playoffs with the rough start they've had. But with a win against the Panthers, they are very much still in this division race.
With the win, the Panthers fall to 3-3 and the Bucs stand at 2-5. They're now just 1.5 games out of that division lead, and what's more, they'll also play the Atlanta Falcons at home next week.
If they win that game next week, too? The Bucs will be 3-5 with a shot to contend for the NFC South lead. It seems ridiculous, but with how paltry the entire division has been in 2026, a string of wins together could put the Bucs firmly in sight of the playoffs after a disastrous beginning to the season. Who would have thought?
Bucky Irving proved himself to be an absolute gamechanger once again for the Bucs. In both wins Tampa Bay has had, he's put up a stellar performance, and it's clear he's a major key in what this offense wants to accomplish.
Irving had over 100 yards rushing on the day. He accounted for two of Tampa Bay's touchdowns, and he was undeniably the X-factor in Tampa Bay's big division win. He had an unbelievable 26 touches on the day, funneling the entire offense through his effort.
He's staked his claim as one of Tampa Bay's best weapons. The Bucs probably shouldn't give him almost 30 touches every game, but they might want to make sure their offensive gameplan revolves around him more often than not.

title: Buccaneers’ Todd Bowles Gets Blunt Criticism From Leonard Fournette
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have had far from the start to the season they wanted. They're currently just 1-5 and hold the worst record in the NFC, and another loss to the NFC South-leading Carolina Panthers on Sunday would almost certainly spell doom for the team's playoff hopes.
A lot of the criticism for that start has been directed toward head coach Todd Bowles. Bowles has made the playoffs in all but one of his seasons as head coach of the Bucs, but he's only had double-digit wins a single time and he's had a losing record twice during that time span.
Bowles has faced plenty of criticism over recent weeks from all sorts of people in the NFL world. One of those people has been a former player of his, Leonard Fournette, who played under Bowles as head coach for one year in 2022.
Fournette expounded on that criticism during an appearance on the 4th & South podcast he hosts with former NFL player Jarvis Landry, and he had some honest thoughts on Bowles stemming from the year he played under him in Tampa Bay.
Fournette told Landry that whenever Bowles yelled at the team, he didn't take it seriously — he also mentioned that Bowles' mindset as a defensive head coach made him, in Fournette's eyes, not pay as much attention to the offensive side of the ball.
"He might yell, but it's not one of those yells you take [seriously]," Fournette said on the podcast. "I respect him, but it's like, [when Bruce Arians] got on your ass, he got on your ass... by Bowles being a defense-minded coach, he doesn't pay attention to the offense as much. So I don't know — maybe favoritism?"
In Fournette's only year with Bowles at the helm, he put up 668 yards on 189 attempts with three touchdowns on the ground. He also had three receiving touchdowns on the year.
Fournette's words hold some weight, given that he's played under Bowles, but it's also one opinion among many when it comes to Bowles. Bowles won 10 games in 2024 and also won a playoff game with the Bucs in 2023, so he has a record of success in Tampa Bay, but the problems with his tenure have also manifested themselves year after year as well.
Bowles and the Bucs will try to reverse his fortunes, along with his team's, when they play the Panthers at 1 p.m. on the road Sunday.

title: Our Buccaneers vs. Panthers Score Predictions Are In
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers face a grim outlook for the rest of the season if they fall to 1-6 on the year. They can prevent that by defeating the Carolina Panthers on Sunday, but it won't be easy to win their first division matchup.
The Bucs will have Baker Mayfield back in the fold after a three-game absence, but will that be enough to get a win? Our staff goes over our predictions for Sunday's matchup against the Panthers:
It’s been tough sledding for the Bucs, but they might just have a chance to turn things around.
Division play begins this week against the Panthers, and all signs point towards Baker Mayfield being back.
While I do believe things will look better, I still think the offense is way off from being able to match Carolina’s offense, which will put up points.
I think the Bucs will have a chance to win the game on the final drive, but ultimately fall short once again.
Mayfield's return is spoiled by the Panthers in this one. I simply think that Carolina is the better-coached team right now and that Mayfield may be slow to start back up after returning from his thumb injury.
The Buccaneers have played so poorly this season that they’re already on the verge of switching their primary focus from postseason contention to the top pick in next year’s NFL Draft. Considering we’re not even halfway through the season, I’d consider this season to be a full-scale nightmare for any Bucs fan.
So, am I picking the Buccaneers to bounce back and take down the NFC South-leading Panthers in Carolina, you ask? No. I most certainly am not.
The Panthers head into the game with the top passing attack in the league, and Bryce Young is playing at a high caliber. The Bucs and Todd Bowles have done a fair job of defending these types of offenses this season.
My biggest concern is the offense for Tampa Bay. It’s quite obvious Zac Robinson’s offense doesn’t have an identity and even with Baker Mayfield coming back, I just don’t see it changing much. They’ll have to begin proving me wrong before I pick them to win games. Also, a reminder — the Cowboys are a bad football team.
Tampa Bay's defense will be tested by a Panthers offense that playcaller Brad Idzik has unlocked this season. Bryce Young is stretching the football down the field in a dominant way, so expect the Panthers to score points.
Don't expect the Bucs to do much on offense in return. Zac Robinson's offense has been scattershot this whole season, and while Mayfield should play better than Jalon Daniels, he'll be playing with an injured thumb after a year where he didn't start off so hot anyway. Bucs have to be able to run the ball on Carolina — if they can't, they have no chance of winning.
The Buccaneers still haven't given us a reason to pick them to win a football game. They're 1-5 as it stands, and every BucsGameday staff member thinks they'll be 1-6 whenever they wake up in the morning.

title: Bucs Tabbed As Sellers at Trade Deadline if They Drop to 1-6
full_text:
The 2026 season has not gone the way that the Tampa Bay Buccaneers had hoped.
They have limped to a 1-6 record and there are no real signs that they might turn things around.
The defense has played up to par thus far, but the real issues have been on the offensive side of the ball.
If the Bucs want to remain relevant in the NFC South race to make the playoffs, the first step would be coming away with a victory against the Carolina Panthers.
If they are unable to do so, it appears that they will become sellers ahead of the NFL trade deadline in November.
"Bucs still in NFC South hunt, but a loss Sunday would put them at 1-6," ESPN's Jeremy Fowler posted on X . "If that happens, some in league expect TB to entertain seller mode at that point."
Dropping to 1-6 would be detrimental for Tampa Bay, taking the wind out of the sails that are already barely flapping.
If they indeed do drop to 1-6, it's hard to disagree with Fowler's expectations of them becoming sellers at the trade deadline.
The Bucs' top players have not lived up to their potential or contracts, so being able to dump some of them in order to acquire young, developmental players and/or future draft capital could be the move given a lost season.
While the season wouldn't necessarily be lost at 1-6, the writing would be on the wall that there is little hope of coming away with a successful season.
With Todd Bowles' seat scorching hot, the Bucs staff could look completely different come the offseason. And in turn, the roster turnover could be pretty heavy, so why not go ahead and get a head start?
Tampa has some young pieces to build around, but if they are to lose and become sellers, names like Chris Godwin, Vita Vea, Yaya Diaby, Antoine Winfield Jr., and potentially others will be at the forefront of who could be dealt.
Taking on dead cap money from some of these guys if they were to be traded would be tough, but at this point, it could be seen as the right move as the Bucs look to rebuild a roster that has become stale in certain areas.

title: Baker Mayfield Gets Special Help From World Series-Bound Rays
full_text:
Buccaneers' star quarterback Baker Mayfield has received some help from an unexpected source. According to Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times, the Tampa Bay Rays have helped create a special glove for Mayfield to use while he continues to recover from a dislocated thumb injury he suffered in the team's week three loss to the Minnesota Vikings at the end of the game.
The glove was made by the Rays clubhouse attendant, Nick Bond, and was made with multiple versions in mind, depending on what fits best for Mayfield.
The injury Mayfield suffered was to his throwing hand, and he will look to retain a good grip on the ball going forward in both throwing and scrambling situations. Mayfield himself was a fan of the glove and said that it felt good when used:
“(It’s) not restricting because it’s on the backside. ... For me, just getting used to it. I don’t feel the difference. It’s just like me wearing a glove.” Mayfield said when asked about how using the glove helps him.
For the past three games, Mayfield has sat on the bench while backup quarterback Jalon Daniels has started in his place. Daniels has done decently in relief, posting 501 passing yards, three passing touchdowns, five interceptions, and 126 rushing yards in three total starts.
However, the offense will have a different dynamic with Mayfield in once more at quarterback than Daniels and should open up more of what the team is able to do.
Mayfield will have a good amount of improvement in return from his injury, as he was struggling to begin the 2026 season before he went down. Fresh off a $55 million-per-year extension that saw the Bucs commit to Mayfield as their guy for the foreseeable future, Mayfield posted 615 passing yards, two passing touchdowns, two interceptions, 65 rushing yards, one rushing touchdown, and a handful of fumbles lost in three starts.
Now, Mayfield will look to drag the Bucs out of a brutal 1- 5 situation where the team has many more questions than answers. Time will tell whether the Buccaneers are able to regain some of their form with Mayfield out there, or if the team continues to regress and we simply look forward to a pretty rough season coming to an end for this team.

title: Baker Mayfield Reveals ‘Uncomfortable Meeting’ With Bucs’ Offense
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have been one of the worst offenses in the league thus far.
That's not what was expected coming into the season, but it is unfortunately the reality they find themselves in as we head into the thick of the year.
The running game hasn't been the issue, but more so the passing game and being consistent and efficient.
It hasn't mattered who has been leading the charge at quarterback either, but with Baker Mayfield back in the fold as starter, the hope is that things will start to improve.
And prior to Mayfield making his return, he highlighted a meeting that occurred about turning things around.
“We needed to have it. It's one of those things that's uncomfortable. You can't be sensitive in that. Everybody [has] a hand in it. It was from, I mean, it wasn't just about the last game. It was really more so talking about everything that we've done wrong," Mayfield said.
"The O-Line is playing better and better now, that we need to be detailed in the right spots, quarterbacks have to go through the right reads, have the feet on time. So, just harping on the fact that we're good when we do the right little things right, and so how consistent can we be and just see that thing come to life and go from there?”
Sometimes it's good to have uncomfortable conversations in order to right things, and that is the hope with the Buccaneers.
The offense must turn things around, and it begins with getting back into the weeds and focusing on the details.
Focusing on the little things should help, but everyone involved must be on the same page for this to work.
Mayfield must protect himself and the ball, Zac Robinson must be better at opening up the field and play calling, and the skill players must assert themselves as they have been absent for much of the season.
The idea is there and it seems that everyone involved is ready to right the ship and get the offense humming like we thought coming into the season.
If they are able to accomplish these things, it would be a great sign for how this team could finish out the season.
Getting right this week against the Carolina Panthers would be a huge step in the right direction, and would give the Bucs a huge first division win as they look to win the division and make the playoffs despite their disastrous start.

title: Buccaneers Hit With Major Blow Ahead of Panthers Matchup
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers' calamitous start to the 2026 season took another hit this week when two key starters , RT Luke Goedeke and WR Emeka Egbuka, popped up on the injury report ahead of the team's first NFC South matchup of the season vs. the Carolina Panthers.
As if the Buccaneers' struggles on the field hadn't been frustrating enough, a mysterious illness began making it's way around the Bucs' locker room this week, limiting the participation of numerous starters, including RB Bucky Irving, CB Zyon McCollum, DT Calijah Kancey, K Chase McLaughlin and P Riley Dixon at practice.
The case of Goedeke and Egbuka was more concerning, though, as both players were held out of practice completely on Wednesday and Thursday due to injury. Goedeke has been dealing with a calf injury, while Egbuka was listed out because of a potential concussion as well as a foot injury.
With how poorly the Buccaneers' offense has played so far this season, losing either Goedeke or Egbuka for this game, let alone both of them, would be a major hit to the Bucs' chances of winning a critical game on the road against the number one team in the NFC South Division.
On Friday, both Goedeke and Egbuka took the field for practice with their teammates, providing some much needed optimism that the offense may be at full strength for Sunday's game after all.
Interesting development on Friday this morning for the Bucs. Both Luke Goedeke and Emeka Egbuka are participating after not practicing the last two days. We’ll likely get confirmation Baker Mayfield starts Sunday from Bowles after practice and get word on Goedeke and Egbuka. pic.twitter.com/3xkpU5efdc
Even though both Goedeke and Egbuka returning to practice on Friday seemed like a very positive development, Todd Bowles quickly put that to rest when speaking with the media later in the day. Bowles stated that Goedeke will be out for the game, and it's unlikely that Egbuka will suit up either.
Todd Bowles “looks ready to go” and will start on Sunday against Panthers. Luke Goedeke will not play, while Emeka Egbuka’s availability remains uncertain. Bowles said Egbuka will need to have a “heck of a recovery” to be ready. pic.twitter.com/SfSMKs3uKd
For a team that is desperately clinging to any semblance of hope for this season, a loss to the Panthers on Sunday would not only drop the Buccaneers to a pitiful 1-6 record on the year, but it would also seal their fate as a team whose focus should immediately shift from competing for a playoff berth to competing for the first overall pick in next year's draft.
Losing Goedeke for this game is far from ideal, but if the Bucs were forced to face the Panthers without Goedeke and Egbuka in the lineup, their chances of knocking off Carolina to keep their hope alive for this season would immediately decrease by a significant margin. Even though it's just one game, the Bucs don't have any room for error at this point.
The presence of both Goedeke and Egbuka in the lineup is essential for the Bucs to knock off the Panthers in Carolina this Sunday, and, ultimately, keep their playoff hopes alive for at least one more week. With Goedeke now being ruled out, and Egbuka unlikely to play, things have gone from bad to worse for a Buccaneers team that has already dug itself a huge hole.

title: Todd Bowles Makes His Decision Between Baker Mayfield and Jalon Daniels
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are set to play the Carolina Panthers on Sunday in what could be the most important game of the year. The Bucs are 1-5 as it stands — a victory over the NFC South leaders would gain ground in the division and keep playoff hopes alive, while a loss could be the beginning of the end for Tampa Bay.
In a game like this, the Bucs will naturally want as many of their best players on the field. Perhaps the most important of those players, quarterback Baker Mayfield, has been off the field since Week 3 while he's been recovering from a dislocated thumb he suffered against the Minnesota Vikings.
In Mayfield's stead, undrafted free agent rookie Jalon Daniels has been starting for the Bucs at quarterback. Daniels has played admirably, even winning Tampa Bay's only game in Week 5 against the Dallas Cowboys, and when the week began, head coach Todd Bowles said that they'd begin preparing as if Daniels were set to play in his fourth start as Mayfield worked his way back.
Signs pointed toward Mayfield being ready to go this week, though, and now, Bowles has given us the confirmation we've been waiting for.
Bowles confirmed that Mayfield is ready to go and will start against the Panthers on Sunday, officially marking his return to the field for the first time since Week 3.
Todd Bowles says that Baker Mayfield “looks like he’s ready to go”, so he’ll start Sunday. Luke Goedeke is OUT — Emeka Egbuka needs to clear concussion protocol to play so Bowles said the team will see, but he’s currently still in protocol. pic.twitter.com/Znw8PO8QIr
Mayfield threw for 615 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions during his opening three-game stint. He also fumbled the ball three times, losing all of them to the defense.
Now, he's set to come back with some precautions, given the injury to his thumb. He's set to play with a glove that features a plate restricting movement in his injured thumb, which the Bucs' training staff developed with the Tampa Bay Rays. Mayfield told the media Thursday that the plate would not restrict his throwing motion, however.
Mayfield also mentioned that the biggest obstacle was taking impacts to his hand from snaps from center Graham Barton. He feels good about his ability to take those snaps on Sunday.
I think I was more so concerned about the impact of getting the ball from under center with Graham [Barton] sending it back there," Mayfield said. "It feels fine gripping it, throwing it — it's just the impact stuff, that was really what my concern was, and it's felt great so far.”
The Buccaneers play the Panthers — one of Mayfield's former teams — at 1 p.m. on Oct. 25.

title: Robert Saleh Denies Titans Have a QB Problem After Browns Loss, But Cam Ward's Stats Beg to Differ
full_text:
Any excitement that the Tennessee Titans earned from their Week 6 win over the Indianapolis Colts was more than betrayed in today's defeat. The Titans had the Cleveland Browns right where they wanted them in the first quarter, jumping out to a 14-0 lead through seven minutes.
What followed was a slow meltdown spelled by little to no consistent momentum. The offense scored late in the fourth quarter (on the ground, unsurprisingly), only for the Browns to march back down the field and easily secure a game-winning field goal, taking the victory 27-24.
The defense's regression is one thing, and that's issue is worth an entirely different discussion. But the hot topic right now is Cam Ward. More specifically, the topic is Ward's place in this offense.
Do the Titans have a QB problem? Robert Saleh doesn't think so, but Ward's numbers don't lie.
"I don't think it's a quarterback problem," Saleh said, when asked about the blame that has to go around as a result of the offense's consistent failures. "It's [the blame] all the way across the board. He [Ward] missed some throws that he's gotta make... but overall, there's enough to go around for everybody."
But who, exactly? Carnell Tate's fumble is the obvious example, but his five receptions for 69 yards led the team. The rookie WR also came down with a contested catch in the red zone that led to an easy game-tying score in the fourth quarter.
Tony Pollard did his part, scoring a tied-career-high three touchdowns and rushing for 129 yards. Ward was only sacked once today - the offensive line made good on their dues, too.
That leaves Ward himself. Look no further than the stat sheet for evidence that Tennessee's biggest issue is unfortunately under center.
Ward went 20/31 through the air, throwing an interception for the fifth week in a row. He's only thrown four touchdowns on the season up to now. Against Cleveland, the former first overall pick once again came short of 200 yards (with 181), while Deshaun Watson broke 300 for the other team.
Oh, and Ward didn't throw a score. We're past the point of patience and firmly in the realm of undeniable regression. With better protection and more playmaking options, Ward is worse this season than he was as a rookie.
The Titans wouldn't be 7-0 if Ward had improved; that isn't the point here. But could Tennessee have beaten the Giants in Week 3 if Ward hadn't thrown a pick on the goal line? Would the Titans have stood a chance against the Texans two weeks ago if the offense had generated a single touchdown?
Three or four wins would be a lot better than one and, even for the defense's faults, that unit has generated opportunities for the offense to pitch in. Even today, in allowing 27 points, the Titans had two takeaways.
If that doesn't sound like a QB problem, what is? The sooner Coach Saleh accepts that and opens the door to Ward's job, the sooner we see what the Miami product is made of when he's actually fighting for something in Nashville.
Until then, this is the product fans will have to get used to.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: 3 Major Takeaways From Titans' Heartbreaking Home Loss to Browns: Tony Pollard's Career Game Not Enough
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans entered today's matchup with the Cleveland Browns coming off their first win of the season. Momentum like that can't be wasted for a 1-5 team and a first-year head coach with his back against the wall.
That makes today's result the most disappointing of the year so far. The Titans fall to 1-6 at home in a more than winnable game. Between blown leads and lapses on either side of the ball, it's hard not to feel worse than ever about this franchise.
Here are our three major takeaways from the Titans' 27-24 loss, starting with a bright spot.
Pollard had a career game against the Cleveland Browns last season. His 161 yards and two scores propelled Tennessee to a late-season victory on the road.
Today, with both Tyjae Spears and Nick Singleton inactive, the Titans' RB1 had himself another huge day. Pollard punched in three touchdowns (tied for a career high), chalking up 129 yards on 25 carries. Pollard added 26 yards receiving to his total.
In the final year of his contract, Pollard has been one of Tennessee's most reliable weapons. His future in Nashville remains unsure. However, he'll be forced to carry a massive load so long as Ward and this offense fail to generate momentum elsewhere.
Even in a loss, Pollard had his best game of the 2026 season against Cleveland, and one of the best games of his career. The 29-year old deserves real flowers.
After a slow start to his first campaign as a Titan, offseason pickup Cor'Dale Flott had his second straight interception today.
Flott picked off Deshaun Watson in the first quarter, lending the Titans some of the early momentum that allowed Tennessee to pull out to a 14-0 lead. That lead was lost, brought to a tie, and then Tennessee's defense fell apart on the final drive, ultimately losing. Deshaun Watson threw for an inexcusable 308 yards.
Still, especially compared to fellow signee Alontae Taylor's struggles in the secondary, Flott's rising ability to force turnovers is a promising trend for Saleh's defense. The d-line looked worse, and the Browns put up 27 points.
Flott gets credit nonetheless for his singular ability to force a turnover. You take what you can get, especially in a game like this one.
It would've been hard for Ward to fall short of his 11/22, 102-yard performance from last week's contest against the Indianapolis Colts. He got better today, but the Titans still need more from their QB.
Ward went 20/31 through the air for no scores, one interception, and of course, a loss. The second-year QB made a few passes that had to be blamed on his WRs. Carnell Tate fumbled, Wan'Dale Robinson dropped. It wasn't all on Ward today.
But Tennessee's passer still failed to make up for the defense's shortcomings today, with 181 yards. Where Saleh's defense won in spite of the offense last week, Ward failed to make up the necessary ground when the Browns' offense pulled away today.
The defense fell apart on the final drive, but are the Titans even in that position if Tennessee capitalizes on a goal-line opportunity to take a two-score lead in the first half? The Titans need more from everyone, though especially their first overall pick.

title: The 1 Obvious Way Titans Can Capitalize on Best First Half of Season and Beat the Browns
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans scored 14 points in the first seven minutes of today's game. Nissan Stadium was rocking at an undeniable season-high, and the home team appeared to be in full control of the contest against the Cleveland Browns.
As things typically go with the 2026 Titans, that momentum didn't last for the entire half. One goal-line stand by Cleveland was the difference between Tennessee retaking a two-touchdown lead early in the second quarter. What could've been a 21-7 advantage for the Titans melted into a 17-14 deficit at the half.
But this was still easily the team's best first half of the year, and there's plenty of reason to think that the Titans can build on that in the second period. Cleveland's offense is likely to keep testing Tennessee's defense through the air - Cor'Dale Flott already has a pick, but the Titans are on their heels.
A successful second half - and historic second straight win - is within reach for Robert Saleh's Titans. The team just needs to play to their strengths in the second half, and be unafraid of keeping their foot on the pedal if Tennessee pulls back into the lead.
That strength is clear: Tony Pollard is having a dominant game. Scheme for the veteran at all costs.
Cam Ward's second-quarter interception, thrown behind WR Elic Ayomanor and right into the hands of CB Denzel Ward, should tell the Titans everything they need to know about the offense today. Once again, the passing game isn't here, at least not reliably.
Pollard, on the other hand, has 16 carries for 92 yards and two touchdowns. He had a third score reversed, which led to that unfortunate fourth-down stand. Per PFF, he had the most first-quarter yards of any RB this season, with 87.
Still, this is Pollard's second breakout performance vs. the Browns in a row. Last December, the back rushed for a career-high 161 yards and two touchdown in a Tennessee victory. Something about this matchup works for Pollard, and the Titans shouldn't shy away from that.
The obvious complication here is the absence of both Tyjae Spears and Nick Singleton in the backfield. The Titans are trotting out fourth-string RB Michael Carter, who has yet to be trusted with a carry in today's matchup.
Again, Ward passing 7/11 for 58 yards, the aforementioned interception, and no scores, leaves Tennessee with little choice in the matter. As Cleveland's offense starts to pick up steam, it will likely be up to Pollard to help extend Titans drives in the final two quarters.
Trade candidate or not, our complaints about Pollard being used as a workhorse in this offense are moot today. The Titans need a win, and so long as Pollard is effective, he's the key.

title: Titans' Inactives vs. Browns: Alontae Taylor's Return Highlights Relatively Healthy Tennessee Team
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans are set to host the Cleveland Browns as they try to win consecutive games for the first time in nearly four full years.
To do so, they’ll have to make it happen without two notable offensive playmakers: RB Tyjae Spears and WR Calvin Ridley have both been ruled out, along with RB Nick Singleton, TE Kylen Granson, T Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, DT Jackie Marshall, and CB Jaylon Jones.
Spears and Singleton both being out means an already struggling backfield will now be forced to rely on the likes of RBs Julius Chestnut and Michael Carter whenever RB Tony Pollard needs a breather.
Ridley being out is also notable since he's one of the Titans' most intriguing trade candidates . The conspiracy theorists within the fanbase are already coming up with their own theories as to why he's actually inactive for this game. Nonetheless, he won't be out there later today. As for the Browns, QB Tayler Green (3rd QB), LB Justin Jefferson, CB Noah Igbinohene, RB Audric Estime, DT Mike Hall Jr., and C Parker Brailsford have all been ruled out.
The most notable name not on that list is CB Denzel Ward, who was questionable with a hand injury, but he is officially active for the Browns.
He will undoubtedly see his fair share of WR Carnell Tate throughout the game, so if he’s not 100 percent, this could be something the rookie can possibly take advantage of as the game unfolds, especially in situations when they get into hand fighting for position and/or 50-50 balls.
Arguably the biggest news of the day is CB Alontae Taylor returning to the lineup after being a healthy scratch last Sunday. HC Robert Saleh announced that Taylor did some work at nickel throughout the week, and that’s rather noteworthy because that’s a position he’s been successful at in the past.
The Titans signed the former Vols star in hopes of him being their top boundary corner for the foreseeable future. Unfortunately, it’s become clear rather quickly that Taylor may not be best suited for that role after all.
It’ll be interesting to see how much Taylor plays today, especially at nickel since CB Marcus Harris has already established himself as this team’s best nickel.
Will we see any secondary packages with Harris on the outside and Taylor inside? And if so, how well does that work? Only time will tell.
Shaun is a longtime Titans fan who has years of experience in the field. He missed being on the team beat, and is here to change that. He also writes scripts for EA Sports' Madden games, where fans may have heard his work.

title: Titans' Home Matchup vs. Browns: 3 Things Tennessee Fans Should Expect on Game Day
full_text:
There's hope in the air in Nashville right now. The Tennessee Titans are coming off their first win of the season. With healthy playmakers and more momentum than they've had all year, today's matchup with the Cleveland Browns presents a window for Tennessee to get back on track.
"Back on track" for a 1-5 team may simply mean winning another game. But if the Titans do so, it will be the first time they've won back-to-back contests since 2022. You have to take that, no matter the context.
As for what to expect from Week 7, we've got three things to look out for as the Titans host the Browns, starting with a positive note on one of the team's brightest spots.
This may be an easy one, but Tate's continued emergence as an elite WR despite the offense around him is impossible to ignore.
The rookie pass-catcher caught six of his seven targets last week vs. the Colts, including one touchdown, on his way to 70 total yards. Per Mike Herndon, he's had the most productive first six games of any receiver in Titans history.
Even at Cam Ward's worst - last week certainly qualified - he's finding ways to get Tate involved. Duds are growing few and far between for Tate, and no matter how things go against the Browns, it's safe to say that Tate will have more than his fair share of opportunities to run away on the stat sheet.
Deshaun Watson throws the ball a lot, regardless of how many passes he's completing. The Browns' offense has struggled in the past two weeks (we'll touch on that trend), but that isn't for a lack of trying. This puts the Titans' secondary in an especially important spot.
Watson has thrown for 1,174 yards this season, notching seven touchdowns to just two picks. He's attemtping an average of 29 passes per game, with a season-high 33 attempts coming twice in a row against the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Jets in Weeks 5 and 6, respectively.
Seven of Cleveland's 10 touchdowns have come through the air this season. You get the picture. The Titans are facing a pass-first team coming off a week in which Saleh's secondary secured two interceptions. Something has to give.
No matter which way it gives, fingers will be pointed at the likes of S Amani Hooker, CB Cor'Dale Flott, and others.
On the whole, Cleveland's offense shouldn't be expected to struggle mightily for the third week in a row. It's uncharacteristic for this 4-2 group to score 13 or less points two weeks straight. Prior to that drought, the Browns scored 20+ points for three weeks straight.
This is an offense that, while inconsistent, has been better than the Titans' own offense and has exhibited the ability to explode against good defenses - their 27 points in a win over the aforementioned Steelers is perhaps the greatest example.
However, the Colts scored 20 points in their loss to the Titans last week. We can have a good defensive showing from Tennessee and a relative bounce back from Cleveland's offense at the same time. Relative is the key word there.
In fact, that's what most of us here at Titans On SI expect. Let's hope the line is drawn in the same way today, and that Tennessee's defense can make up for a scoring unit that simply hasn't proven their ability to win that Titans games up to now.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: CB Alontae Taylor's 1 Simple Position Change Could Save His Role With Titans
full_text:
When Alontae Taylor was brought to Nashville this offseason on a three-year, $58 million deal, nobody expected the highly touted CB to be benched in Week 6. More than likely, nobody expected the Titans to bench him at all. But the Titans did, and then the Titans won.
In Taylor's first game fully on the sidelines, Tennessee's secondary came down with two interceptions. Amani Hooker, who filled in for Taylor in covering Indianapolis Colts' WR1 Josh Downs, had what may have been the best game of his career.
Naturally, discussions about Taylor's role in Robert Saleh's defense caught fire. It seems clear now that Saleh sat him for football reasons (which paid off), but talks of a potential midseason trade picked up and haven't let off since.
Nobody wants to see one of Tennessee's premier offseason pickups give way to a trade that would likely see the Titans settle for mid-to-late-round draft compensation. All the same, if the team is better without him, it'd be better to rip that bandage sooner rather than later.
However, Coach Saleh isn't ready to give up on his big-pickup corner just yet. The Titans' coach plans to shift Taylor away from being solely played at the CB spot. The change has the potential to save Taylor's waning reputation in Nashville.
First things first, Taylor is taking the right steps for a player who was suddenly benched. Saleh acknowledged Taylor's positive energy during the game in spite of not playing, noting that the CB has had a good week of practice since.
When it comes to Taylor's return to the field, Saleh said, "We've gotten him some nickel reps... he's attacked the heck out of it."
"Our nickel is a lot different than the nickel that most nickels play, where it's a lot of man coverage." Saleh expressed a desire to identify Taylor's "fastball," between his ability to play both corner and nickel.
Taylor impressing in reps at the latter spot may be his key to working into the impactful position that the Titans brought him in to achieve in the first place. The roadblock in place for Taylor is, of course, Marcus Harris, who has played well at nickel for Tennessee.
"He still has to go earn it," Saleh added, praising Harris' work in his defense. "You've got to have multiple players at multiple spots."
Taylor's height and athleticism, at 6'1" 200 lbs, presents a promising physical makeup for a corner. But his career eight sacks (including one this season) speak to a potential advantage that he may have in the slot.
We're playing a waiting game that will likely last the entirety of this season to see where Taylor ends up in Saleh's defense. However, after a slow start to his first run in Nashville, Saleh giving Taylor the chance to shine in a different spot should be a hugely promising sign for Titans fans.
Tomorrow's duel with the Cleveland Browns could serve as a telling test for Taylor, depending on how much he sees the field. All eyes on Week 7.

title: 1 Bold Prediction on Offense and Defense for Titans' Home Battle vs. Browns
full_text:
The 1-5 Tennessee Titans somehow have us excited about football this week. Last Sunday's 26-20 win over the Indianapolis Colts painted a picture of a team capable of many of the metrics Robert Saleh was supposed to hit in his first season.
Better late than never right? Well, we've yet to see if Week 6 was any more than a lucky break like the last six or so Tennessee wins (over two seasons) have been. Tomorrow's battle with the 4-2 Cleveland Browns should be a great litmus test either way.
Ahead of that matchup, I'm making two bold predictions for the Titans: One on offense, and one on defense. We'll begin with the unit that has been less effective through six games.
Somehow, Cam Ward hasn't thrown a single score to a tight end this season. I suppose it doesn't help that he's only thrown four in general, but looks to the TEs have been extremely limited. Starter Gunnar Helm only has nine receptions for 60 yards on the season.
I am predicting that both of those things will change in Week 7.
Earlier this week, Ward said TEs have "one of the hardest jobs in the NFL," before hitting on his need to connect with Helm specifically. "That's something that we want to be able to do, is get Gunnar going. He's a very reliable red zone target."
Fellow TE Daniel Bellinger is also involved in the passing game, and could be in line for extended looks. But after arguably Ward's worst passing performance of the year last week, OC Brian Daboll will have to mix things up if his unit is to tick in the right direction for once.
It can only go up from here for the TEs. If changes are to be made, you have to think they get more involved; and if they get more involved, Helm will be the first to benefit.
On the flip side of the ball, I predict that the Titans' defensive line will come close to replicating their game-winning outing from last week.
Saleh's front sacked Colts QB Daniel Jones a whopping six times, with DT Jeffery Simmons forcing a fumble in a different instance. Against one of the NFL's weaker offensive lines (the Browns have let Deshuan Watson be sacked a league-high 24 times), the Titans have a path to repeat that success.
I don't believe the Titans will get as many as six sacks again. Although, with the defense hot and benefiting from an advantage on paper, four or five sacks feels right. Maybe a bit bold, but that's the nature of this article, after all.
Simmons had 1.5 sacks by himself in the Titans' win over the Browns last December. Look for another big game from Tennessee's leading man, to boot.

title: 4 Names, Obvious and Surprising, That Titans Could Deal Ahead of 2026 NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans haven't gotten off to the start they wanted or expected. This past Sunday marked the Titans' first win of the season with a 26-20 victory over the Indianapolis Colts in Lucas Oil Stadium, improving their record to 1-5 for the season. That's a far cry from the team bettering their three-win count from the last two years.
While that improvement is still possible, it certainly won't be easy.
Currently, Tennessee's route to making the playoffs is extremely challenging, with the Jacksonville Jaguars mounting the top of the AFC South with a 4-2 record. No team in NFL history has started the season 0-5 and still made the playoffs. The Cleveland Browns await Tennessee tomorrow.
With the NFL trade deadline is coming up on Nov. 10, this is the prime time for the Titans to sell at the build draft capital heading into the offseason. Given the state of this team and their rebuild, that may mean selling big. Here are a few potentially surprising candidates that Tennessee could move.
It's another year of DT Jeffery Simmons' name mentioned in the NFL trade rumor mill. The Titans' defensive captain was listed as No. 1 on The Athletic's trade big board .
The three-time All-Pro and perennial Pro Bowler is coveted for his dominance on the field at a premium position. His trade value should warrant decent picks, especially for a defensive player. There are two reasons that Tennessee may keep Simmons.
Firstly, the Titans would take on $21.2 million in 2027 if they traded Simmons due to his three-year extension he signed prior to the 2026 season.
Tennessee signed DT Jordan Elliott and DT John Franklin-Myers in the offseason to partner with Simmons. Franklin-Myers has dealt with injuries but remained active, and Elliott was recently cut due to an off-the-field incident involving a firearm.
Nonetheless, if the Titans front office looks to punt on the season, moving Simmons could bolster Tennessee's draft picks more than any other player. Losing Simmons has been feared in Nashville for a long time now, but it's been consistently mentioned for a reason.
Another name that could be moved from the Tennessee defense is S Amani Hooker. The 28-year-old has gathered more than 450 tackles and 14 interceptions across his eight-year career.
Similarly to Simmons, Hooker's deal is good through the 2028 season, which would add value to a potential deal.
Defensive backs are common trade deadline acquisitions for teams looking to contend for a Super Bowl, and the Titans could capitalize on his peak value, especially before he reaches his age-30 season.
This year already, Hooker is responsible for two of the Titans' four interceptions. His durability of playing 13 or more games in each of the last three seasons may make it hard for the Titans to trade him away, but the appeal should be there across the league nonetheless.
Tony Pollard has been perhaps the most common name floated in trade propsitions for the Titans this offseason.
The 29-year-old Pollard has been the Titans' go-to back all season. He has the 13th most carries with 87 at four yards per carry. Tennessee has used Pollard as a workhorse over his three-year tenure in Nashville.
While Pollard's stats don't jump off the page, he has only missed two games across his previous four seasons. An impressive feat considering he's getting close to 300 touches per season. Over the previous four seasons, Pollard has rushed for 1,000-plus yards. Value for running backs is typically low.
Regardless, if the Titans are ready to turn the younger and arguably more versatile backup RB Tyjae Spears, this deadline would be the perfect time to do it.
Spears is in his age 25 season, and third-string rookie RB Nick Singleton is 22. Moving Pollard at the deadline would make the backfield younger for a position group that doesn't favor players after the age of 30.
After recording a healthy scratch against the Colts on Week 5, CB Alonte Taylor could be in a potential mid-season trade.
Prior to the 2026 season, the Titans signed Taylor to a three-year deal worth $58 million. Unfortunately, Taylor hasn't panned out like the Titans hoped this season. Head coach Robert Saleh told the media after the benching that he's exploring a change in Taylor's role from a corner to a nickel.
At 27 years old, there's plenty of upside left in Taylor, drafted in the second round out of Tennessee, and had four solid years in New Orleans. His career numbers of eight sacks, three forced fumbles and four interceptions are truly unique.
Taylor's contract may hinder other teams from making a deal. In the meantime, the Titans are hoping the CB bounces back for the better at a new position.
